Name of the applicant: [Applicant]
Application Dated : 21.09.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1358)/IC/16 dated 20.10.2017

1. What is remuneration of every MPs & Ministers of Parliament.
Reply: The Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules as amended from time to time: 1.The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954. 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules,1957 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilites (Members of Parliament)Rules, 1956 4. The Medical Facilties (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowance) Rules, 1986 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the Purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The aforementioned Act/Rules are available on Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, Govt. of India website and can be accessed through http://mpa.nic.in/MPA/act.aspx. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.

2. Which perquisite are provided to every MPs & Ministers.
Reply: The details of facilities/benefits provided to the MPs, Lok Sabha is available in bilingual in the website www.loksabha.nic.in. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.

3. Details of total expenditure of Lok Sabha Session.
Reply: The expenditure on proceedings of Parliament Session is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments. There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Ministries/Departments/Rajya Sabha Secretariat etc. in connection with the conduct of Parliament. Session-wise expenditure incurred out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha is not available with IFU. However, Head of account-wise expenditure incurred [from Financial year 2009-10 to 2016-17 (upto 31.3.2017)] out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha and booked by P&AO, Lok Sabha, is available on Lok Sabha homepage under link: http://164.100.47.194/loksabha/Secretariat/DemandLokSabha.aspx

4. What amount of expenditure is making on the tours of every MPs.
Reply: Conference Branch deals with the visits of Indian Parliamentary Delegations going abroad under bilateral exchange and for attending Parliamentary Conferences related to IPU & CPA events. The details of such visits in connection with the Inter Parliamentary Union (IPU), Commonwealth Parliamentary Association (CPA) and Conference Branch (other than IPU Cell and CPA Cell) is available on the website of Lok Sabha `www.loksabha.nic.in' under the link `Conference'. The applicant may be advised to access the above website.

5. Please provide information regarding total number of sessions of Parliament during the year 2016 and how many sessions is attended by each MPs and Ministers of Parliament.
Reply: Number of sessions of Lok Sabha in the year, 2016 is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Resume of Work'. An attendance register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member wise Attendance -> All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.
*******
response_full_text: The Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament are regulated by specified Acts/Rules available on the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs website. Details of facilities/benefits to MPs are available on www.loksabha.nic.in. Session-wise expenditure out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha is not available with IFU; however head of account-wise expenditure (FY 2009-10 to 2016-17) is available on the Lok Sabha homepage. Details of tour/delegation visits are available on the Lok Sabha website under 'Conference'. Number of sessions in 2016 and member attendance details are available on www.loksabha.nic.in.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated 11.08.2017 (recd. on 19.09.2017)
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1341)/IC/17 dated 17.10.2017

Sl. No. 1: Please provide the information regarding total number of days of sessions held during the last two years and the current year. How many members were absent during this period. Does Parliament follow digital signature system. Provide information regarding deductions made from the salaries and allowances of members of Parliament due to absence from the sittings of the House. Also provide a copy of the service manual of Parliament and list of members who remain absent from the sittings of the House along with their names, Party affiliation, address and phone number.
Reply: Information relating to sittings of Lok Sabha since 2015 is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. www.loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Resume of Work'. As regards the 12th session, requisite information is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. www.loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Bulletin-I'. Hence, the applicant may access information from the above website link.
An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member-wise Attendance -> All Members respectively.
The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day.
The list of all the members of 16th Lok Sabha along with their names, party affiliation etc. is available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under heading Members -> Sitting Members -> Alphabetical List respectively. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information.
At present, there is no biometric system for recording the attendance of members in Lok Sabha.
The Salary, Allowances and other facilities provided to Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules: 1. The Salary, Allowances and pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended) 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956. 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959. 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960. 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986. 7. The Members of Parliament Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986. 8. The Members of parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha i.e. http://mpa.nic.in/MPA/act.aspx.
As regards the information relating to Sitting Members of the present Lok Sabha (i.e. Members' name, Party name, address and Phone number) the same is available on the Lok Sabha Website <www.loksabha.nic.in> under the heading 'Members' 'Sitting Members' 'Members' Biographical Sketch' (Alphabetical). These details can also be accessed under the heading “Contact Details”. (Sample copy enclosed).
response_full_text: Information relating to sittings of Lok Sabha since 2015 is available on the Lok Sabha website. An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers). Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register during all sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha are available on the Lok Sabha website. The list of all members of the 16th Lok Sabha with names and party affiliation is available on the website. At present, there is no biometric system for recording attendance of members in Lok Sabha. The Salary, Allowances and other facilities of MPs are regulated by eight specified Acts/Rules, available on the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs website. Information on Sitting Members' name, party, address and phone number is available on the Lok Sabha website under Members' Biographical Sketch / Contact Details (sample copy enclosed).

Reply: An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Further, soft copy of the text of Lok Sabha Debates (including Questions and Answers) is available on the website of Lok Sabha at: http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Debates/DebateAdvSearch16.aspx (for debates), http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qtextsearch.aspx (for questions). Since Shri Navjot Singh Sidhu was also a member of Rajya Sabha, it is for the Rajya Sabha Secretariat to furnish the relevant information as per their records.

questions: लोक सभा सचिवालय में वर्ष 2005 से अब तक नियुक्त केंद्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी एवं प्रथम अपीलीय प्राधिकारी के नाम की सूची (मुद्दा संख्या 4)
भारत सरकार/राज्य सरकारों/न्यायालयों में प्रयोग की जाने वाली भाषा से संबंधित जानकारी
थाना-कुंडली, जिला-सोनीपत (हरियाणा) आदि से संबंधित अन्य विविध मामले
response_summary: लोक सभा सचिवालय ने बताया कि आवेदन की विषयवस्तु केवल केंद्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी और अपीलीय प्राधिकारियों की सूची (मुद्दा सं. 4) से संबंधित है, जो संलग्न है; शेष मुद्दे विभिन्न राज्य सरकारों/लोक प्राधिकरणों से संबंधित होने के कारण डीओपीटी के कार्यालय ज्ञापन के अनुसार अंतरित नहीं किए जा सकते, और आवेदक को सलाह दी गई कि वह संबंधित राज्य सरकारों/प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क करे।

प्रशासन से प्राप्त की जाए। ऐसे मामले में आवेदन को राज्य सरकार/संघ राज्य क्षेत्र प्रशासन को अंतरित करने की

title: RTI on Applicability of DoPT Pay Fixation Order to Ex-Servicemen
subject: RTI seeking information on the applicability of a DoPT Office Memorandum on pay fixation for re-employed Ex-Servicemen in Lok Sabha Secretariat.
questions: Is this DoPT OM [No.3/19/2009-Estt. (Pay II) dated 05.04.2010] applicable to Ex-Servicemen working in your office or not.

How many Ex-Servicemen applied for pay fixation and how many of them got their pay re-fixed as per DoPT OM No. 3/19/2009-Estt (Pay II) dated 05.04.2010 and 08.11.2010 respectively?
Give the names, designation and Deptt./Section/Branch of all Ex-Servicemen who got their pay fixed as per DoPT OMs mentioned in para 3.

No reply text was available for the fourth point (names/designations of Ex-Servicemen who got pay fixed).

title: RTI on Calculation of Per-Minute Cost of Parliament Session
subject: RTI seeking details of how the cost per minute of running a parliamentary session is calculated and the total annual cost.
questions: How cost of per minute of a running parliamentary session is calculated? What are all the factors considered & taken in to account for cost evaluation? Is that a arbitrary value? What is the cost of per minute of running parliament and total cost per year?

title: RTI on Salary, Attendance and Removal Rules for MPs
subject: RTI seeking information on the rules governing salary payment, attendance requirements, and removal of Members of Parliament for non-attendance.
questions: Criteria to pay salary to the MPs
How much attendance compulsory to get salary from Government for MPs?
Whether it is necessary for MPs to inform their working schedule to the Speaker, Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha.
How many MPs have followed this Rule.
Removal of MPs on the basis of "No Work No Pay".
response_summary: The Secretariat explained the Acts and Rules regulating MP salary, allowances and pensions, clarified that salary is payable for the whole term regardless of attendance (though Daily Allowance depends on attendance), noted that MPs usually inform the Speaker regarding Leave of Absence, pointed the applicant to Lok Sabha's website for related committee reports, and explained that 'No work no pay' is not a laid-down principle though a seat can be declared vacant under Article 101(4) for 60 days' unauthorised absence. Point 6 of the original application was separately forwarded to the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation.

response_full_text: 1. Criteria to pay salary to the MPs - The Salary, perks and other allowances to Members of Parliament (including nominated members) are regulated by the following Act/Rules: 1. The Salary, Allowances and pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended) 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956. 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959. 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960. 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986. 7. The Members of Parliament Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986. 8. The Members of parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha which can be accessed through http://164.100.47.132/LssNew/members/AMENITIES.aspx. However, a pamphlet containing the requisite information is also enclosed herewith. 2. How much attendance compulsory to get salary from Government for MPs? - A Member is entitled to receive salary during the whole term of office. Attendance is only required for calculating Daily Allowances for each day of attending session and other parliamentary duties. 3. Whether it is necessary for MPs to inform their working schedule to the Speaker, Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha - The Lok Sabha members usually inform Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha regarding Leave of Absence from the sittings of the House for a particular period. 4. How many MPs have followed this Rule - The details regarding grant of leave of absence to the members of Lok Sabha are available on the website of Lok Sabha under the heading Committees-Other Parliamentary Committees-Committee on Absence of Members from the sittings of the House-15th Lok Sabha- reports presented respectively. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. 5. Removal of MPs on the basis of 'No Work No Pay' - The principle of 'No work No pay' has not been laid down in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. The seat of a Member may, however, under the provisions of Article 101(4) be declared vacant by the House, if he/she for a period of 60 days is (without permission of the House) absent from all meetings thereof, provided that in computing the said period of sixty days, no account shall be taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or is adjourned for more than four consecutive days.

subject: RTI seeking complete information on bravery awards, certificates of honour and monetary benefits given to government servants for their role during the December 2001 militant attack on Parliament.

questions: Is soft drinks manufactured by Pepsi and Coca-cola banned in Indian Parliament? If so, why?

subject: आरटीआई आवेदन में सरकारी भाषा-प्रयोग, जाट आरक्षण संबंधी मामलों तथा लोक सभा सचिवालय के के.ज.सू.अधि./अपीलीय प्राधिकारियों की सूची से संबंधित सूचना मांगी गई।
questions: भारत सरकार/राज्य सरकारों/न्यायालयों में प्रयोग की जाने वाली भाषा और जाट आरक्षण आदि से संबंधित मामलों की जानकारी।
लोक सभा सचिवालय में वर्ष 2005 से अब तक नियुक्त के.ज.सू.अधि. (CPIO) और अपीलीय प्राधिकारियों की सूची (मुद्दा सं. 4)।
response_summary: लोक सभा सचिवालय ने केवल मुद्दा सं. 4 (के.ज.सू.अधि. और अपीलीय प्राधिकारियों की सूची) का उत्तर संलग्न सूची के रूप में दिया; शेष मुद्दे विभिन्न संगठनों/राज्य सरकारों से संबंधित होने के कारण अंतरित नहीं किए जा सके, तथा आवेदक को संबंधित प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क करने की सलाह दी गई।

सूचना प्रकोष्ठ, संसद भवन, नई दिल्ली-110001
सं. 1(1192)/स.प्र./16                                                                    दिनांक 16.09.2016

प्रेषक

विषय: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना।

महोदय,
माननीय लोक सभा अध्यक्ष को संबोधित और इस सचिवालय में दिनांक 24.06.2016 को प्राप्त आपके
दिनांक 13.06.2016 के आरटीआई आवेदन, जो भारत सरकार/राज्य सरकारों/न्यायालयों में प्रयोग की जाने
वाली भाषा और जाट आरक्षण आदि से संबंधित अन्य विविध मामलों के बारे में है, के संदर्भ में मुझे यह बताने
का निदेश हुआ है कि केवल के.ज.सू.अधि. और अपीलीय प्राधिकारियों की सूची से संबंधित मुद्दा सं. 4 के बारे
में आपके आवेदन की विषयवस्तु लोक सभा सचिवालय से संबंधित है और यह संलग्न है।

2. आवेदन के अन्य मुद्दे लोक सभा सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं हैं बल्कि ये विभिन्न संगठनों/एजैंसियों/राज्य
सरकारों से संबंधित हैं। आपका आवेदन डीओपीटी के दिनांक 12.06.2008 और 24.09.2010 के कार्यालय
ज्ञापन सं. 10/2/2008-आईआर के मद्देनजर अंतरित नहीं किया जा सकता जिसमें यह कहा गया है कि यदि
कोई व्यक्ति कोई ऐसी सूचना प्राप्त करने के लिए किसी लोक प्राधिकारी के पास आवेदन भेजता है जो किसी
राज्य सरकार अथवा संघ राज्य क्षेत्र प्रशासन के अधीन किसी लोक प्राधिकरण से संबंधित हो तो उस प्राधिकरण
के आवेदन प्राप्त करने वाले के.ज.सू.अधि. द्वारा आवेदक को यह सूचित किया जाना चाहिए कि अपेक्षित सूचना
संबंधित राज्य सरकार/संघ राज्य क्षेत्र प्रशासन से प्राप्त की जाए। ऐसे मामले में आवेदन को राज्य सरकार/संघ
राज्य क्षेत्र प्रशासन को अंतरित करने की आवश्यकता नहीं है।

3. अतः, आपको सलाह दी जाती है कि अपेक्षित सूचना प्राप्त करने के लिए आप विभिन्न राज्य सरकारों और
लोक प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क करें।

4. 10/- रुपये के आवेदन शुल्क की रसीद सं. 4324 दिनांक 24.06.2016 संलग्न है।

5. इसे के.ज.सू.अधि. का अनुमोदन प्राप्त है।

भवदीय,
संलग्न: यथोपरि।

response_full_text: Parliament Library of Lok Sabha Secretariat maintains hard copy of Lok Sabha Proceedings. Lok Sabha Debates are microfilmed. Lok Sabha Debates from 1996 onwards are available on the web page of Lok Sabha. A Digitisation Unit has been setup to digitize the remaining debates. Video recordings of the selected Lok Sabha Proceedings since 1992, entire Lok Sabha proceedings from 22 April 1994 onwards and recordings of LSTV Programmes since its inception in 2006 are available in the archives of A.V & T Unit, comprising: 1543 Cassettes in U-Matic Format (24 Feb 1992 - 1 Sep 1997 selected/entire), 2905 Cassettes in VHS format (24 Feb 1992 - 26 Feb 2009), 3142 Cassettes in Betacam Format (19 Nov 1997 - 22 Mar 2006), 2260+ Cassettes in DVC Pro Format (from 16 Feb 2006), and 25950 Cassettes in DVC Pro Format (LSTV programmes since 2006). The applicant may make a specific request for particular recordings, which will be provided on DVD at Rs. 150/- per DVD (up to 2 hrs) for personal, non-commercial use, on advance payment by cash or demand draft in favour of 'DDO, Lok Sabha'.

title: MP absence from House and rule for raising public interest issues
subject: RTI query (points 14 & 15) on consequences of an MP's absence from the House and the rule under which MPs can raise public interest issues.
questions: Is the MP unaware of being present in the House. If a parliamentary member is absent from the House, then what action is possible on him.

A Member of Parliament can ask a Question on a matter of public importance as per the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha and Directions by the Speaker, Lok Sabha relating to admissibility of Questions. title: First appeal seeking details of MP Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi's medical treatment record
subject: Applicant's first appeal sought fuller details on whether Members of Parliament use private/government hospitals and their treatment expenditure records, specifically regarding Shri Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi's disease and treatment cost.
questions: Seeking regarding MPs is taking health service in any hospital (private or government or both) and maintain record of all treatment expenditure of all those MPs.
response_summary: The MSA Branch clarified that CGHS beneficiaries, including MPs, can take treatment at CGHS/Government hospitals or, in emergencies, private hospitals; it stated that Shri Priya Ranjan Dasmunshi had availed treatment only at Apollo Hospital, New Delhi, as spouse of the then MP Smt. Deepa Dasmunshi who became a Cabinet Minister with effect from 28.10.2012, after which no record is maintained by the branch.

1 | संसद सदस्यों के संबंध में जानकारी मांगी गई है कि क्या उन्होंने किसी अस्पताल (निजी या सरकारी अथवा दोनों) में स्वास्थ्य सेवा ली है और उन सभी संसद सदस्यों के सभी उपचार पर हुए खर्च का अभिलेख | संबंधित शाखा ने सूचना दी है कि सीजीएचएस के दिशानिर्देशों के अनुसार, संसद सदस्यों सहित सीजीएचएस लाभार्थी सीजीएचएस अस्पताल/सरकारी अस्पताल से उपचार करा सकते हैं। तथापि, आपातकालीन स्थिति में लाभार्थी किसी निजी अस्पताल में भी उपचार करा सकते हैं। एमएसए शाखा के रिकार्ड के अनुसार, श्री प्रियरंजन दासमुंशी ने श्रीमती दीपा दासमुंशी, तत्कालीन लोक सभा सदस्य के पति होने के कारण केवल अपोलो अस्पताल, नई दिल्ली से उपचार कराया है, जो 28.10.2012 से कैबिनेट मंत्री बन गई थीं। इसलिए, 28.10.2012 के बाद संबंधित शाखा में कोई रिकार्ड नहीं है।

title: RTI on mobile connections and expenditure provided to Members of Parliament
subject: Applicant sought details of mobile phone connections and expenditure provided to Members of Parliament, including a list of MPs with their mobile numbers and email IDs.
questions: Information reg. expenditure on mobile number
Please provide which mobile connection have been provided to all Members of Parliament by the Government.
Please provide name of MPs who are using government mobile numbers.
Information reg. expenditure on mobile number and provided details for last five years
List of MPs with mobile number and email ID
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that mobile telephone facility is regulated by the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956, with each MP provided two mobile connections (MTNL and BSNL); it did not name specific MPs using government numbers, and referred the applicant to the Lok Sabha website and Sales Counter for the members' list and contact details.

title: Information on non-functioning days and cost of Lok Sabha sessions
subject: RTI seeking information on the number of days of non-functioning of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha since the 5th Lok Sabha and the associated costs.
questions: Information on number of days of non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha since 5th Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Fixed cost of functioning of/partial functioning
Cost such as salary/other expenses of Members of the House for such days and any other expenses indicating reasons etc.
response_summary: Information on non-functioning days is available on the Lok Sabha website for the 13th to 16th Lok Sabhas; earlier data would require disproportionate diversion of resources under Section 7(9). No mechanism exists to calculate day-wise session cost, and the query was also transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]

Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1082)/IC/15 dated 25.08.15

1. Information on number of days of non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha since 5th Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha —
Regarding information on non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha since the 5th Lok Sabha onwards, which stretches over a period of more than 45 years. Information about details of non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha during the 15th, 14th and 13th Lok Sabhas, is available at Lok Sabha website i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in -> Resume -> Archive -> 15th, 14th and 13th Lok Sabhas -> Statement showing time lost due to interruption and adjournments (Session and date-wise). The first two sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha is also available on the same website. Hence, the applicant is advised to access information during the period from 1999 till the second session of the 16th Lok Sabha from above website link. During the 3rd and 4th sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha, the House has been adjourned due to interruption for 3 hours and 26 minutes and 7 hours and 11 minutes respectively.
Moreover, it is stated that as per Section 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005 "information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the Public authority.." And to search for number of days of non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha since the year 1971 (commencement of 5th Lok Sabha) would divert a sizeable amount of time and manpower of the Secretariat.
However, the applicant is advised to visit the Parliament Library by taking prior appointment with Sh. Sunil Kesari, Director to access Lok Sabha debates for information regarding the time lost due to interruptions and adjournments in House prior to 1999, since the same is not available on the Lok Sabha website.

2. Fixed cost of functioning of/partial functioning; Cost such as salary/other expenses of Members of the House for such days and any other expenses indicating reasons etc. —
There is no mechanism to calculate the expenditure for a day of session. To conduct Parliament Session, numerous public authorities viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, NDMC, MCD, Delhi Jal Board, CPWD, Delhi Police, SPG, CRPF and several ministries are involved. Hence, such information is maintained by multiple public authorities involving several Ministries under various head of expenditure. Hence, it is not available on records of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules: The Salary, Allowances and pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended); The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957; The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956; The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959; The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960; The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986; The Members of Parliament Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986 & The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988.
The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in.
Also transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
response_full_text: Regarding information on non-functioning or partial functioning of Lok Sabha since the 5th Lok Sabha onwards... [see extracted_text Annexure for complete reply].

title: RTI on official opposition party quorum rule and Mavalankar Formula
subject: आवेदक ने विपक्ष के आधिकारिक दर्जे हेतु 10% कोरम नियम, मावलंकर फार्मूला, संसद अधिनियम 1977 और NHRC/CVC/CIC निकायों के चयन में विपक्ष नेता की भूमिका की जानकारी मांगी।
questions: Act which requires quorum of 10% in Lok Sabha before a party is considered as the official opposition party.
Details of Mavalankar Formula.
Copy of Parliament Act 1977.
Provision to select the bodies of NHRC, CVC, CIC.
Has any Party demanded to give recognition as Opposition party?
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified there is no requirement for the Secretariat to answer a query rather than furnish information; that there is no such thing as the 'Mavalankar's Formula' (Shri G.V. Mavalankar was the first Speaker, 1952-56); that no Act titled 'Parliament Act, 1977' exists (likely meaning the Salary and Allowances of Leader of Opposition Act, 1977, whose query was forwarded to Ministry of Law); the NHRC/CVC/CIC point was transferred to M/o Parliamentary Affairs; and it confirmed that Smt. Sonia Gandhi, MP, along with Shri Mallikarjun Kharge and Capt. Amarinder Singh, had written to the Speaker seeking recognition of the Leader of the Congress Party as Leader of Opposition.

Three Members of Parliament are staying w.e.f. 24.7.15 and two nominated MPs are staying in Hotel Janpath w.e.f. 13.8.2015. Party wise information is not maintained. Regarding conveyance - There is a transport desk in Parliament House from where vehicles are provided to facilitate the Members to go from Parliament House Complex to their residences and vice-versa.

The expenditure on working of Parliament is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments. Under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha, Head of account-wise allocation is made for booking the expenditure incurred on Members of Lok Sabha and staff of Lok Sabha Secretariat. No separate budget provision is kept for session-wise proceedings of Lok Sabha. Allocation made under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha from the Financial Year 2009-10 to 2015-16 is available on Lok Sabha homepage. However, a copy of the same for the Financial Year 2015-16 is enclosed herewith.

Table office of the Secretariat deals with the proceedings viz. Zero Hour (Special Mention), Matters under Rule 377, Calling Attention, Adjournment Motion and Submission. Members of different political parties submit their notices under above mentioned proceedings on the day or for the week they desire to raise the matter/subject in the House. Notices admitted are raised/laid by members in the House and incorporated in the Lok Sabha proceedings; the applicant may access such information on Lok Sabha website under 'Debates' -> 'Uncorrected Debates'. Legislative Branch-I deals with discussions on Motions under rule 184 and Short Duration Discussions under rule 193; from the application it is not clear exactly what the applicant wants, so he may clarify the exact information required.

An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers). Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha are available on the Lok Sabha website under Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance Total. The applicant may visit the website to access the desired information.

title: RTI on Legal Status of Parliamentary Committees and Employees
subject: RTI seeking clarity on the status (government/semi-government/private) of Parliamentary Committees, and whether their employees are deemed Government Servants entitled to Central Government pay benefits, and whether such committees fall under the RTI Act.
questions: What is the status of the committees which are constituted by the act of Parliament? i) Government Status ii) Semi Government Status iii) Private
Whether the employees working under such committees are treated/deemed to be Government Servant. Please give specific answer in the form of "YES" or "NO".

Whether the employees working under such committees are eligible for benefits of Pay Commissions, D.A. and other facilities etc. declared by the Central Government from time to time? Please give specific answer in the form of "YES" or "NO".
Whether these committees come under the preview of the RTI Act 2005. Please give specific answer in the form of "YES" or "NO".
response_summary: The reply explained that only the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament is constituted by an Act of Parliament, and that Lok Sabha Secretariat employees are governed by the Lok Sabha Secretariat (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, and are not Central Government Employees. Direct yes/no answers to the specific sub-questions were not explicitly given.

1.
What
is
the
status
of
the
committees
which
are
constituted
by
the
act
of
Parliament?
i)Government Status
ii)Semi Government Status
iii)Private
The term 'Parliamentary Committee' has been
defined in rule 2(1) of the Rules of Procedure and
Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha as under:-

'Parliamentary Committee' means a Committee
which is appointed or elected by the House or
nominated by the Speaker and which works under
the direction of the Speaker and presents its
report to the House or to the Speaker and the
Secretariat for which is provided by the Lok Sabha
Secretariat.

Accordingly, a Parliamentary Committee may be
constituted in pursuance of the provisions of the
Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of
either House or motions adopted by the House, or
pursuant to the provisions of an act of Parliament
or under the inherent powers of the Hon'ble
Speaker or the Chairman, Rajya Sabha.

Only one Parliamentary Committee i.e. Joint
Committee
on
Salaries
and
Allowances
of
Members of Parliament has been constituted by
the Act of Parliament. The Lok Sabha Secretariat
is providing  Secretarial Assistance to the above-
said Committee.  In exercise of powers conferred
by Article 98(3) of the Constitution, the Lok Sabha
Secretariat(Recruitment
and
Conditions
of
Service) Rules, 1955 have been framed and
promulgated by the President after consultation
with the Speaker, Lok Sabha on 01st October,
1955.  Thus,  Lok Sabha Secretariat, the
Legislative Wing of the State, is a separate body
and functions under the administrative control of
Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha.   Accordingly,  the
employees of the Lok Sabha Secretariat are
governed
by
the
Lok
Sabha
Secretariat(Recruitment
and
Conditions
of
Service)
Rules,
1955
and
are
not
Central
Government Employees
2.
Whether the employees working
under
such
committees
are
treated/deemed
to
be
Government Servant.   Please
give specific answer in the form
of "YES" or "NO".
3.
Whether the employees working
under
such
committees
are
eligible
for
benefits
of
Pay
Commissions, D.A. and other
facilities etc. declared by the
Central Government from time
to time?  Please give specific
answer in the form of "YES" or
"NO".
4.
Whether these committees come
under the preview of the RTI Act
2005.

Please
give
specific
answer in the form of "YES" or
"NO".

rows: Status of committees constituted by act of Parliament (Government/Semi-Government/Private)

Only the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament is constituted by an Act of Parliament; Lok Sabha Secretariat employees are governed by the LSS (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, and are not Central Government Employees.
Whether committee employees are deemed Government Servants, eligible for Central Govt pay benefits, and whether committees fall under RTI Act 2005 (Yes/No sought)
No explicit Yes/No answer given; see reply to point 1.

Name of the Applicant: Sh. XXXXXXXXX

Points raised
Reply
(in brief)

1. List of Lok Sabha members elected from Karnataka in general elections 2014 and their
constituencies.
The information about the list of Lok Sabha members elected from Karnataka in 2014 (i.e.
16th Lok Sabha) and their constituency, is available on the Lok Sabha website
<www.loksabha.nic.in> under the heading 'Members' -- 'Sitting Members' -> 'State Wise
List' (Sample copy enclosed).

2. Number of Questions asked, debates participated and bills presented by the Members in 16th
Lok Sabha till date.
The information regarding the State-wise MPs is not maintained separately by
the Question Branch (Lok Sabha). However, the Questions asked by Members of Parliament
during the current Lok Sabha along with their replies are available on the Lok Sabha website
i.e. loksabha.nic.in under the heading 'Questions' or directly through the following
links:-
http://164.100.47.94/Loksabha/Questions/StatisticalStatements.aspx(Statement-4).
http://164.100.47.94/Loksabha/Questions/Qmembersearch.aspx
http://164.100.47.94/Loksabha/Members/MemberHomePage.aspx
The applicant is requested to go through the above website/links.

The applicant may be informed that Union Ministers introduce Bills in their official capacity
and not as individual Members. From the query of the applicant, it seems that he is
interested in information regarding the Private Member Bills. However, a list of the Bills
piloted by Union Ministers hailing from State of Karnataka, during the Sixteenth Lok Sabha, is
given below:
1. The Appropriation (Railways) No.2 Bill, 2014
2. The Appropriation (Railways) No.3 Bill, 2014
3. The Railways (Amendment) Bill, 2014.
4. The Repealing and Amending Bill, 2014.
5. The Appropriation Acts (Repeal) Bill, 2015
6. The Repealing and Amending (Fourth) Bill, 2015.
7. The High Court and the Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Services)
Amendment Bill, 2015.
8. The Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Bill, 2015.
9. The Commercial Division and Commercial Appellate Division of High Court and
Commercial Courts Bill, 2015.
10. The Election Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2016.
11. The Collection of Statistics (Amendment) Bill, 2017.
All these Bills were piloted by Shri D.V. Sadananda Gowda.
Legislative Branch-II does not maintain any State-wise, member-wise catalogue of
Private Members' Bills introduced in Lok Sabha.
However, a total of 774 Private Members' Bills were introduced during current Lok Sabha, of
which a total of 718 Private Members' Bills are pending in Lok Sabha till date.
The applicant may access the list of Private Members' Bills pending in Lok Sabha
from the following link :-
Lok Sabha Home Page > Business > Bulletin-II dated 26.5.2017

3. Attendance of the members of 16th Lok Sabha till date session wise.
An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy
Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign it against their names in token of having
attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing
the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha
are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings
Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members-> Member-wise Attendance -> All
Members respectively.
The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of
the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day.
The applicant is requested to visit the website and access the desired information.

4. Text of the Questions raised/asked by Mr. P.C. Mohan
Please see reply to point no. 2 above.

5. Details of expenditure by Shri P.C. Mohan under MPLAD Fund till date
Transferred to M/o Statistics & Programme Implementation.

6. Attendance of Mr. Rahul Gandhi in 16th Lok Sabha till date
Please see reply to point no. 3 above.

title: Creation of LARRDIS Director Posts RTI Reply
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ / Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat (LARRDIS / Administration Branch-I / O&M Section)
subject: RTI seeking file notings, rules and financial implications concerning the creation of Director and Additional Director posts in LARRDIS, and related O&M studies and restructuring history.
questions: An authenticated copy of the file(s) notings wherein the post of six Directors and thirteen posts of Additional Directors in LARRDIS were created vide Order No.PDA-1334/2016 dated 5th January, 2016.

A copy of the Rules/Regulations/Instructions under which procedure is codified for creating/abolishing posts in various Services of Lok Sabha Secretariat and whether the same was followed in creating the above mentioned posts in LARRDIS.

The basis of creating these temporary posts retrospectively with effect from 17.11.2015 to 31.3.2018 by the order issued on 05/07/2016. Whether these temporary posts would be converted to permanent after 31.03.2018 or would be abolished thereafter. Please provide copy of Rules which authorise creation of posts in such manner alongwith a copy of the decision of the Competent Authority to continue or abolish the post after 31.03.2018.

The financial implications involved for operationalising of these 19 posts including the cumulative effect on promotion in the down line in LARRDIS. Whether budgetary provisions were made before creating these posts. If yes, please provide the opinion of IFU/O&M. If not, the grounds on which the prior opinion of IFU/O&M was not obtained.

Whether any study by O&M Section was done or O&M recommended to create aforesaid posts for LARRDIS before creating these 19 posts. If yes, a copy of the recommendations of the O&M Section for creating these posts may be provided. If not, the grounds on which the posts were created may kindly be provided.

Whether posts in other Services in a similar manner as the creation of above mentioned 19 posts in LARRDIS of Lok Sabha Secretariat have been created since 2000. If yes, please furnish a copy of the order and the basis of creating such post in other Services of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
The details of the Units/Branches/Desks etc in various Services in operation with Administrative approval of AN-I in Lok Sabha Secretariat and their mandate may kindly be provided.

As listed vide Office Order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016, a list of Units/Desks/Sections/Branches/Wings etc. in operation in LARRDIS which are de facto functioning without the recommendation of O&M/Administration Branch-I.

Whether any O&M study has been made so far in respect of LARRDIS Service during the last 10 years for re-structuring of Service/creating/abolishing the posts. If yes, a copy thereof may kindly be provided and if not, the reasons thereof.

Whether any of the Chairman of the Parliamentary Committees has ever suo moto requested for deputing personnel of LARRDIS or for providing research assistance/inputs to the Parliamentary Committees. If yes, copy/copies of such letters/notes may kindly be provided.
response_summary: The Secretariat enclosed file notings on the post creation, cited Rule 3 of the LSS (Recruitment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 1955, referred financial and O&M related queries to the enclosed file notings, stated some queries were hypothetical or vague, noted no O&M restructuring study had been done for LARRDIS in the last 10 years, and stated one point regarding Parliamentary Committee requests was still under process.

subject: RTI concerning whether Parliament Museum officers are governed by LSS Conduct Rules, the regularisation of a named Deputy Curator, dependent/pension benefit claims, and an alleged FIR against him.
questions: Please supply the information whether officers of Parliament Museum are governed by the LSS Conduct rules which are more or less in congruence with the CSS Conduct rules.
If yes, please supply the information whether officers recruited against ex-cadre posts can be regularized (in violation of DoPT guidelines) as per the LSS Conduct Rules.
If No, then please supply me information under what provisions of the LSS Conduct Rules, were the services of Suman Datta, Dy. Curator regularized.

Please supply the information whether LSS allows parents of officials of the Secretariat who are drawing pension from Central/State exchequer to be shown as dependents on their children who are working in the Secretariat and allows such pensioners to claim double advantage of seeking Leave Travel Concessions as well as medical re-imbursement from the Secretariat in addition from the office from which retired.

If, no, please supply me information whether Suman Datta has shown his father who is a retired State Government employee and drawing pension as dependent upon him by giving a false declaration to the Secretariat to claim pecuniary advantage for himself.
Information whether employees of Lok Sabha Secretariat are required to keep the office intimated is any FIR is lodged against them or when they are appearing before any court of law.
Information whether LSS is aware that an FIR has been registered against Shri Suman Dutta under Section 498 A/406/34-IPC in PS Naveen Shahdra, Delhi-110094
Information as to what action does LSS propose to take against Shri Suman Dutta for hiding information from LSS regarding registration of FIR

Point 1 & 2: What is the current Telephone allowance for a Member of Parliament? What was the Telephone allowance for a Member of Parliament in April 2014? Information/Reply: There is no provision of such Telephone allowance given to MPs. 1,50,000 local calls in a year is provided to Members under the MSA Act, 1954. The excess calls made by a Member are adjustable from the free local calls available to him for the next year. The unutilized calls of a year are carried over to the subsequent years till the seat of a member becomes vacant.
Point 3: What are the different type of allowances a Member of Parliament is entitled to receive other than pension Information/Reply: The Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament are regulated by: 1. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957; 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959; 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960; 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowance) Rules, 1986; 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the Purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986; 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. These are available on the Lok Sabha website (www.loksabha.nic.in) under 'Members' > 'Salary Act and Rules'.
Point 4, 5 & 6: What is Pension for a Member of Parliament presently. What was the Pension for a Member of Parliament in April 2014. Is it true that if a person becomes Member of Parliament for one day also, he is entitled to get the pension. If yes, then how much. Information/Reply: Every person who has served as a member of the Provisional Parliament or either House of Parliament for any period is entitled to pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month with effect from 18.05.2009. Where any person has served the Parliament for a period exceeding five years, he/she shall be entitled to an additional pension @ Rs.1,500/- per month for every year in excess of five years. For the purpose of calculation of years for determination of additional pension, a period of nine months or more is rounded off to one complete year.

No. 1 Reply: The procedure to watch the proceedings of the Lok Sabha for a common man is that his filled application form recommended by Hon'ble MP (Lok Sabha) available at the CPIC/Reception Office (Lok Sabha)/Official website of Lok Sabha (www.parliamentofindia.nic.in), providing the details (Applicant's and his father's name in full, age, occupation, full local address and permanent address) required in the proforma and duly signed by an Hon'ble MP (Lok Sabha) from his constituency or any other constituency. The passes for the galleries may be issued one-day advance only. Children below the age of 10 years are not permitted. The proceedings can be watched during the session period (i.e. when the House is in session) subject to the security clearance and availability of the seats in the public gallery. In the inter session period show rounds are organised by Parliament Security Service (PSS) officials in the working days. For this list of visitors recommended by Hon'ble MP (Lok Sabha) is essentially required.

subject: आरटीआई आवेदन में भर्ती विज्ञापन में आयु सीमा स्पष्ट न किए जाने और भिन्न-भिन्न आयु सीमा दर्शाए जाने के बारे में जानकारी मांगी गई।
questions: मैं यह जानना चाहता हूँ कि विज्ञापन में आयु सीमा क्यों नहीं दी गई है? विज्ञापन में अलग-अलग आयु सीमा दर्शाते हुए ही क्यों प्रकाशित की गई है?

जानकारी/उत्तर: आवेदक द्वारा अपने आर टी आई आवेदन में आर टी आई अधिनियम की धारा 2(च) के तहत परिभाषित कोई जानकारी नहीं मांगी गई है। एक लोक प्राधिकारी को आर टी आई अधिनियम के तहत ऐसे प्रश्नों, स्पष्टीकरणों या राय से संबंधित आवेदनों पर विचार करने की आवश्यकता नहीं है जो अभिलेखों में उपलब्ध नहीं है या जिन्हें अभिलेखों से प्राप्त नहीं किया जा सकता।

title: Upper Age Limit for Translator and Hindi Assistant Posts Query
subject: Applicant raised queries/grievances about the upper age limit fixed for Translator and Hindi Assistant posts in Lok Sabha Secretariat compared to Rajya Sabha and SSC norms.
questions: This is a higher post.
A candidate who done PG become 25 or 26 years and he needs time to preparation for 02 years he become overage if the upper age limit is fixed for 27 years only.

For MTS which is group C post and minimum qualification required high school the upper age limit is 25 years if for High School based job need 25 years then how it could be only 27 years for Post Graduation Job.
If Rajya Sabha is giving 30 years upper age limit to apply for the Translator post then why in Lok Sabha it is only 27 years.
In Staff Selection Commission the upper age limit is 30 years for the Translator post then why in Lok Sabha it is only 27 years.

In Lok Sabha for the post of Hindi Assistant the upper age limit is 27 years which is Junior Post to Translator then how could be the same age limit for Junior and senior post and if Hindi Assistant needs three years experience to get promote for the Translator then why in direct recruitment it is only 27 years.
There is no Age limit for the Emp of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha who have completed 03 years then why only 27 years for others.
If you are giving same relax to the employees of Rajya Sabha then why not same Rules are being followed.
response_summary: The Secretariat replied that no specific information as defined under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act had been sought, as the queries were opinions/clarifications rather than requests for recorded information, which a CPIO is not obligated to answer.

response_tables.title: Point-wise Information/Reply

response_full_text:
1. There is no member by the name of Ashwini Chopra in 16th Lok Sabha. However, there is a member named Shri Ashwini Kumar in 16th Lok Sabha representing Karnal Parliamentary Constituency of Haryana. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by Shri Ashwini Kumar during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha under Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member-wise Attendance -> All Members. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information.
2. Number of days Lok Sabha sat since 2014 is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Resume of Work'. As regards the 11th and ongoing 12th session, requisite information is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business'-> 'Bulletin-I'. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.
3. Debate participation by Shri Ashwani Kumar, MP (Lok Sabha) is available on the Homepage of Hon'ble Member and can be accessed from the link given. It is for information of the applicant that there is a Homepage of every sitting member of Lok Sabha which shows participation by him/her including Questions raised, etc.

questions: क्या आवेदक के आवेदन और प्रमाणपत्रों में कोई कमी थी, जिसके कारण आवेदक के आवेदन पर विचार नहीं किया गया?
आपके कार्यालय द्वारा आवेदक को पत्राचार के माध्यम से कोई जानकारी न भेजने के क्या कारण थे?

क्या उपरोक्त विज्ञापन के प्रत्युत्तर में सभी पदों हेतु प्राप्त आवेदनों पर कार्यवाही नहीं की गई? या इन पदों के लिए रिक्तियों को रद्द कर दिया गया? यदि रद्द कर दिया गया तो रद्द करने के कारण बताएं। कृपया वर्ष 2009 के आवेदन की फोटोकॉपी उपलब्ध कराएं।

आपके विभाग के नियम/विनियम क्या हैं, जिनके तहत आवेदक के आवेदन पर विचार नहीं किया गया। इसके अतिरिक्त, कृपया उन अधिकारियों/कर्मचारियों के नाम और पदनाम भी बताएं जिनके निरीक्षण में ये आवेदन आमंत्रित किए गए थे और नियुक्ति हेतु कार्यवाही की गई थी।
इन सभी पदों हेतु आपके कार्यालय में प्राप्त आवेदनों की कुल संख्या बताएं।
यदि वर्ष 2009 के दौरान प्रकाशित विज्ञापन के आधार पर ये पद भरे गए थे तो आवेदक के आवेदन पर ध्यान न देने का कारण बताएं।
response_summary: विज्ञापन सं. 2/2009 के तहत विभिन्न पदों हेतु प्राप्त आवेदनों की पद-वार संख्या, प्रारंभिक व मुख्य परीक्षा का विवरण दिया गया। बताया गया कि आवेदनों का रिकॉर्ड नष्ट कर दिया गया है, अतः शेष विस्तृत जानकारी उपलब्ध नहीं है।

response_full_text: विज्ञापन सं. 2/2009 द्वारा अधिसूचित रिक्तियों हेतु पद-वार प्राप्त कुल आवेदनों की संख्या: (i) कार्यकारी/विधायी/समिति/प्रोटोकॉल सहायक 24,512 (ii) स्टाफ कार ड्राइवर (ओजी) 1400 (iii) जूनियर प्रूफ रीडर 415 (iv) जूनियर लाइब्रेरी असिस्टेंट 2303 (v) संसदीय रिपोर्टर ग्रेड-दो 1475। कार्यकारी/विधायी/समिति/प्रोटोकॉल सहायक के पदों हेतु 22,563 आवेदन योग्य पाए गए और 14.03.2010 को आयोजित प्रारंभिक परीक्षा हेतु बुलाए गए। 11,246 उम्मीदवार परीक्षा में शामिल हुए। उपरोक्त पद हेतु मुख्य परीक्षा का अंतिम परिणाम 06.10.2010 को घोषित हुआ। आवेदक द्वारा मांगी गई अन्य जानकारी के संबंध में बताया जाता है कि विज्ञापन सं. 2/2009 द्वारा अधिसूचित विभिन्न रिक्त पदों हेतु प्राप्त आवेदनों के रिकॉर्ड नष्ट कर दिए गए हैं।

title: MPLAD Fund, Adarsh Gram, MP Maurya RTI Reply Details
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell), लोक सभा सचिवालय
subject: आवेदक ने संसद सदस्य श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य से संबंधित एमपीलैड निधि, आदर्श ग्राम योजना, सुविधाओं और परिसंपत्तियों की जानकारी मांगी।
questions: आवंटित एमपीलैड निधि का विवरण।
आदर्श ग्राम योजना के तहत संसद सदस्य द्वारा गांव को गोद लिए जाने के संबंध में जानकारी।
ग्रामीण विकास अभियांत्रिकी विभाग, इलाहाबाद को आबंटित कार्य।
फूलपुर निर्वाचन क्षेत्र में संसद सदस्य द्वारा कौन सा कार्य किया गया है और किन गांव के लिए; उनके निर्वाचन क्षेत्र के विकास के लिए उठाए गए प्रश्न/मामले।
संसद सदस्यों को प्रदान की जाने वाली सुविधाएं और उन पर सरकार द्वारा वहन किया जाने वाला मासिक व्यय।
श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य, संसद सदस्य की चल और अचल सम्पत्ति का ब्यौरा दें।

श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य, संसद सदस्य के विरूद्ध कितनी प्राथमिकी और आरोप पत्र दर्ज किए गए हैं? विभिन्न न्यायालयों में चल रहे मुकदमों, संसद सदस्य के न्यायालयों में उपस्थित होने की तिथियां और न्यायालयों में मुकदमों की स्थिति के बारे में जानकारी प्रदान करें।
माननीय प्रधानमंत्री इत्यादि के साथ औपचारिक बैठक का ब्यौरा दें।
response_summary: अधिकांश बिंदुओं को संबंधित मंत्रालयों (सांख्यिकी एवं कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयन मंत्रालय, ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय, प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय) को अंतरित कर दिया गया। संसद सदस्य की परिसंपत्तियों की घोषणा की प्रति संलग्न की गई तथा शेष जानकारी हेतु लोक सभा वेबसाइट का संदर्भ दिया गया। मुकदमों/प्राथमिकी संबंधी जानकारी सचिवालय के पास उपलब्ध न होने की बात कही गई।

response_tables.title: बिंदुवार सूचना/उत्तर

response_full_text:
1. आवंटित एमपीलैड निधि का विवरण - दिनांक 20.7.2017 को सांख्यिकी और कार्यक्रम कार्यान्वयन मंत्रालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया है।
2. आदर्श ग्राम योजना के तहत संसद सदस्य द्वारा गांव को गोद लिए जाने के संबंध में जानकारी - दिनांक 20.7.2017 को ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया है।
3. ग्रामीण विकास अभियांत्रिकी विभाग, इलाहाबाद को आबंटित कार्य।
4. फूलपुर निर्वाचन क्षेत्र संबंधी प्रश्न - प्रश्न शाखा (लोक सभा) द्वारा अलग से विषय-वार जानकारी नहीं रखी जाती है। तथापि, लोक सभा में संसद सदस्य द्वारा पूछे गए प्रश्न और उनके उत्तर लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर 'Questions' शीर्षक के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध हैं। श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य द्वारा वाद-विवाद में भाग लेने की जानकारी माननीय सदस्य के होमपेज पर उपलब्ध है। दिनांक 20.7.2017 को ग्रामीण विकास मंत्रालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया है।
5. संसद सदस्यों को प्रदान की जाने वाली सुविधाएं संबंधित अधिनियम/नियमों (1954, 1957, 1956, 1959, 1960, 1986, 1988) द्वारा विनियमित की जाती हैं, जो लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं। श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य पर सरकार द्वारा किए गए मासिक व्यय के संबंध में आवेदक द्वारा मांगी गई जानकारी नहीं रखी जाती है, तथापि माननीय अध्यक्ष/उपाध्यक्ष/नेता प्रतिपक्ष/संसद सदस्य के व्यय का त्रैमासिक विवरण वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है।
6. श्री केशव प्रसाद मौर्य, संसद सदस्य द्वारा प्रस्तुत परिसंपत्तियों और देयताओं की घोषणा की एक प्रति इस पत्र के साथ भेजी जा रही है।
7. संसद सदस्य के विरूद्ध प्राथमिकी/आरोप पत्रों के संबंध में कोई जानकारी विशेषाधिकार और आचार समिति शाखा में उपलब्ध नहीं है।
8. माननीय प्रधानमंत्री के साथ बैठक का ब्यौरा - दिनांक 20.7.2017 को प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया है।

title: Rules on displaying political symbols while taking oath as MP/MLA
subject: RTI seeking clarification on whether an elected representative may display political affinity, national flags of other countries, or party dress codes while taking oath as MP/MLA.
questions: When a person takes oath as minister either MP or MLA, can the person display his political affinity like putting up party scarf, cap, symbol. What does law say in this regard.
If an elected representative takes oath as MP or MLA putting on Pakistan Flag as a dressing style, will that be allowed or is it a violation and person needs to be disqualified.
If an elected representative takes oath as MP or MLA putting on Indian flag as dressing style, will that be allowed or is it a violation and person needs to be disqualified.
If an elected representative takes oath as MP or MLA putting on RSS dress code, will that be allowed or is it a violation and person needs to be disqualified.

If an elected representative takes oath as MP or MLA putting on Party dress code i.e. BJP saffron scarf or Congress Scarf will that be allowed or is it a violation and person needs to be disqualified.
To my knowledge once and while a person takes oath, he/she cannot display party affinity at the time of taking oath.
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that oath/affirmation to newly elected members is administered by the Speaker/Deputy Speaker/Presiding Officer, and cited Rule 349 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, which bars members from displaying badges (other than the National Flag as a lapel pin) or exhibiting flags/emblems in the House; points 3-6 were not separately answered in the available text.

Speaker or any of Presiding Officer or Panel of Chairman who administer oath/affirmation to the newly elected members of Lok Sabha in General Elections/Bye-elections. title: No minutes maintained for informal SC/ST Committee meeting on Navyug School teachers

subject: RTI (routed via Section 11 consultation from M/o Personnel) seeking minutes of a Parliamentary Committee on the Welfare of SC/ST meeting held on 17.04.2013 regarding SC teachers of Navyug School under NDMC.

title: Rules on creating LARRDIS units, committee allocation and Library book records under RTI
subject: RTI (filed by a Secretariat officer) seeking rules and orders on creating/abolishing Branches/Units in LARRDIS, allocation of Parliamentary Committees to LARRDIS officers, and records of books purchased and missing from the Parliament Library.
questions: Please provide copy of the Rules/ Regulations/ Instructions/ Guidelines/ Procedure for creating/ abolishing Branches/ Units/ Sections/ Desks/ Wings in the Services of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Please provide copy of the order/ procedure/ Instructions/ Rules/ Regulations under which a decision was taken to start Research work in Library of Parliament.

Also provide the genesis of nomenclature of LARRDIS and when it came into existence in Lok Sabha Secretariat. When Library Service in Lok Sabha Secretariat was established and what was its mandate. Please provide copy of that Order/ Rules/ Regulations/ Instructions/ Guidelines etc.

An authenticated copy of Administrative Approval/ Order of Competent Authority for creating Branches/ Sections/ Desks/ Units as mentioned vide Office Order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th may, 2016 may kindly be provided.

As mentioned in the aforesaid Office Order, please provide the copy of the administrative approval of AN-I which created the aforesaid units as well as the O&M recommendations for creating such Units/ Wings/ Sections/ Desks/ Branches mentioned against the name and designation of the 58 officers of the LARRDIS.

Whether any of the 10 distinct Services as mentioned in para 2.18 of the 4th Report of the Parliamentary Pay Committee which was accepted by both Presiding Officers i.e. Chairman Rajya Sabha and Speaker, Lok Sabha, has been authorised by itself to create any Units/ Wings/ Sections/ Desks without the Administrative approval of AN-I and without the recommendations of O&M Section. Please provide copy of such order/ instructions/ guidelines etc.
A copy of the guidelines/ instructions which have been followed in allocating Parliamentary Committees to the officers of LARRDIS vide Office Order No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016 may be provided.

As per the aforesaid Office Order dated 11th May, 2016, the works mentioned against the names of some officers of the LARRDIS, refers to Economic and Financial Affair Wing, Defence & International Affairs Desk; Legal & Constitutional Affairs Wing, etc. Information may be provided whether these Wings/ Sections etc. are doing original research work on such subjects, and copies of each officer's original publication work in the last five years.

What are the grounds for allocating Standing Committees/ Financial Committees to the Officers of LARRDIS vide Office order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016. Please provide the authenticated copy of the order/ instructions in this regard.

Whether it is a fact that the 4th Parliamentary committee Reports mentioned that the function of each of the 10 Services are complementary and supplementary and their officers/staff are not freely interchangeable; whether deputing LARRDIS to LAFEAS vide Office Order 1878 dated 11/05/2005 violates the spirit of both Presiding Officers, and if so on what grounds.

What is the total numbers of books purchased so far by the Parliament Library since 1995 and how many of them are now not available/ missing. Whether any action has been taken to redeem those missing books.

How many school text books from 1st to Graduation level have been purchased by the Parliamentary Library and the grounds for purchasing the same alongwith the financial implication involved for such purchase and name & designation of the Officer authorizing such purchase.
response_summary: The Secretariat answered that creation/abolition of Branches/Units is done administratively via O&M Section proposals; several specific administrative-approval records sought were either enclosed (Annexure-I) or stated as not available; two points were declined as being 'queries' the public authority is not bound to answer under the RTI Act; and details on Parliament Library book purchases/missing books and school textbook purchases were said not to be maintained in the exact form sought, with the applicant (a Secretariat officer) advised to inspect the relevant registers/catalogue directly.

Please provide copy of such order/instructions/guidelines etc.
Reply: The information sought is a query and the Public Authority is not bound to answer queries under Right to Information Act, 2005.
Point 7. A copy of the guidelines/instructions which have been followed in allocating Parliamentary Committees to the officers of LARRDIS vide Office Order No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016 may be provided.
Reply: Copy of the relevant approval/order enclosed in reply to Point No.4 above may be referred.
Point 8. As per the aforesaid Office Order dated 11th May, 2016, the works mentioned against the names of some officers of the LARRDIS, refers to Economic and Financial Affair Wing, Defence & International Affairs Desk; Legal & Constitutional Affairs Wing, etc. Information may be provided whether these Wings/Sections etc. are doing original research work on such subjects. In this context the information regarding original research work being done by these Officers at Sl.No.1,2,4,5, to 21, 23 to 35,38,39,41,42 as mentioned in Office Order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016 may kindly be provided. Copy of each of the original publication work in the last five years published in the National and International journal/magazines may also be provided whether the above officer are domain experts.
Reply: Whenever an officer is allocated the work pertaining to a Wing/Section/Branch, as has been done in the case of the officers mentioned vide Office Order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016, the officer concerned has to exercise his/her duties in accordance with the Procedure and Practice of their Wing and as per the Orders/Directions of the higher authorities. Bringing out publications in individual capacity by the officer concerned is not part of his/her official duties. (individual reply from the officers concerned are enclosed).
Point 9. What are the grounds for allocating Standing Committees/Financial Committees to the Officers of LARRDIS vide Office order Part-I No.1878 dated 11th May, 2016. Please provide the authenticated copy of the order/instructions in this regard.

Point 10. Whether it is a fact that the 4th Parliamentary committee Reports which was accepted by Chairman of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha mentioned that the function of each Services (10 Service) are complementary and supplementary to the other and their officer and staff are not freely interchangeable owing to the special and distinct nature of duties of each Service. In this context, deputing a particular service (LARRDIS) to another Service i.e. LAFEAS vide Office Order 1878 dated 11/05/2005, is not the violation and spirit of both the Presiding Officers of both the Houses. If yes, provide the grounds of such violation. If not, the reasons thereof.
Reply: The information sought is a query and the Public Authority is not bound to answer queries under Right to Information Act, 2005.
Point 11. What is the total numbers of books purchased so far by the Parliament Library since 1995 and how many of them are now not available/missing. Whether any action has been taken to redeem those missing books.
Reply: Books purchased/added to the Parliament Library between 01 January 1995 to 31 May 2016 have been entered in the Accession Register from B127926 to B213140. The applicant being Officer of the Secretariat, if he so desires may inspect the Accession Registers by contacting at telephone no. 23034768. The information desired in the form is not maintained. However, it is for information that on the advice of the O&M Section from time to time, physical verification of books is done by the Library. Reply: The information desired in the form is not maintained. OR He may visit the undermentioned web page as books added to the Parliament Library are available there: http://10.21.202.209:8380/opac/. A copy of the Procedure & Practice of the Acquisition Section Page 7 (point 3.15) (placed on the file) related to the competent authority for purchase of books may be passed on to the Information Cell for onward transmission to the applicant. Further, for financial implications the Expenditure Control Registers are maintained in the Section. The applicant may be advised to inspect the Registers (if he so desires) by contacting at Tel. No. 23034768.

subject: आवेदक ने एक आंख वाले व्यक्ति से संबंधित कानून और ब्यौरा मांगा, जो लोक सभा सचिवालय के बजाय सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय से संबंधित पाया गया।
questions: एक आंख वाले व्यक्ति के संबंध में कानून और उससे संबंधित ब्यौरा
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि आवेदन की विषयवस्तु लोक सभा सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं बल्कि सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय से संबंधित है, और चूंकि आवेदन शुल्क अविधिमान्य था, आवेदन को अंतरित नहीं किया जा सका; आवेदक को सीधे संबंधित मंत्रालय से संपर्क करने की सलाह दी गई।
extracted_text:
लोक सभा सचिवालय
संसद भवन, नई दिल्ली
सूचना प्रकोष्ठ
सं. 1(945)/आईसी/2016 18.05.2016
प्रेषक
के. सोना
उप सचिव एवं कें.स.ज.सू.अ.
प्रेषिती
[Applicant]
[address redacted]
विषयः सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना।
महोदय,
इस सचिवालय में दिनांक 18.05.2016 को प्राप्त आपके अदिनांकित आरटीआई आवेदन, जिसमें एक आंख वाले व्यक्ति के संबंध में कानून और उससे संबंधित ब्यौरा मांगा गया है, के संदर्भ में मुझे यह बताने का निदेश हुआ है कि आवेदन की विषयवस्तु लोक सभा सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है अपितु सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय, भारत सरकार से संबंधित है।
2. इसके अलावा, आपके द्वारा आईपीओ सं. 20एफ 469234 के माध्यम से भेजा गया आवेदन शुल्क आहरण और संवितरण अधिकारी, लोक सभा' अथवा 'वेतन और लेखा अधिकारी, लोक सभा' के पक्ष में देय न होने के कारण अविधिमान्य है।
3. अतः आपका आवेदन उन्हें अंतरित नहीं किया जा सकता। आपसे अनुरोध है कि संबंधित लोक प्राधिकारी से संपर्क करें और सीधे जानकारी प्राप्त करें।
4. अविधिमान्य आईपीओ सं. 20 एफ 469234 इस पत्र के साथ संलग्न है।
5. इसे के.ज.सू.अधि. का अनुमोदन प्राप्त है।
संलग्न: 10/- रुपए का आईपीओ सं. 20 एफ 469234
response_full_text: आवेदन की विषयवस्तु लोक सभा सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है अपितु सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय, भारत सरकार से संबंधित है। आपका आवेदन उन्हें अंतरित नहीं किया जा सकता क्योंकि आवेदन शुल्क अविधिमान्य है। आपसे अनुरोध है कि संबंधित लोक प्राधिकारी से संपर्क करें और सीधे जानकारी प्राप्त करें।

subject: आवेदक ने लोक सभा एवं राज्य सभा के जैन समुदाय से संबंधित सदस्यों की संपर्क जानकारी और उनमें से केंद्रीय मंत्रियों का ब्यौरा मांगा।

Name of the applicant: [Applicant]
Reference: Letter No.1 (934)/IC/14
Point 1. Statement of President of India dated 09.06.2014 — Reply: The information sought by the applicant at point no.1 is available on the Lok Sabha website (http://loksabha.nic.in) in the column ‘New Events’
Point 2. Rules of Code of Conduct of members. — Reply: The Committee on Ethics (13th Lok Sabha) in its Second Report recommended that a Code of Conduct may be framed and incorporated in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha but the same is yet to be incorporated therein. It was again recommended (during 14th Lok Sabha) by the 'Committee to Inquire into various facets of Misconduct and Basic Attributes of Standard of Conduct/Behavior expected of Members' in its second report. This recommendation is yet to be adopted by the House. Thus, there is no Code of Conduct for Members of Lok Sabha at present. There is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha preventing a member from engaging in a lawful private activity.
Point 3. What is the total cost of Parliament House yearly and maintenance charges yearly including staff — Reply: Application transferred to the M/o Urban Development, under intimation to the applicant.
Point 4. Whether ex-Speaker get any retiral benefits. — Reply: There are no such retirement benefits given to ex-Speaker from this secretariat. However, ex-Speaker is entitled to avail the facilities that may be provided to ex-Members of Parliament. The Ex-Speaker as Ex-Member of Parliament is entitled to receive pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month for the first five years of total period of membership in Parliament + Rs. 1500/- per month for every year in excess of five years.
Point 5. Whether a sitting MP is allowed to act in films or any other business which affects the status of MP as it is an impediment in the working of Lok Sabha. — Reply: There is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha preventing a member from engaging in a lawful private activity.
Point 6. Is there any amendment in Rules of House that MP cannot act as a Minister in State as it so happened in 1999 by Sh. Girdhar Gamang as Chief Minister of Orissa — Reply: As per records available in the division concerned no amendments of such nature were effected in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha and the Directions by the Speaker, Lok Sabha. Both of these publications are posted in Lok Sabha website.

the

contained 
in

under

title: Bahelia Caste Sub-Caste Status in SC&ST Bill Query
ministry: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
subject: RTI (transferred from Rajya Sabha Secretariat) seeking information on whether the Bahelia caste was treated as a sub-caste of Aheria caste in a Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order Amendment Bill passed by Lok Sabha, its passage status in Rajya Sabha, and related legislative procedure details.
questions: Whether Lok Sabha has considered the Bahelia caste as sub-caste of Aheria caste in the SC&ST Bill passed by Lok Sabha on 24.08.2013 (Bill No. LSSD 11)
Whether the above-mentioned bill has been sent to Rajya Sabha or not and has it been passed by Rajya Sabha or not, if yes, please provide copy of the same
Whether the bill in question been sent to Rajya Sabha in future, please provide details
Whether the Bahelia caste a sub-caste of Aheria caste is being included in the State List of Uttar Pradesh
Complete details of Gazette Notification No. DL (N)/04/0007/2003-13, etc.
Details as to who recommends the bills to be forwarded to the Rajya Sabha
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that the applicant's query likely referred to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order (Amendment) Bill, 2013, which was passed by Lok Sabha on 24.08.2013, transmitted to Rajya Sabha, but lapsed on dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha on 18.05.2014 without being passed there. It explained that inclusion/exclusion of a caste in a State List is the prerogative of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, to which the application was transferred for the relevant points, and cited Rule 96 of the Rules of Procedure regarding transmission of Bills to Rajya Sabha.

Hence, transfer of application under section 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005 is not accepted and the application, alongwith annexures, are returned herewith. Transferred to: CPIO, Ministry of Finance, Department of Financial Services (Welfare Section), 3rd Floor, Jeevan Deep Building, Parliament Street, New Delhi-110001. Copy to the applicant: as the subject matter of the application exclusively pertains to Ministry of Finance, you may contact them directly for further information.

title: LSTV CEO Appointment, Termination and Salary Reversal Query
subject: RTI seeking wide-ranging information on the appointment, extension and termination of the CEO of Lok Sabha TV, related salary reversal, Lok Sabha Speaker's role, dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha, and LSTV panel discussion practices.
questions: Complete information with related correspondence, etc. on each aspect of enclosed submission dated 02.06.2014, e-mailed to Lok Sabha Speaker on given e-mail ID, etc.
Complete information rules regarding (a) appointment (b) extension of appointment (c) termination of CEO of Lok Sabha TV

Complete information together with all related file-notings, etc. on (a) appointment (b) extension of appointment (c) termination of CEO (Shri Rajiv Mishra) of Lok Sabha TV enclosing also copies of letters of (a) appointment (b) extension of appointment (c) termination of CEO (Shri Rajiv Mishra) of Lok Sabha TV
Complete information on role of Lok Sabha Speaker in regarding (a) appointment (b) extension of appointment (c) termination of CEO of Lok Sabha TV

Rights and duties of Lok Sabha Speaker after dissolution of Lok Sabha having elected him/her as Lok Sabha Speaker
Is it true that salary etc. of Shri Rajiv Mishra in respect of May 2014 was once transferred to his bank account?

Complete information together with related file notings, etc on reversal of salary etc. of Shri Rajiv Mishra in respect of May 2014 from his bank account
Does RBI allow banks to transfer/withdrawal etc. of funds from account of an individual without his consent etc.
Complete information on SBI reversing credit-entry of salary etc. of Shri Rajiv Mishra in respect of May 2014
List of personalities on whom LSTV (a) produced and (b) telecast documentaries in tenure of Smt. Meira Kumar as Lok Sabha Speaker, etc.
Criterion to invite panellists on panel discussions of Lok Sabha TV mentioning specifically about some persons 'black-listed' from such panel-discussions
Names of ten most invited panellists mentioning number of times each of such panellists were invited for panel discussion on LSTV
Number of times mentioning dates when undersigned petitioner was invited for appearing at Lok Sabha TV
Any other related information
File notings on movement of RTI petition
response_summary: The Secretariat answered most of the 17 points, forwarding copies of the recruitment order for the LSTV CEO post, file notings on the CEO's appointment/termination, confirming the 15th Lok Sabha was dissolved on 18.05.2014, explaining that the CEO's fee for May 2014 was transferred then the bank was asked to stop payment following his termination, and providing a list of most-invited panellists. Points 10 and 11 (relating to RBI and SBI) were transferred to those authorities under Section 6(3), and point 1 was forwarded to the Ministries of Urban Development and Law & Justice. Some points required further comments from the concerned division and were supplied later along with a first-appeal reply.

THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA 
 
94. Vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and 
Deputy Speaker.— A member holding office as Speaker or Deputy Speaker of 
the House of the People— (a) shall vacate his office if he ceases to be a member 
of the House of the People; (b) may at any time, by writing under his hand 
addressed, if such member is the Speaker, to the Deputy Speaker, and if such 
member is the Deputy Speaker, to the Speaker, resign his office; and (c) may be 
removed from his office by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a 
majority of all the then members of the House: Provided that no resolution for 
the purpose of clause (c) shall be moved unless at least fourteen days’ notice has 
been given of the intention to move the resolution: Provided further that, 
whenever the House of the People is dissolved, the Speaker shall not vacate his 
office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People 
after the dissolution.

An earlier letter had also returned an invalid IPO for Rs. 10/- submitted as application fee.

title: RTI on PM's rally powers, MP salaries and Lok Sabha sitting hours
subject: The applicant sought information on the Prime Minister's constitutional powers to hold political rallies, the working hours/time lost in the Lok Sabha, and the salary and allowances of MPs and the Speaker.
questions: Information regarding legal position of PM; whether the Constitution gives the PM any power to hold a rally regarding their party; whether the PM has power while being PM to hold a rally and criticize their opposition/regional party.
Information regarding 1st to 16th Lok Sabha, how much time worked and how much time was wasted (due to adjournments/interruptions).
Details of salary of MPs and Speaker.
Details of allowances given to MPs and Speaker.
Details of allowances given to retired MPs and Speaker.
Who is responsible for non-working of a Lok Sabha Session.
response_summary: The Secretariat forwarded the query on the PM's legal/rally powers to the Prime Minister's Office; provided sitting/hours-of-sitting data for the Lok Sabhas along with an Annexure and referred to the Lok Sabha website for time lost due to adjournments; listed the Acts/Rules governing salary, allowances, pension and other benefits of MPs and the Speaker (with a reference to the relevant website section); and forwarded a related query to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
