title: Parliament Session Expenditure, MPLADS, Lokpal and Women's Reservation Bill Status
subject: मानसून सत्र के खर्च, संसद सदस्यों के वेतन, विधेयकों की स्थिति (लोकपाल एवं महिला आरक्षण) संबंधी सूचना की मांग।
questions: What was the total amount spend on last Parliament monsoon sessions.
What is the amount spend on tea, coffee, snacks and meals for MPs in last Parliament monsoon session.
No. of hours two Houses had functioned during the last Monsoon session
What is the net worth of gifts or other monetary gifts given to each MPs for both Houses of Parliament in the monsoon session for there attended.
What is the total amount of salary given to an MP in both Houses of Parliament for month.
What was the amount of money spend to conduct Parliament Session per hour.
Who had posed maximum number of questions in both the Houses of Parliament in the last monsoon session.
Who had taken most time to speak in the either House of Parliament.
How many no. of MPs had not used MPLADS not even a single rupee so far for the development of their constituencies.
What was the amount spend for maintaining Parliament Building and staff in last year i.e. 2012
How many Bills discussed and passed in the Monsoon Session.
What is the present status of Women Reservation Bill and Lokpal Bill.
Why Lokpal Bill has not been passed in Parliament. What are recommendations of Parliamentary Committee on Lokpal Bill.
response_summary: Several points were answered directly (session hours, bill passage statistics, building maintenance costs, status of the Women's Reservation and Lokpal Bills), while some queries were stated as not maintained by the Secretariat, transferred to other Ministries/Rajya Sabha Secretariat, or redirected to the Lok Sabha website.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: 12.11.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1596)/IC/13 dated 11.12.2013

1. What was the total amount spend on last Parliament monsoon sessions.
Reply: Such information is not maintained by this Secretariat. Information regarding expenses on Parliament is maintained by multiple agencies involving several Ministries under various heads namely, Lok Sabha Secretariat, Delhi police, Special Protection Group, Delhi Jal Board, NDMC, DTC, CPWD and other Ministries concerned. There is no mechanism to calculate the expenses incurred session-wise.

2. What is the amount spend on tea, coffee, snacks and meals for MPs in last Parliament monsoon session.
Reply: Copy of the application already transferred to M/o Railways.

3. No. of hours two Houses had functioned during the last Monsoon session.
Reply: Lok Sabha functioned for 73 hours and 11 minutes during the monsoon session (14th session of the 15th Lok Sabha).

4. What is the net worth of gifts or other monetary gifts given to each MPs for both Houses of Parliament in the monsoon session for there attended.
Reply: No such information is maintained in the Secretariat.

5. What is the total amount of salary given to an MP in both Houses of Parliament for month.
Reply: A pamphlet containing entitlement of Salary, Allowances, and other facilities to Members of Parliament is enclosed.

6. What was the amount of money spend to conduct Parliament Session per hour.
(covered with reply to point 1)

7. Who had posed maximum number of questions in both the Houses of Parliament in the last monsoon session.
Reply: The details of information sought by the applicant with respect to Lok Sabha is available in Lok Sabha website i.e. www.parliamentofindia.nic.in/ and http://loksabha.nic.in. The applicant may be advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.

8. Who had taken most time to speak in the either House of Parliament.
Reply: No such information is maintained in the Secretariat.

9. How many no. of MPs had not used MPLADS not even a single rupee so far for the development of their constituencies.
Reply: Already transferred to M/o Statistics & Programme Implementation.

10. What was the amount spend for maintaining Parliament Building and staff in last year i.e. 2012.
Reply: Amount spent on Civil Works = Rs. 44488 (figure in thousand). Amount spent on Electrical Works = Rs. 36725 (figure in thousand).

11. How many Bills discussed and passed in the Monsoon Session.
Reply: During the Monsoon Session, 2013, 14 Government Bills were discussed by Lok Sabha, out of which 13 Bills were passed by Lok Sabha. One Bill remained part-discussed.

12. What is the present status of Women Reservation Bill and Lokpal Bill.
Reply: There is no such Bill with the title "Women Reservation Bill". It appears that the applicant wants information in respect of the Constitution (One Hundred and Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2008... The Bill is presently pending in Lok Sabha. As regards the Lokpal Bill, it appears the applicant wants to know the status of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011. The Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on 22.12.2011 and passed by the House on 27.12.2011. The Bill is presently pending in Rajya Sabha.

13. Why Lokpal Bill has not been passed in Parliament. What are recommendations of Parliamentary Committee on Lokpal Bill.
Reply: As the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011 is pending in Rajya Sabha, the query pertains to Rajya Sabha Secretariat. A copy of the application has already been forwarded to them by M/o Parliamentary Affairs.
response_full_text: Answers were provided point-wise: expenditure figures not maintained centrally (multiple agencies involved); tea/coffee expense query transferred to M/o Railways; Lok Sabha functioned 73 hours 11 minutes in the monsoon session; no information on monetary gifts to MPs; salary/allowance pamphlet enclosed; question statistics available on Lok Sabha website; no information on longest speeches; MPLADS query transferred to M/o Statistics & Programme Implementation; Rs. 44488 thousand spent on Civil Works and Rs. 36725 thousand on Electrical Works in 2012; 14 Government Bills discussed and 13 passed in Monsoon Session 2013; status of Constitution (108th Amendment) Bill and Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2011 explained; Lokpal query forwarded to Rajya Sabha Secretariat as the Bill is pending there.

subject: RTI seeking information on whether copies of the Constitution of India are provided to newly elected MPs/Ministers, and on procedures/training/penalties relating to the oath of office and secrecy.
questions: Whether copy of the constitution has provided to the Newly elected MP/Minister of 1st Lok Sabha to 16th Lok Sabha

If the same are not provided to the MPs then when this procedure will be start.
Who has attested that all the MPs had read the Constitution of India or not
Whether MPs are informed/trained about the importance of oath before the oath ceremony.
Whether there is any procedure by which it can be observed that the MPs/Ministers are not followed the privacy of oath.
Whether it is compulsory for every MP or minister to take oath of post and privacy
Provide the names of such Members and Ministers who have violated their oath of office and secrecy.
Is there any provision of legal penalty against those Members and Ministers who have violated such an oath? If so, then what can be the maximum punishment under the law?

क्रम संख्या 1
उठाए गए मुद्दे (संक्षेप में): क्या उपभोक्ता संरक्षण (संशोधन) विधेयक, 2015 लोक सभा में लंबित है?
उत्तर: ऐसे शीर्षक वाला कोई विधेयक वर्तमान में लोक सभा में लंबित नहीं है। तथापि, "उपभोक्ता संरक्षण विधेयक, 2015" शीर्षक वाला एक विधेयक वर्तमान में लोक सभा में लंबित है।

क्रम संख्या 2
उठाए गए मुद्दे: उपभोक्ता संरक्षण विधेयक, 2015 को पारित क्यों नहीं किया जा रहा है?
उत्तर: संसद की सभाओं द्वारा किसी विधेयक को पारित किए जाने के संबंध में आवेदक को सूचित किया जाता है कि विधेयक को चर्चा और पारित किए जाने हेतु कब सूचीबद्ध किया जाए, यह निर्णय संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय और संबंधित प्रशासनिक मंत्रालय द्वारा लिया जाता है। इस मामले में लोक सभा सचिवालय की कोई भूमिका नहीं है।

क्रम संख्या 3
उठाए गए मुद्दे: लोक सभा सचिवालय में कितने विधेयक लंबित हैं?
उत्तर: सोलहवीं लोक सभा के ग्यारहवें सत्र के अंत तक लोक सभा में 21 सरकारी विधेयक लंबित हैं। सोलहवीं लोक सभा के ग्यारहवें सत्र के अंत तक गैर-सरकारी सदस्यों के कुल 690 विधेयक लंबित हैं।

क्रम संख्या 4
उठाए गए मुद्दे: लोक सभा में सबसे पहला विधेयक किस वर्ष का है?
उत्तर: लोक सभा में सबसे पहला विधेयक वर्ष 1952 का है, क्योंकि पहली लोक सभा का गठन 17.4.1952 को हुआ था। शाखा में उपलब्ध रिकार्ड के अनुसार गैर-सरकारी सदस्यों का सबसे पुराना विधेयक वर्ष 1952 का है।

department: Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat / सूचना प्रकोष्ठ, लोक सभा सचिवालय
subject: आवेदक ने वर्ष 1998 से 2001 के बीच लोक सभा में पुरःस्थापित एक कथित गोपनीय भूमि अर्जन विधेयक की वर्तमान स्थिति के बारे में जानकारी मांगी।
questions: वर्ष 1998 से 2001 के बीच लोक सभा में भूमि अर्जन से संबंधित एक गोपनीय विधेयक पुरःस्थापित किया गया था। यह विधेयक अभी तक लोक सभा में लंबित है। लोक सभा सचिवालय ने लोक सभा लिंक में जानकारी को अद्यतन नहीं किया है। कृपया इस संबंध में लिखित जानकारी प्रदान करें।
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that no confidential land acquisition bill is pending, but noted that the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement (Second Amendment) Bill, 2015 was introduced on 11.5.2015 and referred to a Joint Committee of Parliament, whose reporting deadline was extended to the last day of the 2017 Budget Session; details of all bills are on the Lok Sabha website. The same application, earlier answered via letter 1(270)/IC/17, had also been separately transferred from the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change and was closed as a duplicate.

1 | वर्ष 1998 से 2001 के बीच लोक सभा में भूमि अर्जन से संबंधित एक गोपनीय विधेयक पुरःस्थापित किया गया था। यह विधेयक अभी तक लोक सभा में लंबित है। लोक सभा सचिवालय ने लोक सभा लिंक में जानकारी को अद्यतन नहीं किया है। कृपया इस संबंध में लिखित जानकारी प्रदान करें। | आवेदक को जानकारी दी जाती है कि लोक सभा में भूमि अर्जन से संबंधित कोई गोपनीय विधेयक लंबित नहीं है। यद्यपि, दिनांक 11.5.2015 को लोक सभा में भूमि अर्जन, पुनर्वासन और पुनर्स्थापन में उचित प्रतिकर और पारदर्शिता का अधिकार (दूसरा संशोधन) विधेयक, 2015, पुरःस्थापित किया गया था। बजट सत्र, 2016 के प्रथम सप्ताह के पहले दिन तक एक प्रतिवेदन प्रस्तुत करने के निर्देशों के साथ इस विधेयक को संयुक्त समिति को सौंपा गया था। बजट सत्र, 2017 के अंतिम दिन तक प्रतिवेदन प्रस्तुत करने हेतु संयुक्त समिति को और समय दिया गया है। आवेदक को सूचित किया जाता है कि लोक सभा अथवा राज्य सभा में पुरःस्थापित सभी विधेयकों से संबंधित जानकारी लोक सभा की वेबसाइट (www.loksabha.nic.in) पर उपलब्ध है। इसे 23.02.2017 को कृषि मंत्रालय को भी अंतरित किया गया।

title: Lok Sabha Secretariat uniform and Liveries Committee rules detailed
subject: RTI seeking details of Lok Sabha Secretariat Conditions of Service Rules concerning officer definitions, uniforms, the Liveries Committee, and decisions on uniform ceilings for different categories of staff.
questions: In Lok Sabha Secretariat Conditions of Service Rules, what is the definition of the term "Officer"? Are the Parliamentary Reporters considered as officers under Lok Sabha Secretariat Conditions of Service Rules as approved by the hon. Speaker?
In Lok Sabha Secretariat Conditions of Service Rules, what is the definition of the term "Uniforms" that are issued to the officers/staff of Lok Sabha Secretariat?
Does the Lok Sabha Secretariat have Liveries Committee? If so who are the Members of the Liveries Committee?

What is the ceiling amount for Parliamentary Reporters for Summer Uniform and Winter Uniform? What are the items that are issued in the name of uniforms for Parliamentary Reporters and for how many years? Is there any difference in the ceiling amount of Parliamentary Reporters and others who sit inside the House, namely Secretary General, Joint Secretary, Director, Deputy Secretary, Under Secretary and Executive Officer? Supply the notings and the details of the ceiling amount in respect of these officers as approved by the Liveries Committee.

Is it a fact that colours and ceilings of uniforms for the personnel sitting inside the Chamber were not decided by the Liveries Committee? Who decided to issue separate set of "uniforms" and separate colours of uniforms to officers sitting inside the Chamber with different ceiling?
Are the uniforms that are issued to the various personnel working in the Lok Sabha Secretariat approved by the Liveries Committee?
Who decided to issue separate set of "uniforms and separate colours of uniforms to officers sitting inside the Chamber with different ceilings? Supply file notings in this regard.

Who decided to issue shirts and ties to officers other than Personnel of Parliament Security Service? Was this issue decided by the Liveries Committee and approved by the Secretary General? If not who has bypassed the Liveries Committee and decided to issue shirts and ties to so called officers other than Parliamentary Reporters?
response_summary: The Secretariat provided complete answers to all eight points, including the definition of 'Officer' under the 1955 Service Rules, confirmation that 'Uniform' is not defined, the composition of the Liveries Committee, uniform ceiling amounts for Parliamentary Reporters versus other officers, and confirmation that uniform-related decisions were made by the Competent Authority (Secretary General), with relevant file notings enclosed.

 Days of sittings of Lok Sabha is governed by Rule 13 of Rules of 
Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha which states as 
under:- 
 
“The House shall sit on such days as the Speaker, having regard to the 
state of business of the House, may from time to time direct.” 
 
Ordinarily, sittings of the House are not held on Saturdays and Sundays. 
In addition to all gazetted holidays observed by the Central Government, 
Raksha Bandhan, Maha Shivaratri, May Day (1 May), Baisakhi, Guru 
Ravi Das's Birthday, Ramnavami and Birth Anniversary of Dr. B.R. 
Ambedkar are also observed as holidays. 
 
 
However, sittings of Lok Sabha may be and has been fixed on 
Saturdays/Sundays/closed holidays for transaction of essential items of 
Government Business.

Days of sittings of Lok Sabha is governed by Rule 13 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha which states as under:- 'The House shall sit on such days as the Speaker, having regard to the state of business of the House, may from time to time direct.' Ordinarily, sittings of the House are not held on Saturdays and Sundays. In addition to all gazetted holidays observed by the Central Government, Raksha Bandhan, Maha Shivaratri, May Day (1 May), Baisakhi, Guru Ravi Das's Birthday, Ramnavami and Birth Anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar are also observed as holidays. However, sittings of Lok Sabha may be and has been fixed on Saturdays/Sundays/closed holidays for transaction of essential items of Government Business.

title: RTI on absence of National Flag in Lok Sabha Chamber
department: General Works Branch, Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: RTI asking why the National Flag of India is not installed in the Lok Sabha Chamber and seeking the rule restricting its installation.
questions: Why is there no National Flag of India installed in the Lok Sabha Chamber.

response_summary: The Secretariat stated the first query did not constitute 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, and cited Rule 349(xiv) and (xvi) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, which restrict members from displaying badges, flags, or emblems in the House (except the National Flag as a lapel pin/badge).

1. Minimum no. of hours necessary for MPs to attend in a single session.
Reply: Article 101 (4) of the Constitution of India inter-alia provides that: "If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant." However, there are no prescribed minimum number of hours/sittings necessary for a member of Parliament to attend in a single session.

2. Attendance record of members of Lok Sabha on the highest, lowest or nil attendance-wise.
Reply: Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance record of members of Lok Sabha on the highest, lowest or nil attendance-wise. An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/ not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members > Attendance of Members>Members-wise attendance total respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information herself. The statement regarding walkouts staged by Members during Sessions of 15th Lok Sabha is ready to dispatch, containing 19 Pages approximately. The applicant may be requested to pay in advance the requisite fees for the same. The information will, thereafter, be furnished to her.

*For information pertaining to this Secretariat, the information fee is required to be paid by way of cash at 'Reception of Parliament Library Building, Lok Sabha Secretariat' against proper receipt or sent through money order or Demand Draft or Bankers Cheque or Indian Postal Order payable to 'Drawing and Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha', in terms of Lok Sabha Secretariat Right to Information (Regulation of Fees & Cost) Rules 2005, and the amendment Rules, 2007. You are also informed that Demand Draft/Bankers Cheque/Indian Postal Order in favour of 'Accounts Officer, Lok Sabha' is also accepted in this Secretariat. Further, the information to be supplied runs in approx. 19 pages and you are requested to furnish Rs. 38/- @ Rs. 2/- per page as information fee for the same.
response_full_text: Article 101 (4) of the Constitution of India inter-alia provides that: "If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant." Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance record of members of Lok Sabha on the highest, lowest or nil attendance-wise. An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/ not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members > Attendance of Members>Members-wise attendance total respectively. In view of the above provision, Members of Lok Sabha would table notices for modification/ annulment of the said rules, if they so desire. No formal approval of Parliament is required. Moreover, the records available in Legislative Branch-I of this public authority for the relevant period have been gone through. No motion for modification/ annulment of the Railway Protection Force Rules, 1987 was adopted by Lok Sabha during the period of 30 days referred to in section 21. title: RTI on Indian Union Muslim League and Muslim League Kerala merger
subject: RTI seeking details of Indian Union Muslim League and Muslim League Kerala State Committee members in Lok Sabha and their merger.
questions: Please furnish list of names of members belonging to Indian Union Muslim League elected to the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election
Please furnish a list of names of members belonging to Muslim League Kerala State Committee elected to the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election
Please furnish details and copies of documents submitted to the Lok Sabha about the merger of Indian Union Muslim League and the Muslim League Kerala State Committee

Please state whether the merged party was accepted and acknowledged by the Lok Sabha as the recognized and authorized party and also furnish a list of names of members belonging to the merged party in the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election.
Of both Indian Union Muslim League and the Muslim League Kerala State Committee, which party is a constituent of the UPA as of now
Please grant access to all connected records pertaining to the queries
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that the Muslim League Kerala State Committee merged with the Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha on approval of the Speaker on 22.6.2012 (represented by MPs E. Ahamed and E.T. Mohammad Basheer), provided copies of the related request and Election Commission order, and stated that party alliance information is not maintained by it; that part of the query was transferred to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application Dated 24.10.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No.1(1496)/IC/13 dated 06.11.2013

1. Please furnish list of names of members belonging to Indian Union Muslim League elected to the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election
Reply: Information regarding party affiliation of all members of Fourth to Fourteenth Lok Sabha is available on the Lok Sabha website www.loksabha.nic.in under the links Members > Former Members Bioprofiles > Fourth to Fourteenth Lok Sabha > Party wise list. Information regarding party affiliation of members of Fifteenth Lok Sabha is available under the links Members > Party wise List. The applicant may peruse the information from the website.

2. Please furnish a list of names of members belonging to Muslim League Kerala State Committee elected to the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election

3. Please furnish details and copies of documents submitted to the Lok Sabha about the merger of Indian Union Muslim League and the Muslim League Kerala State Committee
Reply (2 & 3): On a request made by S/Shri E. Ahamed and E. T. Mohammad Basheer, MPs, Hon'ble Speaker vide order dated 22.6.2012 has approved the merger of Muslim League Kerala State Committee with Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha. Accordingly, Muslim League Kerala State Committee has ceased to exist and is henceforth known as Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha. A copy of the request letter dated 23 March, 2012 given by the MPs alongwith a copy of the Election Commission order dated 3 March, 2012 in the matter is enclosed. The merger of Muslim League Kerala State Committee with Indian Union Muslim League was approved by Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha on 22 June, 2012. As on 22 June, 2012 and till date, S/Shri E. Ahamed and E.T. Mohammad Basheer, MPs represent the Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha.

4. Please state whether the merged party was accepted and acknowledged by the Lok Sabha as the recognized and authorized party and also furnish a list of names of members belonging to the merged party in the Lok Sabha from 1967 till the last election.

5. Of both Indian Union Muslim League and the Muslim League Kerala State Committee, which party is a constituent of the UPA as of now
Reply (4 & 5): Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain information regarding the alliances formed by parties. For information regarding this point, a copy of application has already been transferred to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs on 31.10.2013 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to him. The applicant is requested to contact them for the information related to them.

6. Please grant access to all connected records pertaining to the queries
Reply: All information sought by the applicant has been provided.
response_full_text: Information regarding party affiliation of all members of Fourth to Fourteenth Lok Sabha is available on the Lok Sabha website www.loksabha.nic.in under the links Members > Former Members Bioprofiles > Fourth to Fourteenth Lok Sabha > Party wise list. Information regarding party affiliation of members of Fifteenth Lok Sabha is available under the links Members > Party wise List. The applicant may peruse the information from the website. On a request made by S/Shri E. Ahamed and E. T. Mohammad Basheer, MPs, Hon'ble Speaker vide order dated 22.6.2012 has approved the merger of Muslim League Kerala State Committee with Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha. Accordingly, Muslim League Kerala State Committee has ceased to exist and is henceforth known as Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha. A copy of the request letter dated 23 March, 2012 given by the MPs alongwith a copy of the Election Commission order dated 3 March, 2012 in the matter is enclosed. The merger of Muslim League Kerala State Committee with Indian Union Muslim League was approved by Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha on 22 June, 2012. As on 22 June, 2012 and till date, S/Shri E. Ahamed and E.T. Mohammad Basheer, MPs represent the Indian Union Muslim League in Lok Sabha. Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain information regarding the alliances formed by parties. For information regarding this point, a copy of application has already been transferred to the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs on 31.10.2013 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to him. The applicant is requested to contact them for the information related to them. All information sought by the applicant has been provided.

title: Can elected MPs undertake acting, TV ads and reality shows for pay
subject: The applicant asked whether an elected Member of Parliament can engage in acting assignments, television commercials, reality shows and movies while holding office as a public representative.
questions: Kindly provide information as to if an elected MP can engage in acting assignments/perform in television commercial, take part in promotions/reality shows on television and act in movies in their capacity of public representatives for which they are paid good money. title: Multiple queries on MPs' FIRs, salary, security, disqualification and Lok Sabha expenditure
subject: The applicant raised multiple queries covering FIRs against MPs, MP salary/pension, MPLAD fund, MP security, disqualification of members, foreign trips of the Speaker, members' personal details, and Lok Sabha convention expenditure.
questions: No such information relating to FIR lodged/registered against MPs for criminal cases or the charges of prosecution against them.
The Salary of a Member of Lok Sabha and Speaker of Lok Sabha and pension details; information regarding MPLAD Fund.
Allotment of government accommodation and security arrangements for MPs at Delhi.
Information regarding disqualification of membership of Members of Lok Sabha since 1952.
Desired information pertaining to details of foreign trips undertaken by Speaker, Lok Sabha.
Information pertaining to the names, addresses and photographs of the members elected to the 15th Lok Sabha.
The expenditure on convention of Lok Sabhas and the Head of Account for the same.

The procedure to watch the proceedings of the Lok Sabha for a common man; Budget estimates 2012-13 and 2013-14 in respect of Lok Sabha and Lok Sabha Secretariat and Actual Expenditure incurred out of the Budget Grant of Lok Sabha (2012-13).
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat stated no records are maintained on FIRs against MPs; gave MP/Speaker salary and pension figures; transferred the MPLAD fund query to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation and the security-related queries to the Ministry of Home Affairs; invoked Section 7(9) exemption for disqualification records citing disproportionate diversion of resources (inviting the applicant to visit the Table Office Branch instead); enclosed information on the Speaker's foreign trips and Lok Sabha budget/expenditure statements; and pointed to the Lok Sabha website for members' bio-profiles.

Reply
1.

Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information.

50,000/ per month. Every person who has served as a Member of
Provisional Parliament or either House of Parliament for any period is
entitled to pension @Rs.20,000/  per month w.e.f. 18.05.2009.

furnishing information directly to him.

accommodation at Delhi. The Delhi Police is mandated for providing
security in and around MPs residential areas. However, the matter of
individual security does not pertain to this Secretariat.
Since the matter of protection also relates to the Delhi Police, a copy of
application has been transferred to the Ministry of Home Affairs on
12.12.2013 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing information
directly to him.

response_full_text: An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/ not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members > Attendance of Members>Members-wise attendance total respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. The information regarding members of Rajya Sabha is not maintained by Lok Sabha Secretariat. The video signal from the nine automatic camera sources installed in the Lok Sabha Chamber were suddenly unavailable for telecast. title: Service grievance on seniority and promotion order not covered by RTI
subject: The applicant, an LSS employee, raised a service-related grievance regarding seniority and promotion orders (SA-I/SA-II) compared to colleagues, which was held to be a grievance not answerable under RTI.
questions: In appendix-A, as per order NO.21946 dtd. 12.10.2009 at Sl. NO.23, I was promoted as SA-I, w.e.f. 10.10.2009, as confirmed against vacancies of SA-I with 27 other my colleague. But after long time of 27 months AN-I again released another order on 05.01.2012 order No. 22487, I was given TSP at the place of promotion and promoted as SA-I w.e.f. 05.01.2012 after a period of span 27 months, it losses my seniority of 27 months i.e. Sl. No. 2 of re-appointment of 07 SA-I (Appendix-B). I had joined the LSS and appointed on 03.01.2003 as SA-II on transfer basis but those (Sl. No. 09, 10, 13 & 17) who joined the LSS as SA-II after 03.01.2003 were considered as senior to me as per order No. 21946 dtd.12.10.2009, which affected my seniority and promotion by 27 months compared to another order No. 22487 dtd. 05.01.2012. In the above AN-l decision, I want the corrected and justified AN-I decision with further promotion, seniority and pay fixation discrepancies be corrected and provide me relevant information with affected attachment orders/decision compared to other colleague those who joined after 03.01.2003 as SA-II for promotion, seniority and pay fixation and provide relevant information for my satisfaction as per service rules and continue service one department to other of seniority promotion with pay of more than 33 years of continue service (22 years of BSF and more than 10 years of LSS) without promotion and ACP/MACP.

title: Rules and Accountability for Disruptions by MPs in Parliament
subject: RTI seeking the rules governing MPs' conduct during House proceedings, record-keeping of disruptions, accountability, salary deductions, and past disciplinary action for disruptions.
questions: Which law or Rules regulate the Conduct of the Members of the Parliament while the proceedings of the House are going on.
Whether any record is maintained of the Disruptions made by Members of the House in the proceedings of the House.
Whether there is any accountability of Members for any Disruptions made. If yes, Under which Law and To whom they are accountable.
Whether any deductions are made in the Salaries, Daily Allowances or the Privileges granted to the Members of the House, for any Disruptions made by them in the Proceedings of the House.
Do any physical damage to the Property of the House/Parliament by the Member is to be borne by the Member Himself or by any other fund. Please specify in detail.

Whether any action, whatsoever, has been taken against a Member of Parliament for causing disruptions in the proceedings of the House, in the history of the Parliament. If yes, Please specify the particular instances and the Action taken.
response_summary: The Secretariat cited Rules 349, 373, 374 and 374(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha governing members' conduct, withdrawal and suspension for disorderly conduct, and noted that no record of disruptions per se is maintained. It also cited the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 and gave an example of 25 members of the 16th Lok Sabha suspended for five sittings in August 2015 under Rule 374(A).

Sl. No.	Point(s) in brief	Reply
1.	Which law or Rules regulate the Conduct of the Members of Parliament while proceedings of the House are going on	Rules 349, 373 and 374 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha deal with the conduct of members in Lok Sabha. The details of the above rules are available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the heading Procedures-Rules of Procedure. This branch deals with members of Lok Sabha only. The applicant may be requested to visit the website for the desired information.
2.	Whether any record is maintained of the Disruptions made by MPs in the proceedings of the House	No record regarding disruptions by MPs in the House is maintained in the Proceedings of the House. In this regard, it may be stated that members of different political parties come to the well of the House and raise slogans protesting over various issues of the policy, programme and action of the Government. At times when a large number of members of different political parties simultaneously come to the well of the House and raise slogans, it is not feasible to record the same.
3.	Whether there is accountability of MPs for any disruptions made. If yes, under which Law and to whom they are accountable	Rule 373, 374 and 374(A) of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provides for the withdrawal and suspension of members from the services of the House for disorderly conduct, willful obstruction of the business and persistent abuse of the Rules by the members.
4.	Whether any deductions are made in the Salaries, DA or Privileges granted to the MP for any disruptions made by them in the Proceedings of the House	The Salary and Allowances of Members of Parliament are regulated as per provisions of the Salary Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended, Section 3) of the Act and the Rules made thereunder. The situation in which Salary, Daily Allowance are admissible to MPs is mentioned therein. The Act is available on the website http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Members/Amenities.aspx.
5.	Does physical damage to the property of the House/Parliament by the Member have to be borne by the MP himself or any other fund	No such information is maintained in the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
6.	Whether any action, whatsoever, has been taken against a MP for causing disruptions in the proceedings, in the history of Parliament. If yes, please specify the particular instances and action taken	In a recent instance, 25 members of 16th Lok Sabha were suspended for 5 consecutive sittings of the House w.e.f. 3 August, 2015 to 7 August, 2015 under rule 374(A) of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha (List enclosed). title: Status of Bill Granting Special Status to Hyderabad-Karnataka Region
subject: RTI seeking status of the Constitution (One Hundred-Eighteenth Amendment) Bill, 2012 granting special status to the Hyderabad-Karnataka region under Article 371J.
questions: Whether the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha introduced any Bill for the inclusion of article 371J Bill granting the special status to the Hyderabad-Karnataka region in the lines of 371D in the matters of employment and educational opportunities. If yes please provide the copy of the resolution.

Whether Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha received any resolution passed by the Karnataka State Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council, if yes please provide the copy of the resolution received along with the recommendation of the Karnataka State Government.

Whether the Parliament has appointed any Standing Committee for consideration of the recommendation of the Karnataka State Government or resolution passed by the Karnataka Legislative Council or Assembly to deal with provisions contained in the Constitution (One Hundred Eighteenth Amendment) Bill, 2012, if yes please provide copy of the recommendation of the Parliamentary Standing Committee.

Whether the Parliament has received any recommendation from the Government of India for the proposed Constitution (One Hundred Eighteenth Amendment) Bill, 2012, if yes please provide the copy of the recommendation of the Union Cabinet.
Whether the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha has passed Constitution (One Hundred and Eighteenth) Bill, 2012, if yes please provide copy of the Bill.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat informed the applicant that the Constitution (One Hundred-Eighteenth Amendment) Bill, 2012 was introduced on 7.9.2012, referred to the Standing Committee on Home Affairs which submitted its report on 22.11.2013, and eventually passed by Lok Sabha as the Constitution (Ninety-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2012 and assented to by the President on 1.1.2013. No resolution from the Karnataka Assembly/Council or Cabinet recommendation was received by the concerned Division.

response_full_text: In this regard, it is informed that a Bill namely the Constitution (One Hundred-Eighteenth Amendment) Bill, 2012 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 7.9.2012. Copy of the resolution was not provided by the Administrative Ministry and hence the same is not available with the Division concerned. Division concerned has not received any resolution passed from the Karnataka State Legislative Assembly or Legislative Council. The Bill was referred to the Standing Committee on Home Affairs by Chairman, Rajya Sabha in consultation with Speaker, Lok Sabha for examination and report. The report of the Standing Committee was laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 22.11.2013. Division concerned did not receive any recommendation of the Cabinet. The Bill was passed by Lok Sabha as the Constitution (Ninety-Ninth Amendment) Bill, 2012 on 18.12.2012. Rajya Sabha returned the Bill with amendments as the Constitution (Ninety-Eighth Amendment) Bill, 2012 on 19.12.2012. Amendments made by Rajya Sabha were agreed to by Lok Sabha on 20.12.2012. The Bill was assented to by the President on 1.1.2013. Copy of the Bill as passed by the Houses is enclosed.

title: RTI on Disqualification Documents of 16th Lok Sabha Legislature Parties
subject: The RTI seeks documents submitted by legislature party leaders under the anti-defection rules and communications received under Form II of those rules.

title: Access procedure and fees for Lok Sabha TV programme archives
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ, लोक सभा सचिवालय (Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat)
subject: RTI seeking details on whether and how Lok Sabha TV programme archives can be obtained on CDs/DVDs, related fees, and why programmes are not on YouTube.
questions: Does Lok Sabha TV provide archives of its programmes on request for personal use/research/information purpose on CDs/DVDs?
Unlike the China's Public Broadcaster (CCTV), why Lok Sabha TV documentaries and information rich programmes like 'Insight' and 'Public Forum' are not available on You Tube for downloadable purpose.
If programmes are provided on CDs/DVDs, then what is the correct procedure and necessary fees for the same?

If information is not provided for non-commercial basis on the above format, then under which administrative decision or executive privilege this is done? The rationale for such decision may be explained.
If an era of technology and information revolution, why such rich source of knowledge is not available to curious masse?
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed LSTV archives can be supplied on CD/DVD for personal/research use with an undertaking against commercial use, at Rs.100/Rs.150 per disc plus postal charges, noted that putting programmes on YouTube was under process, and explained the copyright/non-commercial restriction; the last question was marked not applicable.
extracted_text:

Reply: The archives of LSTV Programmes are supplied for personal use / reference purpose on CDs/DVDs on request specifying the purpose and submitting a necessary undertaking that the proceedings would not be used for commercial or any other purposes.
2. Unlike the China's Public Broadcaster (CCTV), why Lok Sabha TV documentaries and information rich programmes like 'Insight' and 'Public Forum' are not available on You Tube for downloadable purpose.

An advance payment may be made by the applicant in cash or by demand draft in favour of 'DDO, Lok Sabha' payable at New Delhi. Postal charges of Rs 100/- may also be included in the DD for sending the CDs/DVDs through Registered post. 5. If an era of technology and information revolution, why such rich source of knowledge is not available to curious masse?

title: अस्पष्ट एवं सचिवालय से असंबंधित RTI आवेदन अस्वीकृत
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ, लोक सभा सचिवालय (Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat)
subject: आवेदक द्वारा दायर अस्पष्ट RTI आवेदन को सचिवालय से असंबंधित बताते हुए तथा अवैध पोस्टल ऑर्डर के आधार पर अस्वीकृत किया गया।
questions: आवेदन में विशेष सूचना के स्थान पर अस्पष्ट प्रश्न पूछा गया, जिसका विवरण मूल आवेदन में उपलब्ध नहीं है।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि आवेदन में मांगी गई सूचना अस्पष्ट है, सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है और आरटीआई अधिनियम की धारा 2(च) के प्रावधानों के अनुरूप नहीं है, अतः कोई कार्यवाही नहीं की जा सकती। आवेदन शुल्क का आईपीओ वापस संलग्न किया गया।

महोदय,
इस सचिवालय में 17.05.2016 को प्राप्त आपके दिनांक 13.05.2016 के आरटीआई आवेदन के संदर्भ में मुझे यह बताने का निदेश हुआ है कि सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत कोई विशेष जानकारी मांगने के बजाय आपने ऐसी सूचना मांगी है जो अस्पष्ट है और इस सचिवालय में उपलब्ध नहीं है। आवेदन की विषय-वस्तु इस सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है और सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 2(च) के प्रावधानों के अनुरूप नहीं है। अतः इस संबंध में कोई कार्यवाही नहीं की जा सकती है।

3. मुझे आपको यह भी सूचित करना है कि सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम के अंतर्गत केवल ऐसी सूचना ही प्रदान की जाती है जो पहले से उपलब्ध हो और जन प्राधिकारी के पास हो अथवा उसके नियंत्रण में हो। जन सूचना अधिकारी का कार्य आवेदकों द्वारा उठाई गई समस्याओं का समाधान करना नहीं है। सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत शिकायतों, सुझावों, सलाहों और निर्देशों आदि पर विचार नहीं किया जाता है। आप अपनी समस्याओं के निराकरण के लिए संबंधित प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क कर सकते हैं।
4. इसे केंद्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी का अनुमोदन प्राप्त है।
भवदीय,
संलग्न: यथोपरि।

title: गृह किराया भत्ता, सुरक्षा वाहन व फेरी सेवा दुरुपयोग संबंधी सूचना (आंशिक)
subject: आवेदक ने सुरक्षा शाखा के अधिकारियों को दिए गए मकान किराया भत्ता, परिवहन भत्ता, फेरी सेवा के दुरुपयोग तथा सुरक्षा संबंधी शिकायतों पर कार्यवाही की जानकारी मांगी।
questions: ऐसे कर्मचारियों की संख्या बताएं जो वर्ष 1990 से 2016 तक मकान किराया भत्ता प्राप्त कर रहे हैं परंतु दिल्ली से बाहर रह रहे हैं।

श्री भगवती प्रसाद रतूड़ी, सहायक निदेशक (सुरक्षा) अपना अस्थायी निवास स्थान दिल्ली में दर्शा कर वर्ष 1990 से वेतन के साथ मकान किराया भत्ता प्राप्त कर रहे हैं, जबकि उनका निवास स्थान गोविंदपुर, मोदीनगर है जहां से वह प्रतिदिन कार्यालय आते हैं। कृपया श्री बी.पी. रतूड़ी द्वारा अब तक मकान किराए भत्ते के रूप में प्राप्त की गई राशि का ब्यौरा प्रदान करें और साथ ही उनके वेतन और अस्थायी निवास से संबंधित प्रमाणपत्र भी प्रदान करें।
श्री बैजवान, निदेशक (सुरक्षा) द्वारा कौन सा वाहन उपयोग किया जा रहा है, वाहन की पंजीकरण सं. बताएं, और उनके द्वारा कितना परिवहन भत्ता लिया जा रहा है।
श्री बैजवान की आई.जी. के पद पर पदोन्नति हो गई है, उनके अपने मूल कार्यालय में कार्यभार न संभालने के संबंध में जानकारी।
श्री बी.पी. रतूड़ी, सहायक निदेशक (सुरक्षा) को सुविधाएं और रियायत दिए जाने के क्या कारण हैं।
सुरक्षा कर्मियों द्वारा संसद भवन परिसर में उपलब्ध फेरी कारों का दुरूपयोग किया जाना और इस पर एक माह में कितनी धनराशि खर्च होती है।
वर्ष 2005 से 2016 (मार्च) के दौरान भारतीय स्टेट बैंक, संसदीय सौध के लिए सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारियों/उनके परिवार के सदस्यों को कितने पास जारी किए गए।
2005-2015 के दौरान सेवानिवृत्त कर्मचारियों को कितने पार्किंग लेबल जारी किए गए।
आवेदक द्वारा श्री आर.एस. पंवार, सुरक्षा अधिकारी के विरुद्ध की गई शिकायत और संसद के सत्र के दौरान केंद्रीय कक्ष में उनकी पत्नी के प्रवेश पर क्या कार्यवाही की गई।
3-4 मार्च, 2016 को वैध पास के बिना एक व्यक्ति को प्रवेश कराने वाले कर्मी के खिलाफ की गई कार्यवाही का ब्यौरा दें।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि मकान किराया भत्ता संबंधी सूचना शाखा में उपलब्ध नहीं है; श्री बी.पी. रतूड़ी व श्री बैजवान नियमानुसार पात्रता अनुसार भत्ते प्राप्त कर रहे हैं; सुरक्षा शाखा द्वारा फेरी सेवा का समुचित रिकॉर्ड रखा जाता है और सुरक्षा कर्मियों द्वारा दुरुपयोग नहीं किया जाता; संसद भवन परिसर की सुरक्षा से संबंधित कुछ सूचना आरटीआई अधिनियम की धारा 8(1)(क) के अंतर्गत प्रकटन से छूट प्राप्त बताई गई।

response_full_text: आवेदक द्वारा मांगी गई जानकारी सचिवालय की शाखा में नहीं रखी जाती है। श्री बी.पी. रतूड़ी, सहायक निदेशक (संसद सुरक्षा सेवा) समय-समय पर नियमों के अधीन अनुमेय अपनी पात्रता के अनुसार मकान किराया भत्ता प्राप्त कर रहे हैं। श्री बैजवान, निदेशक (संसद सुरक्षा सेवा) लोक सभा सचिवालय में प्रतिनियुक्ति आधार पर अपनी नियुक्ति की तारीख से समय-समय पर अनुमेय परिवहन महंगाई भत्ते सहित 3200/- रुपये की दर से परिवहन भत्ता प्राप्त कर रहे हैं। स्टाफ कार नियमों के अनुसार संयुक्त सचिव और इससे ऊपर के स्तर के अधिकारी अपने निवास स्थान से कार्यालय आने-जाने के लिए सरकारी परिवहन सुविधा प्राप्त करने के पात्र हैं, परंतु निदेशक (सुरक्षा) के लिए कोई सरकारी वाहन उपलब्ध नहीं कराया गया है। संसद सुरक्षा सेवा में तैनाती/स्थानांतरण सक्षम प्राधिकारी द्वारा आवश्यकता और उपयुक्तता के आधार पर किया जाता है। संसद भवन परिसर में फेरी सेवा का उपयोग केवल माननीय संसद सदस्यों/पूर्व संसद सदस्यों द्वारा किया जाता है। सुरक्षा कर्मियों द्वारा इसका दुरूपयोग नहीं किया जाता है। संबंधित शाखा द्वारा फेरी सेवा के उपयोग से संबंधित उचित रिकार्ड रखा जाता है। मांगी गई जानकारी से संसद भवन परिसर की सुरक्षा के लिए कार्यनीतिक सुरक्षा पहुंच विनियमों का आंशिक रूप से प्रकटन हो जाएगा, अतः उक्त सूचना को आरटीआई अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 8(1)(क) के अधीन प्रकटन से छूट प्राप्त है।

title: Mavalankar Hall renovation project tender and construction details
subject: Applicant sought detailed information on the renovation of Mavalankar Hall, related tenders, the new construction in Parliament Annexe Complex, and complaints against a named Joint Secretary.
questions: Is proposal for Mavalankar Hall renovation is being considered by Lok Sabha Secretariat?
What is the proposal for renovation of Mavalankar Hall along with estimate details.
When the renovation of Mavalankar Hall will be executed and by which agency?
Whether tender has been floated for renovation of Mavalankar Hall. Copy of relevant notings to be provided.

How many Auditoriums are available in Parliament House and Parliament House Annexe? Details of all auditoriums to be provided alongwith capacity of same and revenue being collected from them in last year?
For what purpose new construction is in progress in the Parliament Annexe Complex.
What is the sanctioned amount for said project and to which agency work is being awarded?
What facilities are being developed in the said project and who will be the users for the same?
How the work has been awarded, whether tender was advertised, if yes details for the same to be provided.
Details of tenders received to be provided in detail i.e. number of tenders, name of the firm, amount etc.
Which firm has been awarded the work and what process has been adopted to award the same?
Whether any committee was nominated for awarding the tender, if yes details for the same to be provided.
What is the completion date for the project?
Whether any complaints have been received against Mr. A.K. Singh, Joint Secretary, Lok Sabha. If yes, copy of complaints to be provided.
Whether any action has been taken on said complaints.
Copy of all file notings with regard to complaints being received against Mr. A.K. Singh, Joint Secretary, Lok Sabha to be provided.
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed the Mavalankar Hall renovation proposal was pending CPWD estimates, stated there is no auditorium in Parliament House/Annexe, and gave detailed information on the new Parliament Annexe Complex construction, its sanctioned amount (Rs. 261,85,48,000/-), tender packages, bidders and awarded firms. Complaint-related queries (points 14-16) were declined as they sought reasons/opinions rather than 'information' as defined under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act.

response_full_text: Yes, proposal for Mavalankar Hall renovation is being considered. Proposal/estimate for renovation of Mavalankar Auditorium is awaited from CPWD. Responsibility for renovation has been entrusted to CPWD; proposal/estimate is awaited. Question of tender does not arise as proposal is awaited. There is no Auditorium in Parliament House and Parliament House Annexe Buildings. New construction is to meet the space requirement of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats. Sanctioned amount of the project is Rs. 261,85,48,000/-. The entire work has been divided into 15 packages by CPWD; Civil component has 3 packages and Electrical component has 12 packages. The first package has been awarded to M/s Globe Pvt. Ltd.; tenders are being called for other packages. Office rooms, Committee Rooms, Auditorium etc. are being developed for use by Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha Secretariats. Tenders were advertised in Navbharat Times, Rashtriya Sahara, The Times of India and Hindustan Times in November 2009; electrical biddings invited online via www.tenderwizard.com/cpwd. Details of multiple bidding firms and amounts were furnished (Ahluwalia Contracts, Tantia Construction, Consolidated Construction Consortium, Unity Infra Projects, JMC Projects, Pratibha Industries, Globe Civil Projects, Era Infra Engineer, Swadeshi Construction). Work awarded to M/s Globe Civil Projects Pvt. Ltd. as per standard CPWD procedures; various electrical works awarded to other named firms. Chief Engineer is empowered to accept lowest tender with prior approval of Central Works Board of CPWD. Stipulated completion date was June 2, 2014. Regarding points 14-16, the applicant has asked a question and not sought information as defined in Sec. 2(f) of the RTI Act.

title: Employee's personal bio-data and certificates denied under privacy exemption
subject: Applicant sought a copy of an employee's bio-data, community certificate, family particulars and educational qualification certificates, which were denied as personal information.
questions: Provide a copy of Bio-data i.e. Name, Father's Name, Permanent Address, Community status etc.

A copy of educational qualification certificates submitted by the employee at the time of joining
response_summary: The Secretariat denied all the requested personal details of the employee, holding that the questions had no relationship to any public activity or interest and that disclosure would cause unwarranted invasion of the individual's privacy, invoking Section 8(1)(j) of the RTI Act, 2005.

response_full_text:
The Constitution of India provides that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. However, neither the Constitution nor the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provide as to how many days Lok Sabha would sit in a session/year. The number of sittings of Lok Sabha for each session is decided by the Government of India and intimated through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs keeping in view the volume of legislative and financial business which Government propose to bring forward before the House.

Information is available in the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.in -> 'Resume of Work' -> 'Archive' and also loksabha.in -> 'Business' ->'Bulletin-I -> 'Archive'.

As regards adjournment of proceedings due to disruption by opposition/members, the requisite information is available on Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.in under the heading 'Debates' -> 'Text of Debate' -> 'Archive'. Hence, the applicant is requested to access the information on the above website.

The expenditure on conducting session in Parliament is incurred by multiple agencies viz., Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban development/CPWD and other Ministries/departments. There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Branches/agencies in connection with the conducting of session in Parliament. Therefore, the Branch concerned of this Secretariat cannot comment on the cost incurred due to adjournments of sessions of Lok Sabha.

questions: Intimate the selection process of Engineers in Parliament House Complex, New Delhi.
Is all Engineer's posted in Parliament House Complex gone through that selection process, if so, name all the Engineers with their period of posting in different capacities since last 10 years.
When Shri R.K. Rastogi, was initially posted in Parliament House Complex. Intimate his initial jurisdiction and initial rank.
Was he ever posted in Parliament House Complex in other capacities? If yes, intimate his entire posting details in different capacities and reasons for shifting from Parliament House Complex.
Intimate name of authorities who recommended his name for posting in various capacities.

Intimate details of the incident when one person whose permanent pass was cancelled by security in Parliament Library Building due to dubious activities was caught with Mr. Gaur. Please intimate the date / year of the incident.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained the CPWD-led selection process for Engineers posted in Parliament House Complex based on ACRs, provided posting details of a named engineer, and stated that the posting history running into 22 pages was ready for dispatch on payment of information fee; it could not trace records of the vague security incident mentioned.

title: RTI seeking list of Money Bills and related Article 100(3)/110 rulings
subject: RTI seeking a list of all Money Bills introduced in Parliament and related information on Bills rejected by Lok Sabha and Speaker's rulings under Article 100(3).
questions: List of all the money bills introduced in the Parliament right from the time of its inception. Even the Finance Minister in his speech on the floor of the Lok Sabha on 11th Mar., 2016 confirmed the existence of such a list
List mentioned above request, the bills which are passed by the Lok Sabha and which are rejected by the same House

The list of bills, where the Hon'ble Speaker of Lok Sabha has used the direction under Article 100(3) of the Indian Constitution and decided the bill concerned as NOT a money bill as per the definition under Article 110(I) of the Indian Constitute
response_summary: The Secretariat advised that the status of a Bill as a Money Bill is indicated in the list of Bills passed and assented to by the President and directed the applicant to use the 'Search' option under the 'Legislation' link on the Lok Sabha website; clarified that a Bill passed by Lok Sabha cannot be rejected by the same House; and stated that Article 100(3) does not relate to Money Bills.

response_full_text:
Status of Bill as Money Bill is indicated in the list of all Bills passed by Houses and assented to by President, which is issued after prorogation of every session. The applicant may be requested to use 'Search' option under the 'Legislation' link on the website of Lok Sabha. The search option allows a user to search for Bills which are Money Bills/Financial Bills/Ordinary Bills. The applicant may select the appropriate category under 'Bill Category' and search accordingly.

A bill passed by Lok Sabha cannot be rejected by Lok Sabha at the same time. The applicant may be requested to clarify.

Article 100(3) relates to "Voting in Houses, power of Houses to act notwithstanding vacancies and quorum" and does not relate to Money Bill.

title: MP facilities, salaries, and assets information sought
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell), Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: Applicant sought information on facilities, salaries and allowances, and asset declarations of Members of Lok Sabha.
questions: (Specific query not stated verbatim — matter transferred to Cabinet Secretariat)
Details of facilities provided to MPs of Lok Sabha, and Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament revised from time to time
(Specific query not stated verbatim — reply: such information is not maintained as it involves several Ministries under various heads)
Information regarding assets (movable/immovable) of Members of Lok Sabha, according to quantum of wealth of individual Members
response_summary: One point was transferred to the Cabinet Secretariat; a pamphlet on MP facilities and a statement of MP salaries/allowances were enclosed; certain cross-ministry information was not maintained; and asset information is maintained only per the Members of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets & Liabilities) Rules, 2004, not by quantum of wealth.

title: Rules on duties of MPs/MLAs and raising grievances in Parliament
department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell), Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: Applicant sought copies of Acts/Rules/Manuals on duties/rights of MPs/MLAs and citizens, and asked who raises questions on the floor of Parliament on behalf of the PM/Speaker/Ministers.
questions: Kindly provide me copies of Acts/Rules/Manuals which are dealing with duties and responsibilities of MPs/MLAs of India.
Kindly provide me copies of Acts/Rules/Manuals which are dealing with Rights of Citizen of India with their people representatives i.e. MPs/MLAs.
The duties and responsibilities and nature of works/job description of President of India/Prime Minister/Minister apart from which are already described in Constitution of India
Who will raise question on the floor of Parliament on behalf of Prime Minister/Speaker/Dy. Speaker/Ministers to redress the grievances of their respective constituency
response_summary: The Secretariat stated that the duties/responsibilities of MPs and rights of citizens vis-à-vis their representatives are defined in the Rules of Procedure and the Constitution of India rather than in separate Acts/Manuals, so no separate information was available; the query on the President/PM/Ministers did not relate to the Lok Sabha Secretariat; and rules for raising questions in Lok Sabha were pointed to specific website links.

department: सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell), Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: Applicant, on transfer from Directorate of Estates, sought details of accommodation earmarked for MPs, upgrade/eviction rules, and related housing policy for Members of Lok Sabha.
questions: No. of accommodations earmarked (category and type wise) for MPs(Lok Sabha) since 2014.

Eviction notices issued to MP(Lok Sabha) and how many cases were evicted since June, 2014
Type-wise policy/norms for eviction of MP from their accommodation
Rule/policy whether general category accommodation can be allotted to a MP
Actual record of maximum permissible period for physical possession to MP after issuing possession letter of an accommodation for its habitual use in last 5 years
Maximum and minimum period as per approved norms/policy to re-allot accommodation after the same is vacated and handed over to the department
In case a general category accommodation, whether the eligibility of a bureaucrat and parameter of eligibility of MP changes?

response_full_text: A new system of assessment of work and conduct of Government employees has been introduced in the Government of India with the revised nomenclature, Annual Performance Assessment Report (APAR) in place of Annual Confidential Report. In the new system, the duly written APAR is to be communicated to the officer reported upon. However, the system of writing of ACRs is still being followed in this Secretariat and therefore, only the adverse remarks recorded in the ACR are to be communicated to the officer reported upon in the light of the relevant instructions on the subject. It may also be submitted that the Annual Confidential Report, as its name suggests, is a confidential document and it contains information about the character, capability and other attributes of the officer reported upon and the entries made therein are based on trust and confidence between the officers involved in initiating and reviewing the CRs. Therefore the disclosure of such documents may harm interpersonal relationships in the Secretariat where the system of writing up of ACRs is still in existence. However, disclosure of adverse remarks is permissible in the relevant instructions taking into account the principle of natural justice and, therefore, the adverse remarks recording in the ACR are invariably being communicated to the officer concerned in order to provide him an opportunity for making any representation against the adverse remarks and also keeping in view the instructions on the subject issued by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (Department of Personnel and Training) O.M. No.10/20/2006-IR dated 21st September, 2007 (copy enclosed). In the light of these facts in particular, it was decided with the approval of the Competent Authority that the copies of ACRs, as desired by the applicant, need not be provided to him.

title: RTI on CPWD engineer posting, transfer and relieving guidelines
department: Central Public Works Department (CPWD) / Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: The applicant sought details of the selection/posting procedure for CPWD Engineers (AE/EE/SE), guidelines for relieving officers on transfer from the Parliament House Complex, and names of officers not relieved as per transfer orders between 1.04.2011 and 30.09.2012.
questions: Point No. 1 - Selection procedure/criteria for posting of AE/EE/SE and also provide the copy of order/guideline & if there is any committee then whether it is a technical committee or administrative committee.
Point No. 2 - Guideline for relieving of any officers i.e. AE/EE/SE on transfer from PH Complex, also provide the copy of the same.

Point No. 3 - The transfer orders are issued by CPWD, in which it is specifically mention that person under transfer should be relived within one month of transfer order. The transferred officer cannot be paid his salary without the permission of Chief Engineer after one month. Please provide the name of officers who have not been relieved whose order has been issued between 1.04.2011 to 30.09.2012 and also, provide the copy of permission letter for transferred officers for payment of their salary.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that Engineers up to Superintending Engineer level are posted based on ACR ratings with Lok Sabha Secretariat's concurrence (enclosing relevant OMs), that transfer/posting orders for CPWD Engineers are regulated by the Ministry of Urban Development, and named Shri Sukhdev Singh, AE (Civil), as an officer transferred in April 2011 who was reposted in PCWZ in August 2012.

Point No. 1 - Selection procedure/criteria for posting of AE/EE/SE and also provide the copy of order/guideline & if there is any committee then whether it is a technical committee or administrative committee. The Engineers upto the level of Superintending Engineers are posted generally on the basis of rating of their ACRs and with the prior concurrence of Lok Sabha Secretariat. Copies of the order/guidelines vide OM Nos. 28/8/2005-EC-I/EW-I dated 21.11.2005, 6.2.1998 D.O. Point No. 2 - Guideline for relieving of any officers i.e. AE/EE/SE on transfer from PH Complex, also provide the copy of the same. The transferred Engineers are relieved from the duty on selection and joining of his substitute. The posting & transfer orders of CPWD Engineers upto the rank of Superintending Engineers are regulated by the Orders of the Government of India, ministry of Urban Development. Copies of the aforesaid orders as mentioned at Point No.1.
Point No. 3 - The transfer orders are issued by CPWD, in which it is specifically mention that person under transfer should be relived within one month of transfer order. response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed that Shri Lalu Prasad stood disqualified from Lok Sabha membership from 30 September 2013 following his CBI Court conviction, under Article 102(1)(e) of the Constitution read with Section 8 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and listed the general constitutional grounds for disqualification of MPs.

title: RTI on MP attendance rules and parliamentary delegations abroad
subject: The applicant sought information on rules governing MP attendance and seat vacancy, duties of MPs, and details of parliamentary delegations abroad; the original point-wise question text is not reproduced in this reply document, only the replies organised by point number.
questions: Point 1 & 3 (reconstructed from reply): Provisions under Article 101(4) of the Constitution regarding declaration of a Member's seat as vacant for absence and the requirement to sign the Attendance Register.
Point 2 (reconstructed from reply): Details of the Attendance Register maintained for Members of Parliament and which categories of members are exempted from signing it.
Point 4 (reconstructed from reply): Whether any article/rule lays down the duties of an MP during a Parliament session or otherwise.
Points 6, 7, 8 & 9 (reconstructed from reply): Original question text not available; Secretariat replied that no information on these points is available.
Points 5 & 10 (reconstructed from reply): Query pertaining exclusively to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation.

Point 11 (reconstructed from reply): Details of Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) who were part of Indian Parliamentary Delegations visiting abroad under bilateral exchanges/official conferences and meetings during the last five years.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained Article 101(4) provisions on seat vacancy for non-attendance, described the Attendance Register and exemptions, stated that MP duties during sessions are not codified, said no information was available for some points, transferred points on Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation to that Ministry, and enclosed a statement on MPs' foreign parliamentary delegations.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application Dated 08.10.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No.1(1408)/IC/13 dated 28.10.2013
Point Nos. Reply
1&3. Article 101 (4) of the Constitution of India provides as follows:- "If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant: Provided that in computing the said period of sixty days no account shall be taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or is adjourned for more than four consecutive days". Hence, a member of the House has to sign the Attendance Register at least once in every 59 days or apply for leave of his absence from the sittings of the House failing which the House can declare his seat vacant.
2. In order to record the attendance of members, an attendance register is maintained for members to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. The Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Ministers and Leader of the Opposition are exempted from the requirement of signing the Attendance Register. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by the members during the last five years of the 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members > Attendance of Members. The applicant may peruse the information. The applicant may however note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day.
4. There is neither any article in the Constitution of India nor any rule in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha which lays down the duties of an MP during the period when Parliament is in session (or otherwise). Consequently no such information is maintained and available with the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
6, 7, 8 & 9. No information on the said points is available.
5 & 10. Since the subject matter of this query exclusively pertains to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme implementation, a copy of the application has been transferred to them on 89.10.2013 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to her.
11. A statement giving details of Members of Parliament, (Lok Sabha) who were part of Indian Parliamentary Delegations visiting abroad under bilateral Parliamentary exchanges and for the purpose of official Conferences and Meetings during last five years is enclosed.
response_full_text: 1&3. Article 101 (4) of the Constitution of India provides as follows:- "If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant..." Hence, a member of the House has to sign the Attendance Register at least once in every 59 days or apply for leave of his absence from the sittings of the House failing which the House can declare his seat vacant. 2. In order to record the attendance of members, an attendance register is maintained... The Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Ministers and Leader of the Opposition are exempted from the requirement of signing the Attendance Register. Details are available on www.loksabha.nic.in under Members > Attendance of Members. 4. There is neither any article in the Constitution of India nor any rule in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha which lays down the duties of an MP during the period when Parliament is in session (or otherwise). Consequently no such information is maintained. 6,7,8 & 9. No information on the said points is available. 5 & 10. Since the subject matter of this query exclusively pertains to the Ministry of Statistics and Programme implementation, a copy of the application has been transferred to them on 89.10.2013 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to her. 11. A statement giving details of Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) who were part of Indian Parliamentary Delegations visiting abroad under bilateral Parliamentary exchanges and for the purpose of official Conferences and Meetings during last five years is enclosed.

title: MP privileges, convicted person statue, and Tamil Nadu MPs attendance
department: Lok Sabha Secretariat (सूचना प्रकोष्ठ / Information Cell)
ministry: Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs (transfer); Rajya Sabha Secretariat (partial transfer)
subject: RTI seeking clarification on parliamentary privileges regarding praising a convicted person, installing a statue of a convicted person, and attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs.
questions: Kindly provide information whether a Member of Parliament can praise a convicted person in Parliament.
Information if a statue of convicted person can be installed in Parliament.

Kindly give me the information of attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs from 22nd September 2016 to 22nd March 2017. Need the details of number of the days Rajya Sabha worked and numbers of the days Tamil Nadu MPs attended assembly session.
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that MPs enjoy privilege of free speech under Article 105 of the Constitution and cannot be questioned in court for statements in the House; the query on installing a statue of a convicted person was held not to be 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act; and attendance data for Tamil Nadu MPs was directed to the Lok Sabha website, with the Rajya Sabha component transferred and the state assembly attendance query declined as it pertains to the Tamil Nadu State Government.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated 27.03.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(429)/IC/17 dated 25.04.2017

Sl. No. 1: Point raised: Kindly provide information whether a Member of Parliament can praise a convicted person in Parliament.
Reply: Subject to the provisions of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, a Member of Lok Sabha is free to express his view in the House and a Member cannot be questioned in any court in respect of anything said in the House. This is a privilege conferred upon them as laid down under Article 105 of the Constitution.

Sl. No. 2: Point raised: Information if a statue of convicted person can be installed in Parliament.
Reply: Does not constitute information under Section 2(f) of RTI Act, 2005.

Sl. No. 3: Point raised: Kindly give me the information of attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs from 22nd September 2016 to 22nd March 2017. Need the details of number of the days Rajya Sabha worked and numbers of the days Tamil Nadu MPs attended assembly session.
Reply: An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha representing the state of Tamil Nadu during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member-wise Attendance -> All Members respectively. The applicant may however note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. As regard information for the Rajya Sabha worked, application has been transferred to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat. Information relating to MPs attendance in assembly session, pertains to State Government of Tamil Nadu and your application cannot be transferred in terms of the instruction of the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, Department of Personnel & Training vide O.M.No.10/2/2008-IR dated 12th June, 2008 in para 3(iv).

Sl. No. 1: Point raised: Whether Income Tax is payable by MPs Lok Sabha
Reply: The Salary and allowances received by the Members are taxed under the head Income from other sources. Since the salary and allowances are taxed under the head Income from other sources such salary and allowances would not be subjected to Tax Deduction at source (TDS). Members will have to discharge their tax liability by paying advance tax and/or self-assessment tax.

Sl. No. 2: Point raised: Payment of salary and allowances to the MPs every year.

The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowance) Rules, 1986 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the Purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The aforementioned Act/Rules are available on Lok Sabha website and can be accessed through www.loksabha.nic.in and by clicking on 'Members' slot and then on 'Salary Acts and Rules'.

Reply: Information sought by the applicant is not maintained by Privileges & Ethics Branch. Hence, no information can be made available.

Accordingly, searching and then providing information for a period of 26 years regarding time lost due to interruptions and adjournment of Lok Sabha would definitely divert a sizeable amount of time and manpower of the Secretariat.

title: RTI on ban of cold drinks/soft drinks in Parliament House Complex
subject: RTI seeking the notification/order banning cold drinks and soft drinks in the Parliament House canteen and the reasons for the ban.
questions: Please provide relevant notification/order/circular etc. for banning the cold drinks in Parliament Canteen.
In which other places cold drink or soft drinks banned along with the premises of Parliament of India.
What is the reason for banning those cold drinks or soft drinks on the premises of Parliament.
If these cold drinks are harmful due to which it is banned in Parliament why it is not banned in all over India.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that following an MP-raised concern in the House about pesticide detection in soft drinks (based on a CSE study), the Chairman of the Joint Committee on Food Management ordered discontinuation of Coke, Pepsi and other soft drinks in Parliament House Complex catering units w.e.f. 6.8.2003, and enclosed the order. Queries about bans elsewhere in India, and why the ban was not extended nationally, were held not to constitute 'information' under Section 2(f)/pertain to the Secretariat.

Reply: The Members of Parliament raised the matter in the House regarding reported detection of pesticides in the popular brands of soft drinks. During the discussion, Shri E. Sl. No. 3: What is the reason for banning those cold drinks or soft drinks on the premises of Parliament.
Reply: Delhi based NGO viz Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) in their study had reported the presence of high levels of pesticides and insecticides in all the major brands of soft drinks. The Members of Parliament raised the matter in the House regarding reported detection of pesticides in the popular brands of soft drinks. During the discussion, Shri E. Ahamed, M.P. as Chairman of the Joint Committee on Food Management in Parliament House Complex announced in the House that taking into account the sentiments being expressed by the Hon'ble Members, the supply of Coke, Pepsi and other soft drinks being served in the Railway Catering Units will be discontinued with immediate effect.

[Annexure: Order dated 20 August 2003 from the Chairman, Parliamentary Committee on Food Management, addressed to Senior Commercial Manager, Railway Canteens: It was hereby ordered that the supply of all soft drinks like Pepsi-Cola, Coca-Cola, Mirinda, Lemon, Fanta, Limca, Sprite, Thums Up, Mountain Dew, Diet Pepsi, 7-Up and all other brands of aerated drinks shall be discontinued in the catering centres/canteens within the Parliament House Complex with immediate effect. Concerned agencies were directed to remove all such advertisement material/refrigerators from the Parliament House Complex immediately, and the Senior Commercial Manager, Railway Canteens, was directed to ensure strict adherence to this order by all employees.
