title: RTI on MP privilege, convicted person's statue, and Tamil Nadu MP attendance
subject: RTI seeking information on whether an MP can praise a convicted person in the House, installation of a convicted person's statue in Parliament, and attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs.
questions: Kindly provide information whether a Member of Parliament can praise a convicted person in Lok Sabha
Information if a statue of convicted person can be installed in Parliament

Kindly give me the information of attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs from 22nd September 2016 to 22nd March 2017. Need the details of number of the days Lok Sabha worked and numbers of the days Tamil Nadu MPs attended assembly session.
response_summary: The Secretariat replied that Members enjoy privilege under Article 105 of the Constitution to freely express views in the House; the statue query was held not to be 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act; and attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs were stated to be available on the Lok Sabha website.

Application dated: 22.03.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(397)/IC/17 dated 13.04.2017

Point No. 1: Kindly provide information whether a Member of Parliament can praise a convicted person in Lok Sabha
Information/Reply: Subject to the provisions of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha, a Member of Lok Sabha is free to express his view in the House and Member cannot be questioned in any court in respect of anything said in the House. This is a privilege conferred upon them as laid down under Article 105 of the Constitution.

Point No. 2: Information if a statue of convicted person can be installed in Parliament
Information/Reply: Does not constitute information under Section 2(f) of RTI Act, 2005.

Point No. 3: Kindly give me the information of attendance details of Tamil Nadu MPs from 22nd September 2016 to 22nd March 2017. Need the details of number of the days Lok Sabha worked and numbers of the days Tamil Nadu MPs attended assembly session.
Information/Reply: The concerned Branch of the Secretariat i.e. Table Office (B) deals with the attendance of members of Lok Sabha: An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha representing the state of Tamil Nadu during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member-wise Attendance -> All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information.

Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(388)/IC/17 dated 16.03.2017

Point No. 1: Information on the rise Income along with the assets including movable and fixed of all Members of Parliament of the present Government.
Information/Reply: Members of Lok Sabha are required to furnish a declaration of Assets and Liabilities in accordance with 'Members of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets and Liabilities) Rules, 2004' with regard to themselves/spouse and dependent children. These declaration of Assets and Liabilities as furnished by the Members till date run into several thousands of pages (5000 pages* approximately) and copies of the same shall be made available to the applicant provided the applicant deposits the requisite charges/fees.
The concerned Branch of the Secretariat i.e. Members Salaries and Allowances deals with the salary and allowances of sitting MPs and pension/family pension of Ex MPs which are regulated by MSA Act, 1954. However, the salary and allowances of MPs are as under: (I) Salary Rs. 50,000/-, (ii) Constituency Allowance Rs. 45,000/-, (iii) Office expense allowance Rs. 45,000/- out of which Rs. 15,000/- is for meeting expenses of stationery items and postage; and Rs. 30,000/- is paid by the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariats to the person(s) as may be engaged by a member for obtaining secretarial assistance provided that one such person must be computer literate as certified by the member himself. The other benefits to Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules: 1. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954. 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957. 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956. 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959. 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960. 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowance) Rules, 1986. 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the Purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986. 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The aforementioned Act/Rules are available on Lok Sabha website www.loksabha.nic.in under 'Members' and then 'Salary Acts and Rules'. Other aspects do not pertain to this branch.
*You may, if you desire deposit Rs. 10000/- (@ Rs. 2/- per page) as information fee for the same to be supplied to you. The information fee is required to be paid by way of cash at 'Reception of Parliament Library Building, Lok Sabha Secretariat' against proper receipt or sent through money order or demand draft or bankers cheque or postal order payable to 'Drawing & Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha', in terms of Lok Sabha Secretariat Right to Information (Regulation of Fees & Cost) Rules 2005, and the amendment Rules, 2007. Demand Draft/Bankers Cheque and IPO in favour of Accounts Officer, Lok Sabha is also accepted. The information will be sent to you on receipt of the aforesaid information fee.

It is pertinent to mention that Rule 10(1) of the CCS(Pension) Rules, 1972 inter alia stipulates that if a pensioner who, immediately before his retirement was a member of Central Service Group 'A' wishes to accept any commercial employment before the expiry of one year from the date of his retirement, he shall obtain the previous sanction of the Government to such acceptance...

title: RTI on Constitution amendments and Bills process
subject: The applicant asked about the number of amendments to the Indian Constitution, the difference between Bills and amendments, the number of Bills introduced in Parliament, and whether Article 121 of the Constitution is an amendment or a Bill.
questions: How many amendments happen in our Indian Constitution?
What is the difference between Bills and amendments?
How many Bills came in Parliament and how many amendments done in our Constitution?
121 article of Indian Constitution is amendment in our Constitution or this is Bill.
response_summary: The Secretariat replied that the Constitution has been amended ninety-nine times so far, explained the difference between a Bill and an amendment (with a booklet enclosed), stated that the number of Government Bills introduced is a Government decision, and clarified that Article 121 of the Constitution is neither a Bill nor an amendment but an article of the Constitution.

Reply: A Bill is a draft law which when passed by the Houses of Parliament and assented to by the President becomes law of the land. In case of Government Bills, it is for the Government to decide as to when and how many Bills are to be introduced in Lok Sabha. As regards amendments in Constitution, please refer to reply at Point No.1 above. 4. Article 121 of Indian Constitution is neither an amendment nor a Bill. It is an article of the Constitution.

Name of the Applicant: Sh. [Applicant]
Application dated: 18.03.2015
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(354)/IC/15 dated 28.04.15
Sl. No. 1. Points raised (in brief): Details of expenditure under MPLADS
Reply: Transferred to M/o Statistics & Programme Implementation
Sl. No. 2. Points raised: Total emoluments received by Ramachandra Hansdah, MP, Lok Sabha Mayurbhanj Parliamentary Constituency
Reply: The information relating to Sh. Ramachandra Hansdah, MP of Lok Sabha is voluminous, the compilation of which will disproportionately divert the resources. However, if the applicant desires, he may be requested to visit the MSA Branch after seeking prior appointment with Executive Officer, Contact no.23034405/4407 and peruse the register meant for the purpose.
Sl. No. 3. Points raised: The house of Sh. Ramachandra Hansdah, MP was raided by CBI recently which recovered huge amount pointing him as an accused in Chit Fund Scam in Odisha etc.
Reply: The definition of information under Section 2(f) of RTI Act,2005 cannot and does not include views/opinions of public authority like Lok Sabha Secretariat as to how much time shall the Hon'ble Speaker take to initiate action against an MP accused of financial misappropriation. The Lok Sabha Secretariat is not in a position to supply any information in this regard. Further, in such matters, Office of Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha has no role.
Sl. No. 4. Points raised: The affidavit copy of the property, qualification, bank loan etc. Detailed submitted by him to Parliament.
Reply: As regards, the details of property and bank loans of Sh. Ramachandra Hansdah, MP is concerned, the same is furnished in the form of Assets & Liabilities declaration which every elected Member is required to provide according to the Member of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets & Liabilities) Rules, 2004 within ninety days from the date on which he/she takes oath. However, such a declaration is awaited from the Member. The information pertaining to Educational Qualification of Shri Rama Chandra Hansdah, MP, 16th Lok Sabha, as provided by him is available in his bio-profile. The Bio-profile is available on the Lok Sabha Website i.e. <www.loksabha.nic.in> under the heading 'Members' -> 'Alphabetical List'-> under the Name of Member. (Sample copy enclosed).
Sl. No. 5. Points raised: As per rule Shri Ram Chandra Hansdah, MP has not attended any session of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for more than six months liable for dismissal with other penalty. Whether such order has been issued to him please give details. If not provide the reason for the same.
Reply: Article 101(4) of the Constitution of India provides that "If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant." Shri Rama Chandra Hansdah, MP attended the sittings of the House on 20.03.2015 i.e on the 55th day of his continuous absence from the sittings of the House. Shri Rama Chandra Hansdah, MP has also submitted an application for leave of absence from the sittings of the House w.e.f. 24.11.2014 to 23.12.2014 and 23.02.2015 to 19.03.2015 on the ground - under judicial custody which is under the consideration of the Committee on Absence of Members from the sittings of the House.

The Information sought is not dealt by the Branch concerned of the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

The Bill was referred to the Departmentally related Standing Committee on Finance for examination and report. The Committee presented its report to Lok Sabha on 21 March, 2012. The Bill is presently pending in Lok Sabha.

title: RTI on Parliament renovation cost, catering expenses and security expenditure

What is the expenditure on the breakfast, lunch and dinner for all the Members of Parliament
What is the cost of running or functioning of Parliament for a single day

title: RTI on Lok Sabha sittings, Bills introduced/passed, and canteen subsidy
department: Lok Sabha Secretariat - Information Cell (RTI Cell)
subject: RTI application seeking data on number of Lok Sabha sittings, Bills laid/passed/rejected, MP allowances, expenditure on House proceedings, and canteen subsidy.
questions: How many sittings of the House take place from 1st January to 31st December?
How many sittings of the House took place in 2014 from 1st January to 31st December?
How many Bills were laid before the House in each year i.e. 2012, 2013 and 2014?
How many Bills were passed by the House in the same year in which they were introduced, in these three years?
How many Bills were rejected by the House in the same year in which they were introduced, in these three years?
What are the expenses incurred for the proceedings of the House for one day or for one sitting?
Details of Daily Expenses or any other privileges, given to each Member of the house per sitting.
Out of which funds and by which authority expenses incurred for the proceedings of the House are borne?
Out of which funds and by which authority the amount given to MPs are borne?
Out of which funds the canteen of Parliament is subsidized?
response_summary: The Secretariat provided figures for Bills introduced and passed by Lok Sabha during 2012-2014, referred the applicant to the Lok Sabha website for total sittings, explained that House proceeding expenditure is spread across multiple agencies with no single dedicated budget head, listed the Acts/Rules governing MP allowances, and stated the canteen subsidy is paid to Northern Railway from a specific budget head.

title: RTI on Leave Granted to MP Shri A. Raja Under Article 101(4)
subject: RTI seeking records of leave applications and Committee proceedings relating to the absence of Shri A. Raja, MP, from sittings of the House under Article 101(4) of the Constitution.
questions: Information regarding the leave applications, file noting, and minutes of meetings of the Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House relating to the absence of Shri A. Raja, MP, under Article 101(4) of the Constitution of India.
response_summary: Citing Article 101(4) of the Constitution, the Secretariat stated that Shri A. Raja, MP, applied for leave on four occasions, all of which were granted by the House on the recommendation of the Committee on Absence of Members, in its 4th, 5th and 6th Reports (available on the Lok Sabha website); copies of related records (29 pages) were offered on payment of Rs.58 as fee. The second query was held to be a request to elicit an answer rather than existing information, which the RTI Act does not obligate the authority to provide.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: 
 [Applicant] 
Application dated : 22.09.2013 
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No.1(1285)/IC/13  
dated 18.10.2013 
 
Sl. No. of  
original 
application 
Reply 
1. 
Article 101(4) of the Constitution of India provides as follows :- 
 
“If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without 
permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may 
declare his seat vacant : 
 
Provided that in computing the said period of sixty days no account shall be 
taken of any period during which the House is prorogued or is adjourned for 
more than four consecutive days.” 
 
Shri A. Raja, MP has applied for leave on four occasions. The leave applications 
were considered by the Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of 
the House. House granted leave to Shri A. Raja, MP on all the four occasions on 
the recommendation by the Committee in its 4th, 5th and 6th Reports.  
 
Copies of the file noting, the leave application and the minutes of the meetings 
held relating to the absence of Shri A. Raja, MP from the sittings of the House 
runs into 29 pages and is ready for dispatch. * 
 
The Reports of the Committee  are uploaded on the Lok Sabha website 
www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Committees > Other Parliamentary 
Standing Committees > Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House > 
Reports Presented > Fourth, Fifth & Sixth Reports. Applicant can peruse the 
information from the website.  
 
2. 
Applicant is not seeking information but is trying to elicit the answer to a query.  
The RTI Act do not cast upon the obligation on the Public Authority to answer 
the queries, in which an applicant attempt to elicit answer to his queries. 
 
                                 
                                 
 You may, if you desire deposit Rs.58/- (@ Rs.2/-per page) as information fee for the same to 
be supplied to you. The information fee is required to be paid by way of cash at “Reception of 
Parliament Library Building, Lok Sabha Secretariat” against proper receipt or sent through 
money order or demand draft or bankers cheque or postal order payable to ‘Drawing and 
Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha’, in terms of Lok Sabha Secretariat Right to Information 
(Regulation of Fees & Cost) Rules 2005, and the amendment Rules, 2007. You are also 
informed that Demand Draft/Bankers Cheque and IPO in favour of Accounts Officer, Lok 
Sabha is also accepted in this Secretariat. The information will be sent to you on receipt of 
the aforesaid information fee.

title: RTI on Directors and Supervisors Posts in Lok Sabha Reporters Service
subject: RTI seeking details of the Director posts and English/Hindi Supervisor arrangements in the Verbatim Reporting Service of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
questions: The date since when two posts of Directors have been created in Reporters Service? Please provide date-wise and name-wise details of the officers who have held the post of Directors in the Service since the creation of these posts.

Details of the period when Directors have assumed the responsibilities of Supervisors and when the posts of English and Hindi Supervisors had been vacant. If the Administration has issued any instructions regarding the number of Hindi and English Supervisors required to be posted to assist the Directors. Please provide a copy of that order.

Concerned division of this Secretariat i.e. Table Office do not maintain record of 
percentage utilization of parliamentary days. However, to calculate the percentage 
utilization of parliamentary days, the applicant may be provided the following 
information:-  
Normally, the sitting of the House commences at 11.00 hours and concludes at 18.00 
hours with a lunch break for one hour from 13.00 hours to 14.00 hours.  Date wise 
timings of sitting of the House during the last three financial years is available on the 
Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in >‘Business’ > ‘Bulletin-I’ > 'Archive'.  
 
Number of days of sittings and number of hours utilized for transaction of business 
during the last three financial years is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz.

therefore be advised to access information from the said website link. Since Resume 
of Work during the 14th Session of 15th Lok Sabha is under process, the applicant 
may be informed that there were 21 sittings of the House and 72 hours and 11 
minutes were utilized for transaction of business.

Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on 
the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. 
 
As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register 
is maintained for members (except Hon’ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker 
and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended 
the sitting of the House on a particular day.  Details of signing/not 
signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the 
sessions of 14th to 16th Lok Sabhas are available on the website of the 
Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-
Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance - All Members 
respectively. 
 
The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member 
attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign 
the Attendance Register for that day. 
 
The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the 
desired information. 
 
The attendance details of members prior to Fourteenth Lok Sabha have 
not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website.  The information is 
available in the records of the Branch and is voluminous. The applicant 
may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally 
peruse the records available in the Branch.

against them

sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are 
charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in 
the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring 
the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query 
appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election 
Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application 
may be forwarded to such public authorities under Section 6(3) of RTI 
Act, 2005.

title: Language used for Lok Sabha proceedings and debates
subject: The RTI raised concerns about the official language of India and the language used for conducting Lok Sabha proceedings, debates, and telecast, alleging violation of citizens' rights due to exclusive use of English.
questions: Official language of India.
Information regarding the language through which the proceedings and debates in Lok Sabha are conducted, given the applicant's claim that only English is used by Members and the Speaker.

It is a matter of violation of rights of 70% people of the country enshrined in Constitution. Please specify the time frame by which a restriction would be imposed on it; telecast of proceedings should be ensured in the official language of the country.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that Lok Sabha proceedings are conducted in Hindi or English as per Article 120 of the Constitution (subject to Article 348), with Members permitted to address the House in their mother tongue with the Speaker's permission, and that Lok Sabha Television telecasts proceedings live in the floor language without editing; two of the three points were transferred to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated 28.08.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1257)/IC/13 dated 22.10.2013

1. Official language of India.
Reply: Already transferred to M/o Home Affairs vide M/o Information & Broadcasting letter no. 1/3/2013-IFC dated 4.9.13.

2. Information regarding the language through which the proceedings and debates in Lok Sabha are conducted etc.
Reply: The applicant has stated that the proceedings and debates of Lok Sabha are conducted only through English language and the same language is also used by the Speaker to make/give observations and rulings in the House. In this regard, it is stated that the proceedings and debates in the House are made through the languages as per the provision under article 120 of the Constitution of India. As per article 120 of the Constitution of India, the business of the House shall be transacted either in Hindi or in English subject to the provisions under article 348. However, members who cannot express themselves in either of the two languages can, with the permission of Speaker, address the House in any of the languages in their mother tongue. Accordingly, the Members of Lok Sabha participate in the proceedings and debates in the House through the specified languages they feel comfortable. As regards the query of the applicant that the observations/rulings of Speaker are also made/given only through English language, it may be stated that there are many instances when the Speaker has made/given observations and rulings in Hindi, though he/she is free to use the language as per the provision under article 120 of the Constitution of India to make observations or to give rulings in the House. Lok Sabha Television only telecast the proceedings of the House (Lok Sabha) live without editing and the Channel telecast the same in floor language i.e. it follows the language of the House. To simplify it, the debates in English are telecast in English, debates in Hindi are telecast in Hindi and the debates in other languages also are telecast in the same languages without any editing.

3. It is a matter of violation of rights of 70% people of the country enshrined in Constitution. Please specify the time frame by which a restriction would be imposed on it. It should be stopped immediately and telecast of the proceedings should be ensured in the official language of the country so as to make it comprehensible for the common man.
Reply: Already transferred to M/o Home Affairs vide M/o Information & Broadcasting letter no. 1/3/2013-IFC dated 4.9.13.

As per article 120, the business of the House shall be transacted either in Hindi or in English subject to the provisions under article 348. However, members who cannot express themselves in either of the two languages can, with the permission of Speaker, address the House in any of the languages in their mother tongue... Lok Sabha Television only telecasts the proceedings of the House live without editing and the Channel telecasts the same in floor language i.e. it follows the language of the House.

title: RTI on Lok Sabha sitting hours, attendance rules and MP foreign delegation expenses
subject: The applicant sought information on Lok Sabha's working hours, Attendance Register rules, Members' Questions, foreign delegation visits of MPs with expenditure, and MP salary/allowances entitlements.
questions: Requisite information regarding total working hours of Lok Sabha during 2012 and 2013.
Rules regarding signing of the Attendance Register by Members for daily allowance during sittings of the House.
Whether there is a rule for late coming / a fixed time by which a Member must sign the Attendance Register.
Details of Questions raised/asked by Members of Lok Sabha alongwith the replies thereto.
[Continuation of query on Questions raised/asked by Members of Lok Sabha.]
[A further point on which the reply states 'Such information is not maintained.']

Statement giving details of Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) who were part of Indian Parliamentary Delegations visiting abroad under bilateral exchange and for Conferences/Meetings during the last three years, with total expenditure incurred.
Records/entitlement of Salary, Allowances and other facilities to Members of Parliament.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated Lok Sabha sat for 73 hours 11 minutes during the 14th Session of the 15th Lok Sabha; explained Attendance Register signing rules; noted Members' Questions are available online; provided detailed statements (with names, dates, destinations and expenditure) of MPs' foreign delegation visits over the last three/four years compiled by the Conference Branch and the Inter-Parliamentary Union Cell; and enclosed a pamphlet on MP salary and allowances entitlements.

title: RTI on MP salary, suspension and reinstatement rules for MPs facing charges
subject: The applicant asked whether MPs draw salary, whether MPs charged with serious crimes like murder can be suspended, and the procedure for reinstatement pending trial.
questions: Whether a MP drawing salary
Suspension of MP charged with murder etc. and allowances to suspended MP
Salary to MP involved in serious offences etc.
Procedure for reinstatement to their job during pendency of trial
response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that an MP is not a Government servant and draws salary/allowances under the Salaries, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954; there is no provision in law for suspending an MP on criminal charges, so the related questions on reinstatement did not arise.

title: RTI on motor garages and servant quarters in North Avenue colony
department: Directorate of Estates (MSA/Estate wing), Lok Sabha Secretariat
area: North Avenue residential colony, New Delhi
subject: RTI seeking details of Motor Garages and out houses/servant's quarters attached to Type-5/5A/6/6A quarters in North Avenue residential colony and their allotment rules.
questions: How many Type 5, Type 5A, Type-6, Type 6 A or any other type quarters which are eligible for Motor Garages and out houses/servant's quarters, under various pools, are there in North Avenue residential colony, New Delhi.
How many Motor Garages and out houses/servant's quarters are there in the above colony under various pools.

Are these motor Garages and out Houses/servant's quarters attached with the Type V houses to be taken over by the Allottee of the house immediately on occupying the house, by virtue of being the occupant of a Type V house or are they allotted separately.
If not, then what are the rules regarding allotment of the Garages and out houses/servant's quarters.
If the Garages and out houses/servant's quarters are allotted separately then is there any priority list maintained.

If a priority list is maintained, kindly provide a copy of current priority list, preferably upto 31st January, 2017 under the provisions of RTI Act and also inform the criteria of maintaining the priority.
Who is eligible to apply for these Garages and out houses/servant's quarters.
What is the period of occupancy of these Garages and out houses/servant's quarters as per the rules, if any.
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed that all quarters/flats under the Lok Sabha MPs Pool are eligible for motor garage and servant quarters subject to availability, gave the count as 129 servant quarter units and 58 motor garage units in North Avenue under the Lok Sabha MP Pool, clarified that these are allotted separately (not automatically with the Type V house) at the discretion of the Chairperson, House Committee, that no priority list is maintained, that all sitting MPs allotted residential accommodation are eligible, and that occupancy lasts the entire period as Member of Lok Sabha.

response_summary: The Committee gave the total number of meetings held across Lok Sabhas (210), declined to supply detailed attendance sheets, minutes, and expert details citing disproportionate diversion of resources under Section 7(9) of the RTI Act (offering inspection instead), and provided details of 28 study visits, their expenditure, and 62 Reports presented.

title: Whether specific financial Acts were passed as Money Bills
subject: The applicant sought to know whether specified Acts (FERA, FEMA, PMLA and their amendments) were introduced and passed as 'Money Bills' under Articles 109 and 110 of the Constitution, and details of any other amending Acts.
questions: I would like to know whether or not the Acts mentioned below were introduced in Lok Sabha as "Money Bill" under article 109 and article 110 of the Constitution: The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973; The Foreign Exchange Regulation (Amendment) Act, 1993; The Finance Act, 1995; The Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999; The Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002; The Prevention of Money-Laundering (Amendment) Act, 2005; The Prevention of Money-Laundering (Amendment) Act, 2009; The Prevention of Money-Laundering (Amendment) Act, 2012.

If there are any other acts which have amended the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1973 or the Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 or the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002 (which are not in the table above), kindly give the same details regarding such Acts too.
response_summary: Lok Sabha Secretariat provided a table indicating that only the Finance Act, 1995 was passed as a Money Bill among the listed Acts (the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1973 and its 1993 amendment, FEMA 1999, PMLA 2002 and its 2005/2009/2012 amendments were not), and stated that the Legislative Branch-I does not maintain a list of amendments to any particular law, asking the applicant to specify Bill titles for further information.

response_full_text: A new system of assessment of work and conduct of Government employees has been introduced in the Government of India with the revised nomenclature, "Annual Performance Assessment Report (APAR)" in place of "Annual Confidential Report". In the new system, the duly written APAR is to be communicated to the officer reported upon. However, the system of writing of ACRs is still being followed in this Secretariat and therefore, only the adverse remarks recorded in the ACR are to be communicated to the officer reported upon in the light of the relevant instructions on the subject. Further, as per Instructional Order No.1326 dated 1st November, 2011 issued by this Secretariat, where the ACR contained below bench mark grading, a copy of the ACR is provided to the officer reported upon for making representation within 15 days. It may also be submitted that the Annual Confidential Report, as its name suggests, is a confidential document and it contains information about the character, capability and other attributes of the officer reported upon and the entries made therein are based on trust and confidence between the officers involved in initiating and reviewing the CRs. Therefore, the disclosure of such documents may harm interpersonal relationships in the Secretariat where the system of writing up of ACRs is still in existence. However, disclosure of adverse remarks is permissible in the relevant instructions taking into account the principle of natural justice and, therefore, the adverse remarks and the below bench mark grading recorded in the ACR are invariably being communicated to the officer concerned in order to provide him an opportunity for making any representation, keeping in view instructions issued by the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions (DoPT) O.M. No.10/20/2006-IR dated 21st September, 2007 and the Lok Sabha Secretariat. In light of these facts, it has been decided with the approval of the Competent Authority that the copies of ACRs, as desired by the applicant, are not being provided to him.

title: Provision of computer equipment to Members of Lok Sabha
subject: The applicant sought information about whether computer equipment is provided free of cost to Members of Parliament and related purchase details.
questions: Details regarding provision of computer equipment (laptop, desktop, printer, e-reader devices etc.) to Members of Lok Sabha, whether provided free of cost, and related purchase/entitlement details (points 1-4 of the original application; exact verbatim question text not available in the extracted document).
response_summary: Lok Sabha Secretariat clarified that computer equipment is not provided free of cost to MPs; instead Members are entitled to purchase such equipment within a monetary limit of Rs. 2 lakhs under the Provision of Computer Equipment (Members of Lok Sabha) Rules, 2009, with a depreciated-cost deposit required after ceasing to be a Member. As of the reply, 503 Members of the current Lok Sabha had purchased computer equipment worth approximately Rs. 9 crore.

questions: अनुसूचित जातियों तथा अनुसूचित जनजातियों के कल्याण संबंधी संसदीय समिति द्वारा सरकारी कर्मचारियों के सेवा संबंधी मामलों से संबंधित अभ्यावेदनों पर विचार करने की प्रक्रिया एवं संबंधित जानकारी।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि समिति की पद्धति और प्रक्रिया के अनुसार सरकारी कर्मचारियों के सेवा संबंधी मामलों से संबंधित अभ्यावेदनों पर समिति द्वारा विचार नहीं किया जाता, राष्ट्रपति शीर्ष पर होने वाला एक निर्धारित अपीलीय वरीयताक्रम है, तथा एक प्राप्त अभ्यावेदन को उचित कार्यवाही हेतु उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार को भेज दिया गया है।

title: लोक सभा सचिवालय में रद्दी कागज उठाने की संविदा दरों की जानकारी
subject: आरटीआई आवेदन में लोक सभा सचिवालय से रद्दी कागज उठाने की संविदा (2017), दरों में अंतर, निविदा प्रक्रिया और कार्टलाइज़ेशन रोकने की नीति के बारे में जानकारी मांगी गई।
questions: वर्तमान में संविदा किसे प्रदान की गई है और किन दरों पर, दिनांक 1.1.2017 से 31.12.2017 तक एक वर्ष के लिए संविदा आधार पर लोक सभा सचिवालय से रद्दी कागज उठाने का दायित्व किसे दिया गया है।
वर्ष 2017 और वर्ष 2016 की संविदा दरों में क्या अंतर है।
वर्ष 2017 के लिए आमंत्रित की गई निविदा में कितने पक्षकारों ने अपनी दरें प्रस्तुत कीं, उनके नाम और दरों का ब्यौरा दें।
सचिवालय द्वारा आमंत्रित निविदा में कार्टलाइज़ेशन को रोकने के लिए क्या कदम उठाए गए। कृपया इस संबंध में अपनाई जाने वाली नीति का विस्तृत ब्यौरा दें।
कार्टलाइज़ेशन को रोकने के लिए सचिवालय द्वारा क्या नीति अपनाई गई है।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि रद्दी कागज उठाने की संविदा मै. एम.वाई.पेपर मर्चेंट प्रा.लि. को दी गई है, वर्ष 2016 और 2017 की दरों में अंतर बताया गया, निविदा में शामिल 6 फर्मों के नाम व दरें दी गईं, तथा कार्टलाइज़ेशन रोकने हेतु खुली मोहरबंद निविदा आमंत्रित करने की नीति बताई गई।

title: Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions 7th Report implementation status
subject: RTI seeking copies of correspondence and statistics on implementation of the 7th report of the Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions, and related action-taken reports.
questions: Supply clear photocopy of all letters possibly sent to the different ministries, department and public authorities in the past from the Secretariat of Lok Sabha, issued since submission of 7th report of the Lok Sabha Committee on Petition under 10th Lok Sabha, presented on 13th May 1993 for implementation and practical action on the said 7th report and official responses or action taken report etc.
How many report of the Lok Sabha Committee on Petitions have been submitted so far in the past etc.

How many action taken report or response with the name of the report, furnished on the Lok Sabha Committee on Petition, accordingly by the different ministries, departments, public authorities of central govt. etc.

How many action taken report or response with name of the report have been practically implemented, furnished on the Lok Sabha Committee on petition, accordingly by the different ministries, departments, etc.

How many action taken report or responses with name of the report have been challenged in the court? Which were furnished on the Lok Sabha Committee on Petition, accordingly by the different ministries, departments, public authorities of central/state govt etc.
response_summary: The reply stated that records nearly 22 years old relating to the 7th report could not be traced; information on reports since the 13th Lok Sabha (2000 onwards) is available on the Lok Sabha website; and questions on implementation and court challenges were held to be outside the definition of 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act since Committee reports have only persuasive value.

If answer of Question No. 1 is yes, then 3.1 Has Ministry of Health conducted any testing (chemical/biological) of Coca-Cola and or Pepsi. 3.2 What are the results of such analysis 3.3 which dangerous/hazardous substances are found in Coca Cola and/or Pepsi during such analysis other than "phosphoric acid"?

Do Pepsi and/or coca cola have any nutritional value?

Does coca-cola contain "cocaine"
Does Pepsi and /or coca cola contain: phosphoric acid? What is the origin of this Phosphoric acid in coca cola: Biological (Natural origin) or synthetic origin
Is synthetic phosphoric acid added in coca-cola and/or Pepsi dangerous to health

Does added phosphoric acid induce health hazard? (Reference: In MSDS of Phosphoric acid, the health rating: 3 – Short exposure could cause serious temporary or moderate residual injury. Can Ministry of Health permit such dangerous chemical as food additive? If yes, on what grounds?

If answer of question No. 12 is yes and answer of Q.No. 13 is No, and if Pepsi and/coca cola is banned for sell in Parliament, what attempts Ministry of Health undertakes to prohibit coca-cola and/or Pepsi in territory of India of to prohibit the advertisement of coca-cola and/or Pepsi
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed that soft drinks (Pepsi/Coca-Cola) are still not supplied/sold in catering units of Parliament House Complex, having been banned vide order dated 6.8.2003. All other questions relating to chemical composition, health hazards, and Ministry of Health's regulatory role were stated to not come under the purview of this Secretariat.

title: Khadi Mark Regulations 2013 laying before Lok Sabha details
subject: RTI seeking information on whether and when the Khadi Mark Regulations, 2013 were laid before Lok Sabha and any subsequent changes.
questions: If the Khadi Mark Regulations, 2013 under the Khadi and Village Industries Commission Act, 1956 have ever been laid before the Lok Sabha.
If yes, when was it laid
How many total number of days was it laid before the Lok Sabha, and
Changes that were proposed by the Lok Sabha to the Khadi Mark Regulations, 2013, if any.
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed the Khadi Mark Regulations, 2013 were laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on 5th February 2014 for a period of 11 days, and since the prescribed 30-day period was not completed due to dissolution of the 15th Lok Sabha, the question of proposed changes does not arise.

title: Status and process regarding Real Estate Regulation Bill and petitions
subject: RTI seeking status of the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Bill, 2013, details of related committees, and the process for public petitions to Lok Sabha and the Speaker.
questions: Status of Real Estate Bill.
Is there any committee which is looking after the real estate bill if yes please give email address/ address/ mobile number/ landline number of all the members of the committee?
When will Real Estate Bill be placed in Lok Sabha.
If we want to give our views to the real estate committee on the real estate bill how can we give our views?
If we want to meet the real estate committee what is the process for doing the same.
Who all are member of Committee on Petitions please give email/address/phone number and mobile number of the members of the Committee.
If a member of public want to give a Petition to Lok Sabha what is the process, please give details.
What is the process to take appointment with Speaker of Lok Sabha
How can one give a petition to Lok Sabha Speaker
If one wants to meet in person the Committee on Petition or dispose before them what is the process for the same.
What all Bill relating to Real Estate are pending in Lok Sabha.
response_summary: The reply states that the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Bill, 2013 was introduced in Rajya Sabha, examined by the Standing Committee on Urban Development, and is pending in Rajya Sabha; matters relating to the Rajya Sabha committee were transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat. Information on Committee on Petitions composition, petition procedure, and Speaker appointment process was provided with references to the Lok Sabha website and Rules of Procedure.

title: MP daily allowance and session disruption loss information
subject: RTI seeking information on daily allowance of MPs, salary deduction for non-attendance/adjournments, and losses incurred due to disruptions in Parliament sessions.
questions: Information regarding daily allowance paid to Members of Parliament and whether salary is deducted due to non-attendance and adjournments, and information regarding loss of money due to adjournments and disruptions in a session of Parliament.
response_summary: The reply explains that MPs receive Rs. 2000 daily allowance when they sign the attendance register during session, there is no provision for salary deduction due to non-attendance/adjournments, and there is no mechanism to calculate losses due to disruptions as such information is spread across multiple agencies and not maintained by this Secretariat.

Point No.
Reply
1.
As regards daily allowance, it is submitted that as per the Salary, Allowances
of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 and rules made thereunder, at present,
during session, the daily allowance @ Rs. 2000/- (Rs. Two Thousand Only)
is paid to the MP when he/she signs the register maintained for the purpose.
Further, there is no provision for deduction of salary due to non-attendance
and adjournments. 
Moreover, the information regarding loss of money due to adjournments and
disruptions in a session of Parliament is maintained by multiple agencies
involving several ministries/departments under various heads namely, Lok
Sabha Secretariat, Delhi Police, Special Protection Group, Home Ministry,
Delhi Jal Board, NDMC, DTC, CPWD, M/o Parliamentary Affairs and other
ministries concerned. Moreover, there is no mechanism to calculate the
losses incurred for sessions by the abovementioned public authorities.
Further, there is no practice of maintaining such information in this
Secretariat
response_full_text: As regards daily allowance, it is submitted that as per the Salary, Allowances of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 and rules made thereunder, at present, during session, the daily allowance @ Rs. 2000/- (Rs. Two Thousand Only) is paid to the MP when he/she signs the register maintained for the purpose. Further, there is no provision for deduction of salary due to non-attendance and adjournments. Moreover, the information regarding loss of money due to adjournments and disruptions in a session of Parliament is maintained by multiple agencies involving several ministries/departments under various heads namely, Lok Sabha Secretariat, Delhi Police, Special Protection Group, Home Ministry, Delhi Jal Board, NDMC, DTC, CPWD, M/o Parliamentary Affairs and other ministries concerned. Moreover, there is no mechanism to calculate the losses incurred for sessions by the abovementioned public authorities. Further, there is no practice of maintaining such information in this Secretariat.

Q: Provide the copies of file noting pertaining to the creation of 112 post(s) vide Order No. PDA 1353/2017 dated 03.02.2017

A: The catering facilities in Parliament House Complex is being provided by the Northern Railway Catering to Members, officers, Staff of the Secretariat and allied and security agencies etc. The Expenditure incurred on running the catering units in Parliament House Complex is borne by the Lok Sabha Secretariat and Rajya Sabha Secretariat in the ratio of 2:1. A: The subsidy include the breakfast and other items as per approved menu and rates.

response_full_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: Nil
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(219)/IC/15 Dated 6.04.2015

Q: Is a Minister or an MP entitled to have a guest accommodation allotted in addition to the accommodation allotted to him. If so provide details of the order/notification/notes of the same.
A: Ministers are not entitled for guest accommodation from Lok Sabha MPs Pool. The guest accommodation may be allotted to an MP, if available, for a period of three months initially on payment of market rent. Once allotment of regular accommodation to the MPs is completed and the houses are occupied by them, the request pending for allotment of guest accommodation would be considered by the House Committee.

Q: Has there been any revision in the guest accommodation policy after May 2014? If so, please provide detailed copy order/notification of the same.
A: The matter is under consideration of the House Committee.

Q: How many Ministers and MPs are currently occupying the guest accommodation? Details of the names of MPs and the guests occupying the houses. Also provide the duration of the allotment.
A: The House Committee, Lok Sabha does not make allotment of accommodation to Ministers. Generally, guest accommodation is allotted for three months. The guest accommodation to a few MPs has been allotted. The compilation of guest accommodation would be done after the regular allotments are completed and the units becoming available would be considered for allotment as guest accommodation.

Q: What are the rentals admissible to be paid by these allottees.
A: This matter pertains to the Directorate of Estates, Ministry of Urban Development. Copy of the application is being forwarded to them for necessary action.

Q: How many homes with the Secretariat are admissible for providing guest accommodations. Details of house may please be provided.
A: No specific accommodations are earmarked for allotment as guest accommodations. Allotment is made subject to the availability of flats.

Q: Has any eviction notice been sent to the Members or their guests for vacating the guest accommodation. Please provide the list of members who have been serviced with eviction notice.
A: No such eviction notices were issued to Members of 16th Lok Sabha, so far.

The applicant, vide his email dated 20.2.2015, referred to the Calcutta High Court Order in W.P. No. 3985(W) of 2014 and stated that the court has been pleased to record that the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2015 is under challenge. He further stated that the notification in question is currently pending in Writ Petition W.P. 5371(W) of 2015 before the Hon'ble Calcutta High Court and hence any Bill going to be issued by ordinance may please be adjourned sine die till the outcome of the Writ Petition. He also attached a copy of the Order dated 6.2.2015 of the Hon'ble Calcutta High Court in W.P. 3985(W) of 2014.
2. It may be seen from the Orders of the Hon'ble High Court of Calcutta that the writ petition filed before the court by the applicant and another has been dismissed by that High Court on the ground that a writ petition challenging the Notification issued by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways permitting plying of e-rickshaws is pending before the Apex Court. The Order of the Court nowhere restricts the Parliament from further proceeding with the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2014.
3. In the above context, it is submitted that a Bill, namely the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2014, seeking to regulate the operation and licensing of e-rickshaws and e-carts and to bring them under the ambit of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, was introduced in Lok Sabha on 5.2.2014. The Bill was passed by Lok Sabha on 8.2.2014 and it is presently pending in Rajya Sabha. In the meantime, an Ordinance, namely the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015, was promulgated by the President on 7.3.2015. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has tabled a notice for introduction of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2015 to replace the above Ordinance. It is understood that the Government will withdraw the Bill pending in Rajya Sabha and introduce a fresh Bill namely, the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2015 in Lok Sabha.
4. As regards the contention of the applicant that the Bill should not be taken up by the House until the outcome of the Writ Petition, attention is invited to Practice and Procedure of Parliament by Kaul and Shakdher (page 24 - Discussion on sub judice matters), which inter alia states that: 'The rule of sub judice cannot stand in the way of legislation. Where a legislation has to be brought, the law-making has to be done, the rule of sub judice does not apply. If the rule of sub judice were to be made applicable to legislation, it would not only make Legislatures subordinate to the courts in that matter but would make enactments impossible because numerous cases concerning a large number of statutes await adjudication at all times in one court or the other. Parliament's main function to make laws will thus come to a standstill. This is neither sanctioned by the Constitution nor justified on merits. Legislatures are supreme and sovereign in the matter of making laws and there is no bar on their working in the field of legislation. The lawmaking power of Parliament is unfettered with regard to legislation even when the subject matter of the legislation is sub judice. Whatever be the case and the merits of the case, Parliament can make any law. A Bill seeking to replace an Ordinance can be discussed in the House notwithstanding the fact that the Ordinance has been challenged in a court of law and the court has issued rule nisi to the Government.'
5. It may further be submitted that in so far as it relates to legislating on sub judice matters, the provisions of the Constitution and the rules governing legislative procedure in Lok Sabha do not put any restriction on the legislative powers of Parliament. Therefore, the contention of the applicant is not valid.
6. In view of the aforesaid position, no action is called for on our part and the PUC may be filed.
response_full_text: The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Bill, 2014 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 5.2.2014, passed by Lok Sabha on 8.2.2014, and transmitted to Rajya Sabha where it is pending. No order regarding admissibility of the Bill has been given by the Hon'ble Speaker. The applicant's contention that the Bill/Ordinance proceedings should be adjourned pending a Writ Petition before the Calcutta High Court was examined and not found valid, since the rule of sub judice cannot stand in the way of legislation and Parliament's lawmaking power is unfettered even when the subject matter is sub judice. The query on Rule 73 was found academic in nature and outside the meaning of 'information' under the RTI Act, 2005, since Rule 73 relates to Resolutions and not Legislation.

Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No.1(207)/IC/15 dated 26.03.2015
Point No.1: As to when the Sub-Rule (1) of Rule 50 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, substituted as per G.S.R.221(E) dated 28.3.2001 as amended by S.O.938(E) dated 24.9.2001; S.O.499(E) dated 9.5.2002 and S.O.59(E) dated 21.1.2003 was placed before the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha along with details, if any. -- Reply: It may be stated that usually sub-rules are not received for laying on the Table of the House. Hence, the date of laying of the above sub-rule could not be traced unless the applicant provides S.O. and G.S.R. number of the notification vide which sub-rule (1) of Rule 50 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 was published in the Gazette of India. The S.O. and G.S.R. numbers which were pointed out by the applicant relate to the substitution/amendment of the Rule 50 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989. The applicant is requested to provide the specific G.S.R./S.O. number of the notification vide which sub-rule (1) of Rule 50 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 was published in the Gazette of India so that the date of laying can be traced, if laid. For information pertaining to Rajya Sabha Secretariat and the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, the application has been transferred to them on 23.02.2015 and 25.03.2015 respectively under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to him.
Point No.2: When the aforesaid Rule has been agreed by the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha along with details. -- Reply: In this regard the applicant may be informed that sub-section(4) of section 212 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides that every rule made by the Central Government under this Act shall be laid as soon as may be after it is made before each House of Parliament while it is in Session for a total period of thirty days which may be comprised in one Session or in two or more successive Sessions and if before the expiry of the Session immediately following the Session or the successive Sessions aforesaid, both Houses agree in making any modifications in the rule/scheme/Notification or both Houses agree that the rule, scheme or Notification should not be made or the Notification should not be issued, the rule, scheme or Notification shall thereafter have effect only in such modified form or be of no effect, as the case may be. Thus rules made under the Motor Vehicles Act are not formally required to be approved by Parliament to make them applicable. If any Member wants to modify the rules, he is required to give notice to that effect. If the modification proposed by the Member is approved by both the Houses, the rule shall stand modified accordingly. The applicant may be informed that records of the Branch have been gone through and it was found that no notice of motion for modification of the said Rule had been tabled by any member. response_full_text: It may be stated that usually sub-rules are not received for laying on the Table of the House. Hence, the date of laying of the above sub-rule could not be traced unless the applicant provides S.O. and G.S.R. number of the notification vide which sub-rule (1) of Rule 50 of the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 was published in the Gazette of India. Sub-section(4) of section 212 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 provides that every rule made by the Central Government under this Act shall be laid before each House of Parliament for a total period of thirty days, and if both Houses agree on modifications, the rule stands modified accordingly. Records of the Branch show that no notice of motion for modification of the said Rule had been tabled by any member. response_full_text:
1. The information relating to the educational qualifications of all Members of 6th (present) Lok Sabha is available in their respective bio-profiles and can be accessed on the Lok Sabha website <www.loksabha.nic.in> under the heading 'Members' - 'Sitting Members' - 'Members Biographical Sketch (Alphabetical)' (Sample copy enclosed). The information can also be accessed on the same website under 'Members' - 'Sitting Members' - 'Members Search' - 'Qualification wise' (Sample copy enclosed).
2. MSA Branch deals with the Salary and Allowances of MP which is regulated by Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 and rules thereunder. This Act and Rules are available on Lok Sabha Website and can be accessed through www.loksabha.nic.in by clicking on Members slot. However, the details of Monthly Salary and allowances of members are as follows: (1) Salary Rs. 50,000 per month (2) Daily Allowances Rs.2000/- per day for each day of residence on duty. Daily allowance shall be paid only when the member signs the register maintained for the purpose. (3) Constituency allowance Rs.45000/- per month (4) Office Expense allowance Rs.45000/- per month out of which Rs. 15000/- is for meeting expenses of stationery items and postage; and upto Rs.30000/- paid by the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariats to the person(s) as may be engaged by a member for obtaining secretarial assistance, provided that one such person must be computer literate as certified by the member himself. The details of income of MPs are not maintained by the Branch. As per the Members of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets & Liabilities) Rules, 2004, Members are required to disclose only details regarding movable and immovable properties. Hence, the details of income of Members of Lok Sabha and its sources is not maintained in the Privileges & Ethics Branch.

It also explained that Exchange Orders are issued for Air India tickets on credit, and other booking methods are not tracked by the Branch.

title: लोकसभा सदस्यों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता, पेंशन एवं आपराधिक मामलों संबंधी आरटीआई
department: हू'ज हू सेल (Who's Who Cell) / सदस्य वेतन एवं भत्ता शाखा
subject: आवेदक ने लोकसभा के 543 सदस्यों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता, सजायाफ्ता संसद सदस्यों/कर्मचारियों की पेंशन पात्रता, तथा भ्रष्टाचार/आपराधिक मामलों में दोषसिद्ध सांसदों की संख्या संबंधी जानकारी मांगी।
questions: कृपया लोकसभा के 543 सदस्यों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता की जानकारी दें।
क्या सजा प्राप्त संसद सदस्य पेंशन प्राप्त करने के हकदार हैं?
क्या भ्रष्टाचार अथवा अन्य मामलों के संबंध में एक माह से लेकर आजीवन कारावास की सजा पाने वाला कोई अधिकारी या कर्मचारी पेंशन प्राप्त करने का हकदार है?

कृपया यह जानकारी दें कि ऐसे कितने संसद सदस्य (लोकसभा अथवा राज्य सभा) हैं जिनके विरुद्ध:- (क) किसी विधि न्यायालय में भ्रष्टाचार तथा आपराधिक मामले लंबित हैं और उनके राजनैतिक दल का नाम भी बताएं; (ख) भ्रष्टाचार एवं अन्य आपराधिक मामलों में किसी विधि न्यायालय द्वारा एक माह से आजीवन कारावास के लिए दंडित/दोषसिद्ध संसद सदस्यों की संख्या बताएं। ऐसे संसद सदस्यों के नाम और उन राज्यों के नाम भी बताएं जहां से ये सांसद आते हैं।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि सभी वर्तमान लोकसभा सदस्यों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता संबंधी जानकारी उनके जीवन-वृत्त में लोकसभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है। पूर्व संसद सदस्य पेंशन प्राप्त करने के हकदार हैं जो संसद सदस्य वेतन, भत्ते और पेंशन अधिनियम 1954 की धारा 8क से शासित होती है, जबकि सजा प्राप्त वर्तमान सदस्य किसी पेंशन के हकदार नहीं हैं। तीसरे बिंदु को 'प्रश्न' मानते हुए सूचना देने से इनकार किया गया। चौथे बिंदु पर बताया गया कि ऐसी कोई जानकारी शाखा में नहीं रखी जाती तथा कोई वर्तमान सदस्य किसी न्यायालय द्वारा दंडित/दोषसिद्ध नहीं है।

कारावास की कर्मचारी जा पाने वाला कोई प्राधिकारी प्रश्नों का उत्तर देने के लिए बाध्य नहीं

संसद सदस्य (लोकसभा अथवा राज्य सभा) | पड़े आपराधिक अथवा भ्रष्टाचार के मामलों से
हैं जिनके विरुद्ध :- संबंधित कोई जानकारी और अन्य संगत ब्यौरा इस
(क) किसी विधि न्यायालय में भ्रष्टाचार के | शाखा में नहीं रखा जाता |
तथा आपराधिक मामले लंबित है और
उनके राजनैतिक दल का नाम भी बताएं
(ख) wera sie अन्य आपराधिक | लोकसभा का ऐसा कोई वर्तमान सदस्य नहीं है
मामलों में किसी विधि न्यायालय द्वारा एक | जिसे किसी विधि न्यायालय द्वारा दंडित/दोषसिद्ध
माह से आजीवन कारावास के लिए दंडित/ | किया गया हो |
दोषसिद्ध संसद सदस्यों की संख्या बताएं ।
ऐसे संसद सदस्यों के नाम और उन
राज्यों के नाम भी बताएं जहां से ये
सांसद आते हैं |
response_full_text:
1. वर्तमान लोकसभा के सभी सदस्यों की शैक्षणिक योग्यता से संबंधित जानकारी उनके संबंधित जीवन वृत्त में दी गई है जिसे 'सदस्य -> वर्तमान सदस्य -> सदस्य जीवन वृत्त (वर्णानुक्रमानुसार)' शीर्षक के अंतर्गत लोकसभा की वेबसाइट <www.loksabha.nic.in> से प्राप्त किया जा सकता है। यह जानकारी 'सदस्य -> वर्तमान सदस्य -> सदस्य खोज -> योग्यता वार' शीर्षक के अंतर्गत भी उपरोक्त वेबसाइट से प्राप्त की जा सकती है।
2. संसद सदस्य कोई भी पेंशन प्राप्त करने के हकदार नहीं हैं। यद्यपि, पूर्व संसद सदस्य पेंशन प्राप्त करने के हकदार हैं और यह पेंशन, संसद सदस्य वेतन, भत्ते और पेंशन अधिनियम 1954 की धारा 8क और उसके अंतर्गत बनाए गए नियमों से शासित होती है।
3. मांगी गई जानकारी एक प्रश्न है और सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत लोक प्राधिकारी प्रश्नों का उत्तर देने के लिए बाध्य नहीं है।
4. लोकसभा के सदस्यों के विरुद्ध दर्ज और लंबित पड़े आपराधिक अथवा भ्रष्टाचार के मामलों से संबंधित कोई जानकारी और अन्य संगत ब्यौरा इस शाखा में नहीं रखा जाता। लोकसभा का ऐसा कोई वर्तमान सदस्य नहीं है जिसे किसी विधि न्यायालय द्वारा दंडित/दोषसिद्ध किया गया हो।

1. List of MPs took oath in their mother tongue
Reply: The list of members of Sixteenth Lok Sabha along with their constituency and State who took oath/made affirmation in different languages is available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the heading business-Bulletin-I-Session No.I (04.06.2014 to 11.06.2014) respectively.

2. How may MPs took oath in Sanskrit

3. First time MPs in 16th Lok Sabha
Reply: List of first time elected Members of 16th Lok Sabha (consisting of 314 members) is available on Lok Sabha website www.loksabha.nic.in under the heading 'Members' 'First Time Elected Members.' (Sample copy of first pages is enclosed) (Appendix-A).

4. Information regarding seat allotment to the MPs
Reply: According to Rule 4 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha "The members shall sit in such order as the Speaker may determine".

5. No. of audience allowed to sit in the Housed during session
Reply: 3678

6. Name of MPs who provided highest no. of passes to attend the session.
Reply: The names wise list of the Hon'ble MPs who were issued highest nos. of gallery passes during the 01st session of 16th Lok Sabha is enclosed. (Appendix – B)

7. How many nominations received for the post of Lok Sabha Speaker
Reply: Following 19 nominations were received for the post of Speaker, Lok Sabha. However, last 3 nominations were not found to be in order. (List of candidates, proposers and seconders enclosed).

7(a). How the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha are elected
Reply: Information pertaining to election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Lok Sabha is available on Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in -> 'Procedures' -> 'Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha' -> 'Election of Speaker and Deputy Speaker and nomination of Panel of Chairperson'.

8(a). Services for general public who visit parliamentary session
Reply: The procedure to watch the proceedings of the Lok Sabha for a common man is that he has to fill an application form available at CPIC/Reception Office (Lok Sabha)/official website of Lok Sabha (www.parliamentofindia.nic.in), duly signed by Hon'ble MP (Lok Sabha). The proceeding can be watched during the session period subject to availability of seats in public gallery.

8(b). Can general public avail the services at Parliament canteen
Reply: MPs and their guests, Ex-MPs, Officers & Staffs working in Parliament House Complex and visitors having valid passes to enter the Parliament House Complex can avail canteen facilities at normal rates on payment basis.

9. Menu of Parliament Canteen and their rates
Reply: The copy of food items available for sale in Parliament House Catering Units alongwith price list available are enclosed. (Appendix – C).

9(a). Who provide catering services at Parliament Canteen
Reply: Northern Railway provides catering services in Parliament House Catering Unit.

9(b). How much subsidy is provided to food items at Parliament canteen?
Reply: The details for establishment cost/subsidy claimed for the year 2012-13 is enclosed. (Appendix – D).

9(c). From where does the groceries and other food items sourced in the Parliament canteen
Reply: The Northern Railway as per their (HQ Office) guidelines procures the raw materials from Government Agencies/Cooperative Stores like Super Bazar, Kendriya Bhandar, National Co-operative Consumers Federation of India, etc. Milk products are procured from DMS/Mother Dairy. Vegetables are procured from Mother Dairy. For procurement of mutton, chicken, fish, sweets and paneer etc., the agencies are fixed by the Northern Railway (HQ Office) through tender system.

10. Youngest and Oldest MP in the 16th Lok Sabha
Reply: Branch concerned of this Secretariat is in the process of seeking detailed information (including the date of birth) from Members of 16th Lok Sabha.

11. Complete information on the Parliamentary privileges Committee
Reply: At the commencement of the House or from time to time, the Speaker shall nominate a Committee of Privileges consisting of not more than fifteen members under rule 313 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. The Committee examines, investigates and reports on any matter referred to it either by the House or the Speaker under rule 226/227. There is no constitutional provision regarding the formation of Committee of Privileges.

11(a) & 11(b). How this committee is formed / Who are the members of this Committee. How are the members of this Committee elected/appointed/nominated.
Reply: The members of the Committee of Privileges are appointed/nominated by the Speaker from amongst the members of Lok Sabha taking into consideration the claims, interests and the strength of various parties and groups in the House so that the Committee is fully representative of all political parties. The Committee of privileges has not yet been constituted.

12, 12(a) & 12(b). Consolidated fund of India / Who provides and maintains this fund / Money contributed to this fund in every union budget
Reply: Transferred to M/o Finance.

Application dated: 04.06.2014
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(890)/IC/14 dated 08.07.14

1 & 1a. When will next parliament session begin etc.
Reply: Details reg. sittings of Lok Sabha for each session is decided by the Government of India and intimated through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs keeping in view the volume of legislative and financial business which Government propose to bring in a financial year before the House.

2. Attendance of Members of Parliament of both the Houses. a) Provide the information for all the MPs of 15th Lok Sabha b) Provide the information of all the MPs in Rajya Sabha since 2009
3. How attendance of MPs attending Parliament sessions is registered
Reply: An attendance register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting; not signing the attendance register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of Fifteenth Lok Sabha are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members → attendance of member → archive – 15th Lok Sabha → members attendance total respectively. 7. Information regarding the decision about selection of MPs to raise matters in House during Zero Hour
Reply: As per present practice in Lok Sabha the notices received on the same day between 0830 hours and 0900 hrs. are balloted and only 20 matters as per their priority in the ballot are allowed to be raised during 'Zero Hour'. However, the Hon'ble Speaker can permit any member in his/her discretion to raise any issue of urgent public importance during 'Zero Hour'
response_full_text: Details regarding sittings of Lok Sabha for each session is decided by the Government of India and intimated through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. An attendance register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Leader of Opposition and Ministers); details are available on the Lok Sabha website. Longest Session – 12th Session of 1st Lok Sabha. Longest Sitting – 21 hours 16 minutes (30.8.1997). As per present practice, notices received between 0830 and 0900 hrs are balloted and only 20 matters as per priority are allowed to be raised during 'Zero Hour'; the Speaker may permit any member to raise urgent issues at his/her discretion.

subject: आवेदक ने संसद सदस्यों के विरूद्ध बैंक ऋण न चुकाने, वित्तीय अनियमितता एवं वाहन/मकान ऋण से संबंधित शिकायतों की जानकारी मांगी।
questions: क्या किसी वर्तमान संसद सदस्य, लोक सभा के विरूद्ध किसी राष्ट्रीयकृत बैंक से लिए गए बैंक ऋण का भुगतान नहीं करने से संबधित कोई शिकायत मिली है?
उन सदस्यों का ब्यौरा दें जो ऋण का भुगतान करने में असमर्थ हैं।
उन सदस्यों की सूची प्रदान करें जिन्होंने ऋण लिया है और भुगतान हेतु उनके वेतन से कटौती की जा रही है।
क्या किसी संसद सदस्य के विरूद्ध वित्तीय अनियमितताएं, बैंकों से धोखाधड़ी, इत्यादि के संबंध में कोई शिकायत प्राप्त हुई है? इसकी प्रति प्रदान करें।
क्या किसी सदस्य को मकान और वाहन खरीदने हेतु ब्याज की कम दर पर ऋण प्रदान किया जाता है? सदस्यों की सूची प्रदान करें।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि पंजाब नेशनल बैंक से एक सांसद के विरुद्ध ऋण न चुकाने की शिकायत मिली थी जिसे वित्त मंत्रालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया; सदस्य वेतन और भत्ते शाखा केवल वाहन क्रय अग्रिम प्रदान करती है, जिसकी वसूली वेतन से की जाती है; वित्तीय अनियमितता/धोखाधड़ी संबंधी कोई शिकायत प्राप्त नहीं हुई है।

क्रम सं. उठाए गए मुद्दे (संक्षेप में) / उत्तर:
1. क्या किसी वर्तमान संसद सदस्य, लोक सभा के विरूद्ध किसी राष्ट्रीयकृत बैंक से लिए गए बैंक ऋण का भुगतान नहीं करने से संबधित कोई शिकायत मिली है? -> उत्तर: रिकार्ड के अनुसार, ऋण का कथित भुगतान न करने के लिए श्रीमती कोथापल्ली गीता, संसद सदस्य के विरूद्ध उपमहाप्रबंधक, पंजाब नेशनल बैंक से एक शिकायत मिली है।
2. उन सदस्यों का ब्यौरा दें जो ऋण का भुगतान करने में असमर्थ हैं। -> उत्तर: आवेदक को सूचित करते हुए दिनांक 07.07.2017 के पत्र के माध्यम से वित्त मंत्रालय को अंतरित कर दिया गया।
3. उन सदस्यों की सूची प्रदान करें जिन्होंने ऋण लिया है और भुगतान हेतु उनके वेतन से कटौती की जा रही है। -> उत्तर: सदस्य वेतन और भत्ते शाखा द्वारा संसद सदस्य (वाहन क्रय अग्रिम) नियम, 1986 के तहत केवल वाहन अग्रिम प्रदान किया जाता है। उक्त अग्रिम की ब्याज सहित वसूली सरकारी कर्मचारियों पर लागू ऋण शर्तों के अनुसार की जाती है। इस समय श्री एस.पी.वाई.रेड्डी, संसद सदस्य के वाहन अग्रिम की वसूली उनके वेतन से की जा रही है। लोक सभा द्वारा सदस्यों को और कोई अन्य ऋण प्रदान नहीं किया जाता है।
4. क्या किसी संसद सदस्य के विरूद्ध वित्तीय अनियमितताएं, बैंकों से धोखाधड़ी, इत्यादि के संबंध में कोई शिकायत प्राप्त हुई है? इसकी प्रति प्रदान करें। -> उत्तर: संबंधित शाखा अर्थात् विशेषाधिकार और आचार शाखा में किसी संसद सदस्य द्वारा वित्तीय अनियमितताएं, बैंकों से धोखाधड़ी इत्यादि किए जाने की कोई शिकायत प्राप्त नहीं हुई है। अतः इस संबंध में कोई जानकारी उपलब्ध नहीं है।
5 और 6. क्या किसी सदस्य को मकान और वाहन खरीदने हेतु ब्याज की कम दर पर ऋण प्रदान किया जाता है? सदस्यों की सूची प्रदान करें। -> उत्तर: कृपया उपर्युक्त बिंदु सं. 3 का उत्तर देखें।

लोहार जाति के सम्बन्ध में रमा देवी (भाजपा) और राजेश रंजन यादव (पप्पू यादव) द्वारा पूछे गए प्रश्नों का उत्तर उपलब्ध कराएं।

मूल आवेदन बिंदु संक्षेप में / उत्तर:
1. लोक सभा विधेयक संख्या 194/2015, जिसमें अधिनियम सं. 48/2006 के निरसन हेतु प्रावधान हैं, (पृष्ठ सं. 11 पर) को अभी तक पारित क्यों नहीं किया गया है और 2016 में इस विधेयक की संख्या क्या है? कृपया साक्ष्य के साथ हिंदी में स्पष्ट सूचना उपलब्ध करायें। -> उत्तर: 2015 का विधेयक क्रमांक 194 अर्थात निरसन और संशोधन (चौथा) विधेयक, 2015 जिसे अन्य बातों के साथ-साथ 2006 के विधेयक संख्यांक 48 को निरसित करने के लिए लाया गया था, को लोक सभा में 27.7.2015 को पुरःस्थापित किया गया था। इस विधेयक को लोक सभा में निरसन और संशोधन (तृतीय) विधेयक, 2015 के रूप में 6.8.2015 को पारित किया गया था। इस विधेयक, लोक सभा द्वारा यथा पारित, पर राज्य सभा द्वारा विचार किया गया तथा निरसन और संशोधन विधेयक 2016 के रूप में 27.4.2016 को संशोधनों के साथ पारित किया गया। राज्य सभा द्वारा किए गए संशोधनों से लोक सभा 3.5.2016 को सहमत हुई। इस विधेयक, सभा द्वारा यथा पारित, को राष्ट्रपति द्वारा 2016 के अधिनियम संख्यांक 23 के रूप में 16.5.2016 को स्वीकृति दी गई। आवेदक लोक सभा की वेबसाइट (loksabha.nic.in) पर 'legislation' लिंक के अंतर्गत अधिक ब्यौरा प्राप्त कर सकता है।
2. लोहार जाति के सम्बन्ध में रमा देवी (भाजपा) और राजेश रंजन यादव (पप्पू यादव) द्वारा पूछे गए प्रश्नों का उत्तर उपलब्ध कराएं। -> उत्तर: श्रीमती रमा देवी, सांसद (लोक सभा) और श्री राजेश रंजन यादव, सांसद (लोक सभा) द्वारा पूछे गए प्रश्न माननीय सांसदों के होमपेज पर उपलब्ध हैं और इन्हे दिए गए लिंक के द्वारा देखा जा सकता है।
3. लोहार जाति का नाम परिवर्तन करने और इसका समर्थन करने वाले सांसदों के सम्बन्ध में जानकारी दें। -> उत्तर: आवेदक द्वारा मांगी गई जानकारी लोक सभा के वेबपेज पर उपलब्ध है और इसे दिए गए लिंक से देखा जा सकता है।

(i) How much hours of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha were destroyed, unfruitful and no works were done after general election 2014 till date. (ii) How much money has been spent by Govt. during those hours after general election till date.

1 | Provide the name of a member of either house of Parliament is with or without permission of the House absent from all meeting thereof for a period of sixty days. | Part reply relating to Lok Sabha: Article 101(4) of the Constitution provides that "if for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant." The list of those members who remain absent from the sittings of the House (Lok Sabha) for more than 15 days and applied for leave of absence have been granted leave of absence from the sittings of the House on the recommendation of the Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House during 16th Lok Sabha is available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the heading committees-Other Parliamentary Standing Committees-Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House reports presented-First to Fourth Report respectively. The applicant visit the said website and access the desired information. Application has been transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat for the information pertaining to them.
2 | Provide the name of a member of either House who has least attended meeting in a period of sixty days from 2014 till the reply of this RTI. | Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of maximum/minimum or least attendance. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 15th & 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance - All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. Application has been transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat for the information pertaining to them.

response_full_text: Part reply relating to Lok Sabha: Article 101(4) of the Constitution provides that 'if for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant.' The list of members who remained absent for more than 15 days and were granted leave is available on the Lok Sabha website under Committee on Absence of Members reports. Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain attendance on the basis of maximum/minimum or least attendance; an Attendance Register is maintained instead, details of which are available on the website. Application has been transferred to Rajya Sabha Secretariat for information pertaining to them.
