title: Queries on JPC procedure, expenses, and MP-Speaker communication in 2G case
subject: Applicant sought information on the Joint Parliamentary Committee's (JPC) decision-making procedure, applicable rules, expenditure on the 2G case JPC, and correspondence between an MP and the Speaker on the matter.
questions: Information be sent whether as per the procedure and process of JPCs, the matters could be decided by it by way of voting or else the matters are obligatory to be studied/decided by making thorough investigation leaving aside the party politics.
Copies of those rules and regulations/procedure be sent as per which the JPCs have to function for proving such matters/issues.
Information be sent highlighting the expenses which have been incurred from public money on the functioning of JPC in 2G case as a whole.

As per the enclosed news item dated 17.11.2013, Mr. Dasgupta, MP is stated to have written a letter to the Speaker of Lok Sabha on the issue in which respect copy of the letter, as has been written by the said MP to the Speaker, be sent as per the process of RTI Act.
Information be sent highlighting the action which the Speaker has taken on the letter in question together with the copies of the record on which the letter in question has been dealt with.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that JPC matters are decided by majority vote (Rule 261), pointed the applicant to the website for JPC rules, stated that 2G JPC expenditure cannot be calculated separately by head, and denied information on MP-Speaker correspondence citing breach of parliamentary privilege under Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: 30.11.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1693)/IC/13 dated 17.12.2013
1. Question raised: Information be sent whether as per the procedure and process of JPCs, the matters could be decided by it by way of voting or else the matters are obligatory to be studied/decided by making thorough investigation leaving aside the party politics.
Reply: All questions at any sitting of a Committee shall be determined by a majority of votes of members present and voting (Rule 261 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha).
2. Question raised: Copies of those rules and regulations/procedure be sent as per which the JPCs have to function for proving such matters/issues.
Reply: The same is available on the website of Lok Sabha www.loksabha.nic.in -> Procedures -> Rules of Procedure -> Parliamentary Committees.
3. Question raised: Information be sent highlighting the expenses which have been incurred from public money on the functioning of JPC in 2G case as a whole.
Reply: Expenditure incurred on the sittings of the Committee cannot be calculated by the JPC Cell as there are various Heads under which expenditure is incurred i.e., (i) Electricity used during the sittings of the Committee and JPC Cell (ii) Expenditure incurred on phone calls (iii) Expenditure incurred over use of internet (iv) Stationery (v) Other expenditure relating to Horticulture, etc. It is, therefore not feasible for JPC Cell to calculate expenditure incurred over each of the sittings of the Committee.
4. Question raised: As per the enclosed news item dated 17.11.2013, Mr. Dasgupta, MP is stated to have written a letter to the Speaker of Lok Sabha on the issue in which respect copy of the letter, as has been written by the said MP to the Speaker, be sent as per the process of RTI Act.
Reply: Furnishing any information regarding communication between MP and Speaker constitutes breach of privilege of Parliament [under Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act, 2005, these documents are exempted from disclosure to the RTI applicant].
5. Question raised: Information be sent highlighting the action which the Speaker has taken on the letter in question together with the copies of the record on which the letter in question has been dealt with.
Reply: Same as above.

rows: Information on whether JPC matters are decided by voting or investigation
All questions at any sitting of a Committee shall be determined by a majority of votes of members present and voting (Rule 261).
Copies of rules/procedure governing JPC functioning
Available on Lok Sabha website under Procedures -> Rules of Procedure -> Parliamentary Committees.
Expenses incurred on functioning of JPC in 2G case
Not feasible for JPC Cell to calculate expenditure over each sitting, as it spans multiple heads.
Copy of letter written by Mr. Dasgupta, MP, to the Speaker
Exempted under Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act, 2005 as it constitutes breach of parliamentary privilege.
Action taken by Speaker on the letter, with records
Same as above (exempted under Section 8(1)(c)).
response_tables.title: Point-wise reply

response_full_text: 1. All questions at any sitting of a Committee shall be determined by a majority of votes of members present and voting (Rule 261 of Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha). 2. The same is available on the website of Lok Sabha www.loksabha.nic.in -> Procedures -> Rules of Procedure -> Parliamentary Committees. 3. Expenditure incurred on the sittings of the Committee cannot be calculated by the JPC Cell as there are various Heads under which expenditure is incurred; it is not feasible for JPC Cell to calculate expenditure incurred over each of the sittings of the Committee. 4 & 5. Furnishing any information regarding communication between MP and Speaker constitutes breach of privilege of Parliament; under Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act, 2005, these documents are exempted from disclosure to the RTI applicant.

subject: Applicant sought details of money spent per day on Parliament sessions, security, maintenance of Parliament, availability of fellowship programmes, and the procedure for a common citizen to visit Parliament.

response_full_text: Such information is not maintained by this Secretariat. Information regarding expenses on Parliament is maintained by multiple agencies involving several Ministries under various heads. There is no separate head of account for booking expenditure on security in Parliament House Complex; expenditure is booked under 'Office Expenses' of Lok Sabha Secretariat. response_tables.title: Year-wise list of candidates with marks obtained (Limited Departmental Competitive Examination)

response_full_text: 07 (Seven) Limited Departmental Competitive Examinations for the post of Junior Clerk. The scheme of examination followed in the last held examination: Preliminary Examination - Part A General Knowledge & Current Affairs (50 marks), Part B General English (50 marks); Main Examination - Paper I Essay, Letter & Grammar (100 marks), Paper II Typing Test @ 40 w.p.m. (100 marks). Year-wise list of candidates with marks obtained provided. The following persons have been appointed on compassionate grounds since 2008: Shri Vinod Kumar, Attendant Gr-III (confirmed); Smt. Kamlesh Rani, Attendant Gr-III (confirmed); Hitesh Kumar Sanwaria, Junior Library Attendant (confirmed); Smt. Rekha, Junior Clerk; Kum. Vandana, Junior Clerk; Shri Arun Singh, Junior Clerk; Shri Dinesh Kumar, Junior Clerk; Smt. Usha Rani, Junior Clerk; Ms. Shilpa Sharma, Junior Clerk; Shri Satpal, Junior Clerk; Ms. Shashi Bala, Junior Clerk; Smt. Anju Singh, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Laxman Kumar, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Jaideep, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Vinod Kumar, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Ali Mohammad, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Amit Kumar Pachouri, Housekeeper Gr-III; Shri Thakur Das, Housekeeper Gr-III. Persons at Sl. No. 4 to 18 are yet to be confirmed. Application of Shri Ishwar Singh Negi, S/o Late Rajender Singh Negi (Housekeeper Gr-I) is pending. Govt. of India instructions on the subject are used as guiding principles; relaxation on specific counts can be given by the competent authority. A copy of the Govt. of India instructions runs into 19 pages and is ready to be supplied on payment of Rs. 38/- (@ Rs. 2/- per page) as information fee.

title: Timeline for laying PSU Annual Reports on the table of Lok Sabha
subject: RTI application seeking the timeline prescribed for laying the Annual Report (including accounts) of a PSU on the table of Lok Sabha, the consequences of missing that timeline, and the effect of the House not being in session.
questions: Is there any timeline prescribed for laying the Annual Report, including the accounts of a PSU on the table of Lok Sabha every year? If yes, what is that timeline? Please also provide the certified copy of the provisions of statute, rule, etc., under which the same has to be laid.
In case timeline is not met for some reasons what are the consequences for the PSU? And when can then the annual report be laid and with what consequences?

In case timeline is not met because the Lok Sabha was not in session for the last some days of the timeline what are the consequences for the PSU? And when can then the annual report be laid and with what consequences?
response_summary: The Secretariat cited the Committee on Papers Laid's Second Report (5th Lok Sabha) recommending that Government Company reports be laid within 9 months of the close of the accounting year, with a delay statement laid within 30 days if not met; explained that the Committee examines such delay statements and may take up the matter with the Ministry if reasons are unsatisfactory; and advised that Ministries should plan so documents are laid before the Winter Session concludes, with documents laid as soon as possible if timelines are missed.

response_full_text: The Committee, therefore, recommend that as in the case of the Reports of the Autonomous Organisations, Reports of Government Companies should also be laid within 9 months of the close of the Accounting Year. The Committee further recommend that where it is not possible for the Government to lay the Report of any Company within that period they should lay on the Table a statement explaining the reasons for not laying the Reports within 30 days from the expiry of the period of nine months and if the House is not in Session at that time, the statement should be laid on the Table within seven day of re-assembly of the House. As advised by the Committee, the Committee examine 'Delay Statement' laid on the Table of the House along-with Annual Report including Audited Accounts for a particular Year and if the Committee find that the reasons for delay furnished by the Ministry are satisfactory, the concerned Ministry may be urged to lay the Annual Report and Audited Accounts within the stipulated time period in future; if reasons are not satisfactory, the Committee may decide to take up the matter for delay with the concerned Administrative Ministry for detailed examination. Normally the Winter Session of Parliament concludes by the end of third week of December every year. Therefore, the Committee advise all the Ministries/Departments to plan in such a way that the documents received from the PSUs could be laid on the Table of the House before the conclusion of Winter Session of Parliament. If for any reason, the Annual Report and Audited Accounts could not be laid on the Table of the House within stipulated time period the documents of the said Organisation should be laid on the Table of the House as soon as possible.

Since the matter is outside the scope of a public authority under the RTI Act, it could not be transferred under Section 6(3) per DoPT instructions, and the applicant was advised to approach the concerned public authority directly.

title: Query on contempt of Parliament and delayed notification laying
subject: RTI application asking whether non-implementation of a rule laid on the table of Lok Sabha amounts to contempt of Parliament, and seeking copies of Explanatory Notes on two Department of Revenue notifications laid before Parliament.
questions: I want to know whether non-implementation of any rule framed under an Act and laid on the table of the Lok Sabha is a contempt of Parliament.
I want to know, in case it is a contempt, what are the actions that would be taken against the guilty officers.
Copy of Explanatory note laid before both the Houses by Deptt. of Revenue vide notification dt. 29 May 1989 etc.
Copy of Explanatory note laid before both the Houses by Deptt. of Revenue vide notification dt. 24 December 2001 etc.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated that 'information' under the RTI Act cannot include opinions, so the hypothetical questions on contempt of Parliament could not be answered, and that no express provision categorizes non-implementation of a rule as contempt since parliamentary privilege law is uncodified. On the Explanatory Notes, it stated the dates the notifications were laid could not be traced from Bulletin Parts I/II, and forwarded the application to the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) which had reportedly not sent the notifications for laying.

response_full_text:
It is stated that the definition of 'Information' under Section 2(f) of the Right to Information Act, 2005 cannot and does not include views/opinions of a public authority like Lok Sabha Secretariat. Therefore, no opinion can be expressed in response to queries No. 1 and 2, which are hypothetical in nature. However, it may be stated that no express provision has been laid down either in the Constitution of India or Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha stating that non-implementation of any rule framed under an Act would constitute breach of privilege or contempt of the Parliament. Further, it may be stated that since the law on parliamentary privileges has not been codified in India, it is therefore, impractical to enumerate as to which acts of commission would constitute contempt of House.
Please see reply to point no. 1.
In this regard, it may be stated that all papers including notifications/Explanatory Notes are sent to Parliament Library for permanent records after laying of the same on the Table of the House. However, it is not clear from the application whether the notifications had actually been laid on the Table of the House or not. Thus, without finding out date of laying of the notifications it would not be feasible for Parliament Library to trace and supply copies of Explanatory Notes to the applicant. Therefore, efforts were made to trace the date of laying of the notifications by going through Bulletin Part-I and SROs para published in Bulletin Part-II for the years 1989, 1990 and 2002, but the same could not be traced. It seems that the Ministry concerned i.e. Ministry of Finance (Department of revenue) had not forwarded the notifications to the Secretariat for laying on the Table of the Lok Sabha immediately after its publication as all Statutory Rules and Orders required to be laid before the House as early as possible within a period of 15 days of their publication in the Official Gazette, if the House is in session. If the House is not in session at the time of publication of such Statutory Rules and Orders, they should be laid on the Table of the House as soon as possible after the commencement of the next session but in any case within 15 days of such commencement (para 11.28 of the 'Government and Parliament'- procedure to be followed by Ministries in connection with Parliamentary work). However, the date of laying of the notification can be traced if the concerned Ministry i.e. Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) could provide the date of sending the Notification to Lok Sabha Secretariat for laying. Copy of the application has been forwarded to M/o Finance to whom approach them directly.
Please see reply to point no. 3.

title: RTI on types of majority used in Parliamentary proceedings
subject: Applicant sought a detailed explanation of the different types of majorities used in Parliament (effective, absolute, simple), and treatment of vacancies, abstentions and absentees.
questions: Detailed explanation on the different majorities used in Parliament, the effective majority, the absolute majority and simple majority as used in Parliament. The applicant has further sought information regarding the inclusion and exclusion of unfilled seats or vacancies, people abstained from voting and also absentees.
response_summary: The information sought was academic in nature requiring understanding of constitutional provisions; the concerned Branch does not compile such information on types of majority, and the applicant was advised to refer to Articles 100, 368 and other relevant articles of the Constitution.

title: List and Classification of Unparliamentary Words Explained
subject: RTI seeking information on the list of unparliamentary words/expressions and how the Speaker classifies such words.
questions: Is there any information on the list of words considered unparliamentary? If so, can the list be shared/disclosed? Even a Website URL link where the list of such words exist is also ok. What is the source of classification of such words?

Many legislators, be it MP/MLA accuse their counterparts from other political parties of using Unparliamentary words in the Parliament/Assembly. So, does the Speaker look at the list of words and decide and classify it as unparliamentary?
response_summary: Lok Sabha Secretariat confirmed it publishes Annual and Quinquennial Issues of Unparliamentary Expressions, explained pricing/availability, noted no URL exists for such a list, and clarified that the Speaker/Chairperson personally classifies unparliamentary words during debates.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: 06.11.2013
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1577)/IC/13 dated 05.12.2013

No. 1. Question raised (in brief): Is there any information on the list of words considered unparliamentary? If so, can the list be shared/disclosed? Even a Website URL link where the list of such words exist is also ok. What is the source of classification of such words?
Reply: Yes, Lok Sabha Secretariat brings out Annual and Quinquennial Issues of Unparliamentary Expressions containing words and expressions declared unparliamentary in Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, State Legislatures and some of Commonwealth Parliaments. The Annual Issue contains entries for a particular year and it is meant for departmental use only. However, Quinquennial Issue is brought out in every five years with the formation of new Lok Sabha and it is a priced publication (Rs.1700/- per copy). It is available for sale from the Sales Counter (Contact no. 011-23034726), Reception, Parliament House, New Delhi. It can also be purchased by sending a letter to Sales Section, Lok Sabha Secretariat along with a Demand Draft of Rs.1700/- (postal charges extra) drawn in favour of DDO, Lok Sabha Secretariat. Besides, a copy of this publication is also available in the libraries of State Legislative Assemblies for consultation and reference purpose. Presently, there is no URL link where such a list exists. These words are sourced from the Reporting Sections of the State Assemblies, Rajya Sabha Secretariat and Lok Sabha Secretariat as well as from 'The Table' magazine brought out by the Society of the Clerks at-the-Table in Commonwealth Parliaments, London.

No. 2. Question raised (in brief): Many legislators, be it MP/MLA accuse their counterparts from other political parties of using Unparliamentary words in the Parliament/Assembly. So, does the Speaker look at the list of words and decide and classify it as unparliamentary?
Reply: During the debates in the House, the Hon'ble Speaker/Chairperson looks into such words and classify/declare them 'unparliamentary', which are then expunged from the records of the debates.

subject: The applicant sought the guidelines and credential checks for selecting an MP as Chairperson of a Parliamentary Standing Committee, and any action taken on a related newspaper report.

What are the credential checks on a M.P. before being selected as Chairperson of a Parliamentary Committee?

response_summary: The Secretariat explained that Chairmen of Parliamentary Committees (except the Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of MPs) are appointed by the Speaker from among Committee members, based on seniority, experience and subject matter, and confirmed that no action had been taken on the newspaper report referenced by the applicant.

What are the credential checks on a M.P. before being selected as Chairperson of a Parliamentary Committee?

response_full_text:
Point No.1 & 2: The Chairmen of all Parliamentary Committees under the jurisdiction of the Speaker, except that of Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament, are appointed by the Speaker from amongst the members of the respective Committees. In the case of Joint Committee on Salaries and Allowances of Members of Parliament, the Committee elects its Chairman at its first sitting after nomination of members of both the Houses to the Committee by Presiding Officers. While appointing the Chairman of a Committee, the Speaker takes into consideration the seniority of member, his experience as a member of the Panel of Chairmen or as the Chairman of any other Parliamentary Committee, and the subject or nature of work of the Committee. If the Speaker himself is a member of a Committee, he invariably is the Chairman of that Committee. Where the Speaker is not a member but the Deputy Speaker is, then the latter is appointed the Chairman.
Point No.3: No action has been taken on the said newspaper report in Times of India dated 11 October 2013.

title: RTI on procedure for identifying MPs who violate party whip
subject: RTI seeking information on the procedure used to identify Members of Parliament who violate their political party's whip during voting, and whether this conflicts with voting privacy.
questions: Is there any information on the procedure followed to identify the Member of Parliament who have violated the whip of registered political party during voting on the bill in case (a) financial bills related voting (b) non-financial bills (c) voice vote. Is it electronic or manual method of identification based on seat number allotted to a member?
Is there any information on such procedure of identification against the spirit of privacy, secrecy of universal franchise enshrined in our constitution
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that voting occurs via voice vote or automatic vote recording machine, that the Secretariat is not informed of the contents of party whips, and that while whip violations cannot be verified in voice votes, the automatic machine displays each member's vote by seat/division number, which parties can check. It also noted that votes cast in divisions are public and published in the day's debates on the Lok Sabha website.
extracted_text:
Name of the applicant - [Applicant]
Application date - 04.11.2013 (Received on 07.11.2013)
Reference Letter No. - 1(1543)/IC/13 Dated 29.11.2013

Point No. | Text in full of the points raised in application | Reply | Reasons for refusal or delay, if any/ Rule quoted by Branches under Section 7 (8) (i) of the RTI Act, 2005
1. | Is there any information on the procedure followed to identify the Member of Parliament who have violated the whip of registered political party during voting on the bill in case (a) financial bills related voting (b) non-financial bills (c) voice vote. Is it electronic or manual method of identification based on seat number allotted to a member? | Voting on Finance Bills as well as Non-Finance Bills can take place either through voice vote or through the automatic vote recording machine (in case of Constitution Amendment Bills, which would come under the category Non-Finance Bills, the voting has mandatorily to be through the automatic vote recording machine). Whip is a direction issued to a member by his political party. Lok Sabha Secretariat is neither aware off nor the parties are supposed to inform the Secretariat about the issuance of a whip or the contents of the whip. It would be impossible to identify as well as to prove whether a member violated the whip issued by the party if the voting has taken place through voice vote. However, when voting takes place through automatic vote recording machine, the printed result of the voting is displayed on the Notice Board in the outer lobby. This result shows the division number (which is also the seat number) of members and also whether they have voted for 'Ayes', 'Noes' or 'Abstention'. Legislature parties can ascertain the manner in which their members have voted through this result. | --
3. | Is there any information on such procedure of identification against the spirit of privacy, secrecy of universal franchise enshrined in our constitution | The votes cast by individual members in divisions (except secret voting) held in Lok Sabha are open to all and are also incorporated in the debates of the day. response_full_text: Voting on Finance Bills as well as Non-Finance Bills can take place either through voice vote or through the automatic vote recording machine (in case of Constitution Amendment Bills, the voting has mandatorily to be through the automatic vote recording machine). Whip is a direction issued to a member by his political party; Lok Sabha Secretariat is neither aware of nor informed about the issuance or contents of a whip. It would be impossible to identify or prove whip violation if voting took place through voice vote. When voting takes place through the automatic vote recording machine, the printed result showing each member's vote (Ayes/Noes/Abstention) by division/seat number is displayed on the Notice Board, allowing legislature parties to ascertain how their members voted. The votes cast by individual members in divisions (except secret voting) held in Lok Sabha are open to all and incorporated in the debates of the day, which are uploaded on the Lok Sabha website.

questions: किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा धमकी दिए जाने के कारण अपनी सुरक्षा की मांग
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि आवेदक ने कोई सूचना नहीं मांगी बल्कि व्यक्तिगत शिकायत व्यक्त की है, जो RTI Act के दायरे में नहीं आती। साथ ही आवेदन शुल्क भी अविधिमान्य पाया गया और आईपीओ वापस कर दिया गया।

लोक सभा सचिवालय
सूचना प्रकोष्ठ संसदीय सौध, नई दिल्ली-110001

सं. 1(1761)/आईसी/2016 07.10.2016

विषयः सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना।

महोदय,
विभिन्न गण्यमान्यों और केन्द्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी, लोक सभा को संबोधित आपके दिनांक 30.09.2016 के आरटीआई आवेदन, जो इस सचिवालय में 03.10.2016 को प्राप्त हुआ था तथा जिसमें आपने किसी व्यक्ति द्वारा धमकी दिए जाने के कारण अपनी सुरक्षा की मांग की है, के संदर्भ में, मुझे यह कहने का निदेश हुआ है कि आपने कोई ऐसी जानकारी नहीं मांगी है, जो इस लोक प्राधिकारी के पास उपलब्ध हो, बल्कि अपनी व्यक्तिगत शिकायत व्यक्त की है । आपके आवेदन की विषयवस्तु इस सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है ।

3. मुझे आपको यह भी सूचित करना है कि आरटीआई अधिनियम के तहत, केवल ऐसी जानकारी दी जा सकती है, जो लोक प्राधिकारी के पास पहले से उपलब्ध हो या उसके नियंत्रणाधीन हो । जन सूचना अधिकारी का कार्य आवेदकों द्वारा उठाई गई समस्याओं का समाधान करना नहीं है । आरटीआई अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत शिकायतों, सुझावों, सलाहों, मतों और निर्देशों पर विचार नहीं किया जाता है । आप अपनी शिकायतों के समाधान के लिए संबंधित प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क कर सकते हैं ।
इसे कें.ज.सू.अ. का अनुमोदन प्राप्त है ।

उप सचिव एवं कें.स.ज.सू. अधि.
संलग्नः यथोपरि ।

title: RTI on irregularities in Executive Officer recruitment since 2000
department: Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat (सूचना प्रकोष्ठ, लोक सभा सचिवालय)
subject: An advocate sought detailed information on alleged irregularities in the recruitment of Executive Officers by the Joint Recruitment Cell of Lok Sabha Secretariat since 2000, and action taken thereon.
questions: Please inform if the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker has received any information/petition during last 4 years regarding irregularities committed by Joint Recruitment Cell in making appointments to the post of Executive Officer since 2000 onwards

Please inform if the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker is aware that persons who failed in written paper or even those who failed to pass the preliminary paper were selected to the post of Executive Officer in 2003, on the basis of a relaxed cut off marks which was never approved by the then Speaker. On the other side, meritorious candidates who passed all the papers and did not require any relaxation were denied appointment, thus, compromising with the merit.

Please inform if the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker is aware that the interest of SC employees suffered adversely due to these illegal appointments in the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

Please inform if the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker, is aware that irregularities/illegalities/fraud/misrepresentations/concealment of facts played a role in selection of few candidates and illegal benefits were given to certain candidates by then officers in gross abuse of their official position.

Please inform if the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker ordered any inquiry to look into the issue of illegal appointments in the Secretariat during the last 12 years.

Please supply an attested copy of the action taken by the Hon'ble Speaker or Secretary-General, Lok Sabha or the Principal Secretary to Hon'ble Speaker on the said information/petition to quash these illegal appointments in the Secretariat.

Please supply the action taken by the Lok Sabha Secretariat against the officers who were involved in irregularities in examination process in the examination for the post of Executive Officer, 2002-2003.

Supply the attested copies of the approved Scheme of examination, marks obtained by each candidate who appeared in the personal interview, reasons for not preparing any separate Departmental Merit List despite being provided for by Circular No. 25072 dated 18.01.2002 at the stages of evaluation of Preliminary Paper, Written Papers and Interview, the need to conceal the important facts, like failing of Smt. Reena M. Jacob and Shri Kalyansundaram in Preliminary Paper.
Also supply the attested copies of the complete file notings/correspondences relating to the examinations held for the post of Executive Officer in the Secretariat in 2000 to 2005.
response_summary: Lok Sabha Secretariat stated that the Joint Recruitment Cell does not maintain a consolidated record of representations across periods, referenced a pending Civil Writ Petition No. 3470/2014 in Delhi High Court, enclosed the examination scheme, related notes, and file notings for the 2002 Executive Officer examination, listed all examinations held 2000-2005, invited the applicant to inspect records at JRC, and offered 49 pages of documents on points 8 & 9 for Rs.98.

title: सरकारी आवास बेदखली, उपदान व संसद वृक्षों संबंधी जानकारी
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (प्रशासन शाखा / संपदा अधिकारी)
subject: आवेदक ने महासचिव को भेजे गए पत्रों की प्रतियां, सरकारी आवास से बेदखली व उपदान (ग्रेच्युटी) राशि रोके जाने से संबंधित नियम, तथा संसद परिसर के वृक्षों पर हाई मास्ट लाइट/तार लगाए जाने की जानकारी मांगी।
questions: वर्ष 2015 और 2016 के दौरान आवेदक ने विभिन्न मुद्दों पर माननीय महासचिव और प्रशासन को कई पत्र भेजे। इनमें से कुछ पत्रों पर तो कार्यवाही की गई किन्तु बाकी अन्य पत्रों पर कोई ध्यान नहीं दिया गया। इसलिए, अगस्त 2015 से 2016 के बीच किए गए पत्राचार की प्रमाणित प्रतियां सूचना के रूप में उपलब्ध कराई जाएं।

क्वार्टर सं. 15/284, बाबा खड़क सिंह मार्ग आवेदक को आवंटित किया गया था और इसका ताला प्रशासन द्वारा बिना किसी सूचना के तोड़ दिया गया। कृपया उन नियमों की जानकारी प्रदान करें जिनके अंतर्गत ऐसी कार्यवाही की गई और साथ ही कब्जा करने की कार्यवाही की पूरी वीडियोग्राफी भी उपलब्ध कराएं।

यदि उपदान की लंबित राशि को क्वार्टर (आवास) से बेदखली किए जाने तक के लिए रोका गया था और प्रशासन शाखा-दो द्वारा मुझे कोई सूचना दिए बिना आवास को अपने कब्जे में लिया गया था, तो कृपया सूचना उपलब्ध कराएं कि मुझे मेरे लंबित देयों का ब्याज सहित भुगतान कब तक किया जाएगा।
संसद परिसर में ऐसे वृक्षों की संख्या बताएं जिन पर हाई मास्ट लाइटें और लोहे का तार लगाया गया है।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि पत्रों की संख्या/दिनांक स्पष्ट न होने से उत्तर नहीं दिया जा सका; क्वार्टर की बेदखली सरकारी स्थान (अप्राधिकृत अधिभोगियों की बेदखली) अधिनियम, 1971 की धारा 4 के अंतर्गत संपदा अधिकारी के आदेश से हुई थी; रोकी गई उपदान राशि अनापत्ति प्रमाण पत्र मिलने पर जारी होती है; तथा संसद परिसर के किसी भी वृक्ष पर हाई मास्ट लाइट या तार नहीं लगा है।

department: Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat (Question Branch)
subject: The applicant, referencing a prior CIC decision, sought to know whether the Committee to Inquire into Allegations of Improper Conduct or any other Lok Sabha authority had tried to identify the person behind a forged MP signature on question notices.
questions: In reference to your RTI reply 1(1609 & 1792)IC/16 dated 01.08.2016 and CIC decision no CIC/CC/2015/900176/SB & 900234/SB dated 04.07.2016, as stated in your earlier reply that all four letters contain the same issue of forged signature of Ex-MP as mentioned in his earlier letter dated 13.12.2005, which was already considered by the Committee to Inquire into Allegations of Improper Conduct on the part of some members: did the inquiry committee just consider the letter or did they try to find out the culprit behind the forgery? Please tell whether the Inquiry Committee, Secretary General, Speaker Lok Sabha or anybody from Lok Sabha has tried to inquire the person behind this forgery or not.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that the Question Branch's procedure is to return notices with unmatched signatures to the Member concerned and that it is the Member's duty to approach the police; six such notices were returned to the then MP Shri Ramsewak Singh on 12.08.2005, and the letter dated 13.12.2005 was considered by the Parliamentary Committee as evidence, but no separate action was taken by the Question Branch to identify the culprit.

Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1449)/IC/16/ dated 30.08.2016
Sl. No. of question in original application | Point in brief | Reply
1 | In reference to your RTI reply 1(1609 & 1792)IC/16 dated 01.08.2016. On CIC decision no CIC/CC/2015/900176/SB& 900234/SB dated 04.07.2016. As you have stated in your reply (page three, serial no. 4 (ii) reply column) all four letters contain the same issue of forged signature of Ex-MP as mentioned in his earlier letter dated 13.12.2005 which was already considered by the Committee to Inquire into Allegations of Improper Conduct on the part of some members. In view of the above paragraph I want to know that the inquiry committee just considered the letter or they have tried to find out the culprit also, who is behind this forgery. After receiving your letter I have gone through the inquiry committee report 5 times but I could not find anywhere that they have tried to inquire that who was the culprit behind this forgery. Please tell me that the Inquiry Committee, Secretary General, Speaker Lok Sabha or anybody from Lok Sabha has tried to inquire the person behind this forgery or not. | As has already been stated in earlier reply dated 14.07.2016 in response to the verdict of Central Information Commission (CIC) dated 04.07.2016, as per procedure, the Question Branch Lok Sabha Secretariat returns all such notices of questions to Hon'ble Members where their signatures are not matched with our data. It is duty of the Hon'ble Member to take up the matter with the appropriate authority i.e. police. As is evident, the Secretariat had already returned six notices of questions with unmatched signatures on 12.08.2005 to Shri Ramsewak Singh, the then Member of Lok Sabha with the request to send them with correct signatures. subject: RTI (transferred from Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs) seeking the attendance record of MP Mr. Nepal Singh (Rampur) and reasons for low attendance if any.
questions: Please provide the attendance record of Mr. Nepal Singh who is MP of Rampur. IF he has low attendance then what is the reason behind it.
response_summary: The Secretariat explained the Attendance Register system and directed the applicant to the Lok Sabha website for member-wise attendance data of the 16th Lok Sabha, noting a member may attend without signing the register. It declined to answer the part about the 'reason' for low attendance, stating this was a question, not an information request, and outside the purview of the RTI Act.

title: RTI on MP salary allowances MPLAD funds and Speaker's remuneration
subject: RTI seeking wide-ranging information on MP salary, allowances, medical benefits, private vehicles, MPLAD funds, Speaker's salary, session interruption losses, and Bureau of Parliamentary Studies and Training courses.
questions: Monthly salary of Member of Parliament
Other allowances given to MPs
Money provided to MPs for Medical treatment
Subsidy given to MPs for Air/Rail etc.
Whether any private vehicles is provided to each MP? If so, how the MP utilise the private vehicles
Fund allocated to MPs development
Whether Speaker, Lok Sabha can get extra salary other than salary.
Loss due to interruption in this session
Short term Study Course relating to Parliament organised by Lok Sabha Secretariat etc.?
response_summary: The Secretariat listed the Acts/Rules governing MP salary, allowances, medical facilities and travel; clarified no private vehicles are provided to MPs; noted MPLAD fund queries were transferred to the Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation; explained that Parliament session expenditure has no separate exclusive budget head; and described BPST's free short study-visit facility. In a follow-up letter, it clarified that the Speaker's salary is governed by the Salaries & Allowances of Officers of Parliament Act, 1953.

1. | Monthly salary of Member of Parliament | The Salary, allowances, etc. to all Members of Parliament (including nominated members) are regulated by the following Act/Rules: (1) The Salary, Allowances and pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended), (2) The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957. (3) The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956. (4) The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959. (5) The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960. (6) The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986. (7) The Members of Parliament Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986. & The Members of parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in.
2. | Other allowances given to MPs | (covered under reply to point 1 above)
3. | Money provided to MPs for Medical treatment | (covered under reply to point 1 above)
4. | Subsidy given to MPs for Air/Rail etc. | (covered under reply to point 1 above)
5. | - Whether any private vehicles is provided to each MP? - If so, how the MP utilise the private vehicles | No. Does not arise.
6-7. | Fund allocated to MPs development | Already transferred to M/o Statistics & Programme Implementation vide letter dt. 22.9.15.
7. | Whether Speaker, Lok Sabha can get extra salary other than salary. | Under process. Information on this point will be supplied later.
8. | Loss due to interruption in this session | The expenditure on working of Parliament is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments. There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Branches/agencies in connection with the conduct of Parliament. Similarly, No separate budget provision is kept for proceedings of Parliament. Under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha, Head of account-wise allocation is made for booking the expenditure incurred on Members of Lok Sabha and staff of Lok Sabha Secretariat. Expenditure incurred alongwith provision made under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha from the Financial Year 2009-10 onwards is available on Lok Sabha homepage under link: http://164.100.47.132/LssNew/Secretariat/DemandLokSabha.aspx Hence, such information is not maintained.
9. | Short term Study Course relating to Parliament organised by Lok Sabha Secretariat etc.? | Apart from the regular Training Programmes, Appreciation Courses, etc. the BPST affords facilities to Officers of Central and State Governments and also to Students and Academics for short Study Visits during which the visitors are provided with the requisite orientation so that they get to know various aspects of Parliamentary Practices and Procedures. This is usually for half-a-day and no fee is charged for such visits. The interested persons/institutions can write to the head of the Bureau of Parliamentary Studies and Training (BPST) for any such request. They can also contact BPST through e-mail i.e. bpst@sansad.nic.in

उत्तर: वर्ष 2017 में संसद सदस्यों की मांग पर लोक सभा सचिवालय ने मंत्रालयों/संस्थाओं से 10 प्रतियां (हिन्दी और अंग्रेजी प्रत्येक भाषा में) प्राप्त कीं। सभापटल पर रखने हेतु मंत्रालयों के नियंत्रणाधीन विभिन्न संस्थाओं से प्राप्त होने वाली वार्षिक रिपोर्ट की प्रतियों की संख्या भी (हिन्दी और अंग्रेजी प्रत्येक भाषा में) 25 से घटाकर 10 कर दी गई।

2. लोक सभा सचिवालय द्वारा पेपरलेस पॉलिसी के अंतर्गत वार्षिक रिपोर्ट की प्रतियों की संख्या में कमी लाने हेतु क्या कदम उठाए गए हैं?
उत्तर: यथोपरि।

3. पिछले वर्ष के दौरान पेपरलेस पॉलिसी के अंतर्गत वार्षिक रिपोर्ट और रेल बजट की प्रतियों की संख्या में कितनी कमी लाई गई है?
उत्तर: जहां तक वार्षिक रिपोर्ट का संबंध है; उत्तर ऊपर दिया जा चुका है। इसके अतिरिक्त वर्ष 2017 से रेल बजट का सामान्य बजट में विलय कर दिया गया है। अतः रेल बजट की अलग से कोई प्रति प्राप्त नहीं की गई है।

subject: Applicant sought details of pension paid to MPs and MLAs, associated expenditure, tenure-wise pension slabs, taxability, and whether 7th Pay Commission benefits apply to them.
questions: How many MP and MLA gets pension every year, share state wise numbers.
How much money spent by the government every year for the same share state wise numbers AND What are the other perks and benefits are given to former MP and MLA.
Is that amount taxable income.
Kindly share the tenure wise pension slab for MP and MLA for the same.
How much money spent from 2004 to 2014 and 2015 to 2017.

response_summary: The Secretariat clarified that MPs receive salary (not pension while serving), pointed to the MSA Act 1954 and related rules for perks/benefits, explained that MP salary/allowances are taxed as 'income from other sources' without TDS, provided a historical pension slab table from 1976 to 2009, explained that ex-MP pension is disbursed by the Central Pension Accounting Office, and confirmed the 7th Pay Commission does not apply to MPs. MLA-specific data was outside this branch's remit.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: 11.09.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1282)/IC/17 dated 27.09.2017

1. How many MP and MLA gets pension every year, share state wise numbers.
Reply: This Branch deals with the Salary and Allowances of Members of Parliament only which are regulated by MSA Act, 1954. MPs get Salary and not pension. Pay and Accounts Office is entrusted with the work of issuing Pension Payment Orders (PPO) on the basis of the approved sanction sent by concerned branch i.e. MSA branch, therefore, CPAO (Ministry of Finance, Dept. of Expenditure), disburse the pension through the bank stated by the ex-MPs.

2 and 4. How much money spent by the government every year for the same share state wise numbers AND What are the other perks and benefits are given to former MP and MLA.
Reply: The Salary and Allowances of Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules: 1. The Salary, Allowances and pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended) 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986 7. The Members of Parliament Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha i.e. http://mpa.nic.in/MPA/act.aspx. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.

3. Is that amount taxable income.
Reply: The salary and allowances received by the Members are taxed under the head of 'Income from other sources'. Since the salary and allowances are taxed under the head Income from other sources, such salary and allowances would not be subjected to Tax Deduction at Source (TDS). Members will have to discharge their tax liability by paying advance tax or self assessment tax.

5. Kindly share the tenure wise pension slab for MP and MLA for the same.
Reply: Details of Pension statement of Members as revised from time to time enclosed. [Pension slab history table: From 09.09.1976 - Rs. 300 p.m. for serving the House for five years, additional pension @ Rs. 50 p.m. for every year in excess of five years but not exceeding Rs. 500 p.m. From 26.2.1985 - Rs. 500 p.m. for serving the House for four years and ten months, additional pension @ Rs. 50 p.m. for every year in excess of five years without any ceiling. From 1.9.1996 (approx.) - Rs. 1365 p.m. for serving the House for four years or two terms of Lok Sabha, additional pension @ Rs. 250 p.m. in excess of five years without any ceiling; persons entitled to ex-MP pension were also made entitled to any other pension in addition. From 20.08.1998 - Rs. 2500 p.m. for serving the House for four years or two terms of Lok Sabha, additional pension @ Rs. 500 p.m. for every year in excess of five years without any ceiling. From 14.09.2001 (approx.) - Rs. 3000 p.m. for serving the House for four years or two terms of Lok Sabha, plus Rs. 600 p.m. for every year in excess of five years without any ceiling. From 09.01.2004 - Rs. 3000 p.m. for any period, plus Rs. 600 p.m. for every year in excess of five years without any ceiling, rounding off nine months or more as one completed year. From 5.09.2006 - Rs. 8000 p.m. for any period, additional pension @ Rs. 800 p.m. for every year in excess of five years without any ceiling, rounding off nine months or more as one complete year. From 18.05.2009 - Rs. 20,000 p.m. for any period, additional pension @ Rs. 1500 p.m. for every year exceeding five years without any ceiling, rounding off nine months or more as one complete year.]

6. How much money spent from 2004 to 2014 and 2015 to 2017.
Reply: Pension to Members of Parliament are paid under Section 8A of the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended). The above Act/Rules are available on website of Lok Sabha which can be accessed through http://164.100.47.132/LssNew/members/AMENITIES.aspx. The Lok Sabha Secretariat issues sanction/orders for grant of pension to Ex MPs. But the pension to Ex MPs is released by the Central Pension Accounting Office, Ministry of Finance (Department of Expenditure), Trikoot III Complex, Bhikaji Cama Place, New Delhi and disbursed through the Bank as opted by the Ex-MP. Lok Sabha Secretariat issues only one time sanction for grant of pension/family pension to Ex MP or their spouse/dependent, as the case may be, and the revised sanction whenever the pension is revised under the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954.

7. Do these MP and MLA also get 7th pay commission benefits.
Reply: 7th Pay Commission benefits is not applicable the MPs.

response_tables.title: Tenure-wise pension slab for Members of Parliament (as revised from time to time)

response_full_text: This Branch deals with the Salary and Allowances of Members of Parliament only, regulated by MSA Act, 1954; MPs get Salary and not pension while serving. Ex-MP pension PPOs are issued by Pay and Accounts Office based on MSA branch sanction and disbursed by CPAO, Ministry of Finance. Salary/allowances are regulated by the MSA Act 1954 and associated Rules (Travelling and Daily Allowances 1957, Housing and Telephone Facilities 1956, Medical Facilities 1959, Allowances for Journeys Abroad 1960, Constituency Allowances 1986, Conveyance Advance 1986, Office Expense Allowance 1988). MP salary/allowances are taxed as 'Income from other sources' without TDS. Tenure-wise pension slabs were provided from 1976 (Rs.300 p.m.) progressively increased to Rs.20,000 p.m. from 18.05.2009, with additional pension per extra year of service. Pension to ex-MPs is paid under Section 8A of the MSA Act 1954 and disbursed via CPAO. 7th Pay Commission benefits are not applicable to MPs.

6. What the criteria is applied of commas, full stops and question marks and half mistakes
Reply: The following instructions/guidelines were followed by the evaluator for evaluation of shorthand transcription scripts: (i) Omission of a word or figure - One error for each word or figure omitted. (ii) Substitution by a wrong word - One error for each wrong substitute. (iii) Insertion of an extra word - One error for each extra word. (iv) Wrong Spelling - One error for each misspelt word. (v) Wrong number of a noun, pronoun or verb etc. (singular form used for plural or vice versa) - One error for each wrong word and each consequentially wrong word. subject: The applicant sought information on demands and rulings regarding the post of Leader of Opposition, Public Accounts Committee chairmen, recognition of A. K. Gopalan as Leader of Opposition, and the Attorney General's opinion on the matter.

Was there any ruling from the Speaker in the Lok Sabha relating to the post of Leader of Opposition in the Parliamentary history? If yes, give the copies of the rulings.

response_summary: The Secretariat stated that as per available records there was never any demand or ruling on the Leader of Opposition post during the periods asked, provided a list of PAC Chairmen, confirmed A.K. Gopalan was not recognized as Leader of Opposition, and stated that the Attorney General's opinion sought during the 16th Lok Sabha could only be shared after a final decision was taken by the Speaker.

department: Information Cell, Lok Sabha Secretariat / Table Office (B) Branch
subject: RTI, transferred from Rajya Sabha Secretariat, asking whether MPs hold a full-time post and whether they can engage in commercial activities while Parliament is in/not in session.

response_summary: The Secretariat stated that the question of MPs being full-time did not pertain to the Table Office Branch, and explained that under Article 102(1)(a) of the Constitution, a person is disqualified from Parliament for holding an office of profit under the Government unless declared exempt by law, which applies regardless of whether Parliament is in session.

Information Sought: Please state if members of parliament (Loksabha and Rajyasabha) are
entitled to participate in other commercial activities like (carrying on business, profession and
other activities) while the Parliament is in session.
Reply: In Democratic form of Governments the concept of disqualifying a holder of office of
Profit under the Government for being chosen as, and for being, a Member of the Legislature
originated from the need to limit the control and influence of the Executive over the Legislature
by means of an undue proportion of office holders being Members of the Legislature.  In India,
this principal is embodied in Article 102(1)(a) of the Constitution of India in regard to the
Members of Parliament which reads as follows:-
"102(1) A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a Member of either
House of Parliament - (a) if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the
Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its
holder."

entitled to participate in other commercial activities like (carrying on business, profession and
other activities) while the Parliament is not in session.

In India, this principal is embodied in Article 102(1)(a) of the Constitution of India in regard to the Members of Parliament which reads as follows: "102(1) A person shall be disqualified for being chosen as, and for being, a Member of either House of Parliament - (a) if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State, other than an office declared by Parliament by law not to disqualify its holder." response_summary: The Secretariat stated that the subject matter does not pertain to Lok Sabha Secretariat but relates to Reserve Bank of India and Ministry of Finance, that legal opinion cannot be sought under RTI, and that the fee submitted (IPO) was invalid, so the application could not be transferred; the applicant was advised to approach the concerned authority directly.

From
K. Sona

[Applicant]

Sir,

With reference to your RTI application dated 06.06.2016, received in this
Secretariat on 08.06.2016 seeking information on BR Act, 1949 and its applicability
to State Cooperative Bank in India and related issues, I am directed to state that the
subject matter of the application does not pertain to the Lok Sabha Secretariat but
relates to Reserve Bank of India and Ministry of Finance.
2. Further, instead of seeking information, you have sought opinion/legal
interpretation about the BR Act.   As per the RTI Act, Public Authority is not obligation
to give advise/opinion to the information seekers.
3. Moreover, the fee furnished by you vide  IPO No.31F 713604  is invalid as it
is not in favour of `Drawing and Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha' or `Pay and Accounts
Officer, Lok Sabha'.
4. Hence, your application cannot be transferred to them.  You are requested to
approach Public Authority concerned and seek the information directly.
5. Invalid IPO No.31F 713604 of Rs.10/- is enclosed herewith.

6. This has the approval of CPIO.

Yours faithfully,
Sd/-
        DEPUTY SECRETARY & CAPIO

Encl. : IPO No. 31F 713604 of Rs.10/-.

Moreover, the fee furnished by you vide IPO No.31F 713604 is invalid as it is not in favour of 'Drawing and Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha' or 'Pay and Accounts Officer, Lok Sabha'. Hence, your application cannot be transferred to them. You are requested to approach Public Authority concerned and seek the information directly. Invalid IPO No.31F 713604 of Rs.10/- is enclosed herewith.

subject: लोक सभा सदस्यों के उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर तथा दैनिक भत्ते के दावे से संबंधित जानकारी मांगी गई।
questions: कृपया इस संबंध में जानकारी प्रदान करें कि क्या जो सदस्य अपने नाम के सामने हस्ताक्षर करने के लिए सदस्यों उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर नहीं करते हैं, वे दैनिक भत्ते का दावा करने के हकदार हैं?
कृपया उन सदस्यों के संबंध में जानकारी प्रदान करें जिन्होंने उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर नहीं किए हैं, परंतु दैनिक भत्ता प्राप्त किया है या दैनिक भत्ते का दावा किया है।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि टेबल ऑफिस शाखा उपस्थिति रजिस्टर का कार्य देखती है और सदस्यों की उपस्थिति संबंधी ब्यौरा लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है। वेतन और भत्तों को विनियमित करने वाले अधिनियम/नियमों की सूची भी दी गई।

बिंदु सं. 1: कृपया इस संबंध में जानकारी प्रदान करें कि क्या जो सदस्य अपने नाम के सामने हस्ताक्षर करने
के लिए सदस्यों उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर नहीं करते हैं, वे दैनिक भत्ते का दावा करने के हकदार हैं?
सूचना/उत्तर: इस संबंध में इस सचिवालय की संबंधित शाखा अर्थात् टेबल ऑफिस लोक सभा के सदस्यों के
उपस्थिति रजिस्टर का कार्य देखती है। सदस्यों (माननीय अध्यक्ष, उपाध्यक्ष, प्रधानमंत्री और मंत्रियों के
अतिरिक्त) के लिए एक उपस्थिति रजिस्टर रखा जाता है। लोक सभा के सदस्यों द्वारा 16वीं लोक सभा के
सभी सत्रों के दौरान उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर करने/हस्ताक्षर न करने संबंधी ब्यौरा लोक सभा की
वेबसाइट अर्थात् www.loksabha.nic.in पर Members—Sitting Members — Attendance of
Members—>Member-wise Attendance — All Members शीर्षकों के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध है।

बिंदु सं. 2: कृपया उन सदस्यों के संबंध में जानकारी प्रदान करें जिन्होंने उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर नहीं
किए हैं, परंतु दैनिक भत्ता प्राप्त किया है या दैनिक भत्ते का दावा किया है।
सूचना/उत्तर: आवेदक से अनुरोध है कि वह वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त करने के लिए लोक सभा की उपर्युक्त
वेबसाइट का अवलोकन करें। संसद सदस्यों (नामनिर्दिष्ट सदस्यों सहित) के वेतन और भत्ते निम्नलिखित
अधिनियम/नियमों द्वारा विनियमित किए जाते हैं:- 1. संसद सदस्य वेतन, भत्ता और पेंशन अधिनियम, 1954
(यथासंशोधित) 2. संसद सदस्य (यात्रा और दैनिक भत्ते) नियम, 1957 3. आवास और टेलीफोन सुविधाएं
(संसद सदस्य) नियम, 1956 4. चिकित्सा सुविधाएं (संसद सदस्य) नियम, 1959 5. संसद सदस्य (विदेश
यात्रा के लिए भत्ते) नियम, 1960 6. संसद सदस्य (निर्वाचन क्षेत्र संबंधी भत्ता) नियम, 1986 7. संसद सदस्य
(वाहन क्रय अग्रिम) नियम, 1986 तथा 8. संसद सदस्य (कार्यालय व्यय भत्ता) नियम, 1988। उपर्युक्त
अधिनियम/नियम संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय, भारत सरकार की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं जिन्हें
http://mpa.nic.in/MPA/act.aspx पर क्लिक करके देखा जा सकता है।

- x -
response_full_text: इस संबंध में इस सचिवालय की संबंधित शाखा अर्थात् टेबल ऑफिस लोक सभा के सदस्यों के उपस्थिति रजिस्टर का कार्य देखती है। सदस्यों (माननीय अध्यक्ष, उपाध्यक्ष, प्रधानमंत्री और मंत्रियों के अतिरिक्त) के लिए एक उपस्थिति रजिस्टर रखा जाता है। लोक सभा के सदस्यों द्वारा 16वीं लोक सभा के सभी सत्रों के दौरान उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर करने/हस्ताक्षर न करने संबंधी ब्यौरा लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है। आवेदक से अनुरोध है कि वह वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त करने के लिए लोक सभा की उपर्युक्त वेबसाइट का अवलोकन करें। संसद सदस्यों के वेतन और भत्ते संबंधित अधिनियम/नियमों द्वारा विनियमित किए जाते हैं जो संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध हैं।

subject: RTI seeking certified copies of note sheets and documents relating to the applicant's own petitions before the Committee on Petitions Branch, and information on its rules, hierarchy and appeal channel.
questions: Sought certified copies of all the concerned documents available in Lok Sabha Secretariat substantiating the contents of the second sentence of para-04 (Four) of the note dated 18.7.2017, initiated in the Committee of Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat stating that the allegation made by the applicant in his rejoinder dated 16.6.2017, are unfounded.

Kindly intimate me those statements of my second Petition dated 29.03.2017 and third Petition dated 16.06.2017 which cast aspersion on the prerogatives of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat and on its working.
Sought certified copies of the prerogatives of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat.

Whether Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat actually dealt his first Petition dated 07.12.2016 submitted in Lok Sabha Secretariat in casual manner and without proper appreciation of the contents of my first Petition dated 07.12.2016 & contents of the 202 pages enclosures enclosed with his first Petition dated 07.12.2016.

Whether Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat actually processed his second Petition dated 29.03.2017 in haste and in casual manner again without proper appreciation of the contents of his second Petition dated 29.03.2017 & the contents of the 95 pages documents enclosed with his second Petition dated 29.03.2017.

Sought certified copies of those documents of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat which contains the facts of actions taken on all the requests made in my third Petition dated 16.06.2017.

Whether the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat is empowered to issue binding nature of instructions to the UPSC to rectify the illegalities committed in UPSC as per the extant Rules, Regulation, Policy, Direction of Lok Sabha Speaker vogue in this regard.

Sought certified copy of the first page of my third Petition dated 16.06.2017 submitted to the Secretary General of Lok Sabha Secretariat without hiding any comment and instruction given on the same by various authorities of Lok Sabha Secretary including the signature and instructions issued by the present Secretary General of Lok Sabha.

Sought the charter of duties and powers vested in various authorities of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat as per the Rule, Regulations, Policy, Directions of the Lok Sabha Speaker by providing certified copies of the same.

Sought information regarding the designations of the whole hierarchy of reporting channel of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat with regard to dealing with the petitions submitted in Lok Sabha Secretariat starting from LDC to the Secretary General of Lok Sabha by providing certified copies of the concerned documents.

Whether any channel of appeal is available in Lok Sabha Secretariat against the decision of declaring any petition as inadmissible hence to be filed through the decision of the Joint Secretary of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat by providing certified copies of concerned Rule/ Regulations/ Policy/ Directives etc.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated that certified copies relating to the applicant's own earlier rejoinder/petitions had already been supplied in response to his prior RTI application and First Appeal, cited the applicable Rules of Procedure and Speaker's Directions governing the Committee on Petitions, provided the reporting hierarchy, and noted that justifications/opinions are not 'information' obtainable under the RTI Act.

Point 1: Sought certified copies of all the concerned documents available in Lok Sabha Secretariat substantiating the contents of the second sentence of para-04 (Four) of the note dated 18.7.2017, initiated in the Committee of Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat stating that "Therefore, the allegation made by [Applicant] in his rejoinder dated 16.6.2017, are unfounded."
Reply: The concerned certified copies of the Note sheets with respect to the examination of a rejoinder dated 16.6.2017 of [Applicant] has already been supplied to the applicant, [Applicant], in reply to his RTI application dated 29.6.2017.

Point 2: Kindly intimate me those statements of my second Petition dated 29.03.2017 and third Petition dated 16.06.2017 which cast aspersion on the prerogatives of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat and on its working.
Reply: The concerned certified copies of the Note sheets with respect to the examination of representation dated 29.3.2017 and a rejoinder dated 16.6.2017 of [Applicant] have already been supplied to the applicant, [Applicant], in reply to his First Appeal dated 22.5.2017 and RTI application dated 29.6.2017, respectively. Further the information regarding the working of the Committee on Petitions is already in public domain, which can be viewed on Lok Sabha website:- www.loksabha.nic.in under 'Committees' and 'Parliamentary Procedures'.

Point 3: Sought certified copies of the prerogatives of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Reply: The Rules/Directions related to the Committee on Petitions are contained in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha i.e. Rules 160 to 169 and Rules 306 to 307 and Directions by the Speaker, Lok Sabha i.e. Direction 38 to 40 and Direction 94 to 96. The detailed information can be viewed on Lok Sabha website:- www.loksabha.nic.in under 'Committees' and 'Parliamentary Procedures'.

Point 4: Whether Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat actually dealt his first Petition dated 07.12.2016 submitted in Lok Sabha Secretariat in casual manner and without proper appreciation of the contents of my first Petition dated 07.12.2016 & contents of the 202 pages enclosures enclosed with his first Petition dated 07.12.2016 as per the concerned record of the Committee on Petitions of Lok Sabha Secretariat available in the form of his original first Petition dated 07.12.2016 and in the form of 202 pages documents enclosed with my original first Petition dated 07.12.2016.
Reply: The Petitions/Representations received in the Committee on Petitions Branch from various individuals, bodies etc. are dealt with on the basis of relevant Rule(s)/Direction(s) on the subject. The concerned certified copies of the Note sheets with respect to the examination of a rejoinder dated 16.6.2017 of [Applicant] has already been supplied to the applicant, [Applicant], in reply to his RTI application dated 29.6.2017. Further, justifications are matter within the domain of adjudicating Authorities and as such cannot strictly be classified as information. Besides, it is also stated that under the RTI Act, only such information can be supplied which already exist and held by the Public Authority. The Public Information Officer is not supposed to create information; or to solve the problems raised by the applicant; or to furnish replies to hypothetical questions.

Point 5: Whether Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat actually processed his second Petition dated 29.03.2017 in haste and in casual manner again without proper appreciation of the contents of his second Petition dated 29.03.2017 & the contents of the 95 pages documents enclosed with his second Petition dated 29.03.2017 as per the concerned record of the Committee on Petitions of Lok Sabha Secretariat available in the form of his second original Petition dated 29.03.2017 and in the form of 95 pages documents enclosed with my original second Petition dated 29.03.2016 copies of which were submitted by me with my third Petition dated 16.06.2017 & available in Committee on Petitions of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Reply: Same as reply given at Points. Nos. 2 & 4. Further, justifications are matter within the domain of adjudicating Authorities and as such cannot strictly be classified as information. Besides, it is also stated that under the RTI Act, only such information can be supplied which already exist and held by the Public Authority. The Public Information Officer is not supposed to create information; or to solve the problems raised by the applicant; or to furnish replies to hypothetical questions.

Point 6: Sought certified copies of those documents of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat which contains the facts of actions taken on all the requests made in my third Petition dated 16.06.2017.
Reply: Same as reply given at Point. No. 1.

Point 7: Whether the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat is empowered to issue binding nature of instructions to the UPSC to rectify the illegalities committed in UPSC as per the extant Rules, Regulation, Policy, Direction of Lok Sabha Speaker vogue in this regard. Also sought straight forward factual information in this regard by providing certified copies of the concerned Rule, Policy, Regulation & Direction of the Speaker of Lok Sabha etc.
Reply: Same as reply given at Points. Nos. 3 & 4.

Point 8: Sought certified copy of the first page of my third Petition dated 16.06.2017 submitted to the Secretary General of Lok Sabha Secretariat without hiding any comment and instruction given on the same by various authorities of Lok Sabha Secretary including the signature and instructions issued by the present Secretary General of Lok Sabha.
Reply: Enclosed as Annexure.

Point 9: Sought the charter of duties and powers vested in various authorities of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat as per the Rule, Regulations, Policy, Directions of the Lok Sabha Speaker by providing certified copies of the same.
Reply: Reply same as given at Points. Nos. 3 & 4.

Point 10: Sought information regarding the designations of the whole hierarchy of reporting channel of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat with regard to dealing with the petitions submitted in Lok Sabha Secretariat starting from LDC to the Secretary General of Lok Sabha by providing certified copies of the concerned documents.
Reply: The present reporting channel of submission is as under:- Executive Assistant/Senior Executive Assistant -> Deputy Secretary -> Additional Director -> Joint Secretary -> Secretary General

Point 11: Whether any channel of appeal is available in Lok Sabha Secretariat against the decision of declaring any petition as - inadmissible hence to be filed through the decision of the Joint Secretary of the Committee on Petitions Branch of Lok Sabha Secretariat by providing certified copies of concerned Rule/ Regulations/ Policy/ Directives etc.
Reply: Reply same as given at Point. No. 3.
response_full_text: The concerned certified copies of the Note sheets with respect to the examination of a rejoinder dated 16.6.2017 has already been supplied to the applicant in reply to his RTI application dated 29.6.2017. The Rules/Directions related to the Committee on Petitions are contained in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha i.e. Rules 160 to 169 and Rules 306 to 307 and Directions by the Speaker, Lok Sabha i.e. Direction 38 to 40 and Direction 94 to 96. The Petitions/Representations received in the Committee on Petitions Branch from various individuals, bodies etc. are dealt with on the basis of relevant Rule(s)/Direction(s) on the subject. Justifications are matter within the domain of adjudicating Authorities and as such cannot strictly be classified as information; the Public Information Officer is not supposed to create information or furnish replies to hypothetical questions. The present reporting channel of submission is: Executive Assistant/Senior Executive Assistant -> Deputy Secretary -> Additional Director -> Joint Secretary -> Secretary General.

4. मुझे आपको यह भी सूचित करना है कि सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम के अंतर्गत केवल ऐसी सूचना
ही प्रदान की जा सकती है जो जन प्राधिकारी के पास हो अथवा उसके नियंत्रण में हो। जन सूचना अधिकारी
का कार्य आवेदकों की समस्याओं का समाधान करना नहीं है। सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के
अंतर्गत शिकायतों, सुझावों, सलाहों, मतों और निर्देशों आदि पर विचार नहीं किया जाता है। आप अपनी
समस्याओं के निराकरण के लिए संबंधित प्राधिकारियों से सीधे संपर्क कर सकते हैं।
5. इसे के.ज.सू.अधि. का अनुमोदन प्राप्त है।

भवदीय,
उप सचिव एवं के.स.ज.सू. अधि.
response_full_text: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत कोई विशिष्ट सूचना मांगने के बजाय आवेदक ने ऐसी सूचना मांगी है जो अस्पष्ट है और इस सचिवालय में उपलब्ध नहीं है। आवेदन की विषय-वस्तु इस सचिवालय से संबंधित नहीं है और यह सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 2(व) के अंतर्गत नहीं आती है। अतः, इस पर कार्रवाई नहीं की जा सकती है। आप एक ही विषय से संबंधित मुद्दों पर बार-बार अनेक आरटीआई आवेदन दायर करते रहे हैं। सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 की धारा 7(9) के अंतर्गत आपसे अनुरोध है कि एक ही मामले से संबंधित आरटीआई आवेदन दायर न करें।

title: RTI on cancellation of Verbatim Reporting Service bifurcation orders
subject: RTI seeking reasons and file notings behind the abolition of orders relating to bifurcation of the Verbatim Reporting Service and creation of temporary posts therein, and a copy of the 2013 Cadre Review Report.
questions: Why was the order regarding bifurcation of Verbatim Reporting Service abolished suddenly when the case is sub-judice?
Why Office Order Pt-I No.1618 dated 19.03.2012 regarding bifurcation of Verbatim Reporting Service on functional basis cancelled suddenly with effect from 14.03.2012 when the case is sub-judice?

Why Order No.PDA-1260/2011 dated 19.03.2012 regarding creation of temporary posts in Verbatim Reporting Service (English) was abolished suddenly with effect from 14.03.2012 although posts were created on the basis of the recommendations made by the O&M Section and approved by the Hon'ble speaker, Lok Sabha when the case is sub-judice?

Why R&CS Order No.PDA-1261/2012 dated 19.03.2012 was abolished suddenly regarding Methods of Recruitment and Eligibility conditions for appointment to various posts in the Lok Sabha Secretariat when the case is sub-judice?

Who has ordered for cancellation of orders? What are the reasons for cancellation suddenly of these orders when the case is sub-judice? Supply the names of the deciding authorities who abolished these orders.
Supply all the file notings in respect of abolition/cancellation of these orders.
Supply a copy of the latest Cadre Review Report 2013.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated a public authority is not obliged to answer queries under RTI, but nonetheless explained that the earlier office orders were cancelled/amended vide subsequent orders dated 04.06.2014 with the approval of the Hon'ble Speaker, and enclosed relevant file notings after severing non-disclosable portions. The Cadre Review Report will be made public only after a final decision is taken.

1. Information regarding different allowances an government providing for MP apart from monthly salary. — Reply: The different Allowances apart from monthly salary which are being provided for Members of Parliament are regulated by the following Act/Rules as amended from time to time: 1. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954. 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957. 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956. 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959. 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960. 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowance) Rules, 1986. 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the Purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986. 8. The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The aforementioned Act/Rules are available on Lok Sabha website and can be accessed through www.loksabha.nic.in and by clicking on 'Members' slot and then on 'Salary Acts and Rules'. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.
2. Requesting to please let us know the products being banned in Parliament of India and if possible reasons for banning these products — Reply: Delhi based NGO viz Centre for Science and Environment (CSE) in their study had reported the presence of high levels of pesticides and insecticides in all the major brands of soft drinks. The Members of Parliament raised the matter in the House regarding reported detection of pesticides in the popular brands of soft drinks. During the discussion, Shri E. Ahamed, M.P. as Chairman of the Joint Committee on Food Management in Parliament House Complex announced in the House that taking into account the sentiments being expressed by the Hon'ble Members, the supply of Coke, Pepsi and other soft drinks being served in the Railway Catering Units will be discontinued with immediate effect.

title: RTI on Lok Sabha Secretariat officer pay scales and Secretary appointments
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought details of Lok Sabha Secretariat officers' pay scales, promotion eligibility criteria, and the process of appointment to the post of Secretary, including deputation appointments made by past Speakers.
questions: The names of officers of the Lok Sabha Secretariat who are in the pay scale of Rs.67000-79000 since the year 2011.
Whether the officers in the scale of Rs.67000-79000 for more than three years are eligible for promotions as Secretary?
Whether relevant parliamentary work experience is still a valid criterion or it has been done away with?
Which names were recommended by the DoPT for consideration and appointment to the post of Secretary in the Lok Sabha Secretariat?
How and under what Rule the names recommended by the DoPT were ignored and under what Rule a new name was introduced and considered?

The names which were not recommended by the DoPT but were introduced by the Lok Sabha Secretariat on their own, the level at which such names were introduced, and whether such power vests with the Secretariat, along with the source of authority (with copies of the relevant note sheet, senior officers' noting, and the Speaker's order).
Whether there is any difference between the office of Speaker and the Lok Sabha Secretariat in the matter of recruitment procedure, and complete details of Rules and Procedure.

Complete details of appointments made on deputation basis to the post of Secretary, Additional Secretary and Joint Secretary by Somnath Chatterjee, Mrs. Meira Kumar and the present Speaker, term-wise, with officer names, cadre, and posts held.
Does the Speaker have the power to appoint anybody as Secretary in the Lok Sabha Secretariat without following the due procedure of appointment?
Whether the Lok Sabha Secretariat is exempt from writ jurisdiction of the Higher judiciary in administrative matters and if yes, the constitutional provision for the same.
response_summary: The Secretariat provided a directory reference for officer pay scales, enclosed the Recruitment and Conditions of Service Order and Cabinet Secretariat recommendation lists, provided relevant file notings and a statement of deputation appointments made by past Speakers (including Somnath Chatterjee and Meira Kumar), and declined to answer three points on the ground that they were queries/opinions not covered under the RTI Act.

लोक सभा सचिवालय
सं. 1(423)/आईसी/2016   दिनांक 10.03.2016

सेवा में: [आवेदक], [पता संपादित]

महोदया,
प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय से अंतरित होकर इस सचिवालय में दिनांक 07.03.2016 को प्राप्त आपके दिनांक 20.02.2016 के आरटीआई आवेदन के संदर्भ में मुझे इस पत्र के साथ इस सचिवालय से संबंधित और यहाँ उपलब्ध तथा सक्षम अधिकारी द्वारा यथानुमोदित सूचना संबंधी विवरण (अनुबंध) भेजने का निदेश हुआ है।
2. केन्द्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी का विवरण इस प्रकार है: श्री जे.एम. बैसाख, निदेशक एवं केन्द्रीय जन सूचना अधिकारी, लोक सभा सचिवालय, कमरा संख्या 164, संसदीय सौध, नई दिल्ली-110001 (दूरभाष 23035386)
3. सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत इस सचिवालय हेतु अपीलीय प्राधिकारी श्री के. विजयकृष्णन, अपर सचिव, लोक सभा सचिवालय, कमरा संख्या एफ-005, जे. ब्लॉक, संसदीय पुस्तकालय भवन, नई दिल्ली-110001 (23035226) हैं। यदि आप उपर्युक्त के संबंध में अपील करना चाहते हैं तो इस पत्र के जारी होने की तारीख से तीस दिन के भीतर अपीलीय प्राधिकारी को अपील कर सकते हैं। अपील हेतु प्रपत्र वेबसाइट www.loksabha.nic.in से डाउनलोड किया जा सकता है।

response_full_text: List of the drivers presently working in this Secretariat is enclosed; the Establishment List indicating drivers is also on the Lok Sabha website. Drivers are deployed with HS, HDS, LOP and senior officers as per a weekly roster; detailed deployment records may be inspected in person if essential in public interest. Arrangements/deployment are made as per administrative decisions. The Secretariat has no branch outside Delhi so drivers are not transferred, though officials are reallocated among branches as needed. Three vehicles with drivers are provided for HS's office and two for HDS's office, with further granular data available for in-person inspection. Drivers do not refuse VIP duty. Due to a shortage of staff car drivers, AN-I Branch utilises five casual labourers with valid commercial driving licences (two since made regular Attendants); no additional allowance is admissible to them. Four Maruti Gypsies are available for HSS/HDS pilot duty and urgent security duties, with log book entries available for inspection.

The Bill, as passed by Lok Sabha was passed by Rajya Sabha with amendments on 4.9.2013, which were agreed to by Lok Sabha on 5.9.2013. The Bill as passed by the Houses of Parliament was assented to by the President on 26.9.2013. A copy of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Bill, 2013 is enclosed.
