title: Parliamentary discussions on Rupee depreciation and related Bills clarified
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought details of parliamentary discussions on the reduction in value of the Indian Rupee and any Bills passed on the subject.
questions: Details of discussion held on reduction in the value of the Indian Rupee vis-a-vis other currencies in Lok Sabha, and details of any Bills passed on the subject.
response_summary: The reply clarified that no discussion specifically on Rupee depreciation was held under rule 193/184, though a general discussion on the economic situation was held on 27.8.2013, and directed the applicant to the Lok Sabha website/Debate search or the Parliament Library for further material; it also stated that no content-wise catalogue of Bills is maintained.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]

No. Reply: During the current Lok Sabha, no discussion under rule 193/184 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha has been held specifically on reduction in the value of India Rupee vis-a-vis other currencies. However, a discussion on the economic situation in the country was held in Lok Sabha under rule 193 on 27.8.2013. Details regarding discussion on reduction in value of Indian Rupee against other currencies in House during the 15th Lok Sabha, (i.e. from 2009 to till date) during Zero Hour (Special Mention), Matters under Rule 377, Calling Attention, Adjournment Motion and Submission is available on the loksabha.nic.in - 'Debates' - 'Debate search' link. Tel no.011-23034778. He may consult the Debates and get requisite material photocopied @ Rs.1/- per page. He will be provided necessary assistance. As regards second part of the point regarding Bills passed on the subject, this Secretariat does not maintain any content-wise catalogue of Bills introduced in or passed by Lok Sabha. If the applicant wants information on any particular Bill on the subject, he may specify the title and year of the Bill.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application Dated: 9.3.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(353)/IC/17 dated 22.3.2017

1. Kindly provide the reason, whose idea was this for inclusion the artistic work portrait/images/scene as Mohenjodaro seal, Vedic Gurukul and Mahatma Gandhi etc. in the notification dated 26 Jan 1950 of the Constitution of India. | The information sought by the applicant could be located in a publication 'A brief note on the Calligraphy of the Constitution of India in English and Hindi' brought out by the Parliament Secretariat in June, 1950. Copies of the relevant pages are enclosed for information of the applicant.

[Enclosed publication excerpt - 'A Brief Note on the Calligraphy of the Constitution of India in English and Hindi', Parliament Secretariat: At the suggestion of Prof. K.T. Shah the question of calligraphy and artistic decoration and printing of the original authoritative copy of the Constitution of India was taken up. It was decided that the work should be started as early as possible and calligraphy should be completed by the 20th January, 1950 and the work of illumination and decoration of the calligraphed pages may continue even after that date till it is completed. The matter to be calligraphed consisted of about 300 pages of 16 1/2"x22", each page containing about 40 lines. It was also proposed to use parchment paper of the size of 14"x18" and a margin of 2 1/2" was to be left at the top and the sides for illumination work and of 4" at the bottom. The rest of the space in the middle of the sheet was to be covered by the calligraphist. The cover was to bear the seal and emblem of the Union with a description in general and concise terms of the contents of the manuscript. At the suggestion of Shri Krishna Kripalani the President wrote to Shri Nandalal Bose of the Santiniketan asking if he would undertake the work of supervision and decoration and illumination of the calligraphed authenticated copy of the Constitution. Shri Nandalal Bose agreed to the President's request but suggested that it would not be possible to make designs based on historical subjects as suggested by the President, owing to shortage of space in the margin, and in the alternative agreed to make ornamental designs covering the whole period of Indian civilization. A decision was also taken to Photo-print the calligraphed Constitution bearing signatures of Members at the end.]
response_full_text: The information sought by the applicant could be located in a publication 'A brief note on the Calligraphy of the Constitution of India in English and Hindi' brought out by the Parliament Secretariat in June, 1950. Copies of the relevant pages are enclosed for information of the applicant, describing how, at the suggestion of Prof. K.T. Shah, the calligraphy and artistic decoration of the Constitution was taken up, and how Shri Nandalal Bose of Santiniketan was engaged, at the suggestion of Shri Krishna Kripalani, to supervise the decoration and illumination, ultimately creating ornamental designs covering the whole period of Indian civilization.

title: RTI on austerity measures and Parliamentary Committee study tours
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought detailed information on the Union government's austerity drive as applicable to the Lok Sabha Secretariat, and on rules and details of study tours undertaken by Parliamentary Committees.
questions: Is it true that an austerity-drive has been initiated at behest of Union government?
Is Lok Sabha covered by the said austerity-drive?
Date when the said austerity-drive came into force, mentioning also if some time-limit/date is fixed to return to normalcy in expenses.
Complete and detailed information on steps taken at Lok Sabha and its Secretariat towards measures to induce austerity to cut down expenses.

Complete and detailed information on rules towards expenses under various heads like also including Travelling allowance, travelling rules, Rules for boarding and lodging etc mentioning also rules about travel by Air India or private airlines, stay in government guest-houses, ITDC hotels or private hotels etc.

Complete and detailed information on various study-tours (separately for each tour) made by different Parliamentary committees ever since present Lok Sabha came into existence; Details may also include names (with parties) of members of study-groups, dates of tours, expenses under different heads, purpose of study tours, places visited, mode of travel mentioning also class of travel and name of airliner, place of stay mentioning also room-class, room-rent, name of hotel/guest-house etc and all other available details
Is there any rule whereby such study-tours may only be allowed by Air India flights for destinations covered by this Airliner?
If yes, please provide details mentioning also occasions when the rule had to be bypassed giving related correspondence/file-Notings/Documents etc on bypassing such rules.
Is there any rule whereby stay of members of study groups is allowed only in government guest-houses, lTDC hotels and other such places relating to public-authorities?
If yes, please provide details mentioning also occasions when the rule had to be bypassed giving related correspondence/file-Notings/documents etc on bypassing such rules.
Are austerity-measures applicable to study-tours undertaken by Parliamentary committees?

If yes, please provide details mentioning also if some exemption in this regard was sought together with action taken on exemption sought together with complete correspondence/documents/fiIe Notings etc.
Is there a system to present study-report prepared on basis of study made by such study groups?
Complete and detailed information on procedure to take action on such study-reports.
Was there any occasion when study-report was not submitted?
If yes, please provide details mentioning also action taken for not submitting such study reports together with complete correspondence/documents/file-Notings etc.
Any other related information.
File-Notings on movement of this RTI petition also.
response_summary: The Secretariat declined to answer opinion-style queries about the austerity drive, enclosed relevant circulars on austerity measures and Air India travel rules, and explained the rules on guest-house/hotel stay for Parliamentary Committee study tours, confirming a system exists for preparing and presenting study-tour reports to Committee Chairpersons, with file notings on the RTI petition's own movement enclosed.

title: Reply on Anti-Cow slaughter bill, Budget timing and soft drinks ban
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought information on a proposed Anti-Cow slaughtering Act, the timing of Budget presentation, and the reasons for banning soft drinks in Parliament House Complex canteens.
questions: Whether a Government Bill titled 'Anti-Cow slaughtering Act' has been introduced in Lok Sabha
Details/history of the timing of presentation of the General Budget and Railway Budget in Lok Sabha
Reason for banning the sale of soft drinks in the canteens of Parliament House Complex
response_summary: The Secretariat confirmed no Bill titled 'Anti-Cow slaughtering Act' has been introduced in Lok Sabha, explained the history and current practice of presenting the General Budget at 11 A.M. since 2001 (changed from 17.00 hrs prior to 1998) and the practice for the Railway Budget, and stated that soft drinks were banned in Parliament House Complex canteens based on Centre for Science and Environment findings on pesticide residues.
extracted_text:
Name of the Appellant: [Applicant]
Application dated nil
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1176)/IC/13

1. As per the records of the Division concerned, no Government Bill titled 'Anti-Cow slaughtering Act' has been introduced in Lok Sabha.
2. The Budget is presented to the Lok Sabha on such day as the President may direct. By convention, the General Budget is presented on the last working day of February each year. Earlier, till the year 1998, Budget used to be presented at 17.00 hrs. However, in the year 2001, the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs requested the Hon'ble Speaker that the General Budget for 2001-2002 be presented at 11 A.M. The Proposal of the Government was acceded to and accordingly the Budget for 2001-2002 was presented at 11 A.M. on 28 February, 2001. Since 2001, the General Budget continues to be presented at 11 A.M. As per past practice, the Railway Budget is usually presented after Question Hour and disposal of formal items of Business, if any, listed for the day.
3. The decision to ban the sale of soft drinks in the canteens of Parliament House Complex was taken on the basis of the findings of the Centre for Science and Environment regarding the presence of pesticide residues in branded soft drinks.
response_full_text:
1. No Government Bill titled 'Anti-Cow slaughtering Act' has been introduced in Lok Sabha as per records of the Division concerned.
2. The Budget is presented to the Lok Sabha on such day as the President may direct; by convention the General Budget is presented on the last working day of February. Until 1998 the Budget was presented at 17.00 hrs; since 2001 (on request of the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs, acceded to by the Speaker) it has been presented at 11 A.M., beginning with the 2001-2002 Budget presented on 28 February 2001. The Railway Budget is usually presented after Question Hour and disposal of formal items of business.
3. The decision to ban sale of soft drinks in Parliament House Complex canteens was based on findings of the Centre for Science and Environment regarding pesticide residues in branded soft drinks.

title: Reply on Bhojpuri language bill, Library Committee and House language rules
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought information on questions raised by MPs, a bill to include Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule, book procurement for the Parliament Library, and rules on languages used in House proceedings.
questions: Details of questions raised by MPs along with replies
Information available on Lok Sabha debates/debate search
Whether any Government Bill to insert Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule was introduced or passed during the Fourteenth Session (Monsoon Session), 2013
Whether any Government or Private Member's Bill to insert Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule is pending in Lok Sabha
Procurement of regional-language books for the Parliament Library as per Library Committee directions
Rules regarding the language of business in the House and the procedure for members speaking in languages other than Hindi/English
response_summary: The Secretariat directed the applicant to the Lok Sabha website for MP questions and debate records; confirmed no Government Bill on Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule was introduced/passed in the Fourteenth Session but noted three pending Private Members' Bills on the subject; described the Library Committee's book procurement practice; and explained the constitutional and procedural rules (Article 120, Direction 115B) governing languages used in House proceedings, including available interpretation facilities.
extracted_text:
Name of the Appellant: [Applicant]
Letter No. 1(1171)/IC/13

1. Details of questions raised by MPs along with replies thereto are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. www.parliamentofindia.nic.in/ and http://loksabha.nic.in/. The applicant is advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.
2. Information is available on Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in - 'Debates' - 'Debate search'. You are advised to access information from the above website link.
3. No Government Bill seeking to insert Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution was introduced or passed during the Fourteenth Session (Monsoon Session), 2013. Private Members' Business (Bills) was not transacted during the Fourteenth Session (Monsoon Session) of Lok Sabha.
4. No Government Bill seeking to insert Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution is pending in Lok Sabha. Three Private Members' Bills seeking to include Bhojpuri language in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution have been introduced by Sharvashri Om Prakash Yadav, J.P. Agarwal and Dr. Ajay Kumar, M.Ps. during the current Lok Sabha (15LS) and are presently pending. Except the Bill introduced by Shri Om Prakash Yadav, M.P. the other two Bills have been placed under category 'A' by the Committee on Private Members' Bills and Resolutions and are being included in every ballot of Private Members' Bills held under rule 27 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha (copy of rule 27 enclosed). As such, the inter-se priority of Private Members' Bills for discussion in the House is determined by ballot. A list of pending Private Members' Bills pertaining to Bhojpuri language is enclosed.
5. As per the directions of the Library Committee mentioned in the Procedure and Practice of the Branch, books in various regional languages mentioned in the 8th Schedule of the Constitution of India are procured to strengthen the regional collection of the Parliament Library. A para in Bulletin Part II of Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha is also published during each session requesting Hon'ble Members to suggest important and valuable books in English, Hindi and Regional language for the Library.
6. As per Article 120 of the Constitution of India, the business of the House shall be transacted either in Hindi or in English subject to the provisions under Article 348. However, Members who cannot express themselves in either of the two languages can, with the permission of the Speaker, address the House in any of the languages in their mother tongue. As per direction 115B(2) of the Directions by the Speaker a member desirous of making a speech in any language other than Hindi, English and the languages (Assamese, Bengali, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, Oriya, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu or Urdu) shall furnish to the officer at the Table or the Parliamentary Notice Office, three authenticated copies of the translation of his speech in Hindi or English in advance for use of the interpreters and later incorporation in the official report of the proceedings of the House. Provided that where a member does not furnish such translation, the fact shall be mentioned in the official report with the remark that the member did not furnish a translation of his speech in Hindi or English. However, at present simultaneous interpretation facility in English/Hindi is available in Lok Sabha for speeches made in Assamese, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam, Manipuri, Marathi, Maithili, Nepali, Odia, Punjabi, Sanskrit, Tamil, Telugu and Urdu languages.
response_full_text: 1. Details of questions raised by MPs along with replies are available on Lok Sabha website. 2. Debate information available on loksabha.nic.in Debates - Debate search. 3. No Government Bill on Bhojpuri language in Eighth Schedule introduced or passed during Fourteenth Session 2013; no Private Members' Business transacted that session. 4. No Government Bill pending; three Private Members' Bills by Sharvashri Om Prakash Yadav, J.P. Agarwal and Dr. Ajay Kumar, M.Ps. are pending, prioritized by ballot under rule 27. 5. Regional language books procured per Library Committee directions; requests for book suggestions published in Bulletin Part II each session. 6. Article 120 governs language of House business (Hindi/English); Direction 115B(2) governs speeches in other languages, with simultaneous interpretation available for several regional languages.

आवेदक का नाम: श्री [आवेदक]
आवेदन की तिथि: 08.02.2017
संदर्भ: लोक सभा सचिवालय पत्र सं. 1(215)/आईसी/17 दिनांक 06.03.2017
बिंदु 1. जिस धातु से प्रतिमा बनाई गई उसका नाम और प्रकृति।
उत्तर: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर की प्रतिमा वर्ष 1967 में संसद भवन परिसर में स्थापित की गई थी। मांगी गई सूचना सचिवालय की संबंधित शाखा अर्थात् सामान्य कार्य शाखा के रिकार्ड में उपलब्ध नहीं है।
बिंदु 2. प्रतिमा की ऊंचाई और चौड़ाई।
उत्तर: संसद भवन परिसर में स्थापित प्रतिमाओं का माप केवल उनकी ऊंचाई के संबंध में ही उपलब्ध है। डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर की प्रतिमा की ऊंचाई 3.66 मीटर है।
बिंदु 3. प्रतिमा पर हुआ व्यय।
उत्तर: प्रतिमा की लागत का वहन संबंधित प्रतिमा के दानदाता द्वारा किया जाता है। प्रतिमा तैयार करने हेतु मूर्तिकार का प्रबंध भी दानदाता (डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर स्मारक समिति) द्वारा किया गया।
बिंदु 4. प्रतिमा का स्थान, प्रतिमा का मूर्तिकार, उद्घाटन की तिथि, फोटो।
उत्तर: प्रतिमा को संसद भवन में लोक सभा मार्ग के समीप स्थित बाहरी लॉन में स्थापित किया गया है। प्रतिमा को श्री बी.वी. वाघ द्वारा तैयार किया गया था। इस प्रतिमा का अनावरण भारत के तत्कालीन राष्ट्रपति डॉ. एस. राधाकृष्णन द्वारा 02.04.1967 को किया गया था। डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर के चित्र की छायाप्रति संलग्न है (अनुबंध)।
बिंदु 5. 14 अप्रैल को बाबा साहेब अंबेडकर की प्रतिमा के नीचे रखे जाने वाले चित्र के चित्रकार का नाम; चित्र प्रथम बार वहां कब रखा गया था।
उत्तर: संसद भवन में डॉ. बाबा साहेब अंबेडकर के जन्म/पुण्यतिथि समारोहों का आयोजन सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय द्वारा किया जाता है। 20.02.2017 को सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय को भी अंतरित किया गया।
response_full_text: डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर की प्रतिमा वर्ष 1967 में संसद भवन परिसर में स्थापित की गई थी; धातु संबंधी सूचना संबंधित शाखा के रिकार्ड में उपलब्ध नहीं है। प्रतिमा की ऊंचाई 3.66 मीटर है। प्रतिमा की लागत और मूर्तिकार का प्रबंध दानदाता (डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर स्मारक समिति) द्वारा किया गया। प्रतिमा संसद भवन में लोक सभा मार्ग के समीप बाहरी लॉन में स्थापित है, इसे श्री बी.वी. वाघ ने तैयार किया और डॉ. एस. राधाकृष्णन द्वारा 02.04.1967 को अनावरण किया गया; चित्र संलग्न है। जन्म/पुण्यतिथि समारोहों का आयोजन सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय द्वारा किया जाता है और संबंधित बिंदु उस मंत्रालय को भी अंतरित किया गया।

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application Dated 18.1.14
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No 216 dated 5.3.14
Point 1. This RTI application is regarding the IT Audit Report (PA 18) on the working of Unreserved Ticketing System being followed in Indian Railways done for the year 2006-07, assessed during 2007-08 and submitted to the Parliament during June 2009. Query: The date on which and the person to whom the above Audit Report is submitted.
Reply: The Audit Report (Performance Audit) No. 18 of 2008 on Union Government (Railways) – Information Technology Audit was presented to Parliament on 24th October, 2008.
Point 2. Query: The procedure to be followed on the Audit Report in taking it up for discussion. Is there any time limit fixed for taking it for deliberations/discussions by Public Accounts Committee?
Reply: The Audit Reports tabled in the Parliament undergo a selection process for detailed examination and Report by the Public Accounts Committee. The subjects are selected for examination by the Committee based on their relative importance and the time available with the Committee. There is no fixed time limit for taking up a particular subject for deliberations/discussions by the Committee.
Point 3. Query: If Audit Report is taken for deliberations by the Public Accounts Committee and arrived at a conclusion and report submitted, please supply me a copy of the report submitted by it to the parliament.
Reply: The Public Accounts Committee have not presented any report on IT Audit Report (PA 18) on the working of Unreserved Ticketing System being followed in Indian Railways done for the year 2006-07 and assessed during 2007-08.
Point 4. Query: Is it necessary for the concerned department/Ministry to submit the parawise remarks for the consideration of the Public Accounts Committee and please specify the time limit within which the parawise remarks should be submitted.
Reply: Yes, the Ministries/Departments concerned are required to furnish parawise Remedial/corrective Action Taken Notes on the Observations of the Audit contained in their Report within a period of 4 months from the date of presentation of the Report to Parliament. Further, they are required to furnish Action Taken Notes on the Observations/Recommendations of the Committee contained in their Report, if any, within a period of six months from the date of presentation of the Report to Parliament.
Point 5. Query: If the parawise remarks are submitted by the Department of Railways/ Railway Board kindly supply me the copy of the same.
Reply: Documents/Notes furnished to the Public Accounts Committee by the Ministries/Department are treated as confidential and cannot be divulged.
Point 6. Query: Kindly specify the kind of action that can be taken by the Parliament or Public Accounts Committee against the Department/Ministry for not submitting its report in time.
Reply: This can be reflected in the Action Taken Report concerned of the Committee. The representatives of the Department concerned may be summoned to explain the reasons for same before the Committee. The Committee may recommend for fixing responsibility for delay in submission of replies.
Point 7. Query: As per the section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act, it is made mandatory for the Public Authorities to productively disclose the CAG and PAC Reports and the Action Taken Report, in their websites under suo moto disclosures. Kindly specify the date before which these will be uploaded in your website.
Reply: The Public Accounts Committee Reports (both Original and Action Taken Reports) are duly uploaded after they are presented to the Parliament. As far as CAG Reports are concerned, the factual information may be obtained from the Office of Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
response_full_text: The Audit Report (Performance Audit) No. 18 of 2008 on Union Government (Railways) – Information Technology Audit was presented to Parliament on 24th October, 2008. The Audit Reports tabled in the Parliament undergo a selection process for detailed examination and Report by the Public Accounts Committee based on relative importance and available time; there is no fixed time limit. The Public Accounts Committee have not presented any report on this IT Audit Report. Ministries/Departments concerned are required to furnish parawise Remedial/corrective Action Taken Notes within 4 months of presentation of the Report to Parliament, and Action Taken Notes on Committee Recommendations within six months. Documents/Notes furnished to the Public Accounts Committee by Ministries/Departments are treated as confidential and cannot be divulged. Non-submission in time can be reflected in the Action Taken Report; departmental representatives may be summoned and the Committee may recommend fixing responsibility for delay. Public Accounts Committee Reports are duly uploaded after presentation to Parliament; CAG Report factual information may be obtained from the Office of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

title: Reply on Procedure and Status of Statue Installations in Parliament Complex
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought information on pending requests, selection procedure, deciding committee, pipeline proposals, and the total number of statues installed in Parliament House Complex.
questions: How many requests/applications for installing statues within the Parliament Complex pending with Lok Sabha Secretariat for approval. Please provide copies of these requests or applications.
What is the procedure to select and install a statue within Parliament Complex. Please give details about process right from the time the application is received.

Is there a parliamentary committee which decides on which portraits or statues should be put up where? If yes, When did the committee meet for the last time? Please provide minutes of meeting of same meeting.

Is there any proposal which is currently in pipeline, for which the location and the sculptor has been decided? If yes please give details in brief about the subject of the sculpture and sculptor to whom the project has been given.
How many statues at present are installed within the Parliament Complex? Please provide a list of these, along with date when they were installed and on whose application were they installed.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated no new statue proposals are pending due to space constraints, described the Joint Committee on Installation of Portraits/Statues process headed by the Speaker, noted the Committee last met on 23.11.2009 with minutes available on payment of copying fee, confirmed no proposal currently in the pipeline, and stated 49 statues are presently installed with a list available on payment of copying fee.

subject: The applicant sought details of the ad hoc committee that inquired into MP Shri Bhagwant Mann's videography of parliament security, the committee's report, and any resulting action.
questions: Provide names of Members of the Committee which was constituted to inquire the case of videography of parliament security apparatus by Shri Bhagwant Mann, MP from Aam Aadmi Party.

What action was taken against Shri Bhagwant Mann, MP from Aam Aadmi Party after submission of investigation report?
Whether any other Member has been found to be involved in a similar activity?

subject: The applicant sought detailed information on the updating, maintenance, and Section 4(1)(b) disclosure practices of the Lok Sabha website.

Frequency of updating the website, etc;

Where can one report in case of broken links and obsolete information on the website;

Copy of acknowledged receipt of letters submitted to NIC responsible for uploading information on behalf of our Lok Sabha, etc. since 2005 to till date;

response_summary: The Secretariat explained that website updating is a continuous, decentralised process carried out by concerned Sections/Branches, that Section 4(1)(b) disclosures are already hosted on the Lok Sabha website, and that NIC (which hosts but does not author content) holds no separate correspondence records.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: Shri [Applicant]
Application dated 28.08.2013 (Received on 09.09.2013)
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(1136)/IC/13

Sl.No. of the original Queries in the RTI Application / Replies:
1. When was the last time Lok Sabha website was updated - Updating of information in the Lok Sabha website is carried out by the various Sections/Branches in the Secretariat. Updating of website is an ongoing and continuous process.
2. Contact details of MPs of both Houses: (a) when last updated; (b) mobile numbers of MPs not on website - Contact details of MPs containing their local as well as permanent addresses and contact numbers are provided in the websites of both Houses respectively. Last time the contact details of MPs of Lok Sabha was updated in January 2013 in the Printed Form. Information about members on website is updated as and when a change is communicated. Contact numbers of MPs (Landline or Mobile or both) are provided as per the information given by them to the Secretariat.
3. Frequency of updating the website, etc - Updating of website is done by the concerned Sections/Branches regularly as and when any new information is available.
4. Details of last 10 updates done - Updation is not done centrally. However, when Lok Sabha is in session, information w.r.t. List of Business, Bulletins and Debates are updated/uploaded on a daily basis.
5. Who is responsible for updating the website - The concerned Sections and Branches are responsible for uploading and updating the information pertaining to them directly.
6. Where can one report broken links and obsolete information on the website - For any query or feedback, one can go to the 'Feedback' link on the Lok Sabha Homepage.
7. Details of information uploaded under section 4(1)(b) of RTI Act, and when uploaded lastly - Information pertaining to Organization Chart, Work allocation to officers, Section-wise Organization of Branches/Divisions, Brief Functioning of Lok Sabha Secretariat, Directory of officials, remuneration paid to employees, various Rules, Orders, Notifications applicable are already available on the website under RTI -> Information Handbook -> Chapter (v). Each branch is responsible for uploading and maintaining information as per Section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act. The applicant is advised to visit www.loksabha.nic.in
8. List of officials responsible for preparing information as per Section 4(1)(b) of RTI Act and uploading on website.
9. Copy of acknowledged receipt of letters submitted to NIC responsible for uploading information since 2005 - NIC has designed and hosted the website. Contents are not uploaded by NIC. Hence, no such record is available.
10. Copy of acknowledged receipt of letters submitted to A.P. response_full_text: Updating of information in the Lok Sabha website is carried out by the various Sections/Branches in the Secretariat as an ongoing and continuous process. Contact details of MPs are provided on the websites of both Houses; last updated in printed form in January 2013 and updated as and when changes are communicated. Website updating frequency depends on availability of new information with concerned Sections/Branches; during session, List of Business, Bulletins and Debates are updated daily. Feedback on broken links may be given via the 'Feedback' link on the Homepage. Information under Section 4(1)(b) of the RTI Act (Organization Chart, work allocation, Directory of officials, remuneration, Rules/Orders/Notifications) is already available on the website under RTI -> Information Handbook -> Chapter (v); each Branch is responsible for uploading and maintaining such information. NIC has only designed and hosted the website and does not upload content, hence no separate acknowledgement record exists with NIC. Application dated 6.02.2017
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(191)/IC/17 dated 7.03.2017

1. Point raised: List of MP who never attended Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha in last 4 sessions of Parliament in both Houses.
Reply: Branch concerned deals with the attendance of members of Lok Sabha. Regarding the absence of members the applicant is informed, as per article 101(4) of the Constitution of India, 'If for a period of sixty days a member of either House of Parliament is without permission of the House absent from all meetings thereof, the House may declare his seat vacant'. The Committee on Absence of Members from the sittings of the House consider and examine cases of leave of absence of members from the sittings of the House. Detailed information regarding members who have applied for leave of absence and have been granted the same by the Lok Sabha during the 16th Lok Sabha is available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the heading Committees->Other Parliamentary Standing Committees->Committee on Absence of Members from the Sittings of the House->Reports presented->First to Seventh Report respectively. As far as attendance of member is concerned, an attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members->Attendance of Members->Member-wise Attendance-> All Members respectively.

2. Point raised: Please provide the attendance percentage of all members of Parliament in both Houses of Parliament.
3. Point raised: Please provide the website in which the details from which overall attendance of member of Parliament can be seen.

4. Point raised: Is Rajya Sabha TV and Lok Sabha TV under Doordarshan or a private firm? Are the 2 TV Channels entirely operated by private agency or by the Government assigned authority?
Reply: Lok Sabha TV is a 24 hour dedicated Television Channel owned and operated by the Lok Sabha Secretariat.

6. Point raised: What is the procedure to visit parliament as visitor
Reply: The procedure to watch the proceedings of the Lok Sabha for a common man is that he has to fill an application form available at CPIC/Reception Office (Lok Sabha)/official website of Lok Sabha (www.parliamentofindia.nic.in), duly signed by an Hon'ble MP (Lok Sabha). The proceeding can be watched during the session period subject to availability of seats in public gallery.

7. Point raised: Is there any online portal to apply as visitor to Parliament
Reply: There is no online portal

8. Point raised: Is compulsory to get recommendation from any MP to visit Parliament.
Reply: Yes, the recommendation of Hon'ble MP is must.

9. Point raised: How much benefits are given to MP for travel purposes in the form of air and train services. How many times can they travel free of cost per year
Reply: Air travel and train travel is provided to a MP as per the provisions contained in the Salary, Allowances and Pension of MP Act, 1954 and Rules made thereunder. Copy of the same Act may be downloaded from the website of Ministry of Parliament Affairs i.e. http://mpa.nic.in/MPA/act.aspx.

10. Point raised: How much did the Govt. of India subsidise the travel of MP to attend Parliament.
Reply: Such information is not maintained.

11. Point raised: How many times have MP taken subsidy but never visited in the last 2 sessions of the Parliament
Reply: -do-

12. Point raised: How much is the rate of food in the Parliament Canteen for different food items
Reply: The information is available on Parliament website http://164.100.47.194/loksabha/writereaddata/our%20parliament/uploading.pdf or www.loksabha.nic.in --> About Parliament--> Parliament Canteens for related information.

13. Point raised: How much is spent as fuel allowance for MP in a year
Reply: Fuel allowances is not given to any MP

14. Point raised: Is there any penalty for blocking question hour from taking place
Reply: No.

15. Point raised: If an MP doesn't attend Parliament what benefits will they lose in the travel allowances.
Reply: As per the provision contained in the MSA Act, train journey or air journey are provided to a MP for attending Parliament Session. If he does not attend the Parliament Session, he will not be provided travel allowance and DA for the said Parliament Session.

16. Point raised: Can an MP reach to Delhi with travel allowance but not attend Parliament
Reply: Such information is not maintained.

17. Point raised: In which portal can all the Questions asked in Question Hour in both Houses be accessed online in document format. Please provide the exact website URL.
Reply: The Questions asked by Members of Parliament in Lok Sabha along with their replies are available on the Lok Sabha website i.e. loksabha.nic.in under the heading 'Questions' or directly through the following link: http://164.100.47.194/Loksabha/Questions/qsearch15.aspx. The applicant may go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.
response_full_text: Branch concerned deals with the attendance of members of Lok Sabha. As per article 101(4) of the Constitution of India, if a member is absent for 60 days without permission the House may declare the seat vacant. The Committee on Absence of Members considers such cases; leave-of-absence reports are on the Lok Sabha website. An attendance Register is maintained (except for the Speaker, Deputy Speaker, PM and Ministers); attendance details are online. Lok Sabha TV is a 24 hour dedicated Television Channel owned and operated by the Lok Sabha Secretariat. To visit Parliament, a visitor must fill an application form, duly signed by an Hon'ble MP; there is no online portal and an MP's recommendation is mandatory. Air and train travel is provided to MPs under the Salary, Allowances and Pension of MP Act, 1954; the amount of subsidy or number of unused free trips is not maintained. Parliament Canteen food rates are available on the Parliament website. No fuel allowance is given to any MP. There is no penalty for blocking question hour. If an MP does not attend a Parliament session, he will not be provided travel allowance and DA for that session. Questions asked by Members of Parliament in Lok Sabha along with replies are available via the Lok Sabha website's Questions search.

title: RTI on suspension/withdrawal of MPs from Lok Sabha under Rules 373-375
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought details of instances of member withdrawal/suspension from the House under Rules 373, 374, 374A and 375 during the 15th Lok Sabha and earlier, and about interruptions/adjournments; part of the request was exempted under Section 7(9) due to volume of records.
questions: During the Fifteenth Lok Sabha (2009 onwards till date), instances of members directed to withdraw from the House under rule 373, suspended under rule 374, or automatically suspended under rule 374A, and details from earlier Lok Sabhas.
Discretion of the Speaker/presiding officer regarding invoking rule 375.
Information regarding adjournment of the House due to interruptions during the 13th, 14th and 15th Lok Sabhas and earlier periods.
Query regarding invoking of rule 349 and related rules by the Speaker.
Accountability of the Speaker/presiding officer for maintaining order in the House.
response_summary: The Secretariat provided a list of suspensions during the 15th Lok Sabha under rules 374 and 374A, noting no withdrawal occurred under rule 373; it invoked Section 7(9) to decline compiling historical records back to the 1st Lok Sabha, advised consulting Lok Sabha debates/website for interruption data, and clarified rules 349, 373-375 are matters of Speaker's discretion not maintained as accountability records.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Annexure to letter No. 1(1124)/IC/13

1. During the Fifteenth Lok Sabha (2009 onwards till date), no member has been directed to withdraw from the House under rule 373 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha. There is one instance when 8 members were suspended for 4 days from the sittings of the House under rule 374. There are two instances when the Chair invoked the provisions of rule 374A of automatic suspension of members from five sittings of the House for the first time since it was incorporated in the Rules. A list of the details of the suspensions mentioned above is enclosed (Annexure). There have been numerous instances of withdrawal and suspension under rules 373 and 374 from the 1st Lok Sabha till the 14th Lok Sabha. However, if the applicant desires, he may be requested to visit the concerned branch after seeking prior appointment [Sh. Uttam Chandra Ray, Legislative Officer (Table Office-B) contact no. 23034860/23073287] and go through the records. Reasons for refusal/delay: Information regarding the numerous instances of withdrawal and suspension of the members from the House beginning from the first Lok Sabha onwards is not readily available and entails examination of multiple sources of information which are available in the records. This would disproportionately divert the resources of the Branch and hence, exemption is sought under rule 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005.
2. It is entirely the discretion of the Speaker or the person presiding over the House at given moment to decide whether the situation warrants invoking the provision of rule 375. There are no conventions, rules or guidelines in this regard.
3. The applicant has not specifically asked for information regarding adjournment of House due to interruption. But from the application it can be presumed that he wants information in this regard. Information pertaining to adjournment of sittings due to interruptions during 13th, 14th and 15th Lok Sabhas (from 1998 to till date) is available on Lok Sabha website. As per Section 7(9) of RTI Act, 2005, an information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority, and to search for information over a period of 60 years since 1952 would divert a sizeable amount of time and manpower. Regarding information prior to 1998, Lok Sabha debates (a priced publication circulated to libraries including the Parliament Library and State Legislature libraries) contain the full details; the applicant may be advised to consult the same for the period 1952-1998. Regarding reasons for interruptions, the concerned branch is not in a position to maintain such information as members of different parties raise slogans simultaneously, making it infeasible to record details.
4. Rule 349 cannot be invoked as it merely lays down rules to be observed by members and does not provide penal powers to the Speaker. It is entirely within the discretion of the person presiding over the House to decide whether to invoke provisions of rule 373, 374, 374A or 375. Rule 374 was invoked once on 24.04.2012 and Rule 374A was invoked twice, i.e. on 23.08.2013 and 02.09.2013, during the 15th Lok Sabha.
5. The Speaker or the person presiding over the House at a given moment is responsible for maintaining order in the House. It is the decision of that person whether to invoke provisions of relevant rules. Secretariat is not in a position to reply to query about accountability.
response_full_text: No member was directed to withdraw under rule 373 during the 15th Lok Sabha; 8 members were suspended for 4 days under rule 374 in one instance, and rule 374A (automatic suspension) was invoked twice. A list of suspensions is enclosed. Exemption under Section 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005 is sought for compiling historical instances since the 1st Lok Sabha as it would disproportionately divert Branch resources; the applicant may instead visit the concerned branch to peruse records. Invoking rule 375 is entirely the Speaker's/presiding officer's discretion with no set conventions. Information on adjournments due to interruptions for the 13th-15th Lok Sabhas is available on the Lok Sabha website; for periods before 1998, Lok Sabha debates (a priced publication) may be consulted, and reasons for interruptions are not maintained given their spontaneous nature. Rule 349 lays down conduct rules only and confers no penal power on the Speaker; rule 374 was invoked once (24.04.2012) and rule 374A twice (23.08.2013, 02.09.2013) in the 15th Lok Sabha. The Speaker/presiding officer decides on invoking relevant rules to maintain order; the Secretariat cannot reply to queries about accountability.

Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]
Application dated: 29.01.2016
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No. 1(187)/IC/16 dated 19.02.2016

1. What all questions were asked by the below mentioned Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) during their tenure. -- The questions asked by all the Members of Parliament of Lok Sabha from November, 1999 onwards alongwith their replies are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qsearch15.aspx. The applicant may go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information. The information prior to November, 1999 is also available in the Parliament Library. Applicant may visit the Parliament Library by contacting Sh. S. P. Roy Choudhary, Addl. Director Tel. No. 011-23034347 or depute someone to cull out the desired information. All necessary assistance will be provided at their end.
2. What was the percentage of their attendance in Lok Sabha. -- Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon’ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance - All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. The attendance details of members prior to fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website. The information is available in the records of the Branch. The applicant may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally peruse the records available in the Branch concerned. For this purpose, he may contact, Legislative Officer (TOB), Ph. No.23034858.
3. How many of them have criminal cases against them and what all are the cases against them? Please mention the IPC sections under which they are booked. -- No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to such public authorities.
response_full_text: 1. The questions asked by all the Members of Parliament of Lok Sabha from November, 1999 onwards alongwith their replies are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qsearch15.aspx. The applicant may go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information. The information prior to November, 1999 is also available in the Parliament Library. 2. Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. An Attendance Register is maintained for members to sign against their names; details of signing/not signing during all sessions of the 15th Lok Sabha are available on www.loksabha.nic.in. Attendance details prior to the fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded and may be perused at the Secretariat. 3. No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha, nor the sections under which they are charged, is maintained in the Secretariat; the query has been forwarded to the Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice.

department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: आवेदक ने वर्ष 1952 से अब तक लोक सभा के लिए निर्वाचित हुए बिहार के बेलदार समुदाय के लोगों की संख्या और उनका विवरण मांगा।
questions: 1952 से अब तक लोक सभा के लिए निर्वाचित हुए बिहार के बेलदार समुदाय के लोगों की संख्या बताएं। कृपया उनके नाम, पते और वर्ष सहित ब्यौरे की प्रमाणित प्रति उपलब्ध कराएं।
response_summary: सचिवालय ने बताया कि सदस्य परिचय प्रकोष्ठ लोक सभा सदस्यों से संबंधित जाति आधारित सूचना का रख-रखाव नहीं करता, परंतु आरक्षित (अजा/अजजा) निर्वाचन क्षेत्रों का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले सदस्यों की जानकारी लोक सभा वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है, और आवेदक को उक्त वेबसाइट देखने की सलाह दी गई।

क्रम सं.1 मांगी गई जानकारी: 1952 से अब तक लोक सभा के लिए निर्वाचित हुए बिहार के बेलदार समुदाय के लोगों की संख्या बताएं। कृपया उनके नाम, पते और वर्ष सहित ब्यौरे की प्रमाणित प्रति उपलब्ध कराएं।

department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought details about the Lok Sabha building's construction, cost, land area, municipal jurisdiction, rooms, telecom/internet connections, canteen, running costs, visitor access, and budget.

How much land occupied. How many building is there and provide the details

Lok Sabha building will come under any municipality

1. When Lok Sabha Building is constructed. Approximate construction cost details and life of Lok Sabha Building -- Reply: Transferred to Ministry of Urban Development.
2. How much land occupied. How many building is there and provide the details.
3. What is the minimum distance between Lok Sabha building and other public houses.
4. Lok Sabha building will come under any municipality -- Reply: New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC).
5. How many rooms are available in Lok Sabha -- Reply: Approximately 150 rooms.
6. Is there any telephone and internet connection. If so, provide the number of telephone and internet connection also bandwidth of internet -- Reply: Official direct line telephone connections and Wi-fi (Internet) under the administrative control of AN-II Branch are provided to the dignitaries and officers of Lok Sabha Secretariat in Parliament House Complex for official purpose. 149 nos. of direct line telephone have been provided; of these, 69 nos. have Wi-fi (internet) facility. Regarding list of food items and cost applicant may visit lok sabha website i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in.

1. | It appears that the applicant wants to know whether the provision of the Constitution regarding official languages, i.e. article 343, has been amended after a period of 15 years from the coming into force of the Constitution so as to extend the use of English for official purposes. It is to inform that article 343 provides, inter alia, that for a period of 15 years from the coming into force of the Constitution, the English language shall continue to be used for all official purposes of the Union. Parliament, by enacting the Official Languages Act, 1963 under clause (3)(a) of article 343 of the Constitution, has provided that the English language may, as from the appointed day, continue to be used in addition to Hindi, for the official purposes of the Union. response_full_text: 1. It appears that the applicant wants to know whether the provision of the Constitution regarding official languages, i.e. article 343, has been amended after a period of 15 years from the coming into force of the Constitution so as to extend the use of English for official purposes. Article 343 provides that for 15 years from commencement of the Constitution, English shall continue for official purposes; Parliament, via the Official Languages Act, 1963, provided that English may continue in addition to Hindi for official purposes of the Union. This point pertains to the Department of Official Language, Ministry of Home Affairs, to whom the application is being forwarded. Points 1 and 3 (relating to Supreme Court practice) were transferred under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act to the Supreme Court of India.

title: RTI on language rules and voice-voting procedure in Lok Sabha
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant asked about the constitutional/rule provisions governing the language used to conduct House business and the procedure for voice voting (Ayes/Noes) in Lok Sabha.
questions: Rules/provisions governing the language (Hindi/English) in which the business of the House is transacted
Rule/procedure under which the Speaker conducts voice voting (Ayes/Noes) in the House
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that under Article 120 of the Constitution the House's business is conducted in Hindi or English at the Presiding Officer's discretion (with simultaneous interpretation available for Eighth Schedule languages), and detailed Rule 367 governing voice voting, noting that the Hindi terms 'HAAN' and 'NAA' are used for Ayes and Noes.
extracted_text:
Annexure
Name of the Appellant: [Applicant]
Letter No. 1(1106)/IC/13
Sl. No. 1: As per Article 120 of the Constitution of India, the business of the House should be transacted by the Presiding Officer either in Hindi or in English as he/she may desire subject to the provision under Article 348. However, members who cannot express themselves in either of the two languages can, with the permission of Speaker, address the House in any of the languages in their mother tongue. At present simultaneous Interpretation facilities in English/Hindi are available in Lok Sabha for languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution.
Sl. No. 2: Rule 367 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provides the following: '(1) On the conclusion of a debate, the Speaker shall put the question and invite those who are in favour of the motion to say 'Aye' and those against the motion to say 'No'. (2) The Speaker shall then say: 'I think the Ayes (or the Noes, as the case may be) have it.' If the opinion is not challenged, he may say twice: 'The Ayes (or the Noes, as the case may be) have it' and the question before the House shall be determined accordingly.' The Hindi version of Rule 367 uses 'HAAN' for 'AYES' and 'NAA' for 'NOES'. As per article 120 of the Constitution, proceedings of the House are conducted by the Presiding Officers either in English or in Hindi as he/she may desire. There have been several instances when the person presiding over the House conducted the proceedings in Hindi at the time of voting and observed 'JO PRASTAV KE PAKSH MEIN HON HAAN KAHEN JO VIRODH MEIN HON NAA KAHEN'.
response_full_text: As per Article 120 of the Constitution of India, the business of the House should be transacted by the Presiding Officer either in Hindi or in English as he/she may desire subject to the provision under Article 348. However, members who cannot express themselves in either of the two languages can, with the permission of Speaker, address the House in any of the languages in their mother tongue. At present simultaneous Interpretation facilities in English/Hindi are available in Lok Sabha for languages included in the Eighth Schedule to the Constitution. Rule 367 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provides that on conclusion of a debate, the Speaker shall put the question and invite Ayes/Noes and declare the result. The Hindi version of Rule 367 uses 'HAAN' for 'AYES' and 'NAA' for 'NOES'.

Sl.No.1 - Point in Brief: Questions asked by the following Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) during their tenure in 15th Lok Sabha (List enclosed).
Reply: The questions asked by the concerned Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) during their tenure in 15th Lok Sabha along with their replies are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qsearch15.aspx. The applicant may go through the above website for obtaining the desired information.

Sl.No.2 - Point in Brief: What was the percentage of the attendance of the following members of Lok Sabha during their tenure in 15th Lok Sabha (List enclosed).
Reply: Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register during all sessions of the 15th Lok Sabha are available on the website of Lok Sabha under Members - Attendance of Members - Member-wise Attendance - All Members. The applicant may note that a member may have attended the sitting but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information.

Sl.No.3 - Point in Brief: How many of them have criminal cases against them and what all are the cases against them? Please mention the IPC sections under which they are booked.
Reply: No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to such public authorities.
response_full_text: Questions asked by MPs during their tenure in the 15th Lok Sabha along with replies are available on the Lok Sabha website (Qsearch15.aspx). Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain attendance on a percentage basis; an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers), and signing details for all sessions of the 15th Lok Sabha are on the Lok Sabha website under Members-Attendance. No information on criminal cases against former or sitting Members is maintained by the Secretariat, as there is no such requirement under the Rules of Procedure; the query, appearing to pertain to the Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, has been forwarded to them.

title: Duplicate RTI query on equal-pay judgment held not maintainable
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant asked whether the Lok Sabha Secretariat had taken cognizance of, and complied with, the Supreme Court's equal-pay-for-equal-work judgment (State of Punjab v. Jagjit Singh) in respect of ad hoc consultants.
questions: Has the Lok Sabha secretariat taken cognizance of Hon'ble Supreme Court judgement Civil Appeal No.213 of 2013 dated 26.10.2016 ordering equal pay for equal work;

Whether the principle of equal pay for equal work enshrined in Article 39(d) and 141 of the Constitution of India and the judgment delivered by the Hon. Supreme Court on 26.10.2016 in the case of State of Punjab and Others v/s Jagjit Singh and others is followed by Lok Sabha Secretariat in the case of consultants engaged on ad hoc basis;

If not the reasons therefor and also why Parliament of India which is the custodian of Constitution of India does not deem it fit to honor the spirit of the Constitution and the judgments of the apex court.
response_summary: The AN-I Branch stated that the information sought was a query, not information, and the Public Authority is not bound to answer queries under the RTI Act, 2005; no substantive answer was furnished.

1. A clear photocopy of any document containing the decision taken by the Hon'ble Speaker in relation to the post of the Leader of the Opposition in this House. -- A decision regarding recognition of the leader of a legislature party in Lok Sabha as the Leader of Opposition is taken on the basis of interpretation of following legal provisions as well as in the light of precedents: I. Directions by the Speaker — Direction 120: "The Speaker may recognize an association of members as a Parliamentary Party or Group for the purpose of functioning in the House and the decision of the Speaker shall be final." Direction 121: "In recognizing a Parliamentary Party or Group the Speaker shall take into consideration the following principles: (1) An association of members who propose to form a Parliamentary party: (j) shall have announced at the time of the general elections a distinct ideology and programme of Parliamentary work on which they have been returned to the House; (k) shall have an organization both inside and outside the House; and (l) shall have at least a strength equal to the quorum fixed to constitute a sitting of the House, that is one-tenth of the total number of members of the House." II. The Leaders and Chief Whips of Recognized Parties and Groups in Parliament (Facilities) Act, 1998 — Section 2: "In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires,- (a) 'recognized group' means,- (vii) In relation to the Council of States, every party which has a strength of not less than fifteen members and not more than twenty-four members in the council; (viii) In relation to the House of the People, every party which has a strength of not less than thirty members and not more than fifty-four members in the House; (b) 'recognized group' means,- (vii) In relation to the Council of States, every party which has a strength of not less than twenty-five members in the council; (viii) In relation to the House of the People, every party which has a strength of not less than fifty-five members in the House; III. The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977 — Section 2 Definition: In this Act, 'Leader of the Opposition', in relation to either House of Parliament, means that member of the Council of States or the House of the People, as the case may be, who is, for the time being, the Leader in the House of the party in Opposition to the Government having the greatest numerical strength and recognized as such by the Chairman of the Council of States or the Speaker of the House of the People, as the case may be. Relevant excerpts from the Directions by the Speaker and above-stated Act are enclosed. The copies of relevant acts can be obtained from the website of the concerned ministry. A complete set of the file notings, legal opinions, all communications to and from Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha regarding recognition of the Leader of Opposition runs into 36 pages* and is ready for dispatch.
2. A clear photocopy of all materials that formed the basis of the said decision of the Hon'ble Speaker.

5. A clear photocopy of all legal opinion obtained by the Hon'ble Speaker or her office or this Secretariat on the subject of recognizing the Leader of the Opposition in this House along with a clear photocopy of all communication sent to any person seeking legal opinion; and

Application Dated: 13.12.2014
Reference: Lok Sabha Secretariat Letter No.1(132)/IC/14 dated 19.03.2015

Point No.1: Provide the information pertaining to Dr. Ram Shanker Katheria (MP) Agra Lok Sabha since his election to Lok Sabha in 2009 till date. How many days has Ram Shanker Katheria attended the Lok Sabha sessions.
Reply: An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing during all sessions of 15th & 16th Lok Sabha are available on the Lok Sabha website under Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance Total. A member may attend but forget to sign the register. The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information. Dr. Ram Shanker Katheria assumed the office of Minister of State in the Ministry of Human Resource Development w.e.f 09 November, 2014. It is not mandatory for ministers to sign the attendance register.

Point No.2: Days for which Shri Ram Shankar Katheria has received attendance allowance and how much.
Reply: Shri Ram Shankar Katheria has been paid for 325 days daily allowances to attend Parliament Session as per The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957.

Point No.3: For how many days travelling allowance has been claimed and for which destination.
Reply: The information relating to travelling allowances and for which destination is voluminous, the compilation of which will disproportionately divert the resources. However, if the applicant desires, he may visit the Branch (by contacting Under Secretary, Phone No. 011-23034405) and peruse the register meant for the purpose. M/o HRD have also replied against the point directly to the applicant.

Point No.4: Does the post of professor in the university come under the purview of "Post of profit" and related details.
Reply: The application has been transferred to M/o Law and M/o HRD on 16.12.2014 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to him. The applicant may contact them for further information on this point.

Point No.5: Can a MP avail a government house in Delhi as well as in other part of the country provided by the university?
Reply: The application has been transferred to DoPT and M/o HRD on 16.12.2014 under intimation to the applicant for furnishing reply directly to him. It may be stated that DoPT have further transferred the application to Department of Expenditure and M/o Urban Development under intimation to the applicant.

Point No.6: Can a MP avail all the benefits provided to him as an MP along with the benefits provided to him by the University where he is serving, such as salary, government accommodation, CCA, Travelling allowance etc. Please support your information with the copy of the act or law in this regard.
Reply: The Salary to Members of Parliament (including nominated members) are regulated by: 1. The Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (As amended); 2. The Members of Parliament (Travelling and Daily Allowances) Rules, 1957; 3. The Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1956; 4. The Medical Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rules, 1959; 5. The Members of Parliament (Allowances for Journeys Abroad) Rules, 1960; 6. The Members of Parliament (Constituency Allowances) Rules, 1986; 7. The Members of Parliament (Advance for the purchase of Conveyance) Rules, 1986; & The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988. The Salary and Allowances to Ministers and LoP are regulated by 'The Salaries and Allowances of Ministers Act, 1952' and 'The Salary and Allowances of Leaders of Opposition in Parliament Act, 1977' and Rules made thereunder.

Point No.7-8: How much office expenditure is allowed to the MP to run an office in his lok sabha area. Please give the breakup of the allowance. Has Ram Shanker Katheria MP, Agra, Lok Sabha(18) reserved claimed any allowance if yes please give full details along with breakup.
Reply: Shri Ram Shanker Katheria, MP, has been paid office expenses allowances as per The Members of Parliament (Office Expense Allowance) Rules, 1988.

Point No.9: Month wise full details of the salary, allowances, HRA, CCA etc received by Sh. Ram Shankar Katheria, MP, Agra, Lok Sabha(18) reserved.
Reply: Please see replies to points above. Moreover, a pamphlet containing the details of salary, allowances and other facilities provided to an MP is enclosed. M/o HRD have also replied directly to the applicant.

There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Ministries/Departments/Rajya Sabha Secretariat etc. in connection with the conduct of Parliament. However, Head of account-wise expenditure incurred [from Financial year 2009-10 to 2015-16] out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha and booked by P&AO, Lok Sabha, is available on Lok Sabha homepage under link: http://164.100.47.194/loksabha/Secretariat/DemandLokSabha.aspx. 2-3. No information regarding change in the cost of running Parliament and factors responsible for these changes is available with concerned Branch in this Secretariat. 4. Information regarding money lost due to adjournment of session of Lok Sabha is not available with Lok Sabha; relevant information may be sought from the concerned Department/Ministry.

Kindly give complete information regarding number and location. -- (i) Total number of quarters at present in Lok Sabha Secretariat Pool is 808. (ii) Total number of 184 quarters will be available after completion of the R.K. Puram Project. The breakup of these quarters is as under: 184+48 Servant Quarters - i) Type-V = 48 ii) Type-IV = 72 iii) Type-III = 32 (iii) Type-II = 32. (iii) As the list is exhaustive, the applicant is advised to visit the Branch in any of the working days to check records regarding type of quarters, its numbers and locations.
2. Whether a priority list is drawn up for allotting quarters from Lok Sabha Pool and the list is uploaded on Intranet? Whether this list is updated regularly? -- Yes. Priority list is drawn up and the same is uploaded on Lok Sabha intranet. This list is updated from time to time.
3. Whether the allotment of quarters is done as per the above list or is this list a mere formality and the actual allotment is made on the basis of some private list? If this list is a mere formality, what is the justification of uploading it on the Intranet? -- Allotment of quarters are made as per priority list.
4. The total number of people in the last five years whose names did not figure in the priority list available on the Lok Sabha intranet, but who were allotted quarters nonetheless. Please inform the reasons therefor? -- Two quarters have been allotted as such viz. (i) Then Joint Secretary (Security) on deputation on functional ground as per orders of Hon'ble Speaker and (ii) Director (Security) on deputation on functional ground as per orders of Hon'ble Speaker.
5. Whether reservation is provided to the Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe employees in the matter of allotment of quarters in Lok Sabha Secretariat? Whether this reservation is given in each category (Type-I,II,III, IV etc,) separately? If so, the number of employees who were given benefit of reservation during the last five years and allotted quarters on this basis and the number of employees who got the quarter on merit? -- Yes. Allotment of type-I,II,III and IV quarters to SC/ST employees are made as per Reservation Roster maintained in the Branch. Since a separate register is maintained in this Branch for the said purpose, the applicant is advised to visit this Branch in any of the working days to check Reservation Roster register.
6. Please provide details of reservation policy adopted in this regard? Whether the officers posted in Administration consider the present reservation policy appropriate? If not, the time by which amendment will be made therein? -- Reservation is given to SC/ST employees for allotment of quarters as per OM No. 12035(20)/74-Pol.II dated 18th September, 1975 and 12035(20)/74-Pol-II dated 01.12.1975 issued by Directorate of Estates Government of India and adopted in this Secretariat on 27.12.1996. The rest of the question does not fall under Section 2(f) of RTI Act, 2005.
7. Whether reservation facility will be provided in the newly constructed quarters of Lok Sabha Pool? If so, the basis of the formula on which reservation will be made along with details thereof. -- The question is not covered under the definition of 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, 2005.
8. Whether the same person has been handling the sensitive charge of allotment of quarters for last several years? If so, the details of transfer policy in Lok Sabha Secretariat if any? Whether above employee can hold the same post till his retirement? -- Transfer/posting is effected keeping in view the functional requirement of the Secretariat and disposal of the Parliamentary work. However, internal work allocation in a particular Division/Branch of the Secretariat is the concern of that Branch/Branch Head. As far as the 2nd part of the point is concerned, the point is a hypothetical query and not covered under the definition of information as defined in Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, 2005.
response_full_text: Total number of quarters at present in Lok Sabha Secretariat Pool is 808. Total number of 184 quarters will be available after completion of the R.K. Puram Project (Type-V=48, Type-IV=72, Type-III=32, Type-II=32). Priority list is drawn up and uploaded on Lok Sabha intranet, updated from time to time. Allotment of quarters is made as per priority list. Two quarters have been allotted outside the priority list on deputation grounds as per orders of Hon'ble Speaker. Allotment of Type-I,II,III and IV quarters to SC/ST employees is made as per the Reservation Roster maintained in the Branch, per OM No. 12035(20)/74-Pol.II dated 18 September 1975 and 12035(20)/74-Pol-II dated 1 December 1975 adopted in this Secretariat on 27.12.1996. Questions on the reservation formula for newly constructed quarters and on staff tenure/transfer policy were held not to fall under the definition of 'information' under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, 2005.

title: MP membership cancellation and Speaker's expunction powers
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant asked whether an MP's resignation or suspension from their party cancels their Lok Sabha membership, and what it means when the Speaker orders that something 'will not be on record'.
questions: When an MP resigns from his party or is suspended, does his or her membership also get cancelled?
When the Speaker says this will not be on record, what does it mean?
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that party resignation/suspension is an internal party matter, coming under the Speaker's purview only via a disqualification petition under the Tenth Schedule; and that 'not on record' refers to the Speaker's Rule 380 power to expunge defamatory/unparliamentary remarks, or unauthorised speech, from proceedings.

No. 2) about matters raised by MPs from Haryana in the House during the 15th Lok Sabha under procedures viz. Zero Hour (Special Mention), Matters under Rule 377, Calling Attention, Adjournment Motion and Submission dealt with by T.O is available on Lok Sabha website link, loksabha.nic.in -> Debates -> Debate search.

--- First Appeal ---
Facts and Background: [Applicant] had filed an RTI application dated 13.01.2014 seeking information about Lokpal Bill, etc. which was received on 22.01.2014. The applicant was replied to by this Secretariat on 19.02.2014. [Applicant] filed first appeal on 17.02.2014, received on 24.02.2014. The appellant contends that till date he has not received the information.

DETAILS OF FIRST APPEAL UNDER RTI ACT, 2005 UNDER SECTION 19(1) & 19(6) AND UNDER SECTION 4
File No. 1(122)/IC/14. Name of the Applicant: [Applicant]. Date of Appeal: 17.02.2014. Date of receipt in the RTI Section: 24.02.2014. Last date of reply: 25.03.2014.
Point raised in the Appeal: The appellant contends that till date he has not received the desired information.
Position taken by the Branch: Information furnished by the concerned division had been supplied to the applicant.

No.1(122)/AA/IC/14
06.03.2014
Decision and Reasons: I have carefully gone through the RTI Application followed by First Appeal. The CPIO has enquired the matter with the division concerned of this public authority. I am satisfied with the contention of the CPIO that the information to the extent pertaining and available with the concerned division of this public authority has already been supplied to the appellant vide letter no.1(122)/IC/14 dated 19.02.2014. However, it appears from the appeal that the appellant has sent his appeal dated 17.02.2014 before receiving reply. Further, since the appellant has not mentioned the pincode, reply might have reached him later than 17.02.2014. The CPIO has also informed that as per practice adopted/followed by the 'Distribution' Branch of this public authority any letter which doesn't have pin code is sent by ordinary post only and in the instant case as well the division concerned has followed the same practice. With the above observations the appeal is disposed of.
(P.K. MISRA), Additional Secretary and First Appellate Authority, Lok Sabha Secretariat

Seeking information on MPs:
Point 1: Percentage of their attendance. Reply: Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of the 14th to 16th Lok Sabhas are available on the website www.loksabha.nic.in under Members -> Attendance of Members -> Member-wise Attendance -> All Members. The applicant may note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The attendance details of members prior to the Fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website; that information is available in the records of the Branch and is voluminous. The applicant may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally peruse the records available in the Branch.

Point 2: Questions asked by them (MPs) during their tenure. Reply: The questions asked by the concerned Members of Parliament from November, 1999 onwards along with their replies are available on the Lok Sabha website (Qmembersearch page). Roy Choudhary, Joint Director, Tel. no. 011-23034347 or depute someone to cull out the desired information. All necessary assistance will be provided at their end.

Point 3: Criminal cases against them (MPs). Reply: No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. There is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to them for necessary action; the applicant is requested to approach them directly.

Point 2: Questions asked by MPs from November 1999 onwards along with replies are on the Lok Sabha website; earlier records are available in the Branch and the applicant may visit the Parliament Library.
