title: MGNREGA Standing Committee submission request partly refused
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought the Department of Rural Development's submission to the Standing Committee on Rural Development on MGNREGA and the Committee's final tabled report.

response_summary: The Secretariat declined to furnish the Department of Rural Development's submission to the Standing Committee, citing Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure of Departmentally Related Standing Committees which treats material circulated to a Committee as confidential until its report is tabled; it directed the applicant to the Lok Sabha website for the Committee's final report already tabled on 19.12.2014.

Point (a): Submission of the Deptt. of Rural Development to the Standing Committee on Rural Development related to MGNREGA.
Reply: Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure (Internal Working) of the Departmentally Related Standing Committees provides: 'The material circulated to the Committee/Sub-Committee shall be treated as Confidential and the contents thereof shall not be divulged to anyone nor shall any reference be made to such information, outside the Committee/Sub-Committee at any time before the report on the subject has been presented to the House. Thereafter, references may be made only to such information as is available in the documents or records laid on the Table.' In light of Rule 8, the request of the applicant to supply the Submission of the Department of Rural Development to the Standing Committee on Rural Development related to MGNREGA may not be acceded to. [Reason for refusal quoted under Section 7(8)(i) of the RTI Act, 2005: Rule 8 of the Rules of Procedure of Departmentally Related Standing Committees.]

Point (b): Final report of the Standing Committee as tabled in Parliament on 19.12.2014.
Reply: The reports of the Committee tabled in Parliament on 19.12.2014 are available on the official website of Lok Sabha www.loksabha.nic.in and can be accessed from there.

title: Compassionate grounds appointment policy and case details sought
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought details of the policy, statistics and specific cases of appointments made on compassionate grounds in the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
questions: The number of posts/positions or percentage of posts/positions earmarked/reserved/set aside in the Lok Sabha Secretariat for filling up on compassionate grounds.

The number of applications received in the Secretariat during the last five years (including the current year) for employment/engagement on compassionate grounds. Please provide year-wise and post/position-wise details.

Requests acceded to during the last five years (including the current year) and the number of cases pending. What is the present status/stage of processing of the pending cases? Year-wise and post/position-wise details may be provided for both the pending and finalized cases.
Whether any vacancy from the compassionate quota/position has been diverted for filling up regular vacancies.
If so, the details of such cases including the number and grounds for their consideration along with copies of approval of the Competent Authority may be provided.

The number of applications received in the Secretariat for employment/engagement on compassionate grounds during the period of Shri Somnath Chatterjee as Speaker, Lok Sabha. How many of them were filled up during that period and how many remained pending?
response_summary: The Secretariat explained that Government guidelines on compassionate appointments are followed subject to competent authority approval, declined to compile five-year application statistics citing disproportionate diversion of resources under Section 7(9), provided a list of persons appointed on compassionate grounds since 2008 and their pending case status, confirmed no compassionate-quota vacancies were diverted to regular vacancies, and enclosed a list of compassionate appointments made during Shri Somnath Chatterjee's tenure as Speaker while noting request-count data for that period is not maintained.
extracted_text:
Name of the Applicant - [Applicant]
Annexure to letter No. - 1(1020)/IC/13

Point (i): The number of posts/positions or percentage of posts/positions earmarked/reserved/set aside in the Lok Sabha Secretariat for filling up on compassionate grounds.
Reply: Guidelines issued by the Govt. of India regarding filling up of posts on compassionate grounds are followed in this Secretariat. However, appointments on compassionate grounds are subject to the approval of the competent authority.

Point (ii): The number of applications received in the Secretariat during the last five years (including the current year) for employment/engagement on compassionate grounds, year-wise and post/position-wise.
Reply: Such information is not maintained in the Branch. Culling out and compilation of information from the records will disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority in terms of Section 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005.

Point (iii): Requests acceded to during the last five years and number of cases pending, present status/stage of processing of pending cases, year-wise and post/position-wise, for both pending and finalized cases.
Reply: List of persons appointed on compassionate grounds since 2008 is enclosed (Appendix-I). The status of other requests for compassionate appointment during the ibid period: (i) Ms. Shashi Bala - Under process. (ii) Smt. Nagina Chaturvedi - not acceded to. (iii) Shri Satpal - Final decision yet to be taken. (iv) Shri Ali Mohammad - Final decision yet to be taken. (v) Ms. Soumya Rao - Not acceded to.

Point (iv): Whether any vacancy from the compassionate quota/position has been diverted for filling up regular vacancies.
Reply: No.

Point (v): If so, the details of such cases including the number and grounds for their consideration along with copies of approval of the Competent Authority.
Reply: [Not applicable, as answer to point (iv) was 'No']

Point (vi): The number of applications received in the Secretariat for employment/engagement on compassionate grounds during the period of Shri Somnath Chatterjee as Speaker, Lok Sabha; how many were filled up during that period and how many remained pending.
Reply: List of persons appointed on compassionate grounds between 2004 and June 2009 in Lok Sabha Secretariat during the tenure of Shri Somnath Chatterjee as Speaker, Lok Sabha is enclosed (Appendix-II). The number of requests received in the Secretariat for appointment on compassionate grounds during the ibid period is not maintained.
response_full_text:
(i) Guidelines issued by the Govt. of India regarding filling up of posts on compassionate grounds are followed in this Secretariat, subject to approval of the competent authority.
(ii) Such information is not maintained in the Branch; compiling it would disproportionately divert resources under Section 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005.
(iii) List of persons appointed on compassionate grounds since 2008 enclosed (Appendix-I); status of other pending requests listed (Ms. Shashi Bala - under process; Smt. Nagina Chaturvedi - not acceded to; Shri Satpal - decision pending; Shri Ali Mohammad - decision pending; Ms. Soumya Rao - not acceded to).
(iv) No.
(v) Not applicable.
(vi) List of persons appointed on compassionate grounds between 2004 and June 2009 (during Shri Somnath Chatterjee's tenure as Speaker) enclosed (Appendix-II); number of requests received during that period is not maintained.

department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant, seeking details about their own case, sought detailed information on promotion proposals, DPC panels, seniority fixation and recruitment examinations concerning the LAFEA Service of the Lok Sabha Secretariat between 1993 and 2012.
questions: Details of the proposals for promotion to various posts in the gazetted cadres of LAFEA Service for the year 2012 as prepared and approved by the competent authority.
Details of the panels for promotion to different gazetted posts of LAFEA Service as prepared by the DPC for the year 2012 and approved by the competent authority.
Names and the order in which officials who were serving in the grade of Additional Director were promoted to the grade of Director on ad-hoc basis w.e.f. 29.03.2012.

Date(s) of occurrence of clear/regular vacancies in the grade of Director subsequent to 29.03.2012 under which the two ad-hoc promotees to the grade of Director could have been covered for promotion on regular basis.
Date(s) on which the files pertaining to promotion of the two officers initiated/moved by the Administration following the occurrence of regular/clear vacancies in the grade.

Details of proposals relating to promotion of officials of services other than LAFEAS that were initiated by the Administration during the period 29.03.2012 to 12.10.2012 and approved by the competent authority (with the date of approval).

title: RTI on Parliament disruptions and time lost partially answered
department: लोक सभा सचिवालय (Lok Sabha Secretariat), सूचना प्रकोष्ठ (Information Cell)
subject: The applicant sought data on the number and reasons for disruptions and quorum failures in Parliament between 1957-2015, time lost due to adjournments, and the associated expenditure.
questions: Numbers of disruptions in Parliament between 1957-2015 and the reasons of interruptions.
The reason of want of quorum.
Time lost due to unusual adjournment.
The expenditure on lost time.
response_summary: The Secretariat stated that reasons for individual disruptions and quorum failures are not maintained since it is impractical to record which members caused them; for time lost due to adjournment, pre-1999 data is not readily available but later data is on the website, with specific hours given for the 16th Lok Sabha's 5th and 6th sessions, while citing Section 7(9) of the RTI Act to explain that compiling the full 58-year history would disproportionately divert Secretariat resources; expenditure on lost time is not maintained at all.

Sl. No. | Point in brief | Reply
1(a) | Numbers of disruptions in Parliament between 1957-2015 and related questions - reasons of interruptions | The reasons of interruptions caused by members is not maintained by the Branch, since members of different political parties come to the well of the House or shout from their respective seats protesting about various issues to criticize the policies, programmes and actions of the Government. Since a large number of members are simultaneously involved with the process of interruptions, it is practically not possible to record the names of members and their parties. Hence we are unable to provide any information in that regard.
1(b) | Reason of want of quorum | Such information is not maintained by the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
2 | Time lost due to unusual adjournment | Information to this point prior to 1999 is not readily available with the Branch. However, information about adjournment of Lok Sabha due to interruptions during the 15th, 14th and 13th Lok Sabhas is available at loksabha.nic.in -> Resume -> Archive -> respective Lok Sabhas -> Statement showing time lost due to interruption and adjournment (Session and date wise). The first four sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha are also available on the same website. During the 5th and 6th sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha, the House was adjourned due to interruptions for 34 hours 08 minutes and 08 hours 37 minutes respectively. It is stated that the applicant has sought information over a period of 58 years. As per Section 7(9) of RTI Act, 2005, information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority; to search for information over 58 years would divert a sizeable amount of time and manpower of the Secretariat.
3 | The expenditure on lost time | Such information is not maintained in Lok Sabha Secretariat.
response_full_text: The reasons of interruptions caused by members is not maintained by the Branch, since members of different political parties come to well of the House or shout from their respective seats protesting about various issues. It is practically not possible to record the names of members and their parties. Information to this point prior to 1999 is not readily available with the Branch; during the 5th and 6th sessions of the 16th Lok Sabha, the House has been adjourned due to interruptions for 34 hours 08 minutes and 08 hours 37 minutes respectively. As per Section 7(9) of RTI Act, 2005, information shall ordinarily be provided in the form in which it is sought unless it would disproportionately divert the resources of the public authority; to search for information over a period of 58 years would divert a sizeable amount of time and manpower of Secretariat. Such information [expenditure on lost time] does not maintained in Lok Sabha Secretariat.

(v)-(vi) Total expenditure on tours, with names/designations of officials who joined, and status of pending bills -- Five study visits were undertaken: (1) 7-14 June 2010 to Mumbai, Goa (Rs.4,81,339), Hyderabad (pending with Ministry) and Kolkata (Rs.2,47,048); (2) 19-24 January 2011 to Thiruvananthapuram (under process), Kochi (Rs.3,57,767) and Bangaluru (Rs.3,46,173); (3) 20-25 May 2011 to Kolkata (Rs.5,60,248) and Gangtok/Darjeeling (pending with Ministry/under process); (4) 8-12 June 2012 to Srinagar, Chennai and Jammu (pending with Ministry); (5) 9-13 February 2013 to [unspecified], Port Blair and Kolkata (pending with Ministry/under process). response_summary: The Secretariat explained that Lok Sabha normally holds three sessions a year (Budget, Monsoon, Winter), that there is no fixed number of sitting days prescribed by the Constitution or Rules, that the number of sittings per session is decided by the Government through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs, and pointed to the Lok Sabha website for session duration details.

4 | Tenure of the Winter, Summer Sessions of the Parliament | The Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Normally, three sessions of Lok Sabha are held in a year: Budget Session (February to May), Monsoon Session (July to September), Winter Session (November to December). The Constitution of India provides that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. However, neither the Constitution nor the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provide as to how many days Lok Sabha would sit in a session/year. The number of sittings of Lok Sabha for each session is decided by the Government of India and intimated through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs keeping in view the volume of legislative and financial business which Government propose to bring forward before the House. Duration of a session and the days of sittings is available on the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Resume of Work' -> 'Archive' and also in loksabha.nic.in -> 'Business' -> 'Bulletin-I'.
response_full_text: The Parliament consists of the President, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha. Normally, three sessions of Lok Sabha are held in a year as under:- Budget Session February to May, Monsoon Session July to September, Winter Session November to December. The Constitution of India provides that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session. However, neither the Constitution nor the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha provide as to how many days Lok Sabha would sit in a session/year. The number of sittings of Lok Sabha for each session is decided by the Government of India and intimated through the Ministry of Parliamentary Affairs. Duration of a session and the days of sittings is available in the Lok Sabha website.

title: लोक सभा सचिवालय द्वारा आरटीआई आवेदन पर सूचना
subject: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना।
questions: 16वीं लोक सभा के दौरान सभा कितनी बार स्थगित हुई ?
मई, 2014 से संसद की कार्यवाही पर प्रतिदिन हुए व्यय का ब्यौरा दें ।
सत्र के दौरान संसद की कार्यवाही नहीं चलने के कारण हुई धन की हानि और ऐसे व्यय को वहन करने वाले अभिकरणों के बारे में भी जानकारी प्रदान करें ।
मई, 2014 अर्थात् राजग सरकार द्वारा कार्यभार ग्रहण करने से लेकर अब तक हुए लोक सभा के सत्रों की संख्या और उसके द्वारा पारित विधेयकों का नाम बताएं ।

विमुद्रीकरण के मुद्दे पर सरकार और विपक्ष के बीच हाल के टकराव से संसद की कार्यवाही प्रभावित हुई है और देश के विकास संबंधी महत्वपूर्ण कार्यों में बाधा पैदा हुई है । क्या इन सदस्यों को विरोध और प्रदर्शन करने के लिए ही चुनकर संसद में भेजा जाता है ?
ऐसे सदस्यों के विरूद्ध अनुशासनात्मक कार्यवाही क्यों नहीं की जाती और उक्त कार्यवाही करने के लिए कौन सा प्राधिकारी अधिकृत है ?
शीतकालीन सत्र में विमुद्रीकरण पर चर्चा दौरान संसद सत्र के न चलने के कारण हुए धन के अपव्यय का ब्यौरा दें । उन एजेंसियों का ब्यौरा दें जो इस व्यय को वहन करेंगी ।
response_summary: लोक सभा सचिवालय ने संसद सत्रों के स्थगन, संसदीय कार्यवाही पर हुए व्यय और बाधित कार्यवाही के दौरान अनुशासनहीनता के प्रावधानों से संबंधित जानकारी प्रदान की है। मांगी गई अधिकांश जानकारी लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है, जिसके लिए विशिष्ट लिंक भी दिए गए हैं। हालांकि, सत्र न चलने के कारण हुई वित्तीय हानि और अन्य मंत्रालयों द्वारा किए गए व्यय का विवरण सचिवालय के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है।

response_full_text:
वर्तमान लोक सभा के दौरान सभा के स्थगित होने की जानकारी लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् loksabha.nic.in→'Business'→'Resume of Work' पर उपलब्ध है । दसवें सत्र के बारे में, वांछित जानकारी लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् loksabha.nic.in→'Business'→'Bulletin-I'पर उपलब्ध है । आवेदक को सलाह दी जाती है कि वह वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त करने के लिए लोक सभा की उपर्युक्त वेबसाइट का अवलोकन करें ।
संसद के सत्र की कार्यवाही पर हुआ व्यय कई अभिकरणों जैसे लोक सभा सचिवालय, राज्य सभा सचिवालय, शहरी विकास मंत्रालय (के.लो.नि.विभाग) और अन्य मंत्रालयों/विभागों द्वारा वहन किया जाता है । संसद की कार्यवाही के संबंध में विभिन्न मंत्रालयों/विभागों/राज्य सभा सचिवालय इत्यादि द्वारा वहन किए गए व्यय को दर्ज करने के लिए कोई विशिट और एकमात्र लेखार्शी नहीं है । तथापि, (वित्तीय र्वा 2009-10 से 2015-16 तक) लोक सभा के बजट अनुदान से हुआ लेखा र्शी-वार और लोक सभा के वेतन और लेखा कार्यालय द्वारा दर्ज किया गया व्यय लोक सभा के होम पेज पर निम्नलिखित लिंक पर उपलब्ध है:- http://164.100.47.194/loksabha/Secretariat/DemandLokSabha.aspx वेतन और लेखा कार्यालय, लोक सभा द्वारा उपलब्ध कराए गए व्यय के आंकड़ों के आधार पर संकलित 01.04.2016 से 31.12.16 तक हुआ व्यय (अलेखापरीक्षित) संलग्न है (अनुबंध) । अन्य मंत्रालयों/विभागों/राज्य सभा सचिवालय द्वारा किए गए व्यय की जानकारी आईएफयू के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है ।
सत्र के दौरान संसद की कार्यवाही नहीं चलने के कारण हुई धन की हानि और ऐसे व्यय को वहन करने वाले अभिकरणों के बारे में जानकारी लोक सभा सचिवालय के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है । संगत जानकारी कई विभागों/मंत्रालयों से संबंधित है ।
आवेदक को सूचित किया जाता है कि मई, 2014 से 16वीं लोक सभा के दस सत्र हो चुके हैं । प्रश्न के दूसरे भाग के संबंध में, आवेदक को सूचित किया जाता है कि सभाओं द्वारा पारित और राट्रपति द्वारा अनुमति प्राप्त सरकारी विधेयकों को दर्शाने वाला विवरण सत्र की समाप्ति के पश्चात् लोक सभा समाचार भाग में प्रकाशित होता है । चूंकि यह जानकारी पहले से ही सार्वजनिक रूप से उपलब्ध है अतः, आवेदक से अनुरोध है कि वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त करने के लिए लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् loksabha.nic.in पर 'Business' लिंक के अंतर्गत 'Bulletin-II' पर देखें । आवेदक समाचार भाग-दो के निम्नलिखित पैरा को देखें और वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त करें ।
लोक सभा के प्रक्रिया तथा कार्य संचालन नियमों के नियम 373, 374 और 374 (क) के अंतर्गत सदस्यों द्वारा अमर्यादित आचरण करने, जानबूझकर सभा के कार्य में बाधा डालने और लगातार नियमों का उल्लंघन करने की स्थिति में सदस्यों को सभा से बाहर निकालने और सभा की सेवा से निलंबित किए जाने का प्रावधान है ।
लोक सभा के प्रक्रिया तथा कार्य संचालन नियम, लोक सभा की वेबसाइट www.loksabha.nic.in पर 'Parliamentary Procedure' लिंक के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध है । माननीय लोक सभा अध्यक्ष सभा (लोक सभा) की कार्यवाही में बाधा डालने वाले संसद सदस्यों के विरूद्ध अनुशासनात्मक कार्यवाही कर सकता है।
कृपया प्रश्न सं. 3 का उत्तर देखें ।

No free food is served, and canteens are run by the Ministry of Railways. Members purchase their own clothes, and no information is available on cloth expenditure. No security is provided by the Lok Sabha Secretariat for MPs in Parliament Complex. Detailed information on other facilities, salary, allowances, and pension for Members and Ex-Members of Parliament is provided in two enclosed annexures.

3. Cloths are purchased by Members by own payment from the market. No such information is available.
4. No security provided to the Members of Parliament in Parliament Complex by the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Two annexure shows the other facilities and Salary, Allowances and Pension provided to the Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) by the Lok Sabha Secretariat are enclosed.
FACILITIES PROVIDED TO MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT BY M.S. BRANCH LOK SABHA SECRETARIAT NEW DELHI
1. Accommodation
(1) Members who come to Delhi prior to publication of Notification by the Election Commission for constituting new Lok Sabha are entitled to transit accommodation.
(ii) Accommodation in the form of a flat is free throughout the term of office to a Member. However, normal licence fee @ Rs. 105 is charged on bungalow.
(i) Sofa covers and curtains are get washed by the CPWD after every 3 months which are provided free of cost to Members.
(iv) Fumiture to be made free of charge to the Members within the revised monetary celling of Rs. 60,000 in respect of durable furniture and Rs. 15,000/- for non-durable furniture. The rental for additional items of furniture shall be charged on the depreciated value of furniture.
(v) Members of Lok Sabha or their families can retain Government Accommodation for a maximum period of one month after their retirement, resignationiremoval or ceasing to be a Member of Lok Sabha on payment of the same rent, if any, which they were paying immediately before the occurrence of any of the events mentioned above.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament may retain Government accommodation for a maximum period of six months from the date of death of such a Member.
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rule, 1956 (as amended).
2. Water and Electricity
(i) 4000 Kilolitre of waler and 50,000 units of Electricity (25,000 units measured on lights meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost in the residence allotted to a Member in Delhi/New Delhi and to a Member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
(ii) Where both husband and wife are Members of Parliament and are residing in the same accommodation, their admissibility for supply of free electricity and water at the residence allotted to them shall be calculated separately
(it) The unconsumed units of electricity and water out of those otherwise admissible to a Member in any year shall be carried over to the subsequent years III his seat becomes vacant
(iv) In case of consumption of electricity and water by a Member in excess of his entitlement for a particular year, such excess consumption of electricity and water shall be adjusted from the units of electricity and water in kilolitre available for the next year.
(v) In case the seat of a Member becomes vacant due to his resignation or completion of term, he will be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water as available for that year within a maximum period of one month from the date on which his seat becomes vacant.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament shall be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water in klolita available to such Member for that particular year within a period of one month from the date of death of that Member.
3. Telephone Facilities
(i) A member is entitled to have two telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, one at his residence or office in Delhi and the other at his usual place of residence or a place selected by him in his constituency or the State in which he resides, 50,000 local calls during a year are free to a Member on each of the two telephones
ANNEXURE I
(ii) A Member is also entitled to have one additionall telephone without payment of installation and rental charges either at his residence in Delhi New Delhi or at his usual place of residence or at the place selected by him within the State in which his constituency is or in the State in which he resides and 50,000 free local calls during a year are allowed on that telephone for internet connectivity purposes.
(ii) The above mentioned 50,000 free local calls admissible on each telephone can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year.
(iv) A Member may use any number of telephones for availing the above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of Member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are bome by the Member himself.
(v) A Member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/BSNL services are not available, with national roaming facility for utilisation in the constituency and the calls made from these telephones may be adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 calls available to them on 3 telephones. However, the registration and rental charges for private mobile phone connection are bome by the Member himself.
(vi) In case a Member makes calls in excess of admissible free local calls in a year, the excess calls can be adjusted from the calls available to him on three telephones for the next year. Further, the unutilised telephone calls of a year are carmed over to the subsequent years till the seat of a Member becomes vacant
(vii) A Member is also entitled to avail broadband facility from MTNL/ BSNL on any one of the above-mentioned three telephones subject to the condition that the Government may pay uplo Rs. 1,500 per month towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL
4. Transport Facilities
The Members are also being provided the following facilities
(i) Ferry Vehicles through Transport Desk
There is a Transport Desk from where vehicles are provided to facilitate the Members to go from Parliament complex to their residences and vice-versa in New Delhi. The transport facility is provided to all Members of Parliament between their residences and Parliament House Complex on a payment of a token amount of Rs. 5/- for each trip,
(ii) Rail Transport
Railway Booking and Reservation Offices function in Parliament House and near Outer Reception Office, Parliament House throughout the year for the convenience of Members of Parliament. The reservation of accommodation in trains for Members and their spouses is made from the Reservation Office, Parliament House and reservation of accommodation for Members' guests/attendants/friends etc. is made from the Reservation Office, near outer Reception Office, Parliament House.
(i) Air Transport
An Air Booking Office of Air India functions in Parliament House throughout the year. Arrangements also exist for Members of Parliament to book air passages with the Air India Booking Office in Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi. The booking can also be done by Members over the telephone in certain circumstances.
(iv) Taxis and Scooters Outside Parliament House Annexe
During Session Period, arrangements are made for availability of laxis and scooters at taxi Stands outside Parliament House Complex with the assistance of Delhi Police, Taxi Stands around Parliament House Complex and Watch and Ward Office Lok Sabha Secretariat.
5. Medical Facilities
(i) Members of Parliament are entitled to same medical facilities as are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-i under Central Government Health Scheme.
(ii) Under the Central Government Health Scheme, as extended to Members of Parliament, a First Aid Post in the Lobby of the Central Hall of Parliament House and a Medical Centre in the basement of Parliament House Annexe function throughout the year to render First Aid to Members of Parliament and to meet the first aid requirement arising in the precincts of the Parliament House Complex.
(ii) The Medical Centre has X-Ray, Ultra Sound, ECG, Pathological Laboratory facilities and consultation in Cardiac, Dental, Ophthalmic, ENT, Gynae, Skin, Orthopaedic, Psychiatric and Surgical Specialties. Apart from this, the services of Dietician, Paediatrician, Physiotherapist are also available on given days of the weeks. The Medical Centre maintains a record of Health status of each Member of Parliament
6. Other Facilities to Members
(a) Diplomatic Passport
A Member and his wife/husband is eligible for the issue of Diplomatic Passport for going abroad on study tour/conference/ private visit
(b) Income Tax Sub-Office
Under arrangements made with Ministry of Finance, an Income Tax Sub-office function in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year for rendering assistance to Members of Parliament in completing their income-tax returns and in resolving their queries relating to the payment of income-tax
(c) State Bank of india Branches af Parliament House and Annexe
Branches of the State Bank of India function in Parliament House and Annexe. Besides the normal banking facilities, they accept payment in respect of income-tax and other direct taxes, investment plans, etc. Safe deposit lockers have also been provided at Parliament House Annexe Branch for the convenience of Members. ATM facility is provided for the convenience of Members in Parliament House/Annexe and Parliament Library Building.
(d) Rationing Sub-Office
With the introduction of statutory rationing in Delhi, a Rationing Sub-Office opened by the Delhi Rationing Authority functions in Parliament House during the Session period for the issue of Ration Cards to Members and their families
(e) Kendriya Bhandar
A branch of the Kendriya Bhandar located at 23, Mahadev Road is open from 09.30 hrs. to 18.30 hrs, for the sale of essential commodities (such as grocery, toilet and househoid items, textiles, watches, etc.).
(1) NDMC Liaison Office
A full-fledged Liaison Office of the NDMC (New Delhi Municipal Council) functions in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year to look into the complaints of Members with regard to meters installed at their residences and all other matters connected with the NDMC, including electricity and water bills of Members.
(g) LPG Service Counter of the Oil industry
The Service Counter of the Oil Industry in regard to supply of LPG and rendering timely service in respect of defective, installation, etc. functions during Session period in Parliament House Annexe for the convenience of Members of Parliament.
(1) Secunty arrangements in Members' residential localities
A Special Cell has been set up by Delhi Police in the Office of the Assistant Commissioner Police, Police Station, Parliament Street, New Delhi, to assist the Members of Parliament to maintain the security of their residences. The timing of the Cell is from 0900 hours to 1900 hours daily. Members are required to inform the Cell as and when they happen to go outside Delhi to enable the Police authorities to make necessary arrangements for the security of their residences during their absence from Delhi.
The Members, for any other assistance they may require from the local police, may also contact the Cell
(i) Army Disposal Vehicles
Members may apply for Army Disposal Vehicles from the Ministry of Defence. The requests received from the Members are forwarded to Ministry of Defence for release of Army Disposal Vehicles from the Army Disposal Stock
(1) Catering Service
Northern Railway is running MPs Canteen in North Avenue for the convenience of Members and their guests. In South i Avenue, catering services is being run by a private caterer. In Westem Court Hostel, the canteen is run by the ITDC.
FACILITIES TO MEMBERS/EX-MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT [As per the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Amendment) Act, 2010]
LOK SABHA SECRETARIAT NEW DELHI
(Amended upto 13th December, 2010)
1. Salary Rs. 50,000/- per month.
2. Daily Allowance Rs. 2,000/- per day for each day of residence on duty. Daily Allowance shall be paid only when the member signs the register maintained for the purpose
3. Constituency Allowance Rs. 45,000/- per month.
4. Office Expense Allowance Rs. 45,000/- per month out of which Rs 15,000/- is for meeting expenses of stationery items and postage; and upto Rs 30,000/- is paid by the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariats to the person(s) as may be engaged by a member for obtaining secretarial assistance, provided that one such person must be computer literate as certified by the Member herself himself.
5. Travelling Allowance
(i) Forward Journey For attending a Parliament Session or meeting of a Parliamentary Committee or for the purpose of attending any other business connected with her/his dulles as a member from her/his usual place of residence to the place of duty, a meraber is entitled to:
(a) By Rall-One free non-transferable First class AC or Executive class of any train pass and one First class and one Second class fare.
(b) By Air One and one-fourth air fare of the airlines in which the member travels.
(c) By Road-Rs. 16/- per km
The member whose usual place of residence is within the radius of 300 kms. from Delhi is entitled to receive road mileage even if the place is connected by superfast/express/mail train.
The members representing the North-Eastern States are entitled to road mileage from their usual place of residence to the nearest airport even though the places are connected by superfast/express/mail train.
(ii) Return Journey After attending a Session, Committee meeting or any other business connected with her/his duties as such member from the place of duty to the usual place of residence same as 5(1) above.
6. Air Travel Facility A Member is entitled to avail herself himself of 34 single air journeys during a year with his/her spouse or any number of companions or relatives. The spouse/companion can travel alone eight times in a year to meet the member. Any journey performed by the spouse, companions or relatives shall be added in computing the ceiling of 34 air journeys. The balance of unused air journeys for a year shall be carried over to the following year. In case a member performs more than 34 air journeys in a year, she/he is allowed to adjust not exceeding 8 air journeys available for the next year.
7. Rail Travel Facility
(a) A member, on the strength of her/his Identity Card, is entitled to travel at any time by any railway in India in first class air-conditioned or executive class. The Identity Card issued to the member is non-transferable.
(b) The Identity Card also entitles him/her to be accompanied by one person in air-conditioned two tier, when he travels by rail.
8. Facilities for Spouse of a Member
(i) One free non-transferable railway pass to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in any train, and if travelled by air, an amount equal to the air fare, from the usual place of residence of a member to Delhi and back during Parliament session subject to 8 such journeys in a year
(ii) The spouse is entitied to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in all the trains with the member from any place in India to any other place in India. A member having no spouse is entitled to accompany with any other person in lieu of spouse in any train in first class air conditioned or executive class from any place in India to any other place in India in addition to the facility already available to her/him in respect of one companion in AC-II tier
9. Water and Electricity
4000 kl. of water and 50,000 units of electricity (25,000 units measured on light meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost at the residence allotted to a member in Delhi/New Delhi or to a member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
The unutilized units of electricity and water are carried over to the subsequent years and any excess consumption in a particular year is adjusted from the units available for the next year.
10. Telephone Facilities
A member is entitled to have three telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, out of which at least one telephone should be installed at her/his residence or office in Delhi and one at herithis usual place of residence or a place selected by the member in herithis constituency or the State in which she/he resides, the third telephone can be installed at either of the aforesaid place. 50,000 local calls during a year are free to her/him during a year on each of the three telephones. However, Chairman of a Parliamentary Committee is exempted from payment of any charges for local calls made from any one telephone installed at her/his residence in Delhi/New Delhi
These 50,000 free local calls can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year. A member may use any number of telephones for availing the aforesaid 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are borne by the member herself himsel
Every member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/ BSNL services are not available, with national roaming facility for utilization in the constituency and the calls made from these mobile phones are adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls available to her him on three telephones However, the registration and rental charges for private mobile connection are borne by the member herself/himself.
The excess calis made by a member are adjustable from the free local calls available to her/him on three telephones for the next year. Likewise, the unutilized calls of a year are carried over to the subsequent years till the seat of a member becomes vacant
A member is also entitled to avail broadband facility from MTNL/BSNL on any one of the above-cited three telephones subject to the condition that only upte Rs. 1,500/- per month are paid by the Government towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL.
The 3G facility as offered by MTNL/BSNL is optional for members. The charges towards the 3G package as well as additional usage of facility will be adjustable within the aforesaid 1,50,000 free calls available to the Member. However, the 3G compatible handset is to be purchased by the member herself/himself.
11. Conveyance Advance Upto Rs. 4,00,000/- are advanced to a member for the purchase of conveyance Recovery of the said advance together with interest thereon, as applicable on loan to Government servants, shall be made from the salary bill of the member in not more than 60 equal monthly installments which shall not extend beyond the tenure of her/his membership
12. Medical Facility Members are entitled to same medical facilities as are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-1 under the Central Government Health Scheme
13. Facilities to Physically Incapacitated Members A member who is physically incapacitated shall be entitled to
(a) By Air: One additional air fare for the accompanied person
(b) By Rail A companion in the same class in which she/he travels in lieu of the air-conditioned two tier class railway pass
(c) By Road One road mileage In case a physically incapacitated member who cannot perform journey by rail or air, she/he is entitled to road mileage for the entire journey performed by her/him by road
14. Facilities to Ex-Members of Parliament
(i) Pension Every person who has served as a member of the Provisional Parliament or either House of Parliament for any period is entitled to pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month with effect from 18.05.2009 Where any person has served the Parliament for a period exceeding five years, she/he shall be entitled for an additional pension @Rs. 1,500/- per month for every year in excess of five years For the purpose of calculation of years for determination of additional pension, the period of nine months or more is rounded off to one complete year
Where an Ex-Member is also entitled to any other pension which is outside the purview of Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (MSA Act), she/he shall be entitled to receive the pension as Ex-Member in addition to such other pension.
Where any person entitled to pension as Ex- Member of Parliament is elected to the office of the President or Vice-President or is appointed as Governor or Administrator or becomes a member of Council of States or House of the People or any State Legislature or metropolitan council of is employed on a salary under the Central or any State Government or any corporation owned or controlled by Central/State Government or any local authority or becomes otherwise entitled to any remuneration from such Government, corporation or local authority, such person shaill not be entitled to any pension as Ex-Member of Parliament However, if the salary/remuneration so payable to such person is less than the pension payable to her/him as Ex-Member of Parliament, such person shall be entitled only to receive the balance as pension
(ii) Family pension to spouse/dependent of deceased Member/Ex-Member The spouse or dependent of a deceased Member/Ex-Member is entitled for the remaining period of her/his life to receive family pension equal to one-half of the pension otherwise admissible to the deceased Member/Ex-Member at the time of her/his death.
The dependent shall get family pension subject to fulfilment of conditions as stipulated in section 2(aa) of the MSA Act.
If the spouseidependent is entitled to any other pension under MSA Act, she/he will not be entitled to receive family pension
No person shall be entitled to claim arrears of family pension for the period prior to 15th September, 2006.
(iii) Rail Travel Facility Under Section BAA of the MSA Act, an Ex-Member is entitled to travel in any train in air-conditioned two tier class along with a companion or in air-conditioned first class if she/he travels alone, on the strength of Ex-MP identity card issued to henhim by Lok Sabhar Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
(iv) Steamer Facility - An Ex-Member of Parliament who had represented Andaman & Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep is entitled to travel by the highest class of accommodation in any steamer sailing between the A&N Islands or Lakshadweep, as the case may be, and from Islands to Mainland in India on the strength of authorization issued to this effect by Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
(v) Medical Facility Central Government Health Scheme is applicable to Ex-Members residing in cities covered by CGHS on payment of contribution at the same rate as they were paying as Member of Parliament. This facility is obtained by Ex- Member direct from Director-General (CGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, New Delhi

response_summary: The CPIO provided information by directing the applicant to the Lok Sabha website, where details about questions raised by MP Rakesh Singh, his participation in debates during the 15th Lok Sabha, and his committee memberships are publicly available. The first appeal, which contended that information was not directly provided and that the CPIO did not transfer the application to other public authorities, was dismissed because the information was already in the public domain and the reply was provided within 30 days.

Decision and Reasons
1. I have gone through the RTI application and the First Appeal.
2. I find that the CPIO has rightfully disseminated the information through
the Under Secretary In-charge of Information Cell, to the appellant by
providing pointed replies (based on the information supplied by the
concerned divisions of this public authority) to the RTI queries. And there
is nothing inconsistent with the provisions of RTI Act in this respect.

provisions of (a) and (b) of Section 6 (3) for transferring the application to
the other public authorities and there was delay on his part (CPIO's part)
beyond 30 days is not tenable as there was no necessity of transferring
the application to other Public Authority because the information was
already held by the Lok Sabha Secretariat which already stood
disseminated as in Public Domain for which appropriate web-link was

subject: Information related to 3D selfie booths or 3D selfie points installed or erected at various railway stations across Central Railway, sought under RTI Act, 2005.
questions: Names of stations across Crly where 3D selfie Booths or 3D selfie Points of PM Narendra Modi installed or erected.
Amount spent or Cost incurred for erecting or installing each 3D Selfie Booths or Selfie Points of PM Narendra Modi across Railway station on Central Railway.
response_summary: The response details the names of stations across Mumbai, Bhusaval, Nagpur, Pune, and Solapur divisions of Central Railway where 3D selfie booths or points of PM Narendra Modi have been installed, distinguishing between temporary and permanent installations. title: RTI Request for Farm Loan and Waiver Data from SBI
department: State Bank of India, Premises & Estate Department
subject: Application under the Right to Information Act – 2005 regarding farm loan and waiver information.
questions: Please provide the total number of farmers who have obtained farm loans from bank and financial institutions as of 01.06.2024. The information may be furnished indicating:
Number of farmers with loans less than one lakh.
Number of farmers with loans between one lakh and 1.5 lakhs.
Number of farmers with loans between 1.5 lakhs and 2 lakhs.
Number of farmers with loans of two lakhs and above.
Please provide the total number of farmers who have received a farm loan waiver in this government. The information should include:
Number of farmers with loans less than one lakh, along with the amount waived.
Number of farmers with loans between one lakh and 1.5 lakhs, along with the amount waived.
Number of farmers with loans between 1.5 lakhs and 2 lakhs, along with the amount waived.
Number of farmers with loans of two lakhs and above, along with the amount waived.
How much amount has the government allocated for the farm loan Waiver.
How much of the allocated amount has been waived so far.
How much amount is pending to be waived for farm loan waiver.
response_summary: The State Bank of India provided data on the number of farmers with farm loans and those who received loan waivers, categorised by loan amount, specifically for SBI data only. The bank stated that information regarding government allocation for farm loan waivers, amounts waived so far, and pending amounts is not known to them, as the total eligible list from government stipulations has not been shared.

response_full_text: 16वीं लोक सभा का 10वां सत्र (शीतकालीन सत्र) 16 नवम्बर, 2016 को आरंभ हुआ था और 16 दिसम्बर, 2016 को इसे अनिश्चित काल के लिए स्थगित किया गया था । इस सत्र का अवसान 18 दिसम्बर, 2016 को हुआ था ।लोक सभा द्वारा 2016 के शीतकालीन सत्र के दौरान चार सरकारी विधेयकों पर चर्चा की गई/पारित किए गए और लोक सभा में आज की तिथि तक बीस सरकारी विधेयक लंबित हैं । लोक सभा द्वारा 16वीं लोक सभा के शीतकालीन सत्र (दसवें सत्र) के दौरान कोई भी गैर-सरकारी सदस्य विधेयक पारित नहीं किया गया । 16वीं लोक सभा के दसवें सत्र के अंत तक कुल मिलाकर 541 गैर-सरकारी सदस्य विधेयक लंबित हैं ।16वीं लोक सभा के 10वें सत्र (शीताकलीन सत्र) के दौरान स्थगन से संबंधित प्र. सं. 3 और 4 हेतु अपेक्षित सूचना लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् loksabha.nic.in→'Business'→'Bulletin-I' पर उपलब्ध है । अतः आवेदक को परामर्श दिया जाता है कि वह उक्त वेबसाइट से वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त कर लें ।सदस्यों (माननीय अध्यक्ष, उपाध्यक्ष, प्रधानमंत्री और मंत्रियों को छोड़कर) के लिए उनके नाम के सामने हस्ताक्षर करने के लिए एक रजिस्टर रखा जाता है ताकि किसी विशेष दिन सभा की बैठक में उनकी उपस्थिति का प्रमाण रखा जा सके । 16वीं लोक सभा के सभी सत्रों के दौरान लोक सभा के सदस्यों द्वारा उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर करने/नहीं करने से संबंधित ब्यौरा लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् www.loksabha.nic.in पर क्रमशः Members-Sitting Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance –All Members शीर्षकों के अंतर्गत उपलब्ध है । तथापि, आवेदक यह नोट कर लें कि ऐसा हो सकता है कि किसी विशेष दिन कोई सदस्य बैठक में उपस्थित रहा हो परंतु उस दिन उसने उपस्थिति रजिस्टर में हस्ताक्षर न किए हों । आवेदक से अनुरोध है कि वह उक्त वेबसाइट देखें और वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त कर लें ।संसद के संचालन पर होने वाले व्यय को अनेक एजेंसियां, अर्थात् लोक सभा सचिवालय, राज्य सभा सचिवालय, शहरी विकास मंत्रालय (के.लो.नि.वि.) और अन्य मंत्रालय/विभाग वहन करते हैं । संसद के संचालन के संबंध में विभिन्न मंत्रालयों/विभागों/राज्य सभा सचिवालय आदि द्वारा किए जाने वाले व्यय को दर्ज करने के लिए कोई विशेष लेखा शीर्ष नहीं है । लोक सभा के बजट अनुदान से किए गए सत्र-वार व्यय का ब्यौरा आईएफयू के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है । पीएंडएओ, लोक सभा द्वारा प्रेषित व्यय के आंकड़ों के आधार पर संकलित नवम्बर और दिसम्बर, 2016 के दौरान लेखा शीर्ष-वार किए गए व्यय (अलेखापरीक्षित) का ब्यौरा संलग्न है (अनुबंध) । अन्य मंत्रालयों/विभागों/राज्य सभा सचिवालय द्वारा किए गए व्यय से संबंधित जानकारी आईएफयू के पास उपलब्ध नहीं है ।लोक सभा की कार्यवाही के दौरान बहुत से सदस्यों ने विभिन्न मुद्दों पर व्यवधान उत्पन्न करने का प्रयास किया । तथापि, 16वीं लोक सभा के विगत शीतकालीन सत्र के दौरान किसी भी सदस्य को लोक सभा के प्रक्रिया तथा कार्य संचालन नियमों के नियम 373, 374 और 374ए के अंतर्गत निलंबित नहीं किया गया ।कृपया बिंदु सं. 7 का उत्तर देखें ।संसद सदस्यों का वेतन संसद सदस्य, वेतन, भत्ता और पेंशन अधिनियम, 1954 के द्वारा विनियमित किया जाता है । आवेदक द्वारा वांछित सूचना का रख-रखाव करने हेतु अधिनियम में कोई प्रावधान नहीं है ।उपलब्ध कराए गए हैं ।श्रीमती सुदेश लूथरा, संयुक्त सचिव, लोक सभा सचिवालय, कमरा सं. 336, संसदीय सौध, नई दिल्ली-110001 (दूरभाषः 23034336)सत्रों की तिथि सरकार द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती है और संसदीय कार्य मंत्रालय द्वारा इस सचिवालय को सूचित की जाती है । आगामी सत्र का अंतरिम कार्यक्रम (16वीं लोक सभा का 11वां सत्र) लोक सभा की वेबसाइट अर्थात् loksabha.nic.in→'Business'→'Provisional Calendar' पर अपलोड कर दिया गया है । अतः आवेदक को परामर्श दिया जाता है कि वह उक्त वेबसाइट लिंक से सूचना प्राप्त कर लें ।

response_summary: लोक सभा सचिवालय ने आवेदक को सूचित किया है कि वर्ष 2003 में विद्युत विधेयक, 2003 और विद्युत (संशोधन) विधेयक, 2003 संसद द्वारा पारित किए गए थे। अंग्रेजी प्रतियाँ संलग्न हैं, जबकि हिंदी संस्करण सचिवालय द्वारा मुद्रित नहीं किया जाता है। अधिनियमों की प्रतियाँ प्रदान करने के लिए आवेदन विधि मंत्रालय को स्थानांतरित कर दिया गया है, और अधिनियम विधि और न्याय मंत्रालय की वेबसाइट पर भी उपलब्ध है। भौतिक प्रतियाँ प्राप्त करने के लिए 168/- रुपये का शुल्क देय होगा।

आवेदक को सूचित किया जाता है कि वर्ष 2003 के दौरान, इस विषय पर दो विधेयक, अर्थात् विद्युत विधेयक, 2003 और विद्युत (संशोधन) विधेयक, 2003 संसद द्वारा पारित किए गए थे । सभाओं द्वारा यथापारित और राष्ट्रपति की अनुमति प्राप्त उपर्युक्त विधेयकों की प्रत्येक की अंग्रेजी संस्करण की प्रति संलग्न है (लगभग 84 पृष्ठ') आवेदक को आगे सूचित किया जाता है कि सभाओं द्वारा पारित विधेयक के हिन्दी संस्करण को लोक सभा सचिवालय द्वारा मुद्रित नहीं किया जाता है । आवेदक को अधिनियमों की प्रतियां प्रदान करने के लिए, आवेदक का आवेदन दिनांक 27.01.2017 को विधि मंत्रालय को भी अंतरित कर दिया गया है । इसके अतिरिक्त, विद्युत अधिनियम, 2003 विधि और न्याय मंत्रालय के निम्नलिखित वेब पते पर भी उपलब्ध है । lawmin.nic.in पर India Code शीर्षक के तहत आवेदक से उपर्युक्त वेब पते का अवलोकन करने और अपनी वांछित सूचना डाउनलोड करने का भी अनुरोध किया जाता है ।

title: RTI Reply on Photography and Selfies in Noida Metro Premises
subject: Reply to RTI Application under RTI Act,2005.
questions: Please provide a copy of the specific ministry order or gazette notification or NMRC internal circular that explicitly prohibits commuters from taking personal photographs or videos using mobile phone within the metro premises and these areas: - Foot Over Bridge connecting the station to public roads Walkways and stairs leading to the security frisking area The concourse area located after the AFC gates but before the platform specifically areas containing only lifts escalators and staircases Platforms without touching yellow line

Does NMRC have a written legal definition for nuisance under section 59 of the metro railways O&M Act 2002 that explicitly includes a stationary selfie or photo with friends taken via a handheld mobile phone without tripods or professional lighting.

Please clarify whether a simple selfie or a selfie with friends or family is prohibited inside NMRC premises including on the concourse FOBS and platforms if no nuisance or obstruction or crowding or security issue is being caused like anything without blocking any walkway or lift or escalator under which specific sub clause of the act is this considered a punishable offense.

Please provide a copy of the Standard Operating Procedure SOP issued to PAC personnel and NMRC security staff regarding the confiscation of mobile phones or the forced deletion of personal photos from a commuter's private gallery.

State the legal authority that allows a NMRC or PAC official to demand a commuter delete a personal photo that does not capture security sensitive equipment like scanners or Security check area or CCTV control rooms.

Since NMRC record every commuter's movement via high-definition CCTV please provide the policy justification for prohibiting a commuter from taking personal photo of themselves or their group within the same area.

Please clarify if there is a legal distinction in NMRC penalty books between Filming a Dance or Reel for social media and taking a static personal photograph If yes provide the different penalty structure for both.

Please provide the total number of persons fines and the total revenue collected under Section 59 Nuisance for the financial years 2023 to 24 and 2024 to 25 and 2025 to 26 categorized specifically for Photography or Videography violations.

Has NMRC conducted any study or holds any record security Audit or Safety Review explaining why photography is permitted in international metros e.g. New York and Tokyo and London and Moscow but prohibited in Noida or same that concluded that mobile photography by commuters is a higher threat in Noida compared to those international Metro systems If yes please provide a copy of such report.
response_summary: NMRC states that filming/photography within metro premises is permitted only under a permission-based commercial policy due to safety and security concerns. Section 59 of the Metro Railways O&M Act 2002 does not specifically define 'nuisance' to include selfies, but lists it as a broad category of conduct. The SOP regarding confiscation of mobile phones and deletion of personal photos is exempt from disclosure under RTI Act, 2005. NMRC/PAC officials are authorized to regulate passenger conduct and may issue instructions against photography if it affects safety, security, or operations. Information on specific penalty distinctions for photography/videography or total fines collected for these violations is not available in the requested form and would disproportionately divert resources, making it exempt. NMRC has not conducted any study or holds records comparing mobile photography threats in Noida to international metro systems.

response_full_text:
The information regarding property asset values of Members of Lok Sabha are not maintained in the Secretariat. As per provisions of RTI Act, 2005, the public authority is not required to create new information.
However, the declarations of Assets & Liabilities as submitted by Members of the present Lok Sabha in accordance with ‘Members of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets and Liabilities) Rules, 2004' are available. The declarations are at present running approximately into 4500 pages. These shall be made available to the applicant on deposit information fee of Rs. 9000/- (@Rs. 2/- per page) for 4500 pages of information.*
Further, as regards the details relating to such declarations of Members of Rajya Sabha and Union Ministers is concerned, the application has also been transferred to the Rajya Sabha Secretariat and Prime Minister's Office (PMO) for furnishing information directly to the applicant. The applicant may approach them for further information.
Lok Sabha Secretariat does not provide any travel car as such to any MP. However, common ferry services are available to MPs for travelling from their residence in Delhi to Parliament House Complex. Expenditure incurred on these ferry vehicles during the current financial year up to 31/01/2016 is Rs. 3847947/-. The expenditure incurred as Medical head during the current financial year up to 31/01/2016 is Rs. 15011703/-. Details about hospitality are not maintained in the Branch concerned of this Secretariat.
The expenditure on working of Parliament is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments.
There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Branches/agencies in connection with the conduct of Parliament. Similarly, No separate budget provision is kept for proceedings of Parliament.
Under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha, Head of account -wise allocation is made for booking the expenditure incurred on Members of Lok Sabha and staff of Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Expenditure incurred along with provision made under Budget Grant of Lok Sabha from the Financial Year 2009-10 onwards is available on Lok Sabha homepage under link :
http://164.100.47.132/LssNew/Secretariat/DemandLokSabha.aspx
*
For information pertaining to this Secretariat, the information fee is required to be paid by way of cash at “Reception of Parliament Library Building, Lok Sabha Secretariat” against proper receipt or sent through money order or Demand Draft or Bankers Cheque or Indian Postal Order payable to ‘Drawing and Disbursing Officer, Lok Sabha', in terms of Lok Sabha Secretariat Right to Information (Regulation of Fees & Cost) Rules 2005, and the amendment Rules, 2007. You are also informed that Demand Draft/Bankers Cheque/Indian Postal Order in favour of 'Accounts Officer, Lok Sabha' is also accepted in this Secretariat.

FACILITIES PROVIDED TO
MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT
BY M.S. BRANCH
LOK SABHA SECRETARIAT
NEW DELHI
"1. Accommodation
(1) Members who come to Delhi prior to publication of Notification
by the Election Commission for constituting new Lok Sabha are
entitled to transit accommodation.
(ii) Accommodation in the form of a flat is free throughout the term of
office to a Member. However, normal licence fee @ Rs. 105 is
charged on bungalow.
(i) Sofa covers and curtains are get washed by the CPWD after
every 3 months which are provided free of cost to Members.
(iv) Fumiture to be made free of charge to the Members within the
revised monetary celling of Rs. 60,000 in respect of durable
furniture and Rs. 15,000/- for non-durable furniture. The rental
for additional items of furniture shall be charged on the
depreciated value of furniture.
(v) Members of Lok Sabha or their families can retain Government
Accommodation for a maximum period of one month after their
retirement, resignation iremoval or ceasing to be a Member of
Lok Sabha on payment of the same rent, if any, which they
were paying immediately before the occurrence of any of the
events mentioned above.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament may retain
Government accommodation for a maximum period of six months
from the date of death of such a Member.
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament)
Rule, 1956 (as amended).
*2. Water and Electricity
(i) 4000 Kilolitre of waler and 50,000 units of Electricity (25,000
units measured on lights meter and 25,000 units measured on
power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from
1st January of every year is supplied free of cost in the residence
allotted to a Member in Delhi/New Delhi and to a Member who
is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
(ii) Where both husband and wife are Members of Parliament and
are residing in the same accommodation, their admissibility for
supply of free electricity and water at the residence allotted to
them shall be calculated separately
(it) The unconsumed units of electricity and water out of those
otherwise admissible to a Member in any year shall be carried
over to the subsequent years III his seat becomes vacant
(iv) In case of consumption of electricity and water by a Member in
excess of his entitlement for a particular year, such excess
consumption of electricity and water shall be adjusted from the
units of electricity and water in kilolitre available for the next
year.
(v) In case the seat of a Member becomes vacant due to his
resignation or completion of term, he will be entitled to consume
the balance units of electricity and water as available for that
year within a maximum period of one month from the date on
which his seat becomes vacant.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament shall be entitled
to consume the balance units of electricity and water in klolita
available to such Member for that particular year within a period
of one month from the date of death of that Member.
3. Telephone Facilities
(i) A member is entitled to have two telephones without payment of
installation and rental charges, one at his residence or office in
Delhi and the other at his usual place of residence or a place
selected by him in his constituency or the State in which he
resides, 50,000 local calls during a year are free to a Member
on each of the two telephones
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament)
Rule, 1956 (as amended)
3
ANNEXURE I
(ii) A Member is also entitled to have one additionall telephone
without payment of installation and rental charges either at his
residence in Delhi New Delhi or at his usual place of residence
or at the place selected by him within the State in which his
constituency is or in the Slate in which he resides and 50,000
free local calls during a year are allowed on that telephone for
internet connectivity purposes.
(ii) The above mentioned 50,000 free local calls admissible on
each telephone can be clubbed together which comes to
1,50,000 local calls in a year.
(iv) A Member may use any number of telephones for availing the
above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the
condition that the telephones are in the name of Member and
the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are
bome by the Member himself.
(v) A Member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of
MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL
or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/BSNL services
are not available, with national roaming facility for utilisation in
the constituency and the calls made from these telephones may
be adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 calls available
to them on 3 telephones. However, the registration and rental
charges for private mobile phone connection are bome by the
Member himself.
(vi) In case a Member makes calls in excess of admissible free local
calls in a year, the excess calls can be adjusted from the calls
available to him on three telephones for the next year. Further,
the unutilised telephone calls of a year are carmed over to the
subsequent years till the seat of a Member becomes vacant
(vii) A Member is also entitled to avail broadband facility
from MTNL/BSNL on any one of the above-mentioned three telephones
subject to the condition that the Government may pay uplo
Rs. 1,500 per month towards the charges of this facility directly
to MTNL/BSNL
4. Transport Facilities
The Members are also being provided the following facilities
(i) Ferry Vehicles through Transport Desk
There is a Transport Desk from where vehicles are provided
to facilitate the Members to go from Parliament complex to their
4
residences and vice-versa in New Delhi. The transport facility
is provided to all Members of Parliament between their
residences and Parliament House Complex on a payment of a
token amount of Rs. 5/- for each trip,
(ii) Rail Transport
Railway Booking and Reservation Offices function in Parliament
House and near Outer Reception Office, Parliament House
throughout the year for the convenience of Members of
Parliament. The reservation of accommodation in trains for
Members and their spouses is made from the Reservation Office,
Parliament House and reservation of accommodation for
Members' guests/attendants/friends etc. is made from the
Reservation Office, near outer Reception Office, Parliament
House.
(i) Air Transport
An Air Booking Office of Air India functions in Parliament House
throughout the year. Arrangements also exist for Members of
Parliament to book air passages with the Air India Booking
Office in Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi. The booking can also
be done by Members over the telephone in certain
circumstances.
(iv) Taxis and Scooters Outside Parliament House Annexe
During Session Period, arrangements are made for availability
of laxis and scooters at taxi Stands outside Parliament House
Complex with the assistance of Delhi Police, Taxi Stands around
Parliament House Complex and Watch and Ward Office
Lok Sabha Secretariat.
5. Medical Facilities
(i) Members of Parliament are entitled to same medical facilities as
are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-i
under Central Government Health Scheme.
(ii) Under the Central Government Health Scheme, as extended to
Members of Parliament, a First Aid Post in the Lobby of the
Central Hall of Parliament House and a Medical Centre in the
basement of Parliament House Annexe function throughout the
year to render First Aid to Members of Parliament and to meet
the first aid requirement arising in the precincts of the Parliament
House Complex.

(ii) The Medical Centre has X-Ray, Ultra Sound, ECG, Pathological
Laboratory facilities and consultation in Cardiac, Dental,
Ophthalmic, ENT, Gynae, Skin, Orthopaedic, Psychiatric and
Surgical Specialties. Apart from this, the services of Dietician,
Paediatrician, Physiotherapist are also available on given days
of the weeks. The Medical Centre maintains a record of Health
status of each Member of Parliament
6. Other Facilities to Members
(a) Diplomatic Passport
A Member and his wife/husband is eligible for the issue of
Diplomatic Passport for going abroad on study tour/conference/
private visit
(b) Income Tax Sub-Office
Under arrangements made with Ministry of Finance, an Income
Tax Sub-office function in Parliament House Annexe throughout
the year for rendering assistance to Members of Parliament in
completing their income-tax returns and in resolving their queries
relating to the payment of income-tax
(c) State Bank of india Branches af Parliament House and Annexe
Branches of the State Bank of India function in Parliament House
and Annexe. Besides the normal banking facilities, they accept
payment in respect of income-tax and other direct taxes,
investment plans, etc. Safe deposit lockers have also been
provided at Parliament House Annexe Branch for the
convenience of Members. ATM facility is provided for the
convenience of Members in Parliament House/Annexe and
Parliament Library Building.
(d) Rationing Sub-Office
With the introduction of statutory rationing in Delhi, a Rationing
Sub-Office opened by the Delhi Rationing Authority functions in
Parliament House during the Session period for the issue of
Ration Cards to Members and their families
(e) Kendriya Bhandar
A branch of the Kendriya Bhandar located at 23, Mahadev
Road is open from 09.30 hrs. to 18.30 hrs, for the sale of
essential commodities (such as grocery, toilet and househoid
items, textiles, watches, etc.).
(1) NDMC Liaison Office
A full-fledged Liaison Office of the NDMC (New Delhi Municipal
Council) functions in Parliament House Annexe throughout the
year to look into the complaints of Members with regard to
meters installed at their residences and all other matters
connected with the NDMC, including electricity and water bills
of Members.
(g) LPG Service Counter of the Oil industry
The Service Counter of the Oil Industry in regard to supply of
LPG and rendering timely service in respect of defective,
installation, etc. functions during Session period in Parliament
House Annexe for the convenience of Members of Parliament.
(1) Secunty arrangements in Members' residential localities
A Special Cell has been set up by Delhi Police in the Office of the
Assistant Commissioner Police, Police Station, Parliament Street,
New Delhi, to assist the Members of Parliament to maintain the
security of their residences. The timing of the Cell is from 0900
hours to 1900 hours daily. Members are required to inform the
Cell as and when they happen to go outside Delhi to enable the
Police authorities to make necessary arrangements for the
security of their residences during their absence from Delhi.
The Members, for any other assistance they may require from
the local police, may also contact the Cell
(i) Army Disposal Vehicles
Members may apply for Army Disposal Vehicles from the Ministry
of Defence. The requests received from the Members are
forwarded to Ministry of Defence for release of Army Disposal
Vehicles from the Army Disposal Stock
(1) Catering Service
Northern Railway is running MPs Canteen in North Avenue
for the convenience of Members and their guests. In South i
Avenue, catering services is being run by a private caterer. In
Westem Court Hostel, the canteen is run by the ITDC.
2
1. Salary
Rs. 50,000/- per month.
2. Daily Allowance
Rs. 2,000/- per day for each day of residence on duty. Daily
Allowance shall be paid only when the member signs the
register maintained for the purpose
3. Constituency Allowance
4.
Rs. 45,000/- per month.
Office Expense Allowance
Rs. 45,000/- per month out of which Rs 15,000/- is for
meeting expenses of stationery items and postage; and
upto Rs 30,000/- is paid by the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha
Secretariats to the person(s) as may be engaged by a
member for obtaining secretarial assistance, provided that
one such person must be computer literate as certified by
the Member herself himself.
5. Travelling Allowance
(i) Forward Journey For attending a Parliament
Session or meeting of a Parliamentary Committee
or for the purpose of attending any other business
connected with her/his dulles as a member from
her/his usual place of residence to the place of
duty, a meraber is entitled to:
(a) By Rall-One free non-transferable First class
AC or Executive class of any train pass and
one First class and one Second class fare.
(b) By Air One and one-fourth air fare of the
airlines in which the member travels.
(c) By Road-Rs. 16/- per km
The member whose usual place of residence
is within the radius of 300 kms. from Delhi is
entitled to receive road mileage even if the
place is connected by superfast/express/mail
train.
The members representing the North-Eastern
States are entitled to road mileage from their
usual place of residence to the nearest airport
even though the places are connected by
superfast/express/mail train.
(ii) Return Journey After attending a Session,
Committee meeting or any other business
connected with her/his duties as such member
from the place of duty to the usual place of
residence same as 5(1) above.
6.
Air Travel Facility
A Member is entitled to avail herself himself of 34 single
air journeys during a year with his/her spouse or any number
of companions or relatives. The spouse/companion can
travel alone eight times in a year to meet the member. Any
journey performed by the spouse, companions or relatives
shall be added in computing the ceiling of 34 air journeys.
The balance of unused air journeys for a year shall be
carried over to the following year. In case a member
performs more than 34 air journeys in a year, she/he is
allowed to adjust not exceeding 8 air journeys available for
the next year.
7. Rail Travel Facility
(a) A member, on the strength of her/his Identity Card, is
entitled to travel at any time by any railway in India in first
class air-conditioned or executive class. The Identity Card
issued to the member is non-transferable.
(b) The Identity Card also entitles him/her to be
accompanied by one person in air-conditioned two tier, when
he travels by rail.
8.
Facilities for Spouse of a Member
(i) One free non-transferable railway pass to travel in
first class air conditioned or executive class in any train,
and if travelled by air, an amount equal to the air fare, from
the usual place of residence of a member to Delhi and back
during Parliament session subject to 8 such journeys in a
year
(ii) The spouse is entitied to travel in first class air
conditioned or executive class in all the trains with the member
from any place in India to any other place in India. A member
having no spouse is entitled to accompany with any other
person in lieu of spouse in any train in first class air
conditioned or executive class from any place in India to any
other place in India in addition to the facility already available
to her/him in respect of one companion in AC-II tier
9. Water and Electricity
4000 kl. of water and 50,000 units of electricity (25,000
units measured on light meter and 25,000 units measured on
power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from
1st January of every year is supplied free of cost at the
residence allotted to a member in Delhi/New Delhi or to a
member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
The unutilized units of electricity and water are carried
over to the subsequent years and any excess consumption
in a particular year is adjusted from the units available for
the next year.
10. Telephone Facilities
A member is entitled to have three telephones without
payment of installation and rental charges, out of which at
least one telephone should be installed at her/his residence
or office in Delhi and one at herithis usual place of residence
or a place selected by the member in her/his constituency or
the State in which she/he resides, the third telephone can
be installed at either of the aforesaid place. 50,000 local
calls during a year are free to her/him during a year on each
of the three telephones. However, Chairman of a
Parliamentary Committee is exempted from payment of any
charges for local calls made from any one telephone installed
at her/his residence in Delhi/New Delhi
These 50,000 free local calls can be clubbed together
which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year. A member
may use any number of telephones for availing the aforesaid
1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the
telephones are in the name of member and the installation
and rental charges of additional telephones are borne by
the member herself himsel
Every member is also entitled to one mobile phone

1,50,000 free local calls available to her him on three
