FACILITIES PROVIDED TO MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT BY M.S. BRANCH LOK SABHA SECRETARIAT NEW DELHI
"1. Accommodation
(1) Members who come to Delhi prior to publication of Notification by the Election Commission for constituting new Lok Sabha are entitled to transit accommodation.
(ii) Accommodation in the form of a flat is free throughout the term of office to a Member. However, normal licence fee @ Rs. 105 is charged on bungalow.
(i) Sofa covers and curtains are get washed by the CPWD after every 3 months which are provided free of cost to Members.
(iv) Fumiture to be made free of charge to the Members within the revised monetary celling of Rs. 60,000 in respect of durable furniture and Rs. 15,000/- for non-durable furniture. The rental for additional items of furniture shall be charged on the depreciated value of furniture.
(v) Members of Lok Sabha or their families can retain Government Accommodation for a maximum period of one month after their retirement, resignation iremoval or ceasing to be a Member of Lok Sabha on payment of the same rent, if any, which they were paying immediately before the occurrence of any of the events mentioned above.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament may retain Government accommodation for a maximum period of six months from the date of death of such a Member.
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rule, 1956 (as amended).
*2. Water and Electricity
(i) 4000 Kilolitre of waler and 50,000 units of Electricity (25,000 units measured on lights meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost in the residence allotted to a Member in Delhi/New Delhi and to a Member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
(ii) Where both husband and wife are Members of Parliament and are residing in the same accommodation, their admissibility for supply of free electricity and water at the residence allotted to them shall be calculated separately
(it) The unconsumed units of electricity and water out of those otherwise admissible to a Member in any year shall be carried over to the subsequent years III his seat becomes vacant
(iv) In case of consumption of electricity and water by a Member in excess of his entitlement for a particular year, such excess consumption of electricity and water shall be adjusted from the units of electricity and water in kilolitre available for the next year.
(v) In case the seat of a Member becomes vacant due to his resignation or completion of term, he will be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water as available for that year within a maximum period of one month from the date on which his seat becomes vacant.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament shall be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water in klolita available to such Member for that particular year within a period of one month from the date of death of that Member.
3. Telephone Facilities
(i) A member is entitled to have two telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, one at his residence or office in Delhi and the other at his usual place of residence or a place selected by him in his constituency or the State in which he resides, 50,000 local calls during a year are free to a Member on each of the two telephones
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rule, 1956 (as amended)
(ii) A Member is also entitled to have one additionall telephone without payment of installation and rental charges either at his residence in Delhi New Delhi or at his usual place of residence or at the place selected by him within the State in which his constituency is or in the Slate in which he resides and 50,000 free local calls during a year are allowed on that telephone for internet connectivity purposes.
(ii) The above mentioned 50,000 free local calls admissible on each telephone can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year.
(iv) A Member may use any number of telephones for availing the above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of Member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are bome by the Member himself.
(v) A Member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/BSNL services are not available, with national roaming facility for utilisation in the constituency and the calls made from these telephones may be adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 calls available to them on 3 telephones. However, the registration and rental charges for private mobile phone connection are bome by the Member himself.
(vi) In case a Member makes calls in excess of admissible free local calls in a year, the excess calls can be adjusted from the calls available to him on three telephones for the next year. Further, the unutilised telephone calls of a year are carmed over to the subsequent years till the seat of a Member becomes vacant
(vii) A Member is also entitled to avail broadband facility from MTNL/BSNL on any one of the above-mentioned three telephones subject to the condition that the Government may pay uplo Rs. 1,500 per month towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL
4. Transport Facilities
The Members are also being provided the following facilities
(i) Ferry Vehicles through Transport Desk
There is a Transport Desk from where vehicles are provided to facilitate the Members to go from Parliament complex to their residences and vice-versa in New Delhi. The transport facility is provided to all Members of Parliament between their residences and Parliament House Complex on a payment of a token amount of Rs. 5/- for each trip,
(ii) Rail Transport
Railway Booking and Reservation Offices function in Parliament House and near Outer Reception Office, Parliament House throughout the year for the convenience of Members of Parliament. The reservation of accommodation in trains for Members and their spouses is made from the Reservation Office, Parliament House and reservation of accommodation for Members' guests/attendants/friends etc. is made from the Reservation Office, near outer Reception Office, Parliament House.
(i) Air Transport
An Air Booking Office of Air India functions in Parliament House throughout the year. Arrangements also exist for Members of Parliament to book air passages with the Air India Booking Office in Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi. The booking can also be done by Members over the telephone in certain circumstances.
(iv) Taxis and Scooters Outside Parliament House Annexe
During Session Period, arrangements are made for availability of laxis and scooters at taxi Stands outside Parliament House Complex with the assistance of Delhi Police, Taxi Stands around Parliament House Complex and Watch and Ward Office Lok Sabha Secretariat.
5. Medical Facilities
(i) Members of Parliament are entitled to same medical facilities as are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-i under Central Government Health Scheme.
(ii) Under the Central Government Health Scheme, as extended to Members of Parliament, a First Aid Post in the Lobby of the Central Hall of Parliament House and a Medical Centre in the basement of Parliament House Annexe function throughout the year to render First Aid to Members of Parliament and to meet the first aid requirement arising in the precincts of the Parliament House Complex.
(ii) The Medical Centre has X-Ray, Ultra Sound, ECG, Pathological Laboratory facilities and consultation in Cardiac, Dental, Ophthalmic, ENT, Gynae, Skin, Orthopaedic, Psychiatric and Surgical Specialties. Apart from this, the services of Dietician, Paediatrician, Physiotherapist are also available on given days of the weeks. The Medical Centre maintains a record of Health status of each Member of Parliament
6. Other Facilities to Members
(a) Diplomatic Passport
A Member and his wife/husband is eligible for the issue of Diplomatic Passport for going abroad on study tour/conference/ private visit
(b) Income Tax Sub-Office
Under arrangements made with Ministry of Finance, an Income Tax Sub-office function in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year for rendering assistance to Members of Parliament in completing their income-tax returns and in resolving their queries relating to the payment of income-tax
(c) State Bank of india Branches af Parliament House and Annexe
Branches of the State Bank of India function in Parliament House and Annexe. Besides the normal banking facilities, they accept payment in respect of income-tax and other direct taxes, investment plans, etc. Safe deposit lockers have also been provided at Parliament House Annexe Branch for the convenience of Members. ATM facility is provided for the convenience of Members in Parliament House/Annexe and Parliament Library Building.
(d) Rationing Sub-Office
With the introduction of statutory rationing in Delhi, a Rationing Sub-Office opened by the Delhi Rationing Authority functions in Parliament House during the Session period for the issue of Ration Cards to Members and their families
(e) Kendriya Bhandar
A branch of the Kendriya Bhandar located at 23, Mahadev Road is open from 09.30 hrs. to 18.30 hrs, for the sale of essential commodities (such as grocery, toilet and househoid items, textiles, watches, etc.).
(1) NDMC Liaison Office
A full-fledged Liaison Office of the NDMC (New Delhi Municipal Council) functions in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year to look into the complaints of Members with regard to meters installed at their residences and all other matters connected with the NDMC, including electricity and water bills of Members.
(g) LPG Service Counter of the Oil industry
The Service Counter of the Oil Industry in regard to supply of LPG and rendering timely service in respect of defective, installation, etc. functions during Session period in Parliament House Annexe for the convenience of Members of Parliament.
(1) Secunty arrangements in Members' residential localities
A Special Cell has been set up by Delhi Police in the Office of the Assistant Commissioner Police, Police Station, Parliament Street, New Delhi, to assist the Members of Parliament to maintain the security of their residences. The timing of the Cell is from 0900 hours to 1900 hours daily. Members are required to inform the Cell as and when they happen to go outside Delhi to enable the Police authorities to make necessary arrangements for the security of their residences during their absence from Delhi.
The Members, for any other assistance they may require from the local police, may also contact the Cell
(i) Army Disposal Vehicles
Members may apply for Army Disposal Vehicles from the Ministry of Defence. The requests received from the Members are forwarded to Ministry of Defence for release of Army Disposal Vehicles from the Army Disposal Stock
(1) Catering Service
Northern Railway is running MPs Canteen in North Avenue for the convenience of Members and their guests. In South i Avenue, catering services is being run by a private caterer. In Westem Court Hostel, the canteen is run by the ITDC.
1. Salary Rs. 50,000/- per month.

4. (ii) Return Journey After attending a Session, Committee meeting or any other business connected with her/his duties as such member from the place of duty to the usual place of residence same as 5(1) above.
6. Air Travel Facility A Member is entitled to avail herself himself of 34 single air journeys during a year with his/her spouse or any number of companions or relatives. The spouse/companion can travel alone eight times in a year to meet the member. Any journey performed by the spouse, companions or relatives shall be added in computing the ceiling of 34 air journeys. The balance of unused air journeys for a year shall be carried over to the following year. In case a member performs more than 34 air journeys in a year, she/he is allowed to adjust not exceeding 8 air journeys available for the next year.
7. Rail Travel Facility
(a) A member, on the strength of her/his Identity Card, is entitled to travel at any time by any railway in India in first class air-conditioned or executive class. The Identity Card issued to the member is non-transferable.
(b) The Identity Card also entitles him/her to be accompanied by one person in air-conditioned two tier, when he travels by rail.
8. Facilities for Spouse of a Member
(i) One free non-transferable railway pass to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in any train, and if travelled by air, an amount equal to the air fare, from the usual place of residence of a member to Delhi and back during Parliament session subject to 8 such journeys in a year
(ii) The spouse is entitied to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in all the trains with the member from any place in India to any other place in India. A member having no spouse is entitled to accompany with any other person in lieu of spouse in any train in first class air conditioned or executive class from any place in India to any other place in India in addition to the facility already available to her/him in respect of one companion in AC-II tier
9. Water and Electricity
4000 kl. of water and 50,000 units of electricity (25,000 units measured on light meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost at the residence allotted to a member in Delhi/New Delhi or to a member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
The unutilized units of electricity and water are carried over to the subsequent years and any excess consumption in a particular year is adjusted from the units available for the next year.

A member is entitled to have three telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, out of which at least one telephone should be installed at her/his residence or office in Delhi and one at herithis usual place of residence or a place selected by the member in her/his constituency or the State in which she/he resides, the third telephone can be installed at either of the aforesaid place. 50,000 local calls during a year are free to her/him during a year on each of the three telephones. However, Chairman of a Parliamentary Committee is exempted from payment of any charges for local calls made from any one telephone installed at her/his residence in Delhi/New Delhi
These 50,000 free local calls can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year. A member may use any number of telephones for availing the aforesaid 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are borne by the member herself himsel

The excess calis made by a member are adjustable from the free local calls available to her/him on three telephones for the next year. Likewise, the unutilized calls of a year are carried over to the subsequent years till the seat of a member becomes vacant
A member is also entitled to avail broadband facility from MTNL/BSNL on any one of the above-cited three telephones subject to the condition that only upte Rs. 1,500/- per month are paid by the Government towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL.
The 3G facility as offered by MTNL/BSNL is optional for members. The charges towards the 3G package as well as additional usage of facility will be adjustable within the aforesaid 1,50,000 free calls available to the Member.
However, the 3G compatible handset is to be purchased by the member herself/himself.
11. Conveyance Advance
Upto Rs. 4,00,000/- are advanced to a member for the purchase of conveyance Recovery of the said advance together with interest thereon, as applicable on loan to Government servants, shall be made from the salary bill of the member in not more than 60 equal monthly installments which shall not extend beyond the tenure of her/his membership
12. Medical Facility
Members are entitled to same medical facilities as are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-1 under the Central Government Health Scheme
13. Facilities to Physically Incapacitated Members
A member who is physically incapacitated shall be entitled to
(a) By Air: One additional air fare for the accompanied person
(b) By Rail A companion in the same class in which she/he travels in lieu of the air-conditioned two tier class railway pass
(c) By Road One road mileage
In case a physically incapacitated member who cannot perform journey by rail or air, she/he is entitled to road mileage for the entire journey performed by her/him by road
14. Facilities to Ex-Members of Parliament
(i) Pension Every person who has served as a member of the Provisional Parliament or either House of Parliament for any period is entitled to pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month with effect from 18.05.2009 Where any person has served the Parliament for a period exceeding five years, she/he shall be entitled for an additional pension @Rs. 1,500/- per month for every year in excess of five years For the purpose of calculation of years for determination of additional pension, the period of nine months or more is rounded off to one complete year

title: RTI Response on Parliamentary Privileges for MPs under Article 105
subject: Information regarding parliamentary privileges for sitting and former Members of Parliament.
questions: What are the privileges conferred upon Members of Parliament by the Constitution of India?
Are these privileges available to former members of Parliament?
response_summary: Privileges are granted to Members of Parliament by Article 105 of the Constitution of India, covering powers, privileges, and immunities. These privileges are exclusively for sitting members and do not extend to former members of Parliament.

Privileges have been conferred upon Members of Parliament

title: RTI Reply on Parliament Expenditure and MP Attendance in Winter Session
subject: Supply of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
questions: Certified copies on record for total expenditure on the Winter Session of Parliament.
Certified copies on record for total expenditure due to non-functioning of Parliament due to protest from Opposition.
Please provide me certified copies or record indicating the attendance of each MP during the entire winter session of the Parliament.
response_summary: The Secretariat states that information regarding the total expenditure on Parliament's Winter Session, including costs due to non-functioning, is not maintained by them as it involves multiple agencies and there is no mechanism to calculate session-wise expenses. For MP attendance records, details are available on the Lok Sabha website, and providing certified copies would disproportionately divert resources, thus an exemption under Section 7(9) of the RTI Act, 2005, is invoked.

Reply
A representation dated 10 December, 2014 from
Shri B.V. Karkhanis, Executive President,
Mukundnagar Central govt. Quarters Occupants
Association, Pune inter alia regarding the sale of
quasi-permanent tenements at Mukundnagar
Colony, was received (copy enclosed). The
representation was examined in the Committee
Branch and on the merits of the representation, it
was decided to forward the representation to the
Ministry of Urban Development for such necessary
action as may deem fit. They were also requested
that the representationist may be informed of the
action taken in the matter. The relevant
representation was forwarded to the Ministry on 15
January, 2015 (copy enclosed). A copy of the said
communication was also forwarded to the
representationist (copy enclosed). As a matter of
fact, Shri Karkhanis had given similar
representations on 27 December, 2014, 26 may,
2015 and 31 August, 2015 (copy enclosed).
On 19 January, 2015, a similar representation was
received from Shri B.R. Patil, Chairman of the
Association of Flood Affected Central govt.
employees, Mukundnagar, Pune.
In his representation, Shri Patil inter alia raised the
same issues which was earlier raised by Shri B.V.
Karkhanis. Since the Committee Branch was
receiving frequent representations on the subject
matter, on 2 March, 2015 it was decided to seek the
comments of the Ministry of Urban Development.
Accordingly, OM to the Ministry was sent on 3
March, 2015 (copy enclosed).
The Ministry on Urban Development vide their OM
dated 19 March, 2015 had given their comments in the
matter.
Meanwhile, the Committee on Petitions directed that
a programme for undertaking study visit of the
Committee be formulated. Since the representation
given by Shri Patil was yet to reach its finality,
during the study visit to Mumbai, it was decided to
afford an opportunity to the representatives of the
Association of Flood Affected Central govt.
Employees to hear their views in the matter in the
presence of representatives of the Ministry of Urban
Development and other authorities concerned
therewith. Communication to this effect was sent to
Shri B.R. Patil on 5 may, 2015. Accordingly, on 20
May, 2015, Shri B.R. Patil represented the matter
relating to sale of quasi-permanent tenements at
Mukundnagr colony before the Committee - which
had also been raised by Shri B.V. Kharkhanis in his
representation dated 10 December, 2014.

Premature disclosure of such information is in violation of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of Lok Sabha and a breach of the privilege of the Committee.
Please see reply point No.1
The information regarding official address/flat allotted to every MP of 16th Lok Sabha is available on the website of Parliament of India i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the link Members and thereafter in Contact details, the applicant can access the details from the said website. The list of Members of the 16th Lok Sabha has been got printed (in English) and is available on sale and may be obtained from Lok Sabha Secretariat Sales Counter, Reception Office, Parliament House, New Delh-110001.

response_full_text: The expenditure on proceedings of Parliament Session is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments. There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Ministries/ Departments/ Rajya Sabha Secretariat etc. in connection with the conduct of Parliament. Session-wise expenditure incurred out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha is not available with IFU. Expenditure incurred (un-audited) for the month of November, 2016 compiled on the basis of expenditure figures furnished by P&AO, LS is enclosed (Annexure).

title: RTI response on criminal cases against Members of Parliament
subject: Supply of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
questions: Provide names of all sitting Members of Parliament against whom criminal cases are pending.
Provide information relating to number of criminal cases pending against sitting Members of Parliament.
Provide information relating to nature of criminal cases pending against sitting Members of Parliament.
Provide information relating to sections of IPC/CrPC under which charges filed against sitting Members of Parliament.
Whether charge sheet has been filed against such Members of Parliament.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat stated that it does not maintain information regarding criminal cases, their nature, or the sections under which charges are filed against sitting Members of Parliament, as there is no provision in its Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business for such record keeping. The Secretariat suggested that the query pertains to other public authorities like the Election Commission of India and the Ministry of Law & Justice, and indicated that the application may be forwarded to them under Section 6(3) of the RTI Act, 2005.

Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. title: RTI for information on Maharaja Manabendra Shah, Ex. MP
subject: Supply of information under RTI Act, 2005, relating to Maharaja Manabendra Shah, MP from Tehri Constituency.
questions: How Maharaja Manabendra Shah Sahib had usually signed his declarations/oath/nominations etc. and correspondences as M.P. as well as other official documents, etc. and during his entire stint as M.P. from 1952 to 2007. Kindly provide authenticated specimen signature specifically during 1956 onwards.

How many times since 1952 and upto demise in January 2007 Maharaja Manabendra Shah Sahib was elected Member of Parliament from Tehri Garhwal and in which years and what other posts did he held on behalf of Government of India viz-various governing bodies of Ministries or as ambassador to other nations, etc.
What did he submit in declarations with Govt. of India in Parliament and with regard to his properties and other holdings with his usual signatures. (Specimen).
What is the history of Tehri Garhwal State and what are the names of Maharaja Manabendra Shah Sahibs Parents, Grandparents and great grandparents.

What is the name of Maharaja Manabendra Shah's grandmother wife of his grandfather Maharaja Kirti Shah who had married to Nepal Royal family Princess (family of General Padam Jang Bahadur Rana, Prime Minister).
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat provided a copy of Maharaja Manabendra Shah's signature for the 14th Lok Sabha and details about his elections and positions via his bio-profile on the Lok Sabha website. His declarations of assets and liabilities for the 14th Lok Sabha were enclosed. Information regarding the history of Tehri Garhwal State, as well as the names of grandparents and great-grandparents, was stated as not maintained or not available with the Secretariat. Some information regarding signatures required a personal visit due to the volume of records, and parts of the application were transferred to the Cabinet Secretariat.

RTI is an overriding law and in compliance of the same, the Privileges & Ethics Branch is inter alia disclosing information about the Assets and Liabilities of the Members of Lok Sabha, which are otherwise confidential under the provisions of the Members of Lok Sabha (Declaration of Assets and Liabilities) Rules, 2004. Further, major portion of information in the custody of Secretary-General is disclosed under RTI by the various Branches. However, certain information cannot be disclosed to the House under RTI, in view of the provisions of Section 8(1)(c) of the RTI Act. To give an illustration, the proceedings of deliberations of a Parliamentary Committee and the documents/information available with a Committee are also not disclosed till the Report of the Parliamentary Committee on the given subject is laid on the Table of the House. Premature disclosure of such information is in violation of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business of Lok Sabha and a breach of the privilege of the Committee.

pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month with effect

Paediatrician, Physiotherapist are also available on given days
of the weeks. The Medical Centre maintains a record of Health
status of each Member of Parliament.
6. Other Facilities to Members
(a) Diplomatic Passport
A Member and his wifelhusband is eligible for the issue of
Diplomatic Passport for going abroad on study tour/conference/
private visit
(b) Income Tax Sub-Office
Under arrangements made with Ministry of Finance, an Income
Tax Sub-office function in Parliament House Annexe throughout
the year for rendering assistance to Members of Parliament in
completing their Income-tax retums and inresolving their queries
relating to the payment of income-tax
(c) State Bank of India Branches at Parliament House and Annexe
Branches of the State Bank of India function in Parliament House
and Annexe. Besides the normal banking facilities, they accept
payment in respect of income-tax and other direct taxes,
investment plans, etc. Safe deposit lockers have also been
provided at Parliament House Annexe Branch for the
convenience of Members. ATM facility is provided for the
convenience of Members in Parliament Housel Annexe and
Parliament Library Buliding.
(d) Rationing Sub-Office
With the introduction of statutory rationing in Delhi, a Rationing
Sub-Office opened by the Delhi Rationing Authority functions in
Parliament House during the Session period for the issue of
Ration Cards to Members and their families.
(e) Kendriya Bhander
A branch of the Kendriya Bhandar localed at 23, Mahadev
Road is open from 09.30 hrs. to 18.30 hrs. for the sale of
essential commodities (such as grocery, toilet and household
iterns, textiles, watches, etc.).
(1) NDMC Liaison Office
6
A full-fledged Liaison Office of the NDMC (New Delhi Municipal
Council) functions in Parliament House Annexe throughout the
year to look into the complaints of Members with regard to
meters installed at their residences and all other matters
connected with the NDMC, including electricity and water bills
of Members.
(g) LPG Service Counter of the Oil Industry
The Service Counter of the Oll Industry in regard to supply of
LPG and rendering timely service in respect of defective,
Installation, etc. functions during Session period in Parliament
House Annexe for the convenience of Members of Parliament.
(h) Security arrangements in Members' residential localties
A Special Cell has been set up by Delhi Police in the Office of the
Assistant Commissioner Police, Police Station, Parliament Street,
New Delhi, to assist the Members of Parliament to maintain the
security of their residences. The timing of the Cell is from 0900
hours to 1900 hours daily. Members are required to inform the
Cell as and when they happen to go outside Delhi to enable the
Police authorities to make necessary arrangements for the
security of their residences during their absence from Delhi.
The Members, for any other assistance they may require from
the local police, may also contact the Cell.
(i) Army Disposal Vehicles
Members may apply for Army Disposal Vehicles from the Ministry
of Defence. The requests received from the Members are
forwarded to Ministry of Delence for release of Army Disposal
Vehicles from the Army Disposal Stock
(1) Catering Service
Northern Railway is running MPs Canteen is North Avenue
for the convenience of Members and their guests. In South
Avenue, catering services is being run by a private caterer. in
Westem Court Hostel, the canteen is ran by the ITDC.

response_full_text:
Sir,
With reference to your letter dated 07.01.2016 (on transfer from Ministry of
Parliament Affairs), received on 07.01.2016, I am directed to forward the statement of
information to the extent pertaining and available in this Secretariat (Annexure) as approved
by CPIO).
Reply for the specific questions:
1. Ferry Services is provided to all the Members of Lok Sabha around Parliament House Complex, from their residence to Parliament House Complex on payment basis.
2. No food is served to MPs free of cost and no separate accounts on expenditure on food it maintained. Canteens are run by the Ministry of Railways in the Parliament House Complex on payment basis.
3. Cloths are purchased by Members by own payment from the market. No such information is available.
4. No security provided to the Members of Parliament in Parliament Complex by the Lok Sabha Secretariat.
Two annexure shows the other facilities and Salary, Allowances and Pension provided to the Members of Parliament (Lok Sabha) by the Lok Sabha Secretariat are enclosed.

Annexure-I: FACILITIES TO MEMBERS/EX-MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT [As per the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament (Amendment) Act, 2010)
1. Salary
Rs. 50,000/- per month.
2. Daily Allowance
Rs. 2,000/- per day for each day of residence on duty. Daily Allowance shall be paid only when the member signs the register maintained for the purpose
3. Constituency Allowance
Rs. 45,000/- per month.
4. Office Expense Allowance
Rs 45,000/- per month out of which Rs. 15.000/- is for meeting expenses of stationery items and postage, and upto Rs. 30,000/- is paid by the Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariats to the person(s) as may be engaged by a member for obtaining secretarial assistance, provided that one such person must be computer literate as certified by the Member herself/himself.
5. Travelling Allowance
(1) Forward Journey For attending a Parliament Session or meeting of a Parliamentary Committee or for the purpose of attending any other business connected with her/his duties as a member from her/his usual place of residence to the place of duty, a member is entitled to:
(a) By Rail-One free non-transferable First class AC or Executive class of any train pass and one First class and one Second class fare.
(b) By Air One and one-fourth air fare of the airlines in which the member travels.
(c) By Road-Rs. 16/- per km
The member whose usual place of residence is within the radius of 300 kms. from Delhi is entitled to receive road mileage even if the place is connected by superfast/express/mail Train.
The members representing the North-Eastern States are entitled to road mileage from their usual place of residence to the nearest airport even though the places are connected by superfast/express/mail train.
(ii) Return Journey After attending a Session, Committee meeting or any other business connected with her/his duties as such member from the place of duty to the usual place of residence same as 5(1) above.
6. Air Travel Facility
A Member is entitled to avail herself/himself of 34 single air journeys during a year with his/her spouse or any number of companions or relatives. The spouse/companion can travel alone eight times in a year to meet the member. Any journey performed by the spouse, companions or relatives shall be added in compuling the ceiling of 34 air journeys
The balance of unused air journeys for a year shall be carried over to the following year. In case a member performs more than 34 air journeys in a year, she/he is allowed to adjust not exceeding 8 air joumeys available for the next year.
7. Rail Travel Facility
(a) A member, on the strength of her/his Identity Card, is entitled to travel at any time by any railway in India in first class air-conditioned or executive class. The identity Card issued to the member is non-transferable.
(b) The Identity Card also entitles him/her to be accompanied by one person in air-conditioned two tier, when he travels by rail
8. Facilities for Spouse of a Member
(i) One free non-transferable railway pass to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in any train, and if travelled by air, an amount equal to the air fare, from the usual place of residence of a member to Delhi and back during Parliament session subject to 8 such journeys ina year.
(ii) The spouse is entitled to travel in first class air conditioned or executive class in all the trains with the member from any place in India to any other place in India. A member having no spouse is entitled to accompany with any other person in lieu of spouse in any train in first class air conditioned or executive class from any place in India to any other place in India in addition to the facility already available to her/him in respect of one companion in AC-II tier
9. Water and Electricity
4000 kl. of water and 50,000 units of electricity (25,000 units measured on light meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost at the residence allotted to a member in Delhi/New Delhi or to a member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
The unutilized units of electricity and water are carried over to the subsequent years and any excess consumption In a particular year is adjusted from the units available for the next year.
10. Telephone Facilities
A member is entitled to have three telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, out of which at least one telephone should be installed at her/his residence or office in Delhi and one at her/his usual place of residence or a place selected by the member in her/his constituency or the State in which she/he resides, the third telephone can be installed at either of the aforesaid place. 50,000 local calls during a year are free to herihim during a year on each of the three telephones. However, Chairman of a Parliamentary Committee is exempted from payment of any charges for local calls made from any one telephone installed at her/his residence in Delhi/New Delhi
These 50,000 free local calls can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year. A member may use any number of telephones for availing the aforesaid 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are bome by the member herself/himself.
Every member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/ BSNL services are not available, with national roaming facility for utilization in the constituency and the calls made from these mobile phones are adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls available to her/him on three tolephones. However, the registration and rental charges for private mobile connection are borne by the member herself/himself.
The excess calls made by a member are adjustable from the free local calls available to her/him on three telephones for the next year. Likewise, the unutilized calls of a year are carried over to the subsequent years till the seat of a member becomes vacant.
A member is also entitled to avail broadband facility from MTNL/BSNL on any one of the above-cited three telephones subject to the condition that only upto Rs. 1,500/- per month are paid by the Government towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL
The 3G facility as offered by MTNL/BSNL is optional for members. The charges towards the 3G package as well as additional usage of facility will be adjustable within the aforesaid 1,50,000 free calls available to the Member. However, the 3G compatible handset is to be purchased by the member herself/himself.
11. Conveyance Advance
Upto Rs. 4,00,000/- are advanced to a member for the purchase of conveyance. Recovery of the said advance together with interest thereon, as applicable on loan to Government servants, shall be made from the salary bill of the member in not more than 50 equal monthly installments which shall not extend beyond the tenure of her/his membership.
12. Medical Facility
Members are entitled to same medical facilities as are available to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class-1 under the Central Government Health Scheme
13. Facilities to Physically Incapacitated Members
A member who is physically incapacitated shall be entitled to
(a) By Air: One additional air fare for the accompanied person.
(b) By Rail: A companion in the same class in which she/he travels in lieu of the air-conditioned two tier class railway pass
(c) By Road: One road mileage.
In case a physically incapacitated member who cannot perform journey by rail or air, she/he is entitled to road mileage for the entire journey performed by her/him by read
14. Facilities to Ex-Members of Parliament
(1) Pension Every person who has served as a member of the Provisional Parliament or either House of Parliament for any period is entitled to pension @ Rs. 20,000/- per month with effect from 18.05.2009. Where any person has served the Parliament for a period exceeding five years, she/he shall be entitled for an additional pension @Rs. 1,500/- per month for every year in excess of five years. For the purpose of calculation of years for determination of additional pension, the period of nine months or more is rounded off to one complete year.
Where an Ex-Member is also entitled to any other pension which is outside the purview of Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954 (MSA Act), she/he shall be entitled to receive the pension as Ex-Member in addition to such other pension.
Where any person entitled to pension as Ex-Member of Parliament is elected to the office of the President or Vice-President or is appointed as Governor or Administrator or becomes a member of Council of States or House of the People or any State Legislature or metropolitan council or is employed on a salary under the Central or any State Government or any corporation owned or controlled by Central/State Government or any local authority or becomes otherwise entitled to any remuneration from such Government, corporation or local authority, such person shail not be entitled to any pension as Ex-Member of Parliament. However, if the salary/remuneration so payable to such person is less than the pension payable to her/him as Ex-Member of Parliament, such person shall be entitled only to receive the balance as pension.
(ii) Family pension to spouse/dependent of deceased Member/Ex-Member The spouse or dependent of a deceased Member/Ex-Member is entitled for the remaining period of her/his life to receive family pension equal to one-half of the pension atherwise admissible to the deceased Member/Ex-Member at the time of her/his death. The dependent shall get family pension subject to fulfillment of conditions as stipulated in section 2(aa) of the MSA Act
If the spouse/dependent is entitled to any other pension under MSA Act, she/he will not be entitled to receive family pension.
No person shall be entitled to claim arrears of family pension for the period prior to 15th September, 2006,
(iii) Rail Travel Facility Under Section 8AA of the MSA Act, an Ex-Member is entitled to travel in any train in air-conditioned two tier class along with a companion or in air-conditioned first class if she/he travels alone, on the strength of Ex-MP identity card issued to her/him by Lok Sabha/ Rajya Sabha Secretariat.
(iv) Steamer Facility - An Ex-Member of Parliament who had represented Andaman & Nicobar Islands or Lakshadweep is entitled to travel by the highest class of accommodation in any steamer salling between the ASN Islands or Lakshadweep, as the case may be, and from Islands to Mainland in India on the strength of authorization issued to this effect by Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha Secretariat
(v) Medical Facility Central Government Health Scheme is applicable to Ex-Members residing in cities covered by CGHS on payment of contribution at the same rate as they were paying as Member of Parliament. This facility is obtained by Ex-Member direct from Director-General (CGHS), Ministry of Health & Family Welfare, Government of India, New Delhi.

FACILITIES PROVIDED TO MEMBERS OF PARLIAMENT BY M.S. BRANCH
1. Accommodation
(i) Members who come to Delhi prior to publication of Notification by the Election Commission for constituting new Lok Sabha are entitled to transit accommodation.
(i) Accommodation in the form of a flat is free throughout the term of office to a Member. However, normal licence fee @ Rs. 105 is charged on bungalow.
(i) Sofa covers and curtains are get washed by the CPWD after every 3 months which are provided free of cost to Members.
(iv) Furniture to be made free of charge to the Members within the revised monetary ceiling of Rs. 60,000 in respect of durable furniture and Rs. 15,000/-for non-durable furniture. The rental for additional items of furniture shall be charged on the depreciated value of fumiture,
(v) Members of Lok Sabha or their families can retain Govemment Accommodation for a maximum period of one month after their retirement, resignation/removal or ceasing to be a Member of Lok Sabha on payment of the same rent, if any, which they were paying immediately before the occurrence of any of the events mentioned above.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament may retain Govemment accommodation for a maximum period of six months from the date of death of such a Member.
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rule, 1956 (as amended)
*2. Water and Electricity
(1) 4000 Kilolitre of water and 50,000 units of Electricity (25,000 units measured on lights meter and 25,000 units measured on power meter or pooled together) per annum beginning from 1st January of every year is supplied free of cost in the residence allotted to a Member in Delhi/New Delhi and to a Member who is residing in private accommodation in Delhi.
(ii) Where both husband and wife are Members of Parliament and are residing in the same accommodation, their admissibility for supply of free electricity and water at the residence allotted to them shall be calculated separately.
(iii) The unconsumed units of electricity and water out of those otherwise admissible to a Member in any year shall be carried over to the subsequent years till his seat becomes vacant
(iv) In case of consumption of electricity and water by a Member in excess of his entitlement for a particular year, such excess consumption of electricity and water shall be adjusted from the units of electricity and water in kilolitre available for the next year.
(v) in case the seat of a Member becomes vacant due to his resignation or completion of term, he will be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water as available for that year within a maximum period of one month from the date on which his seat becomes vacant.
(vi) The family of a deceased Member of Parliament shall be entitled to consume the balance units of electricity and water in kilolitre available to such Member for that particular year within a period of one month from the date of death of that Member.
*3. Telephone Facilities
(i) A member is entitled to have two telephones without payment of installation and rental charges, one at his residence or office in Delhi and the other at his usual place of residence or a place selected by him in his constituency or the State in which he resides. 50,000 local calls during a year are free to a Member on each of the two telephones.
"Under the Housing and Telephone Facilities (Members of Parliament) Rule, 1956 (as amended).
(ii) A Member is also entitled to have one additional telephone without payment of installation and rental charges either at his residence in Delhi/New Delhi or at his usual place of residence or at the place selected by him within the State in which his constituency is or in the State in which he resides and 50,000 free local calls during a year are allowed on that telephone for internet connectivity purposes.
(ii) The above mentioned 50,000 free local calls admissible on each telephone can be clubbed together which comes to 1,50,000 local calls in a year.
(iv) A Member may use any number of telephones for availing the above-mentioned 1,50,000 free local calls subject to the condition that the telephones are in the name of Member and the installation and rental charges of additional telephones are borne by the Member himself
(v) A Member is also entitled to one mobile phone connection of MTNL and another mobile phone connection of MTNL/BSNL or any private mobile operator, in case MTNL/BSNL, services are not available, with national roaming facility for utilisation in the constituency and the calls made from these telephones may be adjusted from the above-mentioned 1,50,000 calls available to them on 3 telephones. However, the registration and rental charges for private mobile phone connection are bome by the Member himself.
(vi) In case a Member makes calls in excess of admissible free local calls in a year, the excess calls can be adjusted from the calls available to him on three telephones for the next year. Further, the unutilised telephone calls of a year are carried over to the subsequent years till the seat of a Member becomes vacant
(vii) A Member is also entitled to avail broadband facility fron MTNL/ BSNL on any one of the above-mentioned three telephones subject to the condition that the Government may pay uplo Rs. 1,500 per month towards the charges of this facility directly to MTNL/BSNL
4. Transport Facilities
The Members are also being provided the following facilities:-
(i) Ferry Vehicles through Transport Desk
There is a Transport Desk from where vehicles are provided to facilitate the Members to go from Parliament complex to their residences and vice-versa in New Delhi. The transport facility is provided to all Members of Parliament between their residences and Parliament House Complex on a payment of a token amount of Rs. 5/- for each trip,
(i) Rail Transport
Railway Booking and Reservation Offices function in Parliament House and near Outer Reception Office, Parliament House throughout the year for the convenience of Members of Parliament. The reservation of accommodation in trains for Members and their spouses is made from the Reservation Office, Parliament House and reservation of accommodation for Members' guests/attendants/friends etc. is made from the Reservation Office, near outer Reception Office, Parliament House.
(Air Transport
An Air Booking Office of Air India functions in Parliament House throughout the year. Arrangements also exist for Members of Parliament to book air passages with the Air India Booking Office in Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi. The booking can also be done by Members over the telephone in certain circumstances.
(iv) Taxis and Scooters Outside Partiament House Annexe
During Session Period, arrangements are made for availability of taxis and scooters at taxi Stands outside Parliament House Complex with the assistance of Delhi Police, Taxi Stands around Parliament House Complex and Watch and Ward Office Lok Sabha Secretarial
5. Medical Facilities
(i) Members of Parliament are entitled to same medical facilities as are avaliable to the officers of Central Civil Services, Class- under Central Government Health Scheme.
(ii) Under the Central Government Health Scheme, as extended to Members of Parliament, a First Aid Post in the Lobby of the Central Hall of Parliament House and a Medical Centre in the basement of Parliament House Annexe function throughout the year to render First Aid to Members of Parliament and to meet the first aid requirement arising in the precincts of the Parliament House Complex.
(ii) The Medical Centre has X-Ray, Ultra Sound, ECG, Pathological Laboratory facilities and consultation in Cardiac, Dental, Ophthalmic, ENT, Gynae, Skin, Orthopaedic, Psychiatric and Surgical Specialties. Apart from this, the services of Dietician, Paediatrician, Physiotherapist are also available on given days of the weeks. The Medical Centre maintains a record of Health status of each Member of Parliament.
6. Other Facilities to Members
(a) Diplomatic Passport
A Member and his wifelhusband is eligible for the issue of Diplomatic Passport for going abroad on study tour/conference/ private visit
(b) Income Tax Sub-Office
Under arrangements made with Ministry of Finance, an Income Tax Sub-office function in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year for rendering assistance to Members of Parliament in completing their Income-tax retums and inresolving their queries relating to the payment of income-tax
(c) State Bank of India Branches at Parliament House and Annexe
Branches of the State Bank of India function in Parliament House and Annexe. Besides the normal banking facilities, they accept payment in respect of income-tax and other direct taxes, investment plans, etc. Safe deposit lockers have also been provided at Parliament House Annexe Branch for the convenience of Members. ATM facility is provided for the convenience of Members in Parliament Housel Annexe and Parliament Library Buliding.
(d) Rationing Sub-Office
With the introduction of statutory rationing in Delhi, a Rationing Sub-Office opened by the Delhi Rationing Authority functions in Parliament House during the Session period for the issue of Ration Cards to Members and their families.
(e) Kendriya Bhander
A branch of the Kendriya Bhandar localed at 23, Mahadev Road is open from 09.30 hrs. to 18.30 hrs. for the sale of essential commodities (such as grocery, toilet and household iterns, textiles, watches, etc.).
(1) NDMC Liaison Office
A full-fledged Liaison Office of the NDMC (New Delhi Municipal Council) functions in Parliament House Annexe throughout the year to look into the complaints of Members with regard to meters installed at their residences and all other matters connected with the NDMC, including electricity and water bills of Members.
(g) LPG Service Counter of the Oil Industry
The Service Counter of the Oll Industry in regard to supply of LPG and rendering timely service in respect of defective, Installation, etc. functions during Session period in Parliament House Annexe for the convenience of Members of Parliament.
(h) Security arrangements in Members' residential localties
A Special Cell has been set up by Delhi Police in the Office of the Assistant Commissioner Police, Police Station, Parliament Street, New Delhi, to assist the Members of Parliament to maintain the security of their residences. The timing of the Cell is from 0900 hours to 1900 hours daily. Members are required to inform the Cell as and when they happen to go outside Delhi to enable the Police authorities to make necessary arrangements for the security of their residences during their absence from Delhi.
The Members, for any other assistance they may require from the local police, may also contact the Cell.
(i) Army Disposal Vehicles
Members may apply for Army Disposal Vehicles from the Ministry of Defence. The requests received from the Members are forwarded to Ministry of Delence for release of Army Disposal Vehicles from the Army Disposal Stock
(1) Catering Service
Northern Railway is running MPs Canteen is North Avenue for the convenience of Members and their guests. In South Avenue, catering services is being run by a private caterer. in Westem Court Hostel, the canteen is ran by the ITDC.

response_full_text: The expenditure on proceedings of Parliament Session is incurred by multiple agencies viz. Lok Sabha Secretariat, Rajya Sabha Secretariat, Ministry of Urban Development (CPWD) and other Ministries/departments. There is no specific and exclusive Head of Account for booking the expenditure incurred by various Ministries/ Departments/ Rajya Sabha Secretariat etc. in connection with the conduct of Parliament. Session-wise expenditure incurred out of Budget Grant of Lok Sabha is not available with IFU. Head of account-wise expenditure incurred (un-audited) including Salary, TA and DA of MPs of Lok Sabha during the month of November & December, 2016 compiled on the basis of expenditure figures furnished by P&AO, LS is enclosed (Annexure). The Branch concerned i.e. Members Salaries & Allowances of sitting MPs. The consolidated amount incurred on the Salary and other allowances of Members of Parliament from 16.11.2016 to 16.12.2016 is approximately Rs. 210085018/-. During the winter session, 2016 (10th Session of 16th Lok Sabha), the House sat for 19 hours 26 minutes for transaction of Government and other business. Four Government Bills were discussed/passed by Lok Sabha during the Winter Session, 2016 No Private Member Bill was passed/dicussed by Lok Sabha during winter session (Tenth session) of 16th Lok Sabha. Please see reply at Point No. 2 & 6. An attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Prime Minister and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. The details of replies to Questions listed in the name of Prime Minister in Lok Sabha during the Winter Session of 2016 are available on the Lok Sabha website i.e.loksabha.nic.in under the heading “Questions' or directly through the following link :- http://164.100.47.194/Loksabha/Questions/qsearch15.aspx The applicant is requested to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information.

Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members -> Sitting Members -> Attendance of Members->Member-wise Attendance -> All Members respectively.
Please provide me the percentage of attendance of each members present and absent in Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha from 2014-2016. Please also mention the name of political party to which they belong.

The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but did not sign the Attendance Register for that day.
For party affiliation of the members, the applicant may be advised to access the relevant information from the Lok Sabha website www.loksabha.nic.in under the link Members -> Sitting Members -> Party wise list respectively.
The applicant visit the website and access the desired information.
Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage.
The information on party affiliation of members is also available in the said website.
Provide the list of MP's gone to the foreign trip on the payment of government in the year 2014-2016

The desired information is available on the website of Lok Sabha i.e. www.loksabha.nic.in under the link 'Conference'.
The applicant may visit the website and access the desired information.

The query regarding interim provisions for women to avail benefits before the bill's passing has been transferred to the Ministry of Labour and Employment.

title: RTI on Lok Sabha Secretariat Vacant Posts and Promotions
subject: The RTI concerns vacant posts and promotion processes for various grades in the Lok Sabha Secretariat, along with queries on eligibility, delays, and punitive actions.

When was the last departmental promotion committee meeting held to consider promotion for the posts of Directors, Additional Directors, Deputy Secretaries, Under Secretaries.

Whether any administrative delay due in signing the proposal by competent authority will be compensated by giving the officers promotion from the date of their eligibility or when the vacancy to the post accrued?

Whether there is provision to take punitive action against the official(s) who delay in initiating promotion proposals and those who have responsibility to clear / get clear such files well before the vacancies occurred so as not to dampen the spirit and morale of officers in the chain of promotions which otherwise adversely affect their career progression as well as efficiency.

Queries regarding administrative delays and punitive actions for delays were deemed hypothetical or without specific provisions.

response_summary: The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014, was classified as a Financial Bill under Articles 117(1) and 117(3) of the Constitution. Motions for such Bills are typically passed by voice vote, with a division only if a Member insists and the Speaker approves.

The Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was classified as Financial Bill under article 117(1) and 117(3). The applicant may further be informed that as per article 4(2) of the Constitution, a Bill relating to admission or establishment of new States, formation of new States and alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing States and providing for amendment of the First and the Fourth Schedule to the Constitution is not deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of article 368. The applicant is requested to go through the provisions of articles 2, 3 and 4 of the Constitution for further clarification.
Under which provisional ground the original Characteristics of the said Bill prepared as Constitution Amendment Bill will be changed/converted to a Financial Bill.

The motion that a Bill be taken into consideration or that the Bill be passed, in respect of a Bill other than a Constitution Amendment Bill, is normally passed by voice vote. संसद सदस्यों को प्रदान किए जाने वाले वेतन, भत्ते और अन्य सुविधाएं समय-समय पर यथा संशोधित निम्नलिखित अधिनियम/नियमों द्वारा विनियमित किए जाते हैं :-1. संसद सदस्य वेतन, भत्ता और पेंशन अधिनियम, 1954 (यथा संशोधित) 2. संसद सदस्य (यात्रा और दैनिक भत्ते) नियम, 1957 3. आवास और टेलीफोन सुविधाएं (संसद सदस्य) नियम, 1956 4. चिकित्सा सुविधाएं (संसद सदस्य) नियम, 1959 5. संसद सदस्य (विदेश यात्रा के लिए भत्ते) नियम, 1960 6. संसद सदस्य (निर्वाचन क्षेत्र संबंधी भत्ता) नियम, 1986 7. संसद सदस्य (वाहन क्रय अग्रिम) नियम, 1986 तथा 8. संसद सदस्य (कार्यालय व्यय भत्ता) नियम, 1988 । उपर्युक्त अधिनियम/नियम लोक सभा की वेबसाइट www.loksabha.nic.in पर भी उपलब्ध हैं ।
इस सचिवालय की संबंधित शाखा अर्थात् वेतन एवं लेखा कार्यालय द्वारा रखे जा रहे सदस्यों पर किए गए व्यय संबंधी आंकड़ों से संबंधित वित्तीय शीर्ष-वार विवरण संलग्न है ।

title: Status position in regard to the movement of the RTI Application
subject: Supply of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
questions: Seeking various information relating to Sh. Rakesh Sethi, commandant/DIG CRPF
response_summary: The Secretariat replied to all 8 points of the application. For point 1, it clarified that the matter was a query regarding duties of security personnel, considered as VIP Security duties. For points 2-4, no such information was available with the Secretariat. For points 5-6, the information was forwarded to the Ministry of Home Affairs. For point 7, it was stated that no posts like JDA, PHA exist, and the post of Additional Director (Technical) is being filled following Shri Rakesh Sethi's repatriation. Point 8 was deemed vague.

title: RTI Application Status, Response, and Appeal Decision
subject: Supply of information under RTI Act, 2005
questions: Hindi copy of the Lok Pal Bill as passed by Lok Sabha on 18.12.2013
Copy of the debates /discussions/speeches delivered by MPs, Lok Sabha on Lok Pal Bill as passed by Lok Sabha on 18.12.2013
If the above-mentioned information is available on the website please provide the printout of the same
response_summary: For point 1, the Hindi version of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Bill, 2013, as passed by Parliament, is not printed by Lok Sabha or available in the Parliament Library; however, a Hindi version of the Lok Pal Bill 2011 (47 pages) is available and sent. For point 2, cyclostyled Hindi and English debates are enclosed. For point 3, only English versions of Government Bills are uploaded to the Lok Sabha website, and Hindi versions are not printed or available online. An appeal filed by the applicant, contending non-receipt of information, was disposed of after the Appellate Authority confirmed that the requested information was dispatched on 30.01.2014 by ordinary post (due to the absence of a pincode), suggesting the appeal was filed prematurely.

2. Rajya Sabha Secretariat also transferred identical application dated

3. The applicant was replied to (in Hindi) by this Secretariat on 30.01.2014.
4. Shri Biharilal Thawait filed first appeal on 03.02.2014 received on
10.02.2014. The appellant contends that till date he has not received the
information.
Decision and Reasons
1. I have carefully gone through the RTI Application followed by First Appeal
and the comments of the division concerned of this public authority.

authority.

extent pertaining and available with the concerned division of this public
authority has already been supplied to the appellant vide letter no.1
(20)/IC/14 dated 30.01.2014 along with 47 pages of information (copy of
the Lok Pal Bill as passed by Lok Sabha on 27.12.2011). However, it
appears from the appeal that the appellant sent his appeal dated
03.02.2014 before receiving reply. Further, since the appellant has not
mentioned the pincode, reply might have reached him later than
03.02.2014.
4. The CPIO has also informed that as per practice adopted/followed by the
'Distribution' Branch of this pubic authority any letter which doesn't have
pin code is sent by ordinary post only and in the instant case as well the
division concerned has followed the same practice.

already been sent. The said copy is the same as intimated by the Rajya
Sabha Secretariat for which the application was transferred to this
Secretariat. That clarifies the position related to point no.1 of the
application and again raised in the appeal.

Facilities, salary, allowances etc. provided to MP, Monthly Allowances and copy of Bills etc, Secretarial staff of MP, copy of appointment letter, salary etc.

As per the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954, monthly salary provided to a Member is Rs.50,000 p.m. For other details a pamplet containing the requisite information is enclosed.
The details of Secretarial Staff appointed by the Member are as follows :- One PA has been appointed by the Member Shri Raju Krishnaswamy w.e.f. 01.08.2013 till date salary @ Rs. 30,000 p.m. i.e. Rs. 3,60,000 per annum.
Vehicles etc provided to MP

Vehicles are not provided to MPs for their personal use. However, they are provided ferry services from MPs residential areas to Parliament House/ Parliament House Annexe.

response_full_text:
As per the Salary, Allowances and Pension of Members of Parliament Act, 1954, monthly salary provided to a Member is Rs.50,000 p.m. For other details a pamplet containing the requisite information is enclosed.
The details of Secretarial Staff appointed by the Member are as follows :- One PA has been appointed by the Member Shri Raju Krishnaswamy w.e.f. 01.08.2013 till date salary @ Rs. 30,000 p.m. i.e. Rs. 3,60,000 per annum.
Vehicles are not provided to MPs for their personal use. However, they are provided ferry services from MPs residential areas to Parliament House/ Parliament House Annexe.
However, a copy of the pamphlet showing the details of facilities provided to MPs including the MP of Dadra and Nagar Haveli, is enclosed. The information is also available in bilingual on the website www.parliamentofindia.nic.in

Out of these, 04 persons were appointed/promoted, in the following order, to the post of Security Assistant Grade-I w.e.f. 27.05.2004 (c/288-A), although their seniority - had not been fixed in the grade of Security Assistant Gr-II: 1. Shri Mahipal Yadav 2. Shri Ravinder Kumar 3. Shri Ram Singh 4. Shri Rajesh Kumar Poria
3. The seniority of the remaining two persons namely S/Shri Shivraj Singh Meena and Jay Prakash was fixed on the basis of their date of appointment in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-ll vide Office Order Part-Il No.19887 dated 08.10.2004 (c/287) which was at variance with the relevant provisions of the then R&CS Order No.44 dated 09.03.1956 (c/286), as amended. Shri Jay Prakash was promoted to the grade of Security Assistant Grade-l w.e.f. 27.05.2004 on ad-hoc basis (c/283) and on regular basis w.e.f. 23.02.2005 (c/282). Shri Shivraj Singh Meena has been promoted to the grade of Security Assistant Grade-I w.e.f. 27.05.2004(c/356).
4. The post of Security Assistant Gr-l is filled up 100% by promotion from the feeder grade of Security Assistant Gr-Il. Accordingly, inter-se seniority of 36 persons, which include the following 05 persons, was fixed in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-l vide Office Order Part-ll No.20494 dated 23.03.2006 (c/281) as per their order of selection by DPC, in terms of the new R&CS Order No.PDA-1076/2003 dated 20.12.2003 (c/279) which regulates seniority of officials of the Secretariat, in the order shown below; 1. Shri Mahipal Yadav 2. Shri Ravinder Kumar 3. Shri Ram Singh 4. Shri Rajesh Kumar Poria 5. Shri Jay Prakash
5. However, Shri Jay Prakash submitted a representation indicating the anomalies in fixation of inter-se seniority in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-Il. In his representation, he stated that he had secured second place in the merit order in the panel (dated 14.05.1998) (c/44) for Security Assistant Grade-ll. However, since he was the last person to join the post from that panel, he has been placed at the last position at the time of fixation of inter-se seniority in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-ll. Hence, he had requested for restoration of his seniority as per merit order/his placement in the panel (dated 14.05.1998) (c/44). The representation of Shri Jay Prakash was examined and it was noticed that there was an inadvertent error in fixation of the inter-se seniority of the 06 persons in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-ll appointed on the basis of panel dated 14.05.1998 as indicated at para 1, above. The seniority was not fixed as per the order of merit in the panel.
6. Since the R&CS Order No.44 dated 09.03.1956 (c/52) and also the extant R&CS Order No.PDA-1076/2003 dated 20.12.2003 (c/279) provides for fixation of seniority as per order of merit in the DR panel if the person joined duties within one month from the date of offer of appointment, it was proposed to re-fix the inter-se seniority in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-ll by rectifying the discrepancies occurred and accordingly the proposed inter-se seniority order was circulated vide Memorandum dated 23.05.2011 (c/259) amongst the persons concerned inviting their comments, if any, before issuing the revised seniority list.
7. In response to the above-said Memorandum, comments from one person namely Shri Mahipal Yadav were received. The comments were analyzed point-wise (c/256-259) but no merit was found therein.
8. In view of the position explained above, the DoP&T are requested to offer their considered opinion on the case especially on the point as to whether the inter-se seniority in the grade of Security Assistant Grade-ll in respect of persons appointed from the panel dated 14.05.1998 may be re-fixed as proposed in the Memorandum dated 23.05.2011(c/259). The case was also referred to the Department of Legal Affairs, Ministry of Law and Justice for their considered opinion. However, they advised (c/251) this Secretariat to obtain the comments of DoP&T in the first instance.

2. Instructions/guidelines issued by this Department on the subject of seniority are available on the website of this Department. These instructions/guidelines inter-alia stipulate that the relative seniority, ofcalls direct recruits is determined by the order of merit in which they are selected for appointment on the recommendations of the UPSC or other selecting authority, persons appointed as a result of an earlier selection being ischion to thoses appointed as a result of a subsequent selection. Where promotions are made on the basis of selection by a DPC, the seniority of such promotees shall be in the order, in whichath are recommended for such promotion by the DPC, persons promoted as a result of an earlier DPC being senior to those appointed as a result of a subsequent DPC. The relative seniority of direct recruits and promotees is determined according to the rotation of vacancies between direct recruits and promotees, based on the quota of vacancies reserved for direct recruitment and promotion, respectively, in the Recruitment Rules.
3. The Lok Sabha Secretariat may examine the matter in terms of the aforesaid instructions/guidelines and take further necessary action accordingly. response_summary: Parliament can amend or annul regulations laid on the Table of the House, but is not required to expressly pass them. No motion for modification or annulment of any of the mentioned UGC Regulations was passed by Lok Sabha.

title: RTI Application Status and Response from Lok Sabha Secretariat
subject: Supply of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005
questions: How much amount/money spend for a single Lok Sabha meeting per hour
How many session conducted in the last Lok Sabha
What was the budget amount that government spending in the name of Parliament session
How many Bills get passed in the last Parliament Sessions and what is the performance when compare to remaining tenure Sessions;
Was there any actions taken against those bureaucrats who were absent from Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha discussion
How far safe our Parliament when compare to foreign
Who is responsible if a single session get waste etc.
Why people who accused of criminal cases coming to Parliament.
Please provide the name and number of Bills get passed in last Lok Sabha Sessions and its importance to people of country;
How much amount of time and public money that last government used perfectly to pass a bill
Why there were some number of Bills still in pending like Women Reservations Bill and etc.
How many staff members working to run session successfully etc.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat provided replies to all 12 points of the RTI application. Many requests regarding financial expenditure per hour or per session were denied, stating that such information is not maintained due to multiple agencies being involved and no mechanism for session-wise calculation. Information on bills passed (13 Government Bills in 15th Lok Sabha) and pending (302 Private Members' Bills) was provided, with guidance to external websites for details. Questions regarding Parliament's safety, responsibility for wasted sessions, and criminal cases of MPs were deemed either vague or not covered under Section 2(f) of the RTI Act, 2005. The applicant was directed to the Lok Sabha website for details on legislation importance and advised on the fee for additional information.

In this regard the applicant may be informed that the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Bill, 2014 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 13.2.2014. The Bill was passed by Lok Sabha on 18.2.2014. The Bill, as passed by Lok Sabha, was passed by Rajya Sabha on 20.2.2014. The Bill, as passed by the Houses of Parliament, was assented to by the President on 1.3.2014.
As regards the information of votes in favour and against the Bill, it is informed that most of the Bills are passed by voice vote and number of votes in favour and against is not recorded. In some cases where division is demanded and in cases of Constitution Amendment Bills, the votes are recorded.
In the instant case it appears that the applicant desires to have information regarding the votes caste for and against the Bill and also the relevant Parliamentary Proceedings of the discussion. As regards the votes caste for and against at various stages of the Bill, the applicant may be informed that various motions in respect of the Bill were adopted by voice vote and hence no such record is available.
As regards details on separate State of Telengana it is informed that the same is available on the website of Lok Sabha and can be accessed from the link:-
http://164.100.47.132/LssNew/psearch/Result15.aspx?dbsl=11160

questions: लोक सभा सचिवालय के कें.ज.सू.अधि. और अपीलीय प्राधिकारी का नाम व पता बताएं ।
हिन्दी भाषा के प्रयोग के बारे में जानकारी तथा अन्य संबंधित ब्यौरा

questions: Information relating to criminal cases pending against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha.
Details of expenditure on the working of Parliament, including specific Heads of Account and budget provisions for parliamentary proceedings.
response_summary: The Secretariat does not maintain information on criminal cases against former or sitting Lok Sabha members and suggests forwarding the query to the Election Commission or Ministry of Law and Justice. Regarding parliamentary expenditure, it's incurred by multiple agencies with no specific head of account for proceedings; however, expenditure details from FY 2009-10 onwards are available on the Lok Sabha website.

questions: Can you able to produce me the property asset values of the present cabinet ministers, vice ministers and all the members of Parliament including the prime minister of India and the Rajya Sabha MP. And the expenditure costs did to them for the present members by the government like travel car, medical, hospitality, etc. Then what is the expenditure done during the parliament sessions periodically.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain property asset values of MPs but can provide declarations of Assets & Liabilities for Lok Sabha members (4500 pages for Rs. 9000/-). Information for Rajya Sabha members and Union Ministers has been transferred to the respective secretariats. The Secretariat provides data on common ferry services (Rs. 38,47,947/-) and medical expenditure (Rs. 1,50,11,703/-) for MPs, but details on hospitality or specific parliament-related expenditure are not maintained by the Lok Sabha Secretariat itself, as it involves multiple agencies. Expenditure details from 2009-10 onwards are available on the Lok Sabha homepage.

title: RTI Response: Lok Sabha Secretariat Branches, Typists, and Translation Services
subject: Supply of information under RTI Act, 2005
questions: How many committee Branches are there in Lok Sabha Secretariat including Parliamentary Committees?
How many typists (English/Hindi) are working in these committee branches?
How many branches of Editorial and Translation Service are doing translation of the work of said committees and how many typists (Hindi/English) are working in these branches of Translation Service?

Why there is a huge difference in the number of typists working in Committee Branches and Translation Branches when the work typed by English typist in Committee Branches is translated and typed in Hindi cent percent?

How many times shortage of typists in translation committee branches was assessed during the last 15 years and the efforts made to meet this shortage? What are the measures proposed to be taken to fill up the vacancies of these employees expeditiously?
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat provided information for some queries, referring the applicant to their intranet for general administrative reports. They stated that no typist posts exist in the Secretariat and identified nine Hindi Typists in Translation (Committee) Branches. Certain questions were not answered, as the Public Authority deemed them as 'queries' not covered under the Right to Information Act, 2005.

response_full_text:

title: RTI Response: Information on Lok Sabha Procedures, Data & Telecast
subject: Supply of information under the Right to Information Act, 2005.
questions: The procedure to let citizens suggest important topics to be discussed in the House. If such procedures does not exist, what are the alternatives.

What are the names of the staff who have been allotted quarter above their entitlement at the time of allotment in last seven years.

Whether Joint Secretary, LSS is entitled for Type VII accommodation
Whether Additional Secretary, LSS is entitled for Type VII accommodation.
How many officials of Lok Sabha Sectt have been given type VII accommodations? List of official's along with designation, address to be provided.

If yes, the details & category of houses/ bungalows transferred/ exchanged.
If yes, whether approval of concerned authorities were taken. Details of the same to be provided.
Whether any allotment has been made out of turn by exchanging the pool house of LSS & MPs/General Pool.
List of applicants/members awaiting allotment of type-VII Bungalow.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat responded to an RTI application regarding staff quarter allotments. They specified quarter categories, confirmed seniority maintenance, and provided a list of 10 officers allotted quarters above their entitlement based on Rule 4 of the 1974 Allotment of Residences Rules. The Secretariat also stated that providing copies of old official orders would cause dislocation, offering an on-site visit instead, and clarified that no officer is awaiting a Type VII Bungalow allotment as per the 2016 Priority List.
