An Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 16th Lok Sabha are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance Total respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information.
The requisite information is available in the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in ->'Business' -> 'Resume of Work' -> 'Archive'. As regards the 3rd session of the 16th Lok Sabha, the information can be accessed from the Lok Sabha website, viz. loksabha.nic.in ->‘Business' -> ‘Bulletin-I' date wise.

title: लोक सभा सचिवालय द्वारा दिव्यांगजन और किराएदारों के अधिकार संबंधी आरटीआई जवाब
subject: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना।
questions: हाल ही में शीतकालीन सत्र में संसद द्वारा पारित विधेयक में उल्लिखित निःशक्त व्यक्तियों की 21 श्रेणियां कौन सी हैं ।
इसके अलावा निःशक्त व्यक्तियों के कल्याण हेतु बनाए गए किन्हीं तीन नियमों की भी जानकारी दें ।
निःशक्त व्यक्तियों को संसदीय चुनावों में कोई आरक्षण क्यों नहीं दिया जाता ?
निःशक्त व्यक्तियों का प्रतिनिधित्व करने हेतु राट्रपति द्वारा संसद में एक भी निःशक्त व्यक्ति को नामनिर्देशित क्यों नहीं किया जाता ?
क्या संसद द्वारा किराएदारों के अधिकारों हेतु कोई विधेयक पारित किया गया है ?
कानून के अनुसार किराएदारों के मुख्य अधिकार क्या हैं ?
कानून के अनुसार किराया निर्धारित करने हेतु क्या मानदंड हैं ?
यदि किसी किराएदार का कोई स्थायी पता नहीं है तो उसे राशन कार्ड, पहचान पत्र और आधार कार्ड कैसे मिलेगा ?
कोई शिकायत होने पर किराएदार को किस अधिकारी, संस्था अथवा कार्यालय से संपर्क करना चाहिए ।
response_summary: दिव्यांग व्यक्तियों से संबंधित बिल का हिंदी संस्करण संलग्न किया गया है, जिसका अध्ययन कर आवेदक वांछित जानकारी प्राप्त कर सकता है। विकलांगों को आरक्षण और प्रतिनिधित्व से जुड़े प्रश्न सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय को भेज दिए गए हैं। किराएदारों के अधिकारों से संबंधित प्रश्नों के लिए आवेदक से विशिष्ट विधेयक का शीर्षक और वर्ष बताने का अनुरोध किया गया है ताकि प्रासंगिक जानकारी प्रदान की जा सके।

पारित विधेयक में उल्लिखित निःशक्त
व्यक्तियों की 21 श्रेणियां कौन सी हैं ।
इसके अलावा निःशक्त व्यक्तियों के कल्याण
हेतु बनाए गए किन्हीं तीन नियमों की भी
जानकारी दें ।
निःशक्त व्यक्तियों को संसदीय चुनावों में

निःशक्त व्यक्तियों का प्रतिनिधित्व करने हेतु
राट्रपति द्वारा संसद में एक भी निःशक्त
व्यक्ति को नामनिर्देशित क्यों नहीं किया
जाता ?
क्या संसद द्वारा किराएदारों के अधिकारों हेतु
कोई विधेयक पारित किया गया है ?
कानून के अनुसार किराएदारों के मुख्य
अधिकार क्या हैं ?
कानून के अनुसार किराया निर्धारित करने
हेतु क्या मानदंड हैं ?
यदि किसी किराएदार का कोई स्थायी पता
नहीं है तो उसे राशन कार्ड, पहचान पत्र
और आधार कार्ड कैसे मिलेगा ?

अधिकारी, संस्था अथवा कार्यालय से संपर्क
करना चाहिए ।
उत्तर
चूंकि सभाओं द्वारा पारित विधेयक के हिन्दी
संस्करण का मुद्रण नहीं किया गया है और
राज्य सभा द्वारा पारित विधेयक को लोक सभा
ने बिना किसी संशोधन के पारित कर दिया है,
अतः राज्य सभा द्वारा पारित विधेयक के हिन्दी
संस्करण की एक प्रति इस पत्र के साथ संलग्न
है । आवेदक विधेयक के प्रावधानों का अध्ययन
करके वांछित सूचना प्राप्त कर सकता है ।
इन प्रश्नों से संबंधित जानकारी संबंधित
प्रशासनिक मंत्रालय अर्थात् सामाजिक न्याय
और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय के पास उपलब्ध होगी
अतः इन प्रश्नों को पहले ही मंत्रालय के पास
भेजा जा चुका है ।
आवेदक, यदि चाहे तो, किसी ऐसे विशिट
विधेयक के शीक और र्वा का उल्लेख कर
सकता है जिसके संबंध में उसने जानकारी
मांगी है ताकि उस विधेयक के संबंध में उसे
संगत जानकारी प्रदान की जा सके ।

title: RTI Response on Lok Sabha Expenditure for Winter Session 2016
subject: Supply of information under the RTI Act, 2005.
questions: Expenditure incurred by government of India for the day-to-day operations of the Lok Sabha for the Winter Session of 2016.
Expenditure incurred for conveyance/transportation of the Members of Parliament for the Winter Session of 2016.
Expenditure for utilities, food & beverage and other expenses for the Winter Session of 2016.
Salary and other remuneration paid to MPs for the winter Session of 2016.
response_summary: The Lok Sabha Secretariat provided a partial response regarding expenditure for the Winter Session 2016. Expenditure on Parliament proceedings is incurred by multiple agencies, and there's no single head of account. Session-wise budget grant data is not available with IFU, but un-audited November 2016 figures are enclosed; December 2016 data should be collected from P&AO. Expenditure for MP conveyance was approximately 8 Lakhs, while utility and food expenses are not maintained by the Secretariat, being a matter for M/o Railways. Salaries and allowances for MPs from 16.11.2016 to 16.12.2016 totaled approximately Rs. 210085018/-.

rows: दर्शक दीर्घा से सभा की कार्यवाही देखने के लिए विवरण

आम व्यक्ति के लिए लोक सभा की कार्यवाही देखने की प्रक्रिया यह है कि उसे सी पी आई सी/लोक सभा के स्वागत कार्यालय/लोक सभा की अधिकृत वेबसाइट (www.parliamentofindia.nic.in) पर उपलब्ध आवेदन पत्र भरना होगा । साथ ही प्रपत्र में अपेक्षित विवरण (आवेदक और उसके पिता का पूरा नाम, आयु, व्यवसाय, पूरा स्थानीय और स्थायी पता) भरकर अपने निर्वाचन क्षेत्र या किसी अन्य निर्वाचन क्षेत्र संसद के एक माननीय सदस्य (लोक सभा) द्वारा विधिवत हस्ताक्षरित करवाना होगा । दर्शक दीर्घाओं के लिए केवल एक दिन पहले ही पास जारी होते हैं । 10 वर्ष से कम आयु के बच्चों को अनुमति प्रदान नहीं की जाती है। कार्यवाही सत्र की अवधि (अर्थात् जब सभा का सत्र चल रहा होता है) के दौरान देखी जा सकती है, बशर्ते कि दर्शक दीर्घा में स्थान उपलब्ध हों ।

questions: Whether the family members of Martyrs of Parliament attack on 13 December invited on the occasion, if no guidelines in this regard
Is there any proposal is under consideration to install the statues of nine martyrs of Parliament attack in Parliament House.
response_summary: For the first question, the function in memory of the martyrs of the Parliament attack on 13th December is organized by the Rajya Sabha Secretariat. Monday, July 25, 2016/Shravana 3, 1938 (Saka)

Observation by the Speaker
"Hon'ble Members, as you are aware on 22 July, 2016 several Members of
the House raised the matter of the serious breach of security of the Parliament
House by the improper conduct of Shri Bhagwant Mann, MP by videographing
and posting critical footage of Parliament House Complex on a social media. I
had also expressed my serious concerns in this regard. The Parliament is the
sanctum sanctorum of democracy. Our Parliament was attacked in 2001 and
thirteen security men and parliamentary personnel had sacrificed their lives to
protect us. After the attack, the security arrangements for the Parliament were
reviewed and the complete security apparatus, security systems and procedures
have been completely overhauled to secure the Parliament. The act of the
member of audio visual recording of the Parliament and posting it on the social
media puts the security of the Parliament in peril. In the light of the serious
security implications and consequences of these actions, I had given an
assurance to the House that I will look into the matter. In view of the extreme
gravity of the matter, I have discussed it with the Leaders of political parties in
Lok Sabha and all of them have unanimously agreed to the course of action I
propose to take.
2

this incident and submit its Report. The Inquiry Committee shall inquire into the
serious security implications and related aspects germane to and arising out of
the conduct of audio visual recording around Parliament House Estate and in the

incidents in future, and, recommend appropriate action in the matter.

Executive/Legislative/Committee/Protocol Officer: SC - 01, ST - 05, OBC - 01, Physically Challenged persons - 03 [Locomotor disability)
Research/Reference Officer: SC - 01, ST - 01, OBC - 03, Physically Challenged persons - 01 (Visual Impairment)

rows: I seek the information as available in whatever means i.e. Parliamentary Conventions, Rules of Procedures and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, Rulings by the Chair and significantly under the appropriate provisions in Presidential and Vice-Presidential Elections Act, 1952 or even rules framed thereunder which permit a sitting member of Parliament belonging to either House of People or else Council of States, who has although taken oath as Chief Minister of a State but has not been elected as a Legislator of that state, to cast his vote for the President of India as well as Vice-President of India Elections within the Parliament or in their respective Houses as MP. Also please provide me the information regarding if there have been precedents, if any, in this regard. To make my point clear, I would like to refer to cases of UP Chief Minister, Yogi Adityanath, and Goa Chief Minister, Shri Manohar Parrikar, who though still happen to be sitting MPs of Lok sabha and Rajya Sabha respectively from the state of Uttar Pradesh who would cast their votes as MPs in upcoming President of India as well as Vice-President of India elections scheduled for June/July, 2017.

Branch concerned does not deal with the election of President & Vice-President of India. However, a sitting member of Lok Sabha, even if he/she has taken a oath as Chief Minister can still attend and participate in the debate/voting for the period of six months, if he/she has not resigned from the membership of the House before that period. [Article 101(2) read with Article 164(4) of the Constitution]. Following are some precedents in Lok Sabha in this regard: (i) On 17 April, 1999 during the Fourth Session of Twelfth Lok Sabha, Shri Girdhar Gamang, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Chief Minister of Odisha also attended Lok Sabha / House on the Motion of Confidence in the Council of Ministers. (ii) Shri Yogi Adityanath, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh also attended Lok Sabha / House on 21 March, 2017. (iii) Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh also attended Lok Sabha / House on 22 March, 2017.

response_full_text: Branch concerned does not deal with the election of President & Vice-President of India. However, a sitting member of Lok Sabha, even if he/she has taken a oath as Chief Minister can still attend and participate in the debate/voting for the period of six months, if he/she has not resigned from the membership of the House before that period. [Article 101(2) read with Article 164(4) of the Constitution]. Following are some precedents in Lok Sabha in this regard: (i) On 17 April, 1999 during the Fourth Session of Twelfth Lok Sabha, Shri Girdhar Gamang, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Chief Minister of Odisha also attended Lok Sabha / House on the Motion of Confidence in the Council of Ministers. (ii) Shri Yogi Adityanath, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh also attended Lok Sabha / House on 21 March, 2017. (iii) Shri Keshav Prasad Maurya, who was a member of Lok Sabha and thereafter became the Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh also attended Lok Sabha / House on 22 March, 2017.

title: लोक सभा सचिवालय द्वारा संसद के व्यय और कार्यवाही पर RTI प्रतिक्रिया
subject: सूचना का अधिकार अधिनियम, 2005 के अंतर्गत सूचना प्रदान करना ।
questions: भारत सरकार द्वारा संसद सत्र के दौरान राज्य सभा और लोक सभा के कार्यकरण पर प्रतिदिन किया गया व्यय ।
वर्ष 2016 में (01.01.2016 से 21.12.2016 तक) सभा की कार्यवाही चलने अथवा न चलने संबंधी सूचना ।
response_summary: लोक सभा सचिवालय ने बताया कि संसद के कार्यकरण पर कई एजेंसियां व्यय करती हैं और इसके लिए कोई विशेष या पृथक लेखा-शीर्ष नहीं है। हालांकि, वित्तीय वर्ष 2009-10 से 2016-17 तक का मदवार व्यय लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर उपलब्ध है। वर्ष 2016 के दौरान लोक सभा की बैठकों से संबंधित जानकारी भी लोक सभा की वेबसाइट पर 'Business'→'Resume of work' सेक्शन में उपलब्ध है। स्थगनों/व्यवधानों के कारणों का ब्यौरा दर्ज करना संभव नहीं है क्योंकि ये विभिन्न राजनीतिक दलों के सदस्यों द्वारा विभिन्न मांगों और विरोधों के कारण उत्पन्न होते हैं।

If the files in question have not been located, whether the matter was ever brought by the Branch/Officer(s) concerned to the notice of the Secretary-General and the Hon'ble Speaker, Lok Sabha under whose sole authority the above mentioned R&CS Orders and Notifications were issued for seeking necessary directions from them on the matter since these have serious administrative implications for future decisions on service matters of the employees of the Secretariat;

OF PARLIAMENTARY AFFAIRS (SHRI PAWAN KUMAR
BANSAL): Sir, on behalf of my senior colleague, Shri
Pranab Mukherjee, I beg to move:
"That the Bill further to amend the Prevention of
Money-laundering Act, 2002, as passed by Rajya
Sabha, be taken into consideration."
Sir, the Prevention of Money-Laundering Act, 2002
was enforced in the year 2005. Gaining from the
experience and also trying to bring the provision in line
**Introduced with the recommendation of the President.
Very briefly, I would like to refer to the substantive
amendments that we have moved in the Bill that are
before the House today. These include (1) the addition of
more offences to the Schedule to the Prevention of
Money-Laundering Act, such as offences to do with
terrorist financing, (2) the inclusion of a new category of
offences, namely, offences of cross border implications-
this will effectively remove the threshold of Rs.30 lakh
for predicate offences of Part B of the Schedule in cases
of international activities; (3) to bring money changers,
money transfer service providers, and international
payment gateways within the reporting regime; and (4) to
bring one Designated Non Financial Business, namely,
casinos under the reporting regime.
There were certain difficulties also experienced in the
enforcement of the Act, which are now sought to be
removed by providing that the proceeds of crime-and
this is a very important one can be provisionally attached
even when these are in the possession of a person who
has not been charged with a predicate offence; and
secondly, to provide that such order of provisional
attachment of the proceeds of crime can be confirmed
by the Adjudicating Authority. The provisional attachment,
which was initially permitted for a period of 30 days, can
now be continued up to 150 days.

amendments that we have moved in the Bill that are
before the House today. These include (1) the addition of
more offences to the Schedule to the Prevention of
Money-Laundering Act, such as offences to do with
terrorist financing, (2) the inclusion of a new category of
offences, namely, offences of cross border implications-

bring one Designated Non Financial Business, namely,
casinos under the reporting regime.

enforcement of the Act, which are now sought to be
removed by providing that the proceeds of crime-and
this is a very important one can be provisionally attached
even when these are in the possession of a person who
has not been charged with a predicate offence; and
secondly, to provide that such order of provisional
attachment of the proceeds of crime can be confirmed
by the Adjudicating Authority. The provisional attachment,
which was initially permitted for a period of 30 days, can
now be continued up to 150 days.

rows: Kindly furnish me the details of the tentative date of preliminary Lok Sabha protocol assistant exam.

The Preliminary Examination for the post of Executive/Legislative/Committee/Protocol Assistant is proposed to be held in second half of August, 2017. (Due to non-availability of required number of schools in all the 04 cities on an earlier date.) However, the above information is purely tentative. The applicant is advised to regularly keep on visiting our Website: http://www.loksabha.nic.in Recruitment Advertisements and Notices for further updates.
How many candidates have applied (completely registered)

Initially the total number of registration of applications for the above said post was 1,11,691 and the number of completed registration was 67,388. These figures contained multiple applications submitted by the candidates. After deduction of the multiple applications, the total number of completed applications comes to 44,804 [SC-9568, ST-1765, OBC-14847 and UR-18624 = 44804] which are being further scrutinized/re-checked.
Does the candidate has to secure minimum (50% cut off) percentage in each and every component/segment.

Para 5 V. of the Advertisement No. 04/2016 reads as under :- "The minimum cut off percentages of marks in Written Test in an examination is 50%, 45% and 40% for vacancies in General, OBC and SC/ST categories, respectively. The above percentages are relaxable by 5% in case of physically Challenged persons of relevant disability and category for appointment against the vacancies reserved for physically challenged persons. (The physically challenged persons with Locomotor disability will not be entitled to avail this relaxation in marks). These percentages are the minimum marks which a candidate is required to secure in each paper/component and aggregate in the written test. However, the cut-off percentages may be raised in individual component/paper/aggregate to arrive at reasonable vacancy : candidate ratio." In this regard, it may be further stated that "The preliminary Examination will be a qualifying Examination. Only those candidates who obtain the minimum qualifying marks in each component and aggregate in the Preliminary Examination will be called for the Main Examination. The marks secured by the candidates in the Preliminary Examination will not be counted while preparing the final selection list."

response_full_text:
The Preliminary Examination for the post of Executive/Legislative/Committee/Protocol Assistant is proposed to be held in second half of August, 2017. (Due to non-availability of required number of schools in all the 04 cities on an earlier date.) However, the above information is purely tentative. The applicant is advised to regularly keep on visiting our Website: http://www.loksabha.nic.in Recruitment Advertisements and Notices for further updates.
Initially the total number of registration of applications for the above said post was 1,11,691 and the number of completed registration was 67,388. These figures contained multiple applications submitted by the candidates. After deduction of the multiple applications, the total number of completed applications comes to 44,804 [SC-9568, ST-1765, OBC-14847 and UR-18624 = 44804] which are being further scrutinized/re-checked.
Para 5 V. of the Advertisement No. 04/2016 reads as under :- "The minimum cut off percentages of marks in Written Test in an examination is 50%, 45% and 40% for vacancies in General, OBC and SC/ST categories, respectively. The above percentages are relaxable by 5% in case of physically Challenged persons of relevant disability and category for appointment against the vacancies reserved for physically challenged persons. (The physically challenged persons with Locomotor disability will not be entitled to avail this relaxation in marks). These percentages are the minimum marks which a candidate is required to secure in each paper/component and aggregate in the written test. However, the cut-off percentages may be raised in individual component/paper/aggregate to arrive at reasonable vacancy : candidate ratio." In this regard, it may be further stated that "The preliminary Examination will be a qualifying Examination. Only those candidates who obtain the minimum qualifying marks in each component and aggregate in the Preliminary Examination will be called for the Main Examination. The marks secured by the candidates in the Preliminary Examination will not be counted while preparing the final selection list."

With reference to your online RTI application dt. 31.01.2016 (received on 01.02.2016), I am directed to forward information to the extent pertaining to and available in this Secretariat (Annexure), as approved by the CPIO.
The questions asked by the concerned Members of Parliament from November, 1999 onwards along with their replies are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qmembersearch.aspx The applicant may be advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information. The information prior to November, 1999 is available in branch concerned of this Secretariat. The applicant is requested to visit the Parliament Library by contacting Shri S.P. Roy Choudhary, Joint Director, Tel. no. 011-23034347 or depute someone to cull out the desired information. All necessary assistance will be provided at their end.
Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 14th to 16th Lok Sabhas are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance - All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information. The attendance details of members prior to Fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website. The information is available in the records of the Branch and is voluminous. The applicant may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally peruse the records available in the Branch.
No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to them for necessary action. You are requested to approach them directly.

rows: Seeking information on MPs: Question asked by them during their tenure

The questions asked by the concerned Members of Parliament from November, 1999 onwards along with their replies are available on Lok Sabha website i.e. http://164.100.47.192/Loksabha/Questions/Qmembersearch.aspx. The applicant may be advised to go through the above website of Lok Sabha for obtaining the desired information. The information prior to November, 1999 is available in branch concerned of this Secretariat. The applicant is requested to visit the Parliament Library by contacting Shri S.P. Roy Choudhary, Joint Director, Tel. no. 011-23034347 or depute someone to cull out the desired information. All necessary assistance will be provided at their end.
Percentage of their attendance

Lok Sabha Secretariat does not maintain the attendance of members on the basis of percentage, minimum and maximum attendance etc. As far as attendance of members is concerned, an Attendance Register is maintained for members (except Hon'ble Speaker, Deputy Speaker and Ministers) to sign against their names in token of having attended the sitting of the House on a particular day. Details of signing/not signing the Attendance Register by members of Lok Sabha during all the sessions of 14th to 16th Lok Sabhas are available on the website of the Lok Sabha i.e., www.loksabha.nic.in under the headings Members-Attendance of Members-Member-wise Attendance - All Members respectively. The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information. The attendance details of members prior to Fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website. The information is available in the records of the Branch and is voluminous. The applicant may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally peruse the records available in the Branch.
Criminal cases against them

No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to them for necessary action. You are requested to approach them directly.

The applicant may, however, note that it is possible that a member attended the sitting of the House on a particular day but forgot to sign the Attendance Register for that day. The applicant may be requested to visit the website and access the desired information. The attendance details of members prior to Fourteenth Lok Sabha have not been uploaded on the Lok Sabha website. The information is available in the records of the Branch and is voluminous. The applicant may be advised to come to Lok Sabha Secretariat and personally peruse the records available in the Branch.
Criminal cases against them

No information relating to criminal cases registered against former or sitting Members of Lok Sabha nor the sections under which they are charged is maintained in the Secretariat. Further, there is no provision in the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha requiring the Lok Sabha Secretariat to maintain such information. As the query appears to pertain to other public authorities such as Election Commission of India and Ministry of Law and Justice, the application has been forwarded to them for necessary action. You are requested to approach them directly.

Therefore, the RTI application is transferred to the CPIOs of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment and the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for direct response to the applicant.
